title: Beyond the ballot, October 7 families call for a different kind of Israeli politics
body: Moshe Shapiro wants Israelis to learn to live together with the same seriousness with which they learned to protect wildflowers.Shapiro, whose son Aner was killed on October 7, 2023, while throwing grenades back out of a roadside shelter to protect fellow Nova music festival-goers, is among the bereaved relatives behind Hamechane, an initiative seeking to make social cohesion a national responsibility.Ahead of the elections, he joined Hoda Daxa and Shai Zohar in an interview with The Jerusalem Post about what that would require – and whose place in Israeli society needs to be recognized.“Unity is an operating system, an approach,” said Zohar, the uncle of Capt. Omer Neutra, a lone soldier from New York who was killed on October 7. His body was taken to Gaza and returned in November 2025. Daxa's husband, Col. Ehsan Daxa, commander of the 401st Armored Brigade, was killed commanding troops in northern Gaza in October 2024.For Shapiro, the wildflower campaign offers an example of how such a change can take root. Beginning in the 1960s, it combined legal protection with public education, turning a cause championed by a small group into something generations of children grew up knowing. He wants respect for others, even across deep disagreements, to become just as ingrained.A search for common ground“Hamechane,” meaning “the denominator,” expresses the search for common ground. The organization's members include bereaved families, captivity survivors, and people wounded in the Israel-Gaza War. They want the next government to establish, within its first 100 days, a national framework for social cohesion.For the three interviewees, the urgency comes from lives they are trying to honor, and a country they fear could repeat its failures.Zohar argued that the divisions preceding October 7 helped bring Israel to catastrophe. He regards internal polarization as the country's greatest existential threat and warned that, without addressing it, Israelis risk paying that price again. He cautioned that Israelis cannot risk slipping backward, that it is “something we must prevent at all costs.“We have already paid an immense price,” he added.His warning accompanied a more personal admission: Until he heard Daxa, a member of Israel's Druze community, speak about the Nation-State Law, he had not understood what it meant to her community.“It went over my head,” he said. “Today I understand it better.”The 2018 Basic Law reserves national self-determination in Israel to the Jewish people, defines Hebrew as the state's language, and gives Arabic special status. It contains no explicit guarantee of equality. Druze critics have argued that it excludes them from the country to which they belong and for which their community's soldiers fight.The High Court upheld the law in 2021, interpreting it as compatible with equality protections. The dispute nevertheless returned during the war: In November 2023, Druze spiritual leader Sheikh Muwaffaq Tarif called for constitutional recognition of the community's rights, while the coalition promised separate legislation on Druze status.For Daxa, the question of belonging also arises in ordinary encounters. She recalled traveling by train with her children and speaking Arabic. Nobody said anything, she explained, but she noticed passengers' discomfort.“Hatred doesn't distinguish,” she said.She was explicit about the limits of a unity understood only as solidarity among Jews.“There are partners here,” she said, describing people who already feel part of Israeli society and want to contribute as active participants.The group's work, she explained, begins with what its members have come to understand through loss. They bring different opinions and will vote for different parties. What makes conversation possible is a willingness to learn rather than being certain that one side is right and the other wrong.“We come with an open heart,” she said.Shapiro described a yearlong process of developing a shared vision. He had participated in other initiatives, including efforts to encourage dialogue during the judicial reform legislation dispute. In Hamechane, he found religious and secular Jews, ultra-Orthodox (haredim), Druze, and people from the Right and Left.“This is the face of Israeli society,” he said.The relationships formed through that process imbued him with the confidence that cooperation is possible. Nobody, he emphasized, has had to conceal or abandon their opinions.His own family contains sharp political differences, he said. Learning to handle them means recognizing that the relationship matters, while allowing disagreement to be expressed respectfully, he explained. He wants that responsibility extended to the country.His grandfather Haim-Moshe Shapiro signed Israel's Declaration of Independence and served as a minister. Before the Six Day War, he pressed prime minister Levi Eshkol to bring opposition parties into the government and appoint Moshe Dayan defense minister.Moshe recalled his grandfather's insistence on bringing political rivals into government as Israel faced the prospect of war. In June 1967, just before the Six Day War, the government was expanded to include two opposition parties: Gahal, led by Menachem Begin, and Rafi, whose members included Dayan. Begin joined the cabinet, and Dayan became defense minister.Aner's writing gives that inheritance another voice.Kaleidoscope of religious, secular, right-wing, left-wingIn a social media post written before October 7, Aner reacted to graffiti defacing an image of the Lubavitcher Rebbe. He questioned the categories through which Israelis were seeing one another: religious, secular, right-wing, left-wing. People were speaking in black-and-white terms, dividing the world between those on their side and “them.”“There really is no 'them,'” he wrote at the time.In an essay on otherness, boundaries, and dialogue, psychoanalyst Shmuel Ehrlich links the possibility of dialogue to recognizing the other's humanity and accepting that conflicting feelings can coexist within a relationship. His account echoes the openness the three describe: making room for complexity, in ourselves as well as in those with whom we disagree.During the shiva for Aner, Moshe recalled that he saw cooperation between people from opposing political camps and believed the divisions his son had written against were receding. He now describes the return of that hostility with disappointment.Hamechane aims to make cooperation endure beyond emergencies. Alongside its call for government action, Hamechane seeks to encourage personal connections and dialogue between people from different backgrounds through schools, workplaces, and communities.Shapiro envisages teaching children from a young age about different communities and how to listen to others and handle disagreement. He also wants action in communications, including measures against online activity that inflames hatred. He worries about political speech that reduces entire groups to caricatures.Politicians, he said, have begun to sound like bots. He wants people to return to speaking like people, addressing substance rather than circulating slogans.These are proposals for what a national effort could address. The initiative has not settled the precise structure of the body it seeks. Its representatives say elected officials and professionals should develop that framework, with responsibility extending across government and society.Daxa acknowledged that the group does not possess all the professional answers. Recognition of polarization as a national danger, she believes, would itself mark a beginning.Her husband's example gives her a way to describe the conduct she hopes to encourage. Whatever the subject, including haredi enlistment, Ehsan could articulate the other person's perspective.“Even if he didn't agree, he still had the ability to see, understand, and respect,” she said.For Zohar, Omer's life offered a similar example of connection. Raised on Long Island, he came to Israel to serve in the IDF. His uncle described him as someone who brought people together, linking Diaspora Jewry and Israel.Honoring that life, Zohar said, means taking responsibility for the society that remains.Shapiro returned to the subject of the shelter where Aner died. Apart from the two friends he arrived with, he said, his son did not know the people behind him. One of those friends was Hersh Goldberg-Polin, who was taken hostage from the shelter and murdered by his Hamas captors alongside five other hostages in a tunnel in Rafah in August 2024.For Aner, Moshe said, the politics, religious identities, and backgrounds of the people inside the shelter with him did not determine whether he would protect them.“We're not asking people to sacrifice their lives,” Moshe said.What he asks is that they listen, make room for others, and recognize that disagreement does not cancel their obligations to one another.Among the words Aner left behind were lines his father read aloud during the interview:“There are wars we have no choice but to fight.There are battles we cannot help but lose.And there is hatred looking for a place, now finding fertile ground.There is also time to wake up and love.”Read more about Hamechane here: hamechane.org.il

title: US updates Israel travel warning, cites growing threat from Iran-backed Houthis
body: The US State Department issued an updated travel advisory notice for Israel on Friday, warning of an increased threat of armed attacks by Iran-backed Houthi terrorists and the potential for a rapid escalation of regional hostilities.The update did not change Israel's overall travel advisory classification, which remains at Level 3, urging American citizens to reconsider travel due to terrorism and unrest. The existing risk indicators and restrictions on travel to certain areas of the country also remain unchanged.In its warning on armed conflict, the State Department cited previous Houthi attacks against Saudi Arabia, including strikes on civilian airports and critical infrastructure that resulted in civilian casualties and major travel disruptions.The department warned that hostilities involving the Houthis could escalate rapidly beyond the areas immediately affected, potentially posing additional risks to travelers across the region.The updated warning comes against the backdrop of previous missile threats originating from Yemen, which have required Israel to activate air defense systems and issue civilian alerts.US maintains restrictions on travel to Israeli border areasDespite the updated regional threat assessment, Washington has not raised its overall warning level for Israel. The State Department continues to advise Americans to reconsider travel because of terrorism and unrest, while maintaining stricter Level 4 restrictions in several designated areas.These restrictions cover areas north of the Route 85, Route 90, and Route 87 boundaries in northern Israel; locations within 11.3 kilometers of the Gaza Strip; and areas within 2.4 kilometers of the Israel-Egypt border, except near the Taba crossing, also known as the Menachem Begin crossing.The State Department said Israeli authorities restrict travel in the designated northern areas because of IDF activity and presence, and instructed Americans not to travel there for any reason.US government employees working in Israel face the same geographical restrictions. Official travel to these areas requires approval from the US Embassy's security office.The advisory also reiterated that, as of August 26, family members are permitted to accompany US government employees stationed in Israel. However, Washington warned that additional security measures affecting US personnel could be introduced as conditions evolve.The State Department emphasized that Israel's security environment remains complex and can change rapidly, warning that violence could occur without advance notice.Regional tensions could also prompt airlines to cancel flights or reduce services to and from Israel, potentially disrupting travel plans even in areas not subject to the highest-level restrictions.Americans urged to prepare for missile and drone threatsThe advisory urged American citizens planning to visit Israel to remain vigilant, avoid demonstrations and large gatherings, and familiarize themselves with emergency procedures.Travelers were advised to identify nearby bomb shelters and download the Home Front Command's Red Alert application, or similar services, to receive real-time warnings about incoming rockets, missiles and armed drones.Israel's Home Front Command emergency warning systems have been used during previous missile attacks, providing residents with alerts intended to help them reach protected areas.The military has also updated its advance-warning capabilities to give civilians more time to prepare for certain missile threats.The State Department encouraged American travelers to enroll in its Smart Traveler Enrollment Program, which enables the US Embassy to distribute security updates and contact citizens or their emergency contacts during a crisis.Americans were also urged to develop independent evacuation plans that do not rely on US government assistance, follow instructions from local security officials, and exercise particular caution near checkpoints and areas with a significant security presence.The advisory further recommended purchasing comprehensive travel insurance that covers emergency medical treatment, evacuation assistance, and trip cancellations.The warnings underscore the continued importance of civilian preparedness amid regional missile and drone threats, with Israeli authorities having previously reviewed the timing and operation of emergency alerts during periods of heightened tensions.Although the October 23 notice highlighted the increased potential for Houthi aggression, it did not announce additional restrictions on travel to Israel or a change in the State Department's assessment of the country's overall travel risk.

title: Letter from Cornell's Jane Doe: University president appeared to 'disbelieve' assault allegations
body: Cornell University's Jane Doe told faculty members that she felt  “unsupported and disbelieved” by the Ivy League university's president, Michael Kotlikoff, NBC reported on Wednesday. In a letter to Cornell's faculty senate, Doe provided what she called a secondhand account of a meeting between Kotlikoff and the then-president of her sorority, Tri Delta. “After the conversation she shared with me, with concern, that President Kotlikoff's initial response was along the lines of, 'Why did she wait so long to report it?'” Doe wrote in the letter. “She interpreted his question as an expression of doubt in the veracity of my story.”The meeting was held months after October 19-20, 2024, when Doe was allegedly raped by seven members of the now-defunct Chi Phi fraternity.She alerted campus police to the incident on November 8, 2024.Cornell claims comments were taken out of contextThe meeting that Jane Doe is claiming to provide a secondhand account of occurred in January 2025. In the letter, Doe wrote that her sorority president told her that at least one other faculty member “appeared distressed” at Kotlikoff's line of questioning, and said that the person believed that “the President's response was inappropriate.”Cornell said in a statement that while Kotlikoff did make a similar comment at the meeting, the secondhand account was taken out of context.“The second-hand account of the question asked by President Kotlikoff in a January 2025 meeting in the letter is incorrect, based on a documented first-hand account,” the statement added. “The question 'why did it take so long for the assault to be reported' was directed at bystanders who did not use Cornell's anonymous tip line, despite ongoing social media activity about the incident in October 2024. He was not questioning Jane Doe's reporting.”Cornell's Jane Doe felt the administration didn't believe herBut Jane Doe said in her letter that the comment left her feeling unsupported and disbelieved by President Kotlikoff.“It diminished my confidence in the administration's ability to approach my experience with the understanding, sensitivity, and fairness I had hoped for and expected from what had been my dream school.”This comes ahead of a vote of no confidence in Kotlikoff's administration. Doe's lawyer, Thomas Giuffra, told NBC that the letter she wrote to the faculty senate was for “informational purposes only.”“Jane Doe thought it important that the faculty senate have this information as it deliberates and considers the resolutions or motions before it,” Giuffra said. “Jane Doe would ask the faculty senate to give her letter whatever weight or credibility it deems appropriate.”

title: Protests spread across Syria after disabled man dies in Israeli raid on village
body: Anti-Israel demonstrations were reported across several parts of Syria following the death of a young man with a disability who was shot by Israeli forces during a military incursion into the village of Jamla in western Daraa countryside on Thursday. Protests took place in Idlib, Homs, Damascus, Daraa, Quneitra and along the Syrian coast, with demonstrators protesting Israeli military incursions on Syrian territory, particularly in southern Syria. Israel says its military operations in Syria, which intensified after the fall of Bashar al-Assad's regime, are defensive measures necessary to safeguard its national security. Protests spread across countryThe demonstrations drew significant participation and extended well beyond areas along the border. Confirmed estimates of the number of people taking part were not immediately available. The protests followed an Israeli military operation in Jamla in western Daraa countryside. During the incursion, Israeli forces reportedly searched civilian homes and deployed snipers on residential rooftops. A young man with a disability was shot dead by Israeli forces during the operation. The incident prompted demonstrations in Daraa and other parts of the country, including areas far from the locations of Israeli military activity.

title: Netanyahu switches Israel's position to favor Argentina in dispute over Falklands - report
body: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered diplomats to change Israel's official position on sovereignty over the Falklands and join Argentina in calling for direct talks between Buenos Aires and London for the islands' future, The Telegraph reported on Saturday.The change does not go so far as to formally back Argentina's claim over the Falklands, but it raises fears that Israel could do so if the United Kingdom imposes further sanctions on West Bank settlements, according to the report.Israeli ambassador to the UN Danny Danon called for direct negotiations between the UK and Argentina at a UN session a few days ago.“Israel recognizes the importance that the Argentine public attaches to this issue, as well as its ongoing efforts through diplomatic channels and in accordance with the principles of international law,” he said.While the language did not include formal support for Argentina's claim over the Falklands, government sources told The Telegraph that it marked a significant shift in Israel's position and raises fears that Israel could go further later, especially if Netanyahu wins the upcoming election.“The wording of the statement itself got approved at the highest ranks of the Israeli government,” one source said. “This is the first time Israel has got involved in this conflict.” Israeli embassy denies claimHowever, Israel's embassy spokesperson in the UK, Alex Gandler, denied that Netanyahu had issued any order to shift Israel's position.“No such directive exists,” he wrote on X/Twitter.I categorically deny this allegation. No such directive exists. https://t.co/VI2T9u5T9f— Alex Gandler (@AlexGandler) October 24, 2026Tensions rise between UK, Israel as Argentine ties remain strongThis comes after UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband recently imposed economic sanctions on settlements, accusing Israel of “ethnic cleansing.”Tensions rose as the UK consulate in Jerusalem was downgraded, and most of the staff was expelled.An Israeli official told The Telegraph that the UN intervention had also been taken in the context of “a changing policy from the British government toward Israel,” citing in particular “all the critical statements that the British prime minister and foreign secretary said in the last few weeks, especially regarding sanctions.”Ties between Israel and Argentina have been strong, with Argentine President Javier Milei having visited Israel multiple times, including to light a ceremonial torch on Israel's Independence Day.Milei has expressed consistent support for Israel throughout the war following the October 7 massacre.

title: Two former FBI agents charged with lying to Congress during Hunter Biden laptop inquiry - report
body: Two former FBI officials were charged with making false statements to Congress regarding the investigation into former US president Joe Biden's son, Hunter, ahead of the 2024 presidential election, the Washington Post reported.The US Justice Department (DOJ) announced the charges against Nikki Floris, a former analyst who led the intelligence division in the FBI's Washington field office, and Bradley Benavides, a former deputy assistant director for counterintelligence, on Friday. The charges allege that both intentionally hid information while testifying to the House Judiciary Committee about FBI probes into Hunter Biden and his laptop in 2023.Floris's attorneys claimed that the DOJ had "accused her falsely of a crime on the say-so of politicians, not on the facts," the Washington Post reported. Similarly, Ron Safer, attorney for Benavides, urged the court to hold a hearing to determine if prosecutors had enough evidence for the charges against "two lifetime public servants.""Nikki Floris is a patriot,” her attorneys said in a statement. “She served our nation as a dedicated FBI intelligence officer for nearly 20 years. … It's no coincidence the government is filing these nonsense charges now, years later, on the eve of an election.”The pair face up to five years in prison if found guilty. They were released on Friday morning after a brief appearance before a federal magistrate judge.Former FBI agents allegedly lied about involvement in the Biden investigationFloris and Benavides undermined "the very institutions they swore to uphold," US Attorney Jeanine Pirro, whose office is prosecuting the case, accused in a statement.“Lying to Congress by anyone strikes at the heart of our democratic system­­ but when senior FBI agents lie to Congress believing they are above the law, it's time to bring the hammer of justice down on them."According to an FBI affidavit, Floris repeatedly denied involvement in the Hunter Biden investigations during a hearing at the House Judiciary Committee in 2023. “In reality, she was in frequent communication with the case team for over a year during which she both sent and received information about Hunter Biden,” the affidavit reads.“Floris testified that she knew nothing about the Hunter Biden laptop. In reality, she coordinated the FBI's response to news articles about the laptop in real time.”Testifying a few months later, Benavides told the same committee that he knew little about the case, explaining that he had learned about the laptop from a Wikipedia entry while preparing his testimony. "In reality," the affidavit reads, "he was in constant communication about the laptop over a period of days."A member of the committee said that those answers had “influenced the Committee's investigation significantly, including by thwarting investigative follow-up interviews and subpoenas,” the Washington Post reported.Relevance of Hunter Biden's laptop is a hotly debated partisan issueRepublicans and Democrats have debated the significance of Hunter Biden's laptop, with Republicans claiming it contains evidence of corruption within the Biden family, while Democrats say it was part of a Republican conspiracy.The laptop was handed over to the FBI in 2019 after a computer shop owner said Hunter Biden had dropped it off at his shop and not returned to collect it.The owner told The Washington Post that he decided to turn the laptop over to authorities after he viewed some of its contents.Trump administration has used its power to bring charges against critical officialsUS Magistrate Judge Zia M. Faruqui raised concerns about the timing of the charges in court on Friday. He also asked if the alleged false statements had had a material impact on the investigation.He granted the defense attorney's request for a hearing to weigh government evidence, which will take place on Tuesday - sooner than would typically be expected given the defendants had been sent home.“It's certainly rare,” Faruqui said. “But it is more rare that we have charges that are this old of this nature.”He added that the information in the case "certainly appears quite old," as it was charged over three years after the former agents had testified to Congress. Faruqui said that both Floris and Benavides had "sparkling backgrounds" in law enforcement, the Washington Post reported, adding that they had an interest in clearing their names as quickly as possible."There is a Sword of Damocles hanging over their head … this will follow them for the rest of their lives,” Faruqui said.Since the beginning of the second Trump administration, many FBI agents whom the US president's allies claimed were working against him have been pushed out of the agency. This includes some agents who claim they were only fired because they worked on investigations into US President Donald Trump, and some who say they were fired because they didn't show him sufficient loyalty.

title: Atlanta Falcons face backlash over social media logo resembling Nazi imagery
body: NFL football team Atlanta Falcons faced backlash after changing its profile picture across social media platforms to a logo fans found similar to Nazi imagery on Wednesday. The picture featured the team's old falcon symbol from the 1960s and 1970s, over red, white, and black stripes. The new profile was uploaded ahead of the Falcons' game against the San Francisco 49ers, where the team is set to wear uniforms with a throwback design. The announcement of the new profile picture on X/Twitter was met with thousands of comments pointing out the similarities to Nazi symbolism. Users edited the falcon symbol onto images of flags at Nazi rallies and onto armbands on images of marching Nazi soldiers. The official Encyclopedia Britannica X account responded to the post with an image of comedian Norm Macdonald opening a bit about Germany, saying: "I don't know if you guys are history buffs."The Stop Antisemitism account responded, "Can we have a word ..." @AtlantaFalcons https://t.co/eA73ri6EFx— Encyclopaedia Britannica (@Britannica) October 22, 2026No ill intent behind image, sports logo historian saysSports logo historian Chris Creamer told NBC that there had been no ill intent in the profile picture and that he "can't imagine in a million years" that the Falcons would deliberately align themselves with Nazis.“It's throwback weekend for the team, and the social media team just wanted to dress up like the players were going to, and it's a very common thing that social media accounts do across all sports,” he told NBC.A team representative told NBC that the Falcons do not have a new logo but did not comment further.The profile picture has since been changed back to an image of an Atlanta Falcons helmet.

title: First Nations leaders voice priorities ahead of historic meeting in Ottawa
body:
First Nations leaders are preparing to meet with Prime Minister Mark Carney and the nation’s premiers, the first gathering of its kind in more than two decades.
Tensions between First Nations leaders and the Government of Canada have risen since Carney was elected in 2025, including over legislation that was passed to streamline development of major projects.
Some Indigenous leaders criticized the legislation over a lack of consultation, saying it posed a threat to reconciliation.
The Assembly of First Nations has been preparing for the meeting for months by hosting town halls with chiefs to discuss the actions they want to see governments take.
The AFN released a series of position papers last week on economic development, policing and public safety, employment, and health.
One of the main goals for First Nations leaders is a First Nations sovereign wealth fund. The fund, proposed by Chippewas of the Thames First Nation, would pool capital to ensure First Nations can build long-term wealth in their communities.
Other leaders worry that if the meeting focuses solely on economics, other concerns like homelessness, addiction and suicide may not get the attention they deserve.
“Unless the prime minister, the premiers and the territories are going to look a little bit deeper than resource development or economic reconciliation, I worry that they’re not going to be successful with their agenda,” Jeff Copenance, the chief of Ojibways of Onigaming First Nation, said.
Alberta’s recent referendum shed light on the inclusion of First Nations in decision making after First Nations in the province said there were “unnecessary obstacles” to being able to vote.
Siksika Nation said that while it was pleased with the outcome of the referendum, the polling station in its community was understaffed and it did not receive enough ballots from Elections Alberta.
The Assembly of Manitoba Chiefs (AMC) said it will be bringing its priorities to Ottawa on Monday, with a focus on treaty rights, governance and reconciliation.
The AMC said it will be pressing for action on economic sovereignty while making sure that First Nations are consulted in all decisions affecting them.
“Our Treaties and our alliances with the Crown are agreements between Nations. They are not historical arrangements to be set aside when they become inconvenient,” said Grand Chief Kyra Wilson. “We will not accept a relationship defined by promises without action. We expect to be treated as equal partners, and we expect governments to work with us.”
Wilson said the purpose of the meeting is to develop next steps for how Canada and First Nations leadership can work together moving forward.
“We know that one meeting is not going to resolve longstanding issues that we continually deal with every single day,” she said, adding that participation in the meeting is not consent to any major project or decision.
“The true testament of this meeting and the outcome of this meeting is not the meeting itself. It’s going to come in the action and the commitments that are followed through on in the days, weeks, months and years following October 26th,” Chief Tréchelle Bunn, of the Birdtail Sioux Dakota Nation, said Saturday.
She said she is hoping to share a message with the prime minister demanding accountability following a July 2024 apology to the Dakota and Lakota nations for “generations and decades of discrimination, exclusion, and misrepresentation of our people” that she said has not been followed up with action.
The AMC said it is “sad” that all Chiefs will not be provided the opportunity to speak at the meeting, and while each nation has their own priorities and concerns, the issues of sovereignty, treaty rights and governance affect them all.
“We are not opposed to responsible economic development. We want our people to prosper. We want investment, employment, business opportunities and ownership, and a fair share of the well-generated from our territories,” Chief David Monias of the Nation at Pimicikamak Okimawin said Saturday. “They keep saying that this is about sharing. Well where’s our share of the wealth?”
The chief said he wants to see Bill 39, which fast-tracks major project approvals, repealed.
“Equity is an important opportunity and it’s not a substitute for our rights,” he said.
The AMC said their message is not one of confrontation, but an invitation to build a better relationship between First Nations leadership and the Government of Canada.
Chief Monias used Carney’s own words to express the importance of including First Nations in the decision-making process: “If we are not at the table, we’re on the menu.”

title: New reality show to spotlight affordable African interior design, showcase young talent
body:
Retouched By Flair, an interior design organisation, has unveiled a reality television show to promote African interior design, empower young creatives, and show how homes can be transformed without excessive spending.
The 13-week programme, titled The Retoucher, will premiere in the first quarter of 2027 and feature emerging interior designers competing in design challenges as they transform homes and other spaces.
Creator and Executive Producer Debola Majekodunmi said the initiative was designed to make interior design more accessible while giving young African designers a platform to showcase their creativity and gain visibility.
Speaking at the unveiling in Lagos, Majekodunmi said the project would help promote African design identity, indigenous materials and local creativity, adding that good interior design should not be limited to wealthy people.
“I want every home to be decently dressed up. I want to promote that it is not only the wealthy that can have a good interior design,” she said.
Majekodunmi noted that while African culture had gained recognition through food, music, and fashion, interior design still had significant growth potential and needed wider appreciation.
“We want to promote African interior design. We have beauty in Africa. Africa has been promoted through the food, music, and clothing industries. We want to have our own African interior design. So this is the beginning of it,” she said.
She added that the initiative was expected to expand beyond Nigeria into other African regions, including East, North and Southern Africa, with the long-term ambition of building a franchise.
Majekodunmi said the production would begin with auditions across four locations in Nigeria, including Lagos, Abuja and Port Harcourt, with a fourth location still under consideration.
According to her, about 100 aspiring designers are expected to emerge from the auditions before proceeding to a boot camp for training, mentoring and further assessment.
The process will eventually produce 20 shortlisted contestants who will participate in the 13-week programme.
The organisers also plan to invite homeowners from different backgrounds to submit their homes for transformation. The selection is expected to include people from different economic circumstances and life experiences, giving contestants opportunities to address practical design needs.
Majekodunmi said the show would combine education, creativity and empowerment, with the contestants expected to apply their skills to real-life spaces.
“We are transforming homes and empowering lives. That is it. We have come to empower homes, we have come to transform lives,” she said.
She added that the organisers were pleased with the reception at the unveiling and hoped the programme would grow into a wider movement for African interior design.
Veteran Nollywood filmmaker and producer of the show, Tade Ogidan, said The Retoucher would combine competition, audience participation and practical design challenges.
Ogidan explained that contestants would work on different types of spaces, including interiors and exteriors, showing how creative ideas can improve people’s living environments.
He also disclosed that the programme would feature transformations of homes belonging to people who might not ordinarily afford professional interior design services.
“We have part of the concept where we will take people in poor homes. They would all pitch in to say, ‘Come and do up our home, come and do up our home.’
“We will look at it, and then we will go and give them the surprise of their lives, do up the place to become somewhere they would love,” he said.
Ogidan added that viewers would play an active role in the programme, making audience participation an important part of the competition.
At the unveiling, contestants divided into Team Blue and Team Orange were given 25 minutes to transform blank sets using available materials.
Team Orange emerged as the winner after the judges’ assessment and audience voting, which accounted for 40 per cent and 60 per cent of the final scores, respectively.
Team Blue received 16 points from the audience, while Team Orange scored 19 points. The judges’ scores also favoured Team Orange.
The winning team received N200,000, while the runners-up were awarded N50,000.
Strategy Adviser at Retouched By Flair, Hubert Davies, said homeowners could create attractive living spaces without spending too much.
“It doesn’t cost a fortune for you to change your home into your palace,” he said.
Similarly, Jennifer Chukwujekwe, founder of Jenniez School of African Interior Design and former President of the Interior Designers Association of Nigeria, highlighted the sector’s opportunities.
Chukwujekwe also called for greater attention to older people’s needs in interior design, stressing the importance of creating spaces that accommodate their specific requirements.
GDM Group Chief Executive Officer Victor Afolabi said the initiative offered opportunities to improve homes affordably and encouraged partnerships to support the programme and expand its reach.
The Retoucher Project Manager, Jemimah Ododo, said the project would promote designs that reflect African culture and identity while creating opportunities for local talent.
NFVCB added that this would help the Nollywood industry accommodate local, affordable filmmaking budgets beyond Western appeal.
She added that the initiative would demonstrate how indigenous resources and African creativity could produce world-class designs while supporting emerging professionals.
Beyond the television programme, the organisers said they planned to explore training, design exhibitions, partnerships and product development to create further opportunities for young creatives.
They called on brands, broadcasters, building-material manufacturers, retailers, property developers, and investors to support the project through partnerships and sponsorships, aiming to expand its reach and promote African interior design.

title: Zelenskyy imposes sanctions on suppliers to Russia’s defense industry
body:
President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyy has signed decrees enacting decisions by the National Security and Defense Council of Ukraine (NSDC) to impose sanctions on Russian entities and individuals. These parties are involved in the production of Russian ballistic missiles or supply equipment and components to Russian defense industry enterprises for use in military aircraft, armored vehicles, missile systems, and drones.
Relevant decrees, Nos. 1058/2024 and 1059/2024, are dated October 24 and have been published on the head of state’s official website.
The first sanction list includes 51 individuals and 44 legal entities involved in the manufacture of ballistic missiles—weapons that the Russian Federation uses to attack critical and civilian infrastructure, as well as to shell Ukrainian cities and communities. These entities produce and supply raw materials, equipment, and tools used to create long-range strike systems, including the Iskander, Kalibr, Kh-101, and Kinzhal.
The sanction package specifically targets Russian enterprises that manufacture weaponry, components, and related software, as well as the executives of these companies.
All individuals subject to these sanctions are citizens of the Russian Federation. Of the 44 entities on the first list, 42 are registered in the Russian Federation, while two are registered in the People's Republic of China.
Additionally, sanctions have been imposed on 32 Russian citizens and 35 Russian companies that are part of the production and supply chains for high-precision industrial equipment, tools, components, electronics, and raw materials intended for entities that serve Russia’s defense-industrial complex.
Sanctions have also been imposed on enterprises belonging to the Russian industrial group Rusal—entities that are significant to the aggressor state and involved in the production of military aircraft, armored vehicles, missile systems, drones, and other military hardware.
"We are systematically identifying enterprises involved in the production of Russian ballistic missiles and other weaponry, and applying sanctions against them. We are also working to extend these sanctions to other jurisdictions. Taken together, these measures should significantly weaken the capacity of the Russian military-industrial complex to manufacture weapons," noted Vladyslav Vlasiuk, Advisor and Presidential Commissioner for Sanction Policy.

title: Man City beaten by Aston Villa to end perfect Premier League start
body: Manchester City’s perfect Premier League start came to a crashing halt in a 2-1 defeat at Aston Villa as Nicolas Jackson’s double extended an upturn in form for Unai Emery’s new-look side. Enzo Maresca had become the first manager to win his first seven Premier League games in charge of a new club but failed to find a solution to City’s struggles at Villa Park, where they have now lost for the past four seasons. After Jackson blasted home the opener after just six minutes, Villa relied on a brilliant goalkeeping display from Zion Suzuki to keep City at bay. Erling Haaland breifly levelled early in the second half only for Villa to respond on the hour mark when Jackson drilled home Ibrahim Mbaye’s cross. Four years on from Emery’s arrival, which has transformed the club from a sleeping giant into the Champions League, the Spaniard is working more magic despite seeing the spine of his squad in recent seasons decimated. Six of the side that started Villa’s victory in last season’s Europa League left during the transfer window. But the recruitment of the likes of Jackson, Suzuki, Mbaye and Johan Manzambi is already paying dividends after a slow start to the campaign. Until now City have managed to shrug off the cloud hanging over the club’s Premier League future to keep winning on the field. The 10-time English champions are appealing a guilty verdict on over 100 charges of breaking financial rules between 2009 and 2018 that could lead to swingeing sanctions, including relegation. There was little sign of that distraction affecting Enzo Maresca’s men, but they were made to pay for two sloppy defensive errors. A heavy touch by Marc Guehi presented Jackson with possession for the opening goal as he cut inside Elliott Anderson and blasted high past Gianluigi Donnarumma. City largely dominated the remainder of the first half, but could not find a way past Suzuki. Iliman Ndiaye, Rayan Cherki and Abdukodir Khusanov were all denied before Ndiaye struck the post. City’s pressure finally told on 52 minutes when Haaland powered in a header from Ndiaye’s cross for his 13th goal in 10 appearances this season. Josko Gvardiol nearly completed the comeback when Suzuki turned his blistering drive into the crossbar moments later. Instead, it was Villa to got the decisive third goal. Mbaye was played in behind the City defence and from his cross, Jackson’s low effort should have been saved by Donnarumma. The visitors pressed in vain for another equaliser to allow Arsenal the chance to move level on points at the top of the table when they host Everton later on Saturday. A sixth win in seven games in all competitions for Villa lifts them up to sixth. The post Man City beaten by Aston Villa to end perfect Premier League start appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Aston Villa v Man City ratings: Manzambi 6; Jackson 8; Guehi 5, Ndiaye 8
body: Aston Villa ended Manchester City's 100 per cent winning start to the Premier League season when a Nicolas Jackson double earned them a 2-1 victory on Saturday. On the fourth anniversary of Unai Emery's appointment as manager , the Midlands club continued their impressive run against City as they secured a fourth successive win against them at Villa Park. Senegalese striker Jackson opened the scoring with just six minutes on the clock after Villa capitalised on a mistake by City defender Marc Guehi. The away side levelled just after half-time thanks to a towering header from Erling Haaland for his 13th goal in 11 matches across all competitions. But Villa would claim all three points when Jackson fired him from substitute Ibrahim Mbaye's ball into the middle on the hour mark. Victory temporarily lifts Villa up to sixth place with 11 points from eight matches, while City remain top although Arsenal could draw level with them on 21 points if the Gunners defeat Everton later on Saturday. 3 & 4 – Aston Villa are the first side to win three successive Premier League games against Manchester City since Liverpool in December 2016 and the first to win four successive home league matches since Spurs in February 2023. Heroes. pic.twitter.com/xFZzWPNaIP — OptaJoe (@OptaJoe) October 24, 2026 What they said: Aston Villa defender Matty Cash: “The manager gives us tasks but you have to take responsibility too, I do a lot of work on wingers, I think as a full back you have to try to get aggressive and it makes them difficult for them. I thought I did my task well. Getting close to him is the biggest challenge. I was watching clips of him this morning. “We had a lot of change at the start of the season, it was going to take time to gel and get comfortable with each other. Unai Emery is brilliant, having him stay is the main priority for us.” Manchester City captain Ruben Dias: “It is frustrating for us. I felt everyone fought a lot for us. The first 15 minutes we took time to get into the game. They changed the way they set up a bit and it took us time to adjust. We then had chances and momentum and they ended up scoring two goals in two transitions. They were very efficient. There is room to improve and we need to do better. “I felt like we were dangerous in many occasions, even if we didn’t have the finish. I think we need a word of appreciation to all our boys because we kept fighting until the end.” Aston Villa ratings: Zion Suzuki – 8/10: Japanese keeper saved well from Ndiaye, Cherki and Khusanov inside opening 25 minutes. Beaten by Ndiaye effort that hit post and no chance with Haaland goal. A couple of good stops after break and has taken to English football with ease. Matty Cash – 7/10: Up against the threat of Doku and, like many a full-back, found it tough going. Booked for clumsy foul on Belgian early in second half which left him on knife edge for rest of game but stuck to task. Victor Lindelof – 8/10: Former Manchester United defender had helped keep Haaland very quiet only for Norwegian to score with his first attempt. But Swede still produced a fine performance at Villa Park Pau Torres – 8/10: Spanish centre-half played very well alongside defensive partner Lindelof as Villa maintained the form that has seen them lose only once in 10 matches across all competitions. Ian Maatsen – 6/10: Dutch full-back volleyed game's first attempt high and wide. Twice failed to stop Ndiaye cutting inside and firing off shots in first half. Vital header to deny Haaland second goal. Boubacar Kamara – 7/10: Quietly effective in the centre of Villa's midfield, dovetailing well with McGinn and does his job with minimum fuss but it vitally important to Emery's side Joao Gomes – 7/10: Midfielder who was sent off on his Villa debut in the opening game of the season, still looks like a booking waiting to happen but put in decent shift here. It's Jackson again! ⚽️ @AstonVilla are back in front! 🔥 #AVLMCI pic.twitter.com/Lcba6eIkVq — beIN SPORTS (@beINSPORTS_EN) October 24, 2026 John McGinn – 7/10: Was captain's quick thinking after Guehi's mistake for City that set-up Jackson for striker's opening goal. His constant harrying of opponents delighted home fans. Johan Manzambi – 6/10: Curled free-kick from dangerous position well over bar. Worked hard defensively but too easily beaten by Ndiaye ahead of City's leveller, then booked for delaying the restart and hit in groin by ball in matter of minutes. Alysson – 7/10: Brazilian was full of running up and down pitch, making important challenges tracking back and made some dangerous runs forward helping Villa to fifth win in their past seven meetings against City. Nicolas Jackson – 8/10: Showed fine composure to skip past Anderson before thumping finish into roof of net for early Villa lead. Fired another low effort wide of target not long after. Second was first-time finish that keeper should have done better with. Substitutes: Ibrahim Mbaye (On for Alysson, 59') – 7/10: Set-up Jackson's second goal to earn quick-fire assist immediately after coming on. Ross Barkley (On for McGinn, 66') – 6/10: Brought to shore up midfield with City hunting for equaliser. Emi Buendia (On for Manzambi, 66') – 6/10: Argentine was full of energybut earned a late booking as Villa defender their lead. Brian Madjo (On for Jackson, 82') – N/A: Booked for shooting at goal after whistle had blown for foul. Leon Goretzka (On for Gomes, 82') – N/A . Man City ratings: Gianluigi Donnarumma – 5/10: Gave away early corner for taking too long with goal kick. Beaten at near post by rising Jackson finish minutes later. Made mess of shot from Senegalese striker that put Villa back in front in second half. Abdukodir Khusanov – 7/10: Started at right-back with Matheus Nunes again missing through injury, and looked solid. Shifted into centre for second half and the Uzbeki again looked comfortable. Ruben Dias – 6/10: Captain made vital sliding challenge on Alysson to stop Brazilian shooting on goal lat in first half. Had hands full dealing with in-form opponent in Jackson. Marc Guehi – 5/10: Coming on back of errors against Ipswich last weekend, was his awful touch that gifted Villa possession and led to early lead. Booked for pulling down Jackson on edge of box. Hooked at break. Josko Gvardiol – 7/10: Saw rising strike just after Haaland's leveller tipped over bar by Suzuki and had another effort blocked at close range by the Villa Keeper. Caught out of position giving Villa substitute Mbaye too much space to set-up Jackson's second goal. Elliot Anderson – 7/10: Usual relentless running in City engine room and didn't get grip of midfield like he has done at times this season. Booked for foul on Gomes. Enzo Fernandez – 6/10: Went down too theatrically looking for penalty after shove in back from Gomes and referee waved away claims. Far too quiet an afternoon from the £125 million midfielder . Iliman Ndiaye – 8/10: Showed lovely skill to drop shoulder, cut inside and fire off swerving shot that keeper saved well. Curled another effort off the post. Supplied cross for Haaland's goal. Game on at Villa Park! @Erling powers home a header to level the score for @ManCity !🤖 #AVLMCI pic.twitter.com/NgdQ1VzAlM — beIN SPORTS (@beINSPORTS_EN) October 24, 2026 Jeremy Doku – 7/10: Usual dangerous runs down flank, beating Cash at will, but couldn't provide the goal or assist City desperately needed from him. Rayan Cherki – 5/10: Had low shot saved in 20th minute, after being set-up by Doku, and was frustrated with himself not to score. Booked for blatantly holding back Manzambi. Taken off at half-time. Erling Haaland – 7/10: Back in the starting line-up but no attempts on goal in first half with only eight touches of the ball. Inevitably headed City in front after break for his ninth league goal of the season. Saw another goal-bound header cleared by Maatsen. Cut a frustrated figure at times. Substitutes: Phil Foden (On for Cherki, 46') – 5/10: Came on having scored four times in two games but had little impact at Villa Park. Ricoh Lewis (On for Guehi, 46') – 6/10: Brought on at right-back but guilty of one particularly wasteful cross when teammates were well placed in penalty area. Ryan McAidoo (On for Ndiaye, 69') – 5/10: Booked for holding back Maatsen minutes after coming on. One wasteful cross with City chasing game.

title: All Boxers built to one standard, says minister
body: All six hundred and twenty three Mechanised Infantry Vehicle Boxers are being delivered to a common build standard, which has made variant and build configuration effectively the same thing. Ben Obese-Jecty, the Conservative member for Huntingdon, asked for an updated breakdown of the 623 vehicles by variant, build configuration and role, referring back to an answer given in June 2021. Luke Pollard, Minister of State for Defence Readiness and Industry, said: “I refer the hon. Member to the answer I gave on 18 December 2025 to Question 100025, which set out the number of Mechanised Infantry Vehicle (MIV) Boxers contracted for by variant. This information remains extant. As the Boxer programme has developed, build configuration and variant have become effectively interchangeable, with all 623 MIV Boxer vehicles being delivered to a common build standard. Consequently, a separate breakdown by build configuration is no longer relevant. “The Department keeps under review its approach to the disclosure of information, taking account of a range of factors. An updated breakdown by role could pose a risk to operational security and, therefore, I am unable to provide this information.” A common build standard means the hulls and drive modules come off the line identically whatever mission module they eventually carry, which is the design logic of the vehicle: the mission module can be lifted off and another fitted. Ministers confirmed earlier this month that Boxers will be able to recover one another in the field and that the vehicle has been built with the electrical and physical margin to take a remote weapon station later. Boxer is being built in Britain by Rheinmetall BAE Systems Land at Telford and Stockton-on-Tees, with WFEL at Stockport, under contracts covering the 623 vehicles for the British Army. The post All Boxers built to one standard, says minister first appeared on UK Defence Journal .

title: FG’s 90-day cost of living plan is vote-buying – YPP presidential candidate
body: By John Alechenu Abuja-The presidential candidate of the Young Progressives Party, YPP, Architect Peter Agada, has described the Federal Government’s 90-day action plan to ease cost of living as vote-buying that will not work. Read Also: Alake’s attack on Atiku won’t cut food prices, ADC campaign fires back The plan was recently approved by the National Economic Council, NEC, and announced by the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Mr Wale Edun. Agada told Vanguard in Abuja on Saturday that the plan, like previous interventions by the APC-led administration, does not reflect economic reality and is destined to fail. He said his #LabourDirect ward-to-ward development strategy remains the alternative, with capacity to empower Nigerians with N40 million monthly per ward. “LabourDirect can capture all Nigerians within 60 days of implementation. We said 60 days; about 20 days are gone before the elections,” he said. “If they approach me to implement it, Nigerians will have more confidence that they have called one of the candidates to help.” Agada said government should call people who can fix the micro-economy before January 16, not just roll out macro-economic promises. The YPP candidate proposed a dashboard powered by the Labour Direct Information Network, LIN System, to monitor projects, employment, production, tax and revenues from a single application. He recalled that similar measures announced two weeks ago, including subsidy interventions, have shown no results. Agada said, “I align with those who said the economic team has failed. I have listened to many analysts on TV and radio, none spoke positively about the team. They have lost their bearings.” He cited past unfulfilled pledges from 2023, including N75 billion for manufacturing, N75 billion for micro SMEs, N50 billion conditional grants, grain distribution, N200 billion to cultivate 500 hectares, N50 billion each for rice farmers and N100 billion for CNG. According to him, after those announcements, government removed tariffs on food imports, which did not crash food prices. He said, “If you are fighting food inflation, return food prices to where they were before you took office. “There are 85 days to the election and you are announcing a 90-day timeline. After election what happens? These guys are playing mind games.” He urged Nigerians to demand month-by-month job creation data, saying without that, the 90-day plan is just campaign strategy ahead of 2027. It looks like the long-rumored touchscreen MacBook might actually get announced next week , and after using the Lenovo Yoga 9n for our testing of Nvidia’s RTX Spark platform, it got me thinking: this is a lot of what I want from a touchscreen MacBook.
Like the Apple silicon in modern MacBook Pros, RTX Spark is an Arm-based processor with a beefy integrated GPU and lots of unified memory. And the Yoga is the most fun RTX Spark laptop so far because it’s a 16-inch 2-in-1 convertible with a stylus . Its Nvidia-powered compatriots also have touchscreens, like most Windows laptops, but they’re conventional clamshell designs.
The Lenovo Yoga does all your typical 2-in-1 stuff: it can be used as a clamshell laptop, and it can fold its hinge all the way back for tent mode and tablet modes. As a tablet, you can use it in either landscape or portrait orientation, and getting the keyboard out of the way is great for watching movies, playing games with a controller, or integrating your laptop into a multi-monitor desk setup with keyboard and mouse.
The Yoga 9n’s included stylus works for note-taking and drawing on its excellent OLED display, but you can also use it on the haptic trackpad for a Wacom-like experience, without blocking the screen with your hand. And the stylus is magnetic, allowing it to attach to the Yoga’s lid — either on its own, or while housed in its case. I particularly enjoy using the Yoga’s stylus for photo retouching in Lightroom Classic or Photoshop. I haven’t used a stylus for that kind of work in ages, since I gave up my old Wacom, but having one that works on either the screen or the trackpad is incredibly convenient
I expect a touchscreen MacBook Pro would have Apple Pencil support. And like on the Lenovo, it would go a long way to get me back to using a stylus for retouching. But I hope that also like the Lenovo, it works on the trackpad too — the more options, the better. And if a touch-enabled MacBook supports the Apple Pencil (which it should ), I’m also hoping it attaches to the laptop, both for convenience and for wireless charging, as on the iPad Pro. Lenovo’s stylus relies on USB-C charging, which is fine, but not as convenient as always having it charged and ready to go while attached to your laptop.
I don’t expect Apple to make a standard convertible laptop after all this time. Simply joining Windows manufacturers in making a 2-in-1 or swapping the MacBook Pro’s Mini LED for a touchscreen OLED and calling it a day doesn’t seem very Apple. I’m hoping for something special, like Apple’s own take on the Microsoft Surface Laptop Studio — a clever idea that brought the touchscreen forward instead of flipping it backwards — or something totally fresh. And there are hints in macOS 27 that Apple is updating to Golden Gate to make touch functions feel more natural than just poking and prodding at things designed for a mouse cursor. As fun as I find 2-in-1 Windows laptops and Chromebooks, using those desktop operating systems with a finger or a stylus can get clunky.
My hopes are high for Apple to wow us, because this MacBook Pro with touch is sure to be expensive. And Apple’s recent design decisions aren’t faultless. The HomeView’s lack of apps is perplexing. The iPhone Duo is a little messy. Current MacBooks are so great, it’s easy to forget the butterfly keyboard fiasco wasn’t all that long ago. After all this time of holding out on adding a touchscreen to the MacBook, Apple has to make it worth it.

title: Infantino says ‘vast, vast majority’ of soccer supports him ahead of FIFA elections
body:
FIFA’s embattled president Gianni Infantino said he has the backing of the “vast, vast majority” of soccer, despite his failed plan to sell stakes in the World Cup .
Infantino is seeking re-election next year as the head of soccer’s world governing body in the face of attempts to force him to stand down in the wake of the divisive plan.
He infuriated soccer leaders in Europe, North America and Asia over the proposal to sell profits in the World Cup through a commercial subsidiary.
But in an interview released Saturday with the BBC at the Under-15 World Cup in Azerbaijan, Infantino brushed off doubts about him being able to continue as president.
“Well you know I was elected by 211 member associations from all over the world,” Infantino said. “I think what is important is that in an organization like FIFA, there can be different views, different points of view.
“But if we are serious about democracy, about the democratic process, about believing that everyone has the same vote and the same voice all over the world, that football belongs to everyone, if we are serious about that, then we need, to respect as well the views of the vast, vast majority.”
Infantino is standing for a final term in office in March. The deadline for potential candidates to come forward to stand against him is Nov. 18.
His latest comments came after he apologized to FIFA’s ruling council last week for “mistakes” in his secretive investment plan for the World Cup.
Despite his apology, European delegates said they left the meeting disappointed about what they saw as a lack of clarity.
On Friday, the Asian Football Confederation endorsed Infantino for another term as FIFA president in an apparent turnaround in its stance from two months ago when it criticized him for a breach of trust.

title: Iran envoy details agenda of Pezeshkian's visit to Russia
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 24 (MNA) – Iran's ambassador to Russia, Kazem Jalali, has detailed the programs of the President Masoud Pezeshkian's upcoming visit to Russia.
Iranian Ambassador to Russia Kazem Jalali announced to RIA Novosti that Iranian President Masoud Pezzekian will attend the Gas Exporting Countries Forum (GECF) summit in Moscow on Tuesday, October 27.
The Iranian Ambassador to Russia said in that regard: The President of the Islamic Republic of Iran will travel to Moscow to attend the Gas Exporting Countries Forum summit to be held on Tuesday, October 27. We are currently coordinating the details of this trip.
Jalali added: The main topics to be discussed will be economic and trade cooperation between Iran and Russia, such as the North-South Corridor, energy security, food security and the development of trade relations; at the same time, the two presidents will also exchange views on geopolitical, international and political issues.
Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov also announced during his visit to Tehran on October 19 that Vladimir Putin wants to meet with Pezzekian at the Gas Exporting Countries Forum summit in Moscow in late October.

title: Civic activist and UAnimals founder Todorchuk appointed to head AFU Main Directorate for Communications
body:
Oleksandr Todorchuk, Ukrainian entrepreneur, civic activist, founder of the animal welfare organization UAnimals, co-founder of the communications agency Gres Todorchuk, and current service member, has announced his appointment as head of the Main Directorate for Communications of the Armed Forces of Ukraine.
"I have joined the General Staff team, taking charge of the Main Directorate for Communications of the Armed Forces of Ukraine. It is a great responsibility and a significant challenge... I will put forth my best efforts to strengthen this area, as I genuinely believe in the importance of communications during wartime," Todorchuk wrote on Facebook on Saturday, thanking the Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of Ukraine, Mykhailo Drapaty, for the trust placed in him.
He noted that he is currently getting to know the team and familiarizing himself with the scope of work, while also seeking individuals to join the directorate’s team. "It will be challenging, fast-paced, and certainly interesting. Let us combine our knowledge and experience where they are truly needed today and can be of service to the country," Todorchuk wrote.
Born in 1988, Todorchuk is a law graduate of Kyiv International University. In 2010, he co-founded the communications agency Gres Todorchuk, which specializes in communications, cultural, social, and educational projects, together with Yaroslava Gres. In 2016, he established UAnimals, an organization that began its work by campaigning against the exploitation of animals in the entertainment industry. He was mobilized into the Armed Forces of Ukraine in March 2022.
Earlier, the Main Directorate of Communications of the Armed Forces of Ukraine was headed by Colonel Bohdan Mykolaiovych Senyk, who had led the Armed Forces’ Public Relations Directorate since 2016.

title: Zelenskyy on humanitarian operation in Oleshky: Ukraine will fulfill its part; we hope that American mediation will prove effective
body:
President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyy hopes that it will be possible to carry out a humanitarian operation and unblock Oleshky.
“There is also an arrangement regarding Oleshky that should be implemented soon – to unblock access to the city. In the occupied part, the temporarily occupied part, of our Kherson region, the Russians have mined the roads, making the situation dire, extremely dire. We hope this humanitarian operation can be carried out – access to Oleshky can be unblocked, food and medicine can be brought in, and people can leave this combat zone,” Zelenskyy said in his video address Saturday.
“We have been negotiating this for some time and at various levels. Ukraine will do its part. We count on American mediation to work,” Zelenskyy stressed.
As previously reported, the White House announced on Friday that U.S. First Lady Melania Trump had secured truce between Russia and Ukraine, covering the town of Oleshky, to facilitate the delivery of humanitarian aid and prepare for the evacuation of civilians via a designated safe corridor. The local truce is set to take effect on October 29.
According to statements from the Russian side, the Russian Armed Forces, in connection with a humanitarian operation, are implementing a "ceasefire" in the area of ​​Oleshky, on Kherson front, starting at 3:00 a.m. Kyiv time on October 27, and will "ensure the safe movement of a humanitarian convoy to Oleshky for the delivery of essential goods."
The General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine also announced that Ukraine is implementing a ceasefire in a specific area of ​​the temporarily occupied town of Oleshky, in Kherson region, starting at 3:00 a.m. Kyiv time on Tuesday, October 27, to facilitate a humanitarian operation.
The General Staff noted that Ukrainian units have previously carried out multiple missions to deliver humanitarian supplies via drones to the residents of Oleshky and surrounding villages.
"We trust that humanitarian access for the sake of the people in Oleshky will be guaranteed," the statement reads.

title: Ukraine begins process of joining OECD Nuclear Energy Agency – Shmyhal
body:
According to Ukrinform, First Deputy Prime Minister and Energy Minister Denys Shmyhal reported this on Telegram .
He said that "the next step will be an agency assessment mission to analyze Ukraine's nuclear sector, our technical capabilities, as well as our institutional and legal framework. Based on the mission's findings and subsequent decisions by member states, Ukraine may become the next NEA member."
"I had the honor of addressing the meeting's participants and presenting Ukraine's vision for further cooperation with the agency. I am grateful to OECD Secretary-General Mathias Cormann and NEA Director-General William Magwood for their support for Ukraine and assistance in advancing our path toward membership," Shmyhal said.
He stressed that "joining the NEA is an important step toward full OECD membership, European integration and the implementation of the highest nuclear safety standards. Future membership will enable Ukraine to participate more actively in the work of expert committees and working groups, deepen scientific and technical cooperation, and develop research and professional training."
"At the same time, Ukraine is ready to make its own contribution to the agency's work. We have a strong nuclear energy sector, developed infrastructure, experienced engineers and scientists, and extensive expertise in the operation and modernization of nuclear power plants, nuclear safety, radioactive waste management and the development of advanced technologies. We also have unique experience in operating a nuclear energy system during a full-scale war. This experience could benefit the international community in matters of emergency preparedness and risk management. Ukraine is ready to undergo the necessary assessment process, fulfill its obligations, and become an active and responsible member of the NEA community," Shmyhal said.
As Ukrinform reported, Ukraine is applying for membership in the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development's Nuclear Energy Agency (NEA).
The Nuclear Energy Agency is an intergovernmental agency established within the framework of the OECD.
The NEA's mission is to assist its member countries in maintaining and further developing, through international cooperation, the scientific, technological and legal bases required for the safe, environmentally sound and economical use of nuclear energy for peaceful purposes.

title: 2027: Atiku is North’s enemy, says Akume
body: ….Says, power rotation agreed in Kaduna to keep Nigeria one By Omeiza Ajayi, Kaduna As the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) flagged off its presidential campaign on Saturday in Kaduna, Secretary to the Government of the Federation SGF, Senator George Akume, declared that any northerner seeking to contest the 2027 presidential election is an enemy of the region. Former vice president Atiku Abubakar of the African Democratic Congress ADC is the only prominent northern politician seeking to wrestle power from incumbent President Bola Tinubu in the next year’s presidential contest. This was as he reminded Northerners that the agreement on power rotation between the North and the South was reached in Kaduna State to keep the country together. His spokesman, Yomi Odunuga, in a statement on Saturday, said the SGF spoke at a pre-campaign meeting with a large crowd of Benue State indigenes residing in Kaduna. “Remember that it was in this same Kaduna State that we agreed on power rotation between the North and the South. You cannot doubt the credentials of those that reached this agreement at that time, and it was done to keep this country together. We agreed on power shift, and that is what has kept this country going. That is what has retained our territorial integrity,” Akume said. On that basis, he declared that any Northerner seeking to contest the 2027 presidential election is an enemy of the North, insisting that President Bola Ahmed Tinubu remains the right candidate to lead Nigeria beyond 2027. “Anybody who is from the North and running for the presidency is an enemy of the North. Don’t allow that pretender to deceive you. It is not yet our turn. The North’s turn is in 2031. Prepare to vote for Tinubu. Do not allow anyone to destroy the country because of a vaunting personal ambition,” he said. The SGF urged the North to back Tinubu’s re-election bid and wait until 2031 before seeking to return to the presidency. He warned that individual political ambitions should not be allowed to undermine the region’s collective interests. Akume, a former Governor of Benue State, urged Northerners to remain united and resist political manoeuvres capable of weakening the region’s influence. He cautioned against attempts to divide them along political, religious and personal lines, and recalled past political disagreements among Nigerian leaders, warning against repeating mistakes that could weaken the North in national politics. He said the North stands to benefit more from supporting Tinubu’s second-term ambition than from allowing individual political interests to create divisions ahead of the next general elections. Defending the president’s record, the SGF said Tinubu has been fair to all in appointments and does not favour one religion over another. “Let us remember that the President has been fair to all in terms of appointments and others. He doesn’t favour one religion over the other. Just look at the figures. So be careful about what people tell you,” he said. Akume also told his audience that the president has shown his love for Benue State through significant projects. “Let nobody deceive you; Asiwaju loves Benue, and he has displayed that in the number of significant projects the Federal Government is carrying out simultaneously in the state. These projects are diverse in healthcare, roads, education and others. This is being replicated throughout the federation. For example, in the area of education, over 65 per cent of NELFUND has been accessed, and most of them are from the North,” he said. Apparently taking a swipe at Atiku, he said, “Forget that other one making noise that he was going to remove fuel subsidy. He is always flip-flopping. He says something today and changes gear the next minute.” The SGF praised Governor Uba Sani and called for his return to office. “Kaduna State is a historic city that gave us meaning and purpose. So, this is your home too, as Benue State citizens living here. The present governor, Senator Uba Sani, believes in that vision of Saudauna. He is a great man. I want to appeal to you that there is none like Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu in 2027. “I was the governor of Benue State, and the Fulanis were there. It is about leadership. If Asiwaju was not a good leader, I would not tell you otherwise. I will still come to Kaduna to speak with you. Your governor is a good man, and he has done well for this state. Let us return him to power too,” he said. The SGF also stressed the need for national unity, peaceful coexistence and cooperation among Nigeria’s diverse ethnic and religious groups and encouraged the preservation of cultural identity and traditions as a means of promoting understanding among communities. “I believe you are here because you believe in me and because you want to see your son, and that is me in flesh and blood,” he told the gathering. Those who accompanied Akume included a former governor of Jigawa State, Alhaji Saminu Turaki; Dame Pauline Tallen; Senator Abu Ibrahim; the Minister of Water Resources, Prof. Joseph Utsev; and the Minister of Steel Development, Prince Shuaibu Abubakar Audu. The post 2027: Atiku is North’s enemy, says Akume appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Military Kills 15 Terrorists In Borno Air Strike
body: The Joint Task Force (North East), Operation HADIN KAI (OPHK), has recorded another operational success with the neutralisation of 15 terrorists in a precision air strike north-west of Pulka in Gwoza LGA of Borno State. A statement by the Acting Military Information Officer, Headquarters Joint Task Force (North East) Operation HADIN KAI, Captain Mohammed Goni, on Saturday, noted that the operation was conducted at about 11:50 p.m. on 23 October 2026, following credible intelligence and confirmed sightings of terrorist movements in the general area of Pulka. According to the statement, the precision strike was subsequently followed by ground operations to exploit the area and consolidate the operational gains. “The successful engagement highlights the effectiveness of intelligence-driven targeting and coordinated military action in disrupting terrorist movements and degrading their operational capabilities. It also reflects the unwavering commitment of Operation HADIN KAI to denying terrorist groups freedom of action and preventing them from threatening communities within the theatre. “The operation forms part of the sustained offensive posture of troops, supported by effective intelligence gathering and coordinated employment of available military capabilities. Through these efforts, the Theatre Command continues to maintain pressure on terrorist elements, disrupt their activities and strengthen the security environment across the North East. “Operation HADIN KAI remains resolute in its mission to defeat terrorism and insurgency, protect law-abiding citizens and create the conditions necessary for the restoration of normalcy and socio-economic activities in affected communities. The Theatre Command reassures the public that troops will sustain the momentum of ongoing operations with vigilance, determination and professionalism”, the statement read in part. The Theatre Command also called on members of the public to sustain their cooperation with security agencies by providing timely and credible information on suspicious movements and activities, noting that the continued partnership between the military and the civilian population remains essential to consolidating operational gains and achieving lasting peace and security across the North East.
