title: India wants relations with Russia to be further strengthened — Lok Sabha speaker
body:
NEW DELHI, October 24. /TASS/. India favors continued efforts to strengthen relations with Russia that have a long history and are very strong, Om Birla, Speaker of the Lok Sabha, also known as the House of the People (the lower house of India’s parliament), told TASS ahead of a visit by a Duma delegation to New Delhi for the 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum.
"India-Russia relations are old and ancient and very strong. These relations go back to old times. We want these relations further be strengthened," Birla said.
"Indian Prime Minister [Narendra Modi] and [Russian] President [Vladimir] Putin are also very close, the Russian-Indian summit is held annually. Today our people are very connected, very close," the Lok Sabha speaker added.
New Delhi will host the 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum on October 26-27. The theme of the event will be "Strengthening Parliaments for People-Centric Development." Participants are expected to issue a joint statement following the forum.

title: Ebola: Lagos is prepared to respond — Commissioner
body:
The Lagos State government says it has stepped up preparedness measures and is prepared to respond following Nigeria’s confirmation of an imported case of Ebola disease in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT).
The state’s Commissioner for Health, Akin Abayomi, said Lagos remains on “high alert and preparedness” and is treating the situation as a priority.
“Lagos is a gateway city with constant movement to and from Abuja, and we are treating this as a priority,” Mr Abayomi said in a statement posted on X on Friday.
He said the state’s Emergency Operations Centre (EOC) had been working ahead of the confirmation, with measures being put in place across surveillance, isolation, laboratory testing, infection prevention and control.
Mr Abayomi said response teams are conducting simulation exercises to ensure that responders understand their roles before they are needed.
He said the state’s isolation centre has also been upgraded, while additional capacity is being developed.
He noted that training on infection prevention and control is continuing for health workers across public and private health facilities.
The commissioner said Lagos is also establishing a clear laboratory testing pathway, aiming to obtain results within 24 hours.
He noted that screening at airports and other points of entry is being strengthened in collaboration with federal authorities, while disease surveillance is being digitally enhanced on the state’s digital health surveillance platform to support real-time detection, tracing and response.
A “dedicated Ebola Research Committee” is also reviewing the latest evidence on treatment and vaccines to guide the state’s decisions.
The commissioner urged residents to wash their hands regularly with soap and water and avoid contact with the blood or body fluids of anyone who is ill.
He advised anyone who develops fever, weakness, vomiting, diarrhoea or unexplained bleeding, or believes they may have been exposed, not to self-medicate.
“If you develop fever, weakness, vomiting, diarrhoea or unexplained bleeding, or think you have been exposed, do not self-medicate. Call before visiting a health facility,” he said.
Mr Abayomi also urged health workers to maintain a high index of suspicion, ask about patients’ travel history and use appropriate personal protective equipment.
Residents can report suspected cases or possible exposure through “the Lagos emergency numbers, 112 or 767, or the Directorate of Epidemiology, Biosecurity and Global Health on 0802 316 9485.”
The commissioner urged residents to remain calm, stay alert and rely on official information from the Lagos State Ministry of Health.
The government’s preparedness comes against the backdrop of Lagos’ experience during Nigeria’s 2014 Ebola outbreak.
Patrick Sawyer, a Liberian diplomat infected with Ebola, arrived in Lagos on 20 July 2014. He was admitted to a private hospital in the city, where the disease was subsequently confirmed.
Nigeria recorded 20 Ebola cases during the outbreak, including eight deaths, before the country was declared free of Ebola transmission on 20 October 2014 after 42 days without a new case.
The federal government continues to urge states to strengthen their response systems.
The Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Muhammad Pate, said 21 states have updated their Ebola response plans, while the remaining 15 states are being urged to expedite their preparedness and response mechanisms.
The government has also called on healthcare facilities nationwide to strengthen infection prevention and control, promptly identify and isolate suspected cases and report them to public health authorities.
Nigeria currently has one confirmed imported Ebola case, while 44 contacts of the patient are being monitored.

title: Merz warns that Germany faces pressure from extremist parties, 'massive threat' from Russia
body: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz warned on Saturday that Germany was facing pressure from extremist parties and from foreign enemies, including a "massive threat" from Russia, which he said was seeking to destabilize Germany.Speaking at a party conference of the Christian Social Union (CSU), the Bavarian sister party of his conservative Christian Democrats (CDU), he said the parties had the responsibility to push through economic reforms to reinforce Germany's social stability.This is a developing story.

title: Sikorski: Musk Should Fly to Mars, Avoid Mixing Business and Politics
body:
Polish Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski has said he hopes Elon Musk “flies to Mars”, warning the US-based tech entrepreneur against mixing business with politics.
Sikorski, who has a history of public online spats with Musk , made the comments on Friday during a conference in the city of Łódź in central Poland, where he was asked about Europe’s dependence on US technology, including the satellite system owned by Musk.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
Sikorski said: “Mixing business with politics usually ends badly, especially when we talk about Elon Musk… I wish Musk well, he’s a great inventor and I hope he will fly to Mars one day.”
Starlink is an invaluable tool in Ukraine’s defense against Russian attacks, but has been subject to controversy amid accusations of intentional drops in service coverage over the course of Russia’s war in Ukraine.
Sikorski accused Musk of trying to “interfere in the politics of different countries”, after Ukrainian officials earlier this month said services from Starshield – the military version of Starlink – were drastically limited, with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warning that “people will die” as a result.
The reduction in Starlink connectivity came amid a deterioration in Kyiv-Washington relations following the White House’s announcement earlier this month that Russia would be allowed to sell diesel to global markets.
Poland pays around $50 million annually for Starlink services used in Ukraine as part of Warsaw’s support for Kyiv in defending against Moscow’s aggression.
Sikorski said that companies in Europe are already developing alternatives to Starlink.
On Thursday, Finland-based tech firms ICEYE and Nokia announced that they have joined forces to help Ukraine develop its own satellite communications system in partnership with Ukraine’s defense ministry.
Amid a renewed diplomatic drive by Washington to broker an end to Russia’s war in Ukraine after months of stalled negotiations, Sikorski highlighted what he said was Europe’s important role in finding a resolution to the conflict.
“Europe holds the cards”, Sikorski said, adding that Europe finances the Ukrainian state, continues to hold Russian assets that were frozen over its 2022 invasion of Ukraine and delivers weapons to Kyiv to aid in its defense.
“[Russia] has realized that this cannot be resolved solely by an agreement with the US, and that Europe is in the game,” Sikorski added.

title: GTA CEO responds to Abeiku Santana’s concerns over access to her office
body: The Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Tourism Authority (GTA), Maame Efua Houadjeto, has responded to concerns raised by her one of deputies, Gilbert Abeiku Aggrey Santana, over difficulties accessing her for urgent official consultations. In a letter written to the Board Chairperson of the Authority, Mrs Houadjeto said she operates an open-door policy, particularly for executive and senior management officers, and questioned the suggestion that her availability had been a challenge. “In as much as I am surprised and disappointed that the letter does not reflect the true state of my availability to you as my deputy Chief Executive Officer, I propose that we strengthen our internal consultation and communication arrangements through the following measures,” she stated. Her response follows a letter dated 22nd October 2026 in which Mr Aggrey, the Deputy Chief Executive Officer responsible for Marketing and Special Duties, appealed to the Minister of Tourism, Culture and Creative Arts, Abla Dzifa Gomashie, to intervene in what he described as recurring difficulties in accessing the CEO for consultations on urgent operational matters. In his letter, Mr Aggrey said he had, on several occasions, requested meetings through the CEO’s secretary or personal assistant, only to be informed that she was unavailable. He said the situation had made it difficult for him to obtain timely guidance, approvals and decisions needed to carry out his responsibilities, particularly in domestic tourism, special events and marketing. “This situation sometimes causes delays in operations, stakeholder engagements, and the implementation of key assignments,” Mr Aggrey wrote. He stressed that his concerns were not intended as a personal complaint but were aimed at addressing what he considered a communication gap within the institution. “My intention is not to make a personal complaint, but to highlight a communication gap that needs to be addressed in the interest of effective management and institutional efficiency,” he said. Maame Efua proposes measures to improve communication In her response, Mrs Houadjeto acknowledged the need for timely consultations and decisions, particularly on matters with operational, financial, strategic or stakeholder implications. She proposed five measures to improve coordination between the two offices and the Authority’s executive management team. These include scheduled executive consultations to review departmental priorities and operational challenges, as well as a clear procedure for flagging urgent matters and escalating issues when scheduled meetings are not possible. She also proposed that requests for meetings be properly communicated, acknowledged and scheduled by the relevant officers, taking into account the urgency and importance of each matter. Other measures include clarifying delegated responsibilities and approval processes, and encouraging regular engagement among members of the executive management team to minimise delays and ensure the consistent implementation of decisions. Mrs Houadjeto said the measures were intended to improve the Authority’s overall management processes rather than address individual concerns alone. “I wish to emphasize that the objective of these measures is not merely to address individual concerns, but to strengthen the overall effectiveness of our management processes and promote a more responsive, coordinated, and results-oriented institution,” she said. CEO calls for collaborative working relationship The GTA chief executive said management remained committed to professionalism, institutional discipline and harmonious working relationships within the executive management team. She also expressed confidence that the two offices could continue to work together despite differences in schedules, operational demands or administrative processes. “I value the contribution of the Deputy Chief Executive Officer to the Authority and expect that we will continue to work collaboratively, with mutual respect and a shared commitment to achieving our mandate,” she stated. “Differences in schedules, operational demands, or administrative processes should not become impediments to the effective performance of our collective responsibilities.” Mrs Houadjeto proposed a meeting at the earliest mutually convenient opportunity to agree on practical arrangements for implementing the measures outlined in her response.

title: Africa launches West Africa research programme to speed up outbreak response
body: A new regional initiative is seeking to strengthen West Africa’s preparedness for public health emergencies by connecting research institutions and enabling faster, more coordinated responses to disease outbreaks. The Africa Research Preparedness Programme for West Africa is designed to address gaps in research coordination that experts say could delay critical interventions during outbreaks of diseases such as Ebola, Mpox, Lassa fever and COVID-19. Despite the presence of skilled scientists and established research institutions across the continent, preparedness remains uneven, with some clinical trial sites facing challenges transitioning from routine research to emergency response. Head of Africa Strategy and Engagement at the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (CEPI), Shingai Machingaidze, said the programme would adopt a hub-and-spoke model to connect existing research capabilities and support coordinated action during outbreaks. She said the approach would allow countries to work together on research protocols and evidence generation, with the goal of activating clinical research responses within 10 to 15 days of an outbreak. “We have the capacity. What we’re trying to make sure we do better is how we all work together to respond to the same outbreak,” she said. “We are putting together what we call a hub and spoke model to build a coordinated capability to respond. We need speed to respond to outbreak and we cannot do that if we have not prepared enough.” The programme is expected to provide a common platform for institutions across West Africa to align priorities, share expertise and strengthen emergency research systems. Regional institutions join effort The initiative brings together several organisations involved in public health research, regulation and outbreak preparedness. They include the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC), the African Medicines Agency, the World Health Organization’s Regional Office for Africa, the Noguchi Memorial Institute for Medical Research, the Medical Research Council Unit The Gambia, the International Vaccine Institute (IVI) and CEPI. The collaboration is intended to improve the ability of research institutions to mobilise their expertise and resources when outbreaks occur, rather than work in isolation. Associate Director-General of the International Vaccine Institute in South Korea, Birkneh Tadesse, said operational research and clinical trials were also important to efforts to develop vaccines and support responses to outbreaks, including Ebola. “IVI is trying to work on operational research and clinical trials on drugs on vaccines. There is the east and central Africa preparedness programs in the response to the Ebola outbreak also,” he said. Turning research capacity into rapid action The programme comes amid continued concerns about Africa’s ability to respond quickly to emerging and recurring infectious diseases. Experts have warned that the presence of research facilities and scientific expertise does not automatically translate into an effective emergency response without coordination, advance planning and systems that can be activated quickly. The initiative seeks to address that challenge by strengthening links between institutions before outbreaks occur, allowing researchers to coordinate protocols and prepare for clinical studies when emergencies arise. Its effectiveness will depend on sustained investment, clear coordination arrangements and the ability to translate research findings into timely public health interventions. The target of activating clinical research responses within 10 to 15 days will be a key measure of whether the programme can help close the gap between existing research capacity and the urgent demands of an outbreak.

title: Zelensky Says Starlink Speeds Fully Restored, Urges Interceptor Deliveries
body:
President Volodymyr Zelensky announced on Saturday, Oct. 24, that SpaceX’s Starlink and Starshield satellite networks have had their operational speeds restored to pre-restriction levels, easing constraints that had affected counter-drone operations and front-line military logistics.
In a video address published on Telegram, the president confirmed that system diagnostics conducted by military specialists verified that bandwidth and velocity capabilities have returned to required operational thresholds.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
“The most important development for today: Starlink and Starshield operations have been restored to the speeds that existed prior to all these restrictions,” Zelensky stated.
“The restoration began overnight, and by this morning the speeds were already sufficient for operational use. This is very important and significant for our front-line logistics and for defending Ukraine against jet-powered Shaheds.”
Zelensky confirmed that Defense Minister Yevhenii Khmara delivered an official briefing on Saturday morning verifying that technical testing demonstrated full network functionality.
The president expressed gratitude to American partners, lawmakers, media, the US State Department, and US President Donald Trump for addressing the operational issue.
Addressing broader security cooperation with Western allies, Zelensky emphasized that Kyiv is maintaining active consultations with Washington and European partners to restore regular deliveries of surface-to-air interceptors capable of neutralizing Russian ballistic missiles.
The president noted that several critical air defense aid packages, backed by existing political approvals from partner nations, remain pending delivery to Ukrainian armed forces.
“We continue communicating with partners so that other levels of our cooperation with America are restored,” Zelensky said.
“It is very important that deliveries of air defense interceptors – interceptors against Russian ballistics – are renewed. There are packages that we are still awaiting. These include packages from America and from European partners – packages for which political decisions have already been adopted.”
The appeal follows Zelensky’s recent disclosures that Ukraine received only 24 Patriot interceptors from the US over the past three months , despite facing coordinated ballistic barrages and maintaining an estimated operational requirement of roughly 350 interceptors per month.
Zelensky disclosed that Ukrainian delegations are preparing a series of diplomatic consultations in Europe with representatives of the US president and European allies, emphasizing that European capitals must remain directly involved in all stages of prospective peace negotiations.
“Europe must be involved in the diplomatic process,” Zelensky stressed. “Ukraine always involves European partners in diplomatic efforts and counts on their continuation next week.”
The president also revealed that an agreement has been reached to secure humanitarian access to the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky in southern Kherson region , where an estimated 1,700 civilians have faced acute isolation, hunger, and severed medical supplies.
Zelensky explained that Russian forces have heavily mined access roads leading to the left-bank enclave, creating critical survival hazards for remaining residents ahead of the winter season.
“There is also an agreement regarding Oleshky. Its implementation should take place soon so that access to Oleshky is unblocked,” Zelensky said.
“In the temporarily occupied part of our Kherson region, the Russians have mined roads, making the situation difficult – extremely difficult. We hope this humanitarian operation will succeed: unblocking Oleshky , providing access to deliver food and medicine, and allowing people to leave this combat zone.”
Zelensky confirmed that the humanitarian framework had been under discussion across multiple institutional levels, emphasizing that Ukraine will fulfill all operational commitments and counts on the effectiveness of American diplomatic mediation to secure the corridor.

title: Thousands March In France Against Far-Right Party Congress
body: Thousands of people yelling anti-fascist slogans marched in the French city of Orléans Saturday against a congress by far-right leader Marine Le Pen’s National Rally (RN) party there, AFP journalists saw. The protest — held on a day of fresh nationwide demonstrations over the cost of living after ones a week ago that devolved into street violence — criticised both Le Pen and centrist President Emmanuel Macron. France’s President Emmanuel Macron meets with elected officials at the town hall following a shooting in Trappes, near Paris, on October 23, 2026. “Macron resign. Le Pen in prison,” the crowd yelled, while carrying placards that read “The Youth say ‘screw you’ to the National Rally” and “Hotter than fascists”. The two-day RN congress in Orleans was the first big party campaign rally by Le Pen, whom surveys put as the leading candidate to succeed Macron in presidential elections in six months. title: Police arrest man who murdered ex-girlfriend, hid body in sack
body:
The police in Anambra State have arrested a man, Chima Ofoeke, who allegedly murdered his former girlfriend, Mmesoma Umeorini, in Uga, a community in Aguata Local Government Area of the state.
The police spokesperson in Anambra State, Tochukwu Ikenga, disclosed this in a statement on Saturday.
Mr Ikenga, a superintendent of police, said the arrest followed a report by the victim’s mother to the Divisional Police Officer in Umuchu Division that her daughter had been missing since 16 October.
“Acting on intelligence-led information, police operatives, in collaboration with members of the Agunechemba security outfit in Uga, arrested the suspect, who was identified as the deceased’s alleged former boyfriend,” he said.
The spokesperson said the suspect, from Ebonyi State, confessed during preliminary investigation that he murdered the victim because she broke up with him.
He said the suspect subsequently led police detectives to the location where the remains of the deceased were recovered.
Mr Ikenga said the Commissioner of Police in Anambra, Nnanna Ama, has ordered that the case be transferred to the State Criminal Investigation Department Awka, for “a comprehensive and diligent investigation.”
Mr Ama, according to the statement, reiterated the commitment of the police in the state to protect lives and property and urged members of the public to promptly report cases of missing persons and other suspicious activities to the appropriate authorities.
“Further developments will be communicated as the investigation progresses,” he assured.
A video clip obtained by PREMIUM TIMES showed when security operatives arrested the suspect and interrogated him.
In the clip, the suspect was holding a dirty sack which he confessed contained the body of his former girlfriend.
He also confessed that he murdered the victim on a Friday because she ended their romantic relationship
Asked how he murdered the victim, he responded in Igbo language: “I held her neck with her clothes and strangled her until she collapsed.”
Some voices in the background of the clip suggested that the victim’s body must have been cut into pieces to enter the sack.
Murder is outlawed in Section 315 (6) of the Nigeria Criminal Code Act.
Offenders, on conviction, face death sentence, section 319 (1) said.
Several persons have been sentenced to death for murder across the country.
An Aiyetoro High Court in Ogun State, for instance, sentenced a man, Adelake Bara, to death by hanging in June 2022, for shooting and killing one Olaleye Oke.
A high court in Lokoja, Kogi State, in January 2022, also sentenced a man, Muritala Dare to death by hanging for stabbing his colleague to death with a broken bottle.

title: Bawumia proposes reforms to make Ghana West Africa’s leading pharmaceutical manufacturing hub
body: New Patriotic Party (NPP) flagbearer Dr Mahamudu Bawumia has called for increased domestic pharmaceutical production and reforms to position Ghana as West Africa’s leading medicine manufacturing hub. The former Vice President made the proposal during a meeting with the leadership of the Pharmaceutical Society of Ghana (PSGH) at the PSG House in Accra on Thursday, October 22, as part of his ongoing stakeholder consultations. Discussions focused on expanding local medicine production, improving regulatory efficiency, addressing challenges facing pharmacists and strengthening public-private partnerships to support the growth of the pharmaceutical industry. Dr Bawumia said the engagement provided an opportunity to hear directly from current and former leaders of the society on policy interventions needed to expand the sector and improve healthcare delivery. He expressed appreciation to the society’s leadership for their contributions and stressed the importance of building a resilient domestic pharmaceutical industry. He said strengthening local production could help create jobs while improving Ghana’s health security. The proposed reforms form part of a broader discussion about how Ghana can expand its pharmaceutical manufacturing capacity, improve the business environment for local producers and strengthen access to medicines. However, details of specific policy measures, implementation timelines and targets for increasing domestic production were not provided in the information released on the meeting.

title: Service leavers offered wind turbine training
body: People leaving the Armed Forces can take Global Wind Organisation safety and technical training through the Career Transition Partnership as a route into the wind energy industry, and employment fairs are held each year in Edinburgh and Elgin, according to an answer given in Parliament. Imogen Walker, the Labour member for Hamilton and Clyde Valley, had asked what support and training pathways are available to help service leavers into Scotland’s renewable energy industry. Defence Minister Luke Pollard: “The Career Transition Partnership (CTP) provides Service leavers with tailored career support, training and access to employers, including opportunities within Scotland’s renewable energy sector. “Service leavers can work with a CTP Career Consultant to develop a personal resettlement plan and access relevant vocational training. This includes Global Wind Organisation Basic Safety and Basic Technical Training to support routes into the wind energy sector. “CTP also works with employers and industry partners to create employment pathways and delivers annual employment fairs in Edinburgh and Elgin, connecting Service leavers directly with recruiting employers.” Global Wind Organisation training is the industry standard set of certificates covering working at height, first aid, fire awareness, manual handling and sea survival, and the technical module adds mechanical, electrical and hydraulic basics. The Career Transition Partnership is run for the Ministry of Defence by Right Management and supports personnel in the two years before discharge and for two years afterwards. The post Service leavers offered wind turbine training first appeared on UK Defence Journal .

title: Molodist Film Festival Marks 55 Years, Bringing International Cinema to Kyiv Oct. 24-Nov. 1
body:
The 55th Molodist International Film Festival will take place in Kyiv from Oct. 24 to Nov. 1, 2026.
One of Eastern Europe’s leading film events marks its anniversary with a new visual identity while maintaining its mission of discovering emerging talent and helping debut filmmakers find their place in world cinema.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
Founded in 1970 as a student film showcase, Molodist has evolved over more than five decades into an international platform for emerging filmmakers. Its program features feature-length debuts and short films – fiction, documentary and animation – by filmmakers from Ukraine and around the world.
The first festival lasted just two days and featured 33 short films made by students of the Kyiv State Institute of Theatrical Arts named after Ivan Karpenko-Kary. The event was founded by film directors Vadym Chubasov and Viktor Ivchenko.
Since then, Molodist has become a platform for discovering new talent and introducing Ukrainian audiences to international cinema. The festival is accredited by the International Federation of Film Producers Associations (FIAPF), which recognizes its standing on the international film circuit.
The competition program includes student films, short films and feature-length debuts, with a dedicated competition for documentaries. The non-competition program features sections such as Festival of Festivals, Forma, The Century of the Greats and Midnight Screening, among others.
The festival’s top award is the Scythian Deer statuette, presented to winners of its competition programs.
The international jury of the 55th Molodist Film Festival will be chaired by Oleh Sentsov, a Ukrainian film director, screenwriter and writer, former Kremlin political prisoner and serviceman in the Armed Forces of Ukraine (AFU).
Sentsov directed the feature films “Gamer” (2011) and “Numbers” (2019), as well as the documentary “Real” (2024). His honors include the European Parliament’s Sakharov Prize for Freedom of Thought in 2018, Ukraine’s Taras Shevchenko National Prize in 2016 and France’s Legion of Honour.
The international jury also includes Matthijs Wouter Knol of the Netherlands, CEO and executive director of the European Film Academy, Iranian filmmaker and human rights advocate Mahnaz Mohammadi, Ukrainian theater director Yevhen Lavrenchuk, and Latvian film scholar and critic Anita Uzulniece.
The jury will assess student films, shorts and feature-length debuts from around the world and select the recipient of the festival’s Grand Prix.
A separate jury for the National Competition will include Ukrainian director Viacheslav Turyanytsia, Polish film programmer Radek Lipka and French-British film programmer and Film Republic founder Xavier Henry-Rashid.
Screenings will take place at the Zhovten Cinema and the House of Cinema in Kyiv. Festival passes are already on sale. Students can purchase passes at a discounted rate, while Ukrainian military personnel are eligible for free passes upon verification of their service status.
Over 55 years, Molodist has grown from a student film showcase into an international cinema forum while retaining its core mission: supporting a new generation of filmmakers and introducing audiences to films that will help shape the future of cinema.

title: Four people injured in Russian drone attack in Nikopol district, including child
body:
According to Ukrinform, Dnipropetrovsk Region Governor Oleksandr Hanzha reported this on Telegram .
Four people, including a 14-year-old boy, were injured in a Russian drone attack. All the victims were hospitalized. Doctors describe the boy's condition as critical. He was taken to a regional hospital in Dnipro.
A 46-year-old man is also in critical condition. Medical personnel are providing all the victims with the necessary assistance.
As Ukrinform reported, the death toll from the October 20 strike on warehouses near Dnipro has risen to three.

title: ANALYSIS: CBD COP17: Russia, Africa disagree as delegates adopt 14 decisions
body:
A week into the ongoing United Nations Biodiversity Conference (CBD COP17) in Armenia, negotiations have focused on translating global commitments into concrete action to halt biodiversity loss, mobilise conservation funding and strengthen accountability among countries.
Representatives of governments, scientists, Indigenous Peoples, local communities, civil society organisations and other stakeholders from across the world have gathered in Yerevan to advance efforts to conserve nature and ensure the sustainable use of biological resources.
The conference, which kicked off on 19th October, is themed “taking action for nature” and is scheduled to conclude on 30th October.
During the first week of the ongoing negotiations, PREMIUM TIMES observed that the talks focused on implementation, with delegates grappling with how to translate global biodiversity targets into measurable progress.
However, reports of disagreements over financing, access to genetic resources, benefit-sharing and the direction of international cooperation, have highlighted differences among negotiating blocs, particularly Russia and African countries.
The disagreements come against the backdrop of the inconclusive conclusion of COP16 in Cali, Colombia, where several critical issues remained unresolved, leaving delegates in Yerevan to continue negotiations on some of the most contentious aspects of the global biodiversity agenda.
Despite the disagreements, the Executive Secretary of the Convention on Biological Diversity, Astrid Schomaker, said significant progress had been made during the first week of negotiations.
“One week into #COP17Armenia and we are making progress for nature. The stakes have never been higher, and now is the time to act decisively,” she said.
Ms Schomaker said delegates had adopted 14 decisions across the Convention on Biological Diversity and its Cartagena and Nagoya Protocols, describing the development as a significant milestone.
Although she did not list the decisions, she said they advanced work on several issues, including biosafety, invasive alien species, gender equality, awareness-raising, compliance and monitoring.
“These decisions advance work on issues ranging from biosafety and invasive alien species to gender equality, awareness-raising, compliance and monitoring. Each contributes to the foundations we need for more effective implementation of our global biodiversity commitment,” she said.
She noted that the decisions followed hours of negotiations, careful listening and efforts to build consensus among countries.
“At a time when multilateralism faces significant challenges, this progress matters,” she said.
Ms Schomaker said COP17 was particularly significant because countries needed to address existing implementation gaps and hold one another accountable for accelerating progress towards the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (KMGBF).
“Of course, some of the most complex issues are still ahead of us,” she said, adding that the success of the conference would ultimately be measured by the difference its decisions made for nature and people.
The KMGBF remains the central framework guiding negotiations at COP17. Adopted in 2022, it sets out global biodiversity goals and targets, including 23 targets to be achieved by 2030.
The framework’s implementation remains a major concern as countries work to translate national commitments into measurable conservation outcomes.
Although many countries have established national biodiversity targets, questions remain about whether existing policies, financing arrangements and monitoring systems are sufficient to deliver the agreed goals.
Negotiations in Yerevan are, therefore, focusing on strengthening implementation, improving accountability and establishing reliable indicators for assessing progress.
Among the key priorities is the target to conserve at least 30 per cent of the world’s land and inland waters, as well as 30 per cent of coastal and marine areas, by 2030.
Delegates are also working to improve the measurement of progress on issues such as pollution, nutrient reduction and ecosystem restoration.
The outcome of these discussions could determine how effectively governments track their commitments and identify areas requiring urgent intervention.
Biodiversity financing remains one of the most difficult issues confronting negotiators, particularly for developing countries that argue they need substantial financial support to implement the global framework.
Discussions include how to mobilise additional public and private funding, improve access to existing resources and redirect environmentally harmful subsidies towards activities that support nature conservation.
One major issue is the implementation of the Cali Fund, established following COP16 to support benefit-sharing from the commercial use of digital sequence information (DSI) on genetic resources.
The mechanism seeks to ensure that companies benefiting from the use of such information contribute to conservation and the sustainable use of biodiversity.
For African countries, the debate is closely linked to questions of equity, resource ownership and the continent’s capacity to finance conservation.
African negotiators argue that the continent’s rich biological resources contribute to commercial activities globally, while the benefits generated from their use do not adequately support the communities and countries from which those resources originate.
They want benefit-sharing arrangements to deliver tangible financial resources for biodiversity protection, community development and the implementation of national conservation plans.
The negotiations also cover ways to mobilise private investment and redirect environmentally harmful subsidies, with the global framework calling for at least $500 billion annually in harmful incentives to be eliminated or redirected by 2030.
At COP17, Russia has emphasised the need to prevent the politicisation of international environmental agreements and ensure that biodiversity cooperation remains separate from wider geopolitical disputes.
Led in high-level discussions by Russian presidential aide Ruslan Edelgeriyev, the country’s position reflects concerns about international cooperation, national sovereignty and the financial implications of new mechanisms.
Russia has argued that biodiversity conservation should not become subject to geopolitical tensions or unfair competition. It has advocated for scientific and technical collaboration to continue despite broader international conflicts.
On genetic resources and DSI, Russia has stressed the need for non-discriminatory access and voluntary approaches to benefit-sharing.
The Russian delegation has also expressed opposition to establishing new international administrative structures or funding mechanisms where they duplicate existing arrangements, arguing that such bodies could increase costs for member states.
In negotiations on subsidiary issues, including gender-related action plans, Russian delegates have also sought to have their national positions formally reflected in the negotiating record.
These positions have implications for discussions on how biodiversity funding should be mobilised, how benefits should be distributed and how new international mechanisms should operate.
African countries have placed greater emphasis on securing predictable and adequate financing, equitable benefit-sharing and support for implementing the KMGBF.
For many African governments, the debate over genetic resources is not merely about access to scientific information. It is also about ensuring that countries and communities whose biodiversity supports commercial products and research receive a fair share of the resulting benefits.
The continent hosts a substantial share of the world’s biodiversity, including species and genetic resources that support agriculture, pharmaceuticals, biotechnology and other industries.
African representatives argue that the commercial value generated from these resources should contribute more directly to conservation in countries of origin, rather than leaving them to shoulder the costs of protecting biodiversity with limited financial resources.
The Cali Fund has, therefore, become an important part of the broader debate over fairness in the global biodiversity system.
Differences emerge when countries debate the extent to which benefit-sharing should be mandatory, how contributions should be calculated and distributed, and what safeguards should govern access to genetic resources.
Russia’s emphasis on voluntary mechanisms and non-discriminatory access could complicate efforts by African countries to secure stronger benefit-sharing arrangements.
However, the precise implications will depend on the final negotiating language and the extent to which countries can agree on practical rules for implementing the mechanisms.
In an interview with PREMIUM TIMES, Joseph Onoja, director-general of the Nigerian Conservation Foundation (NCF), said Nigeria’s position at the CBDCOP17 mostly dwells on resource mobilisation and technology transfer among others, but that the first week saw discussions that showed that the gaps are still very wide in terms of agreement between the Global North and the Global South.
“Nigeria is favourably disposed to introducing additional climate-related obligations through biodiversity decisions. But Russia is against it. So I hope that the second week will see more progress and agreements between parties,” he said.
Beyond financing, negotiations in Yerevan have addressed the relationship between biodiversity conservation, climate action and land restoration.
The host country has sought to strengthen the links between these issues, following the adoption of the Yerevan Declaration at the pre-COP Leaders’ Summit on 16 October.
The discussions seek to ensure that climate and land-restoration initiatives support biodiversity rather than inadvertently damaging ecosystems or contributing to deforestation.
For example, projects designed to increase carbon storage through forestry and agriculture must also consider their effects on native species, habitats and local communities.
The rights and participation of Indigenous Peoples and local communities (IPLCs) have also featured prominently in the negotiations.
A central concern is ensuring that Indigenous Peoples and local communities are recognised not only as groups to be consulted but also as contributors to biodiversity conservation and beneficiaries of relevant funding and decisions.
These discussions intersect with broader questions about access to genetic resources, traditional knowledge and the distribution of benefits under the Nagoya Protocol.
With the first week of negotiations concluded, delegates face further work on some of the most complex questions surrounding the implementation of the global biodiversity framework.
The adoption of 14 decisions represents progress, but it does not resolve the wider disagreements over finance, accountability, benefit-sharing and international cooperation.
For African countries, the remaining negotiations will be important in determining whether global biodiversity commitments are matched by sufficient financial support and mechanisms that recognise the value of the continent’s biological resources.
For Russia and other countries concerned about the design of international mechanisms, the challenge will be to reconcile national positions with collective efforts to halt biodiversity loss.
The outcome of COP17 will ultimately depend on whether delegates can bridge these differences and agree on measures that move beyond commitments towards measurable results for nature and people.

title: Turkey opens trial of Netanyahu, 34 other Israelis over Gaza-bound Sumud flotilla interception
body: An Istanbul court on Friday opened the trial of 35 Israelis, including Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Defense Minister Israel Katz, National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir, and IDF Chief of Staff Lt.-Gen. Eyal Zamir, over the Israeli Navy's interception of the Gaza-bound Sumud flotilla.Following the first hearing, the court ordered authorities to determine whether the defendants own assets in Turkey, upheld their arrest warrants, and called for consideration of legal proceedings against additional Israelis.The hearing took place at Istanbul's 11th Criminal Court, according to Turkey's state-run Anadolu news agency.Flotilla participants who had filed complaints against Israel attended, along with lawyers and representatives of Turkish organizations. None of the Israeli defendants were present.The court directed authorities to check whether the 35 defendants own real estate or other property in Turkey. There were no reports that assets had been frozen or property seizure orders issued.The court also upheld decisions related to requests for Interpol Red Notices. However, there is no confirmation that Interpol itself has issued such notices against the defendants.Court asks to file separate indictment for alleged Israeli actions against Gazan civiliansIn a separate ruling, the court asked the Istanbul prosecutor's office to consider filing a new indictment detailing alleged Israeli actions against Gaza's civilian population beyond the flotilla interception. The judges said the current indictment focuses on the flotilla incident and addresses allegations concerning events in Gaza only in general and indirect terms.The court also ordered authorities to identify additional people mentioned in the complainants' testimony and consider bringing proceedings against them. These include individuals whom the complainants accused of mistreating them while they were held in Israel. The court also requested information from the International Criminal Court in The Hague through Turkey's Justice Ministry.The case stems from complaints filed by Turkish citizens who participated in the flotilla and were detained after Israeli naval forces intercepted the vessels. They allege that they were subjected to violence during the interception and detention, that their belongings were taken, and that they were held in degrading conditions. At Friday's hearing, flotilla participants testified about alleged abuse by Israeli security personnel.Defendants charged with torture, unlawful deprivation of liberty, causing injury, aggravated robberyThe Turkish indictment charges the defendants with offenses including torture, unlawful deprivation of liberty, causing injury, and aggravated robbery. The allegations have not been proven in court.The list of defendants includes not only the prime minister, ministers, and military officers, but also a journalist, a rabbi, a social media influencer, and individuals whose roles are not specified.The arrest warrants predate the trial. In August, Turkish Justice Minister Akin Gurlek announced that Turkey had begun procedures to seek Interpol Red Notices against Netanyahu and other defendants. Such a notice, if issued, is not an international arrest warrant and does not automatically require Interpol member countries to make an arrest.The Israeli defendants are being tried in absentia. The next hearing is scheduled for March 30, 2027.

title: Koretsky discusses defense, energy, and logistics with Romanian PM
body:
Ukrainian Prime Minister Serhiy Koretsky has held a telephone conversation with Romanian Prime Minister Luca Niculescu. Among other topics, they discussed a Russian strike on a civilian vessel off the coast of Romania, which resulted in the death of one Ukrainian sailor, injuries to four others, and the disappearance of three more; six crew members were rescued.
According to the government portal on Saturday, Koretsky thanked Romania "for its principled stance and clear condemnation of this crime, which constitutes a gross violation of international law and freedom of navigation."
The two leaders held a substantive discussion on defense, energy, and logistics. "We aim to accelerate projects that will expand railway capacity, develop river transport routes, and increase cargo throughput," Koretsky noted.
The Ukrainian Prime Minister proposed that he and his Romanian counterpart establish cooperation through a format of intergovernmental consultations—an approach that has proven effective with other nations.
"I thanked Romania for its consistent support since the very first days of the full-scale invasion. I also invited Mr. Niculescu to Kyiv. This was our first conversation since his appointment, and I took the opportunity to congratulate him on his new position," Koretsky concluded.

title: Protect children from sexual abuse, Raissa Child Protection Initiative urges
body: The Raissa Child Protection Initiative over the weekend held a community durbar at Agbeve, Sowutuom, in Accra to educate residents on child sexual abuse prevention and the need to protect children from all forms of sexual exploitation. The programme forms part of efforts by the non-governmental organisation (NGO) to raise awareness of child protection, educate parents and caregivers on their responsibilities, and encourage community members to report suspected cases of abuse to the appropriate authorities. Founder of the NGO, Ms Raissa Sambou, said protecting children from sexual abuse required the collective responsibility of parents, caregivers, traditional authorities and other members of society. She said children needed safe environments where they could speak about uncomfortable experiences without fear of blame or punishment. Madam Sambou stressed that children who experienced sexual abuse were never responsible for what happened to them and urged adults to listen to them, take their concerns seriously and seek appropriate assistance when necessary. She noted that both boys and girls could be victims of sexual abuse and called for equal protection and support for all children, regardless of their sex. She also urged parents and caregivers to educate children on body boundaries, inappropriate touching and how to seek help from trusted adults. Ms Sambou cautioned that perpetrators could be people known to or trusted by children, adding that parents needed to remain vigilant and establish safeguards to protect their children. She further called on community members not to conceal abuse to protect family relationships or reputations, stressing that the safety and welfare of children must take priority. A legal practitioner and member of the Raissa Child Protection Initiative project team, Alhaji Yussif Baba Suleman, said the 1992 Constitution of Ghana contained provisions to safeguard children’s rights, making it important for people to understand those rights and ensure they were respected. He urged the public not to shield perpetrators of sexual abuse because they were relatives, friends or people close to their families. Alhaji Suleman said offenders must face the full rigours of the law to ensure justice for victims and deter others from committing similar offences He also called on residents to report suspected cases to the appropriate authorities rather than resort to secrecy or informal settlements. The durbar highlighted the importance of community participation in preventing child sexual abuse and ensuring that affected children received the necessary protection and support. Beneficiaries of the forum thanked the organising team for the valuable information shared and hoped such programmes would be held frequently in communities across the country.

title: British jets escort French jets on ‘nuclear strike’
body: RAF Typhoons have escorted French Rafales simulating a nuclear strike mission over the Mediterranean, the first time British aircraft have taken part in a French nuclear exercise, according to the government. Exercise Rummy ran on 20 and 21 October, with the Rafales launching from Saint-Dizier air base in eastern France, the home of the French air force’s airborne nuclear component. No nuclear weapons were involved, and the Ministry of Defence said the exercise was conducted under robust safety and security arrangements and focused on how the two air forces work together. Wes Streeting, the Defence Secretary, said: “This exercise marks a new chapter in the defence nuclear relationship between the United Kingdom and France. “As Europe’s nuclear powers, we have a shared responsibility to contribute to the security and stability of the Euro-Atlantic region. This exercise demonstrates the depth of our partnership, the credibility of our deterrents and our determination to stand together in the face of emerging threats. “In an increasingly dangerous world, our adversaries should be in no doubt: the UK and France remain united in our commitment to European security and to maintaining the deterrence that has helped preserve peace for generations.” Catherine Vautrin, the French Minister of the Armed Forces and Veterans, said: “Having independent nuclear forces does not exclude coordination. Our nuclear cooperation with the United Kingdom keeps deepening: on Tuesday night, UK Typhoons participated for the very first time to a French nuclear exercise alongside Rafales. “Through coordination, our nuclear forces demonstrate that they can contribute even more significantly to the overall security of the Alliance and to the peace and stability of the Euro Atlantic area.” The exercise falls under the Northwood Declaration, the agreement signed last year under which the two countries said that no extreme threat to Europe could arise which would not prompt a response by both, while each retains sovereign and independent nuclear forces and national decision making. Britain and France are the only nuclear armed states in Europe, and the declaration established a joint nuclear steering group to coordinate their policy, capabilities and operations. Saint-Dizier is the base of the 4th Fighter Wing, which operates Rafales carrying the ASMP-A supersonic stand-off missile that forms the airborne half of the French deterrent. The French maintain both an airborne component and ballistic missile submarines, while Britain has relied on submarines alone since the WE.177 bomb was withdrawn in 1998. That changes with the purchase of twelve F-35A aircraft and British entry into NATO’s nuclear mission, which will return a nuclear role to the Royal Air Force after more than a quarter of a century. Air Marshal Johnny Beck told a committee this year that the aircraft were not bought for the nuclear role , while the government has presented the purchase as the means of joining the mission. The Defence Investment Plan commits £63 billion over four years to the nuclear enterprise, funding the Dreadnought ballistic missile submarines, SSN-AUKUS attack submarines, a new sovereign warhead and the supporting infrastructure. The refreshed Lancaster House agreement between Britain and France covers an expanded joint deployable force, deeper nuclear cooperation and work on the next generation of weapons. The post British jets escort French jets on ‘nuclear strike’ first appeared on UK Defence Journal .

title: Unilever Nigeria posts 20% jump in nine-month profit, raises interim dividend fourfold
body:
Unilever Nigeria reported an increase of 20.1 per cent in net profit for the nine months to September, compared to the corresponding period of 2025, according to the latest corporate results of the fast-moving consumer goods manufacturer released on Friday.
The improvement in earnings derived largely from a fairly stronger revenue, which climbed to N184 billion from N155.4 billion a year earlier, thanks to higher sales from the company’s food business.
The food division contributed 66.9 per cent to turnover, up from 61.1 per cent a year ago, while the two other divisions – personal care and beauty & wellbeing – contributed 23 per cent and 10.1 per cent in that order.
Unilever Nigeria, whose products include top brands like Lipton, Knorr, Close-Up, Vaseline and Pears, among others, generated 98 per cent of its revenue through domestic sales during the period, while exports accounted for the rest.
Cost of sales as a percentage of revenue dropped to 53.6 per cent from 58.8 per cent, boosting gross profit.
Marketing and administrative expenses surged by 36.6 per cent to N40.3 billion, driven by increased spending on brand and marketing.
The company sharply reduced its impairment write-back on trade and other receivables to N43.1 million from N834.9 million, softening the pressure on operating profit.
Other income advanced by 166.2 per cent to N651.7 million, helped by higher fees earned on production of tea for Lipton Teas and Infusions Plant Based Limited and proceeds from a Federal Government of Nigeria-issued promissory note.
Profit before taxation advanced by more than one-fifth to N45.6 billion, while profit after tax rose to N26.4 billion from N22 billion.
However, total assets slightly dropped by 0.4 per cent to N179.4 billion, triggered by lower cash and cash equivalents.
In a separate announcement on Friday, the company declared an interim dividend of N2 per share, four times what it paid for the half-year period of 2025, when it distributed N0.50 per share to shareholders. The potential payout of the newly declared dividend stands at N11.5 billion.
“On Wednesday, 18 November 2026, dividends will be paid electronically to shareholders whose names appear on the Register of Members as at Friday, 30 October 2026 and who have completed the e-dividend registration and mandated the Registrar to pay their dividends directly into their Bank accounts,” Unilever Nigeria said.
In March, Unilever Plc, the parent, announced it had struck a deal to merge its global foods business with McCormick & Company, Inc., subject to required regulatory approvals and the satisfaction of other customary closing conditions.
It expects the business combination to create a larger entity specialising in flavours and food products.

title: Aggrieved NDC delegates invoke curses on party executives over alleged bloated register at Atwima Kwanwoma Constituency
body: Some aggrieved delegates of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) in the Atwima Kwanwoma Constituency of the Ashanti Region, who allege that their names have been removed from the party’s electoral register, have invoked curses on party executives over what they describe as their failure to address the issue. Tension is currently mounting at Twedie, where the NDC constituency elections are taking place. Some aggrieved delegates allege the names of qualified delegates have been removed from the electoral album and replaced with those of persons they consider unqualified, purportedly to favour certain candidates in the elections. The aggrieved delegates say they have repeatedly reported the matter to the party’s regional executives for resolution, but their concerns have allegedly not been addressed. They claim the failure of the executives to intervene has left them with no option but to invoke the Antoa deity, calling for spiritual retribution against anyone found culpable in the alleged manipulation. “We have poured libation and slaughtered sheep while invoking Antoa Nyamaa and other river deities to deal with those allegedly responsible for the disputed changes,” they said. Speaking to the media, one of the aggrieved delegates Gifty Kobbina she expressed frustration over the development, insisting that their sacrifices and commitment to the party should not be undermined by what they describe as an attempt to disenfranchise legitimate delegates. “We have suffered for this party, and we will not allow anyone to cheat us. We are calling on Antoa to strike anyone who has a hand in this album manipulation,”she alleged. The aggrieved delegates have warned that failure to resolve their concerns could undermine the credibility of the constituency elections and deepen divisions among party members.

title: It’s Unfair To Compare Us To Barca — Mourinho
body: Real Madrid coach Jose Mourinho said it was unfair to compare his side to Spanish champions Barcelona ahead of Sunday’s La Liga Clasico. Hansi Flick’s Barca have won back-to-back La Liga titles and lead the top flight, in which they are unbeaten, while Mourinho arrived this summer after Madrid went two seasons without a major trophy. The panorama has changed slightly, after Barca suffered their first defeat of the season at Paris Saint-Germain on Tuesday, while Madrid have won their last four matches. Madrid are third in La Liga, trailing Barca by six points before Sunday’s meeting at Camp Nou. “I think the people that thought a week ago Barca would thrash us will keep thinking the same thing,” Mourinho told reporters on Saturday. “I don’t think just for the Paris game, or Madrid’s (4-1 win against) Leipzig, they will change their way of thinking.” Mourinho highlighted that he has only been at the helm a few months, in comparison to Flick, who arrived at Barca in 2024. “People look at us like a finished product, but finished products in football are difficult because they are never finished… but they look at us like we’re in an advanced phase of the process,” continued Mourinho. “We’ve been working for three months, out of that you can take pre-season when the players were arriving (back from the World Cup), and the recent international break, then we’ve been together a month-and-a-half, two months… “This is the start of a product, we’re in an initial phase where the coach is learning, analysing, bit by bit defining paths, the players are learning about the coach… comparing a team in this state (to more established sides), I think is unfair.” Mourinho said form did not matter when it comes to the Clasico. “We’ve been in a good dynamic, winning games, playing well, scoring goals, but in the Clasico it doesn’t matter what you did before, it has no influence,” said Mourinho. “The Clasico is unique, normally the football world stops to watch it. Hopefully it’s a great game. And we win.” Mourinho said he would not change his plans to try and stop Barcelona winger Lamine Yamal. The 19-year-old Spain international is in sublime form and hopes to win the Ballon d’Or award on Monday. “He’s a great player and great players you respect,” added Mourinho. “One thing is respecting, another thing is to change plans, structures, forgetting your own essence. That we will not do, neither for him or any other player of great quality we face.” ‘A Great Colleague’ Barcelona coach Hansi Flick confirmed Jules Kounde was still out injured for the game, along with Dani Olmo, Eric Garcia and Andreas Christensen. The German coach said he expected a Madrid side arriving with “a lot of confidence” and praised his opposite number Mourinho. “I have the highest respect. When you’re managing teams on this level for so many years and you always have success, it’s about quality, he showed this at every club,” Flick told reporters. “Every player from the (Germany) national team who worked under him speaks with a great respect, I think the same. He’s a colleague, a very, very successful colleague and a great colleague.” Flick said the 4-2 defeat in Paris by PSG gave his team some clues as to where they need to improve. “We analysed this game. We did many things really good but we saw some situations where we have to improve,” added Flick. “We have to grow as a team. Tomorrow we play against one of the best teams in the world so it’s a good opportunity to grow. To challenge ourselves, to improve ourselves and to grow as a team.” AFP The post It’s Unfair To Compare Us To Barca — Mourinho appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Kenya records second Ebola death
body:
Kenya has recorded its second Ebola death after a 65-year-old woman died while receiving treatment, leaving seven of the country’s nine confirmed patients receiving care.
The woman, the country’s third confirmed case of Bundibugyo virus disease, was a close family member and direct contact of the first patient, who also died, according to the Kenyan Ministry of Health.
In a statement on Friday, the ministry said the woman developed symptoms on 13 October while under quarantine and was admitted to an infectious disease unit the same day.
“Sadly, she succumbed to the disease early this evening,” the ministry said.
The ministry said the woman’s family had been informed and that arrangements were being made for a safe and dignified burial in consultation with them, in line with public health protocols.
It urged the public and media to respect the family’s privacy as they mourn their loss.
The latest death brings the number of fatalities from the outbreak in Kenya to two, with seven other patients receiving treatment at two isolation facilities.
The ministry said all nine confirmed cases were linked to a single cluster of known contacts, adding that there was no evidence of community transmission.
Kenya confirmed its first case of Bundibugyo virus disease in early October in a man who had travelled from the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) through Uganda. He died on 5 October, according to the World Health Organisation (WHO).
Health authorities subsequently identified infections among people who had been in contact with the initial patient, including family members and healthcare workers.
The 65-year-old woman was already under quarantine when she developed symptoms, allowing health officials to identify and isolate her for treatment.
The WHO said the subsequent cases in Kenya were epidemiologically linked to the initial case, underscoring the importance of contact tracing, quarantine and monitoring people exposed to the virus.
The outbreak has also raised concerns about cross-border transmission in East and Central Africa, particularly as Kenya and Nigeria have reported imported cases linked to travel through Uganda.
Nigeria confirmed its first case of Bundibugyo virus disease on 20 October in a patient in Abuja who had travelled from Uganda. The patient was isolated and receiving medical care, while authorities began tracing people who might have been exposed.
PREMIUM TIMES has reported on investigations into whether the Nigerian and Kenyan cases could be linked to possible exposure at Uganda’s Entebbe International Airport, where both patients reportedly travelled through on 3 October. Health officials have been investigating possible contact through shared equipment or other exposure, but a direct link has not been established.
Bundibugyo virus disease is a form of Ebola disease caused by the Bundibugyo virus, a distinct species from the Zaire ebolavirus responsible for several previous outbreaks.
Ebola is a severe illness that can cause fever, weakness, muscle pain, vomiting, diarrhoea and, in some cases, unexplained bleeding. The virus can spread through direct contact with the blood or other body fluids of an infected person, as well as contaminated materials.
There is currently no approved vaccine specifically for Bundibugyo virus disease, making early detection, isolation, supportive treatment and infection prevention particularly important.
However, the WHO and its partners began the Tumaini clinical trial in DRC, with the first participant receiving the Ervebo vaccine. The trial will assess whether the vaccine, approved for the Zaire strain of Ebola, can also protect against the Bundibugyo virus.
Kenya’s Ministry of Health urged members of the public to avoid contact with the body fluids of anyone suspected of having the disease and not to touch or handle the body of someone who has died from a suspected infection.
It also advised people to wash their hands regularly with soap and water and seek medical attention immediately if they develop symptoms after possible exposure.
The ministry asked anyone experiencing symptoms or concerned about possible exposure to call Kenya’s toll-free emergency line on 719 or contact the health authorities through WhatsApp on 0700 719 719.

title: Investment security key to global gas market stability
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 24 (MNA) – Ali-Mohammad Mousavi, deputy of Iranian oil minister for international affairs says that security of investments and interests of producers are requirments for the security of global gas market.
According to Iranian oil ministry's news service-SHANA, in an interview, Ali-Mohammad Mousavi, deputy oil minister for international affairs and trade and Iran’s representative at international energy forums, discussed the Moscow summit’s objectives, Iran’s agenda, the GECF’s role in global energy governance and opportunities for advancing Iran’s gas diplomacy.
Q: What are the circumstances surrounding the eighth GECF summit, and how do you assess its significance?
Mousavi: The eighth GECF summit is taking place at a critical juncture in the evolution of the international energy system and coincides with the forum’s 25th anniversary. In recent years, the global natural gas market has undergone significant changes driven by geopolitical, economic, technological and environmental factors.
Changes in international gas trade patterns, the expansion of liquefied natural gas (LNG) infrastructure, growing concerns over supply and demand security, intensifying competition for investment and rising energy needs in emerging economies have underscored the importance of dialogue and coordination among gas-producing and exporting countries.
Against this backdrop, the summit provides an opportunity for leaders to exchange views at the highest political level, assess long-term market trends and strengthen common approaches to strategic issues facing the natural gas industry.
The significance of the summit extends beyond reviewing market developments. It can also help reinforce the GECF’s position as an influential platform for international energy dialogue and for safeguarding the legitimate interests of gas-producing and exporting countries.
Q: What level of participation will Iran have at the Moscow summit, and what is planned for the Iranian delegation?
Mousavi: Iran was the principal proponent of establishing the GECF and is one of its founding members. As a country with some of the world’s largest proven natural gas reserves, Iran has consistently played an active and influential role in the forum’s activities.
At the eighth summit, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian will lead a high-level delegation accompanied by Hamid Bovard, caretaker oil minister.
The president’s address to the summit, outlining Iran’s principled positions on international developments and the global energy market, as well as the country’s views on the future of gas cooperation, will be among the main events of the visit.
Before the leaders’ summit, the forum’s 28th ministerial meeting will bring together ministers and senior representatives of member countries. The meeting will review and approve the secretariat’s programs and finalize the documents to be presented to the summit.
The Iranian delegation also plans to hold bilateral meetings with senior officials from member and observer countries, particularly on energy cooperation. Discussions will explore opportunities to expand bilateral and multilateral ties in natural gas trade, investment, infrastructure development, technology transfer, technological cooperation and the use of shared capacities among member countries.
Q: What are Iran’s main priorities and positions at the eighth summit?
Mousavi: Iran’s positions can be outlined along two principal dimensions: political issues and strategic energy priorities.
On the political front, one of the Iranian delegation’s priorities will be to explain the dimensions of the military aggression by the United States and the Israeli regime against Iran and condemn actions targeting the country’s national sovereignty, territorial integrity and security.
In this context, the martyrdom of the Leader of the Islamic Revolution, military commanders and civilians, as well as events related to Minab and Lamerd, will be addressed in line with Iran’s official positions.
In the energy sector, our key priorities include protecting the collective interests of forum members, strengthening the role of natural gas in energy security, ensuring continued investment across the gas value chain, countering unilateral restrictive measures against producers, and expanding technical, commercial and investment cooperation.
We believe energy security is a balanced, multidimensional concept. Achieving it requires simultaneous attention to security of supply for consumers, security of demand for producers, investment security and the sustainability of energy trade flows.
Q: Given recent geopolitical developments, how do you view the relationship between political stability and security in the global gas market?
Mousavi: Because the natural gas industry is capital-intensive, involves long investment recovery periods and depends on extensive production, transmission, processing and export infrastructure, it requires political stability, investment security and predictable market conditions more than many other economic activities.
Any escalation in geopolitical tensions, threats to energy infrastructure, disruption of transportation routes or imposition of unilateral restrictions can affect project financing costs, investment risks and energy prices, ultimately undermining supply security in regional and global markets.
For this reason, we emphasize the need to prevent the politicization of energy trade and its use as an instrument in international relations. I believe the global gas market should develop on the basis of cooperation, mutual benefit, respect for contractual obligations and nondiscriminatory access to technology, equipment and financial resources.
Energy security is a shared responsibility among producers, consumers and countries through which energy is transported. None of these stakeholders can guarantee lasting energy security without taking the interests and concerns of the others into account.
Q: How do you assess the role of natural gas in the global energy mix in the years ahead?
Mousavi: Given its technical, economic and environmental characteristics, natural gas will remain an important pillar of global energy supply in the coming decades.
Compared with coal, natural gas emits less carbon dioxide when burned to produce the same amount of energy. If methane emissions across the supply chain are effectively managed, it can also help reduce greenhouse gas emissions.
In addition, the flexibility of gas-fired power plants allows them to support the integration of intermittent renewable energy sources, including solar and wind power.
Population growth, industrial development, urbanization and rising electricity demand in developing countries also provide considerable scope for natural gas to maintain its role in the global energy mix.
However, energy transition pathways differ from one country to another. Energy policies must reflect each country’s economic conditions, level of development, resource base and national priorities.
At the Oil Ministry, we believe the energy transition should be realistic, equitable and based on diversifying energy sources. It should not lead to unreasonable restrictions on investment in the natural gas industry.
Q: The GECF has emphasized the need for investment in the gas industry. Why is this important?
Mousavi: The sustainable development of the natural gas industry requires continuous, long-term investment across the entire value chain, from exploration and field development to processing, transmission, storage, exports and LNG infrastructure.
Because major gas projects generally require substantial financial resources and long periods for design, construction and operation, a stable and predictable investment environment is particularly important.
Reduced or delayed upstream investment can constrain supply capacity over the medium and long term, intensify price volatility and increase the vulnerability of the global gas market. Such an outcome would benefit neither producers nor consumers.
Accordingly, one of Iran’s key messages at the Moscow summit will be the need to strike a balance among energy security objectives, economic development and environmental considerations.
Producer countries must have fair access to financial resources, advanced technologies and consumer markets. Political barriers and unilateral restrictions should not obstruct the development of natural gas production and export capacity.
Q: What role does the GECF play in developments in the global gas market, and can it be considered an organization similar to OPEC?
Mousavi: The GECF is an intergovernmental organization with a consultative, analytical and cooperative mandate. It was established to strengthen engagement among natural gas-producing and exporting countries.
Unlike OPEC, the GECF does not have a mechanism for setting production quotas or directly managing natural gas supply volumes in the global market.
Structural differences between oil and gas markets, including the significant role of long-term contracts in gas trade, dedicated transmission infrastructure and the regional characteristics of gas markets, mean that cooperation within the forum operates differently.
Nevertheless, the GECF can play an effective role in strengthening natural gas’s position and defending producers’ shared interests by facilitating the exchange of views, experience and information; conducting specialized studies; providing long-term market outlooks; promoting technical cooperation; and coordinating members’ positions in international forums.
Strengthening the secretariat’s technical and research capabilities, expanding technological cooperation and increasing the forum’s participation in global energy discussions can further enhance its role in international energy governance.
Q: What capacity does Iran have to expand gas cooperation with other GECF members?
Mousavi: Thanks to its vast natural gas reserves, strategic geographical position, extensive gas transmission network, long experience in developing and operating gas fields, and technical and engineering capabilities, Iran has considerable potential to expand regional and international cooperation.
Iran’s geographical position, connecting energy-rich regions with consumer markets, offers opportunities to develop regional gas trade and transit cooperation.
Potential areas of cooperation with GECF members include expanding gas exports through pipelines and LNG, establishing swap and transit arrangements, cooperating in field development, participating in processing and infrastructure projects, and exchanging technical expertise.
Cooperation in reservoir management, improving recovery rates, reducing gas flaring, optimizing energy consumption, cutting methane emissions and developing technologies across the gas value chain could also become part of specialized engagement among member countries.
Realizing this potential will require political will among member countries, favorable economic, technical, contractual and investment conditions, and arrangements that ensure mutual benefits for all parties involved.

title: Sahara Foundation Launches New Go-Recycling Hub at Air Force Base in Ikeja
body: Peter Uzoho Sahara Group Foundation has inaugurated its Go Recycling Hub at Sam Ethnan Air Force Base in Ikeja, Lagos, reinforcing its commitment to environmental sustainability, community empowerment and inclusive economic growth. The new hub advances the Foundation’s efforts to transform recyclable waste from an environmental liability into an economic asset, creating income opportunities for households through targeted waste-to-wealth programmes. It also marks another step towards strengthening sustainable waste recovery systems and empowering host communities across Nigeria.
