title: Sealift outline case due this financial year
body: The Strategic Outline Case for the Strategic Sealift Future programme, which will decide how Britain replaces the ships that move the Army’s heavy equipment, is intended to be completed before the end of this financial year, according to an answer given in Parliament. Ben Obese-Jecty, the Conservative member for Huntingdon, had asked whether the case had been completed. Luke Pollard, the Minister of State for Defence, said: “The Strategic Outline Case for the Strategic Sealift – Future programme is intended to be completed this financial year.” A Strategic Outline Case is the first of the Treasury’s five case stages and sets out the need and the range of options before any procurement decision is taken. Ministers confirmed earlier this month that all four Point class roll-on roll-off sealift ships will receive extensive refits, work that keeps the existing capability available while the replacement programme is developed. The Point class carry armoured vehicles, artillery and stores for deployments and exercises, and the fleet underpins Britain’s ability to move a division sized force by sea. The ships were built in Germany and South Korea and entered service from 2002 under a private finance arrangement, with the Ministry of Defence later buying the hulls outright. The post Sealift outline case due this financial year first appeared on UK Defence Journal .

title: Lee Chang Dong ponders the ethics of the camera
body:
Lee Chang Dong’s seventh feature film, Possible Love, is inspired by true events from 2009, when a Korean conglomerate fired a third of its staff – 2,600 employees – after which many died by suicide. Possible Love is the latest in a long line of Lee movies that engage with themes of class or labor or religion or compressed modernity, that uniquely Korean affliction, without feeling didactic.
A different kind of movie would have captured the heat of that labor struggle. Possible Love picks up with the characters in the aftermath, a murkier time that defies easy understanding. The film opens with an epigraph: “Thou shall not covet.” What follows is a movie about characters who covet. They covet each other’s job, designer clothes, spouses, and positionality. Mi-ok (Jeon Do-Yeon) is the long-suffering wife of Ho-seok (Sul Kyung-gu), her laid-off husband. At a funeral of a colleague who died by suicide, Mi-ok and Ho-seok meet another couple, documentary filmmaker Ye-ji (Cho Yeo-jeong) and her rich husband, Sang-woo (Zo In-sung). And off we go.
The Verge spoke with Lee during his trip to New York about how he arrived at his politics, porousness between people, the properties of the camera, and what it is like to work with Netflix. The interview was conducted in Korean and translated into English.
I am also from Daegu. I wonder how this fact shaped you? And more broadly, to whom or what do you owe your political education?
As you know well, Daegu is referred to as the heartland of conservatism in Korea. I went to school there, all the way through university, so I grew up steeped in that conservative disposition and was influenced by it. But until I graduated from college, in the spring of 1980, I didn’t realize how politically conservative Daegu citizens were.
That spring, in May of 1980, I participated in protests against the Chun Doo-hwan regime as a university student. It was on the streets that I met them, the citizens, and experienced their hardline sentiments in a visceral way. It was shocking to me. Afterwards, I thought a lot about how come the people in Daegu were so politically conservative. In light of all that, the thoughts of a person I perceive as myself, that person’s attitude towards the world, could only be bound with a certain kind of tension.
I was interested in how different directors respond to similar social forces in different ways – like Bong Joon Ho’s Parasite and Park Chan Wook’s No Other Choice. I imagine you know them both personally. What is the conversation between you all when working on your various projects?
We do know each other personally, but we seldom talk about our work. It might be the result of coincidence. Though of course, there might be a certain inevitability hidden within them. We lived through the same modern Korean history, and you cannot call that coincidence.
One thing does come to mind. A long time ago, I think before he made Mother, Bong Joon Ho told me over drinks that he had almost finished writing a script and wanted to show it to me. It was a story about a mother, and he was wrestling with how he could portray that person’s pain, whether he even had the right to. He said he wanted to show me the script. But once he sobered up, maybe he forgot, because he never showed it to me. Later, when I saw the film, I felt I might understand what he had been talking about.
Possible Love is concerned with similar questions: How can I portray another person’s story, another person’s pain? What position am I in? How much distance should I keep from them? You could say that these questions around the ethics of the camera are connected to the worry Bong Joon Ho had back then.
Like Ye-ji, I come from the so-called margins, and now report on that terrain, which is perhaps why watching her character pursue a near-vampiric level of access, I felt something close to repulsion. How were you able to represent the filmmaker–participant dynamic so accurately?
I can’t say how accurate it is. I don’t think Ye-ji’s attitude can be generalized. Not every documentary filmmaker has a rich husband. Nevertheless you can say Ye-Ji captures something universal about filmmakers, or those who deal in other people’s stories, directors such as myself, or reporters, in that they aren’t exactly the people they portray. Even if they came from a lower class, they are no longer of it. Their position in life has changed. And yet, in order to do their work, what do they do? When someone else’s suffering unfolds dramatically in front of them, are they to capture the moment on tape, or should they step away from the camera? Or maybe it isn’t unfolding dramatically in front of them, in which case, do they create a certain effect by producing the moment, by staging it?
[Image: What does it mean to capture someone on film? https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/Possible-Love_NYFF64_05.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all]
I think those are basically properties of the camera. The moment you hold a camera you have power, and the camera operates according to that power.
It’s not so much that I portrayed it so precisely, but these properties of the camera are something worth thinking through together.
For us filmmakers, we don’t belong to the world of our subjects, nor are we on the side of capital either. We are in the middle where we are, it can be said, in a neutral, or perhaps cowardly position. Despite that, those who make movies, those who tell stories of others, in the end, can, through their efforts, bring about some small change.
In this film, Ho-seok ends up pouring out what’s inside of him in front of the camera, which functions as a kind of treatment, even if that isn’t what Ye-ji intended.
Possible Love is a collaboration between you and screenwriter Oh Jung-mi. How did you two come to work together, and what does that collaboration look like?
She is a student I met at Korea National University of Arts. You could say it’s a school that draws the most talented and ambitious students, and she was special even among them. By special I mean she was creative and wrote well, of course, but she also has a perspective, and the ability to take a step back and regard something, and find meaning in things.
As I get older, I grow duller and numb, and set in my ways, and she is a friend who reliably jolts me out of it, which is very precious to me.
I think I’m lucky. Not just with Oh Jung-mi but everyone around me that I work with is very precious to me, and I feel lucky to have met them.
The problem with Oh Jung-mi, though, is that while working together, I kept scrapping projects. So she suffered. But she never left. She stayed beside me, and even though she herself is someone who makes and develops films, she has given me a lot of help up to now.
Ye-ji documents in service of higher purpose. Mi-ok’s character snaps photos of the table spread for no purpose at all. The footage from the helicopter captures a moment of police brutality. How does the function of cinema compare to all the other instances in which we hit record?
Ye-ji has a desire to capture in her camera vanishing laborers [and] the value of their labor — not unlike her dry cleaner father. And yet, it is undeniable that she also regards their lives as source material for her own movie. As narrative filmmakers, stories of others in pain often is nothing but material for a commercial movie.
As for Mi-ok, she knows about the properties of the camera, but she, too, has a desire: to broadcast her pain, and her problems. She has a secondary desire, which is that she wonders if her husband’s traumas may not be healed through the camera, because she believes that his biggest issue is keeping all his problems, his despair and his anger, hidden.
So each has their own desires regarding the camera.
As a filmmaker, firstly, I had the goal of conveying the contents of the documentary Ye-ji was making, of capturing the sufferings of the laid-off laborers. I believed what Ye-ji tried to show, I had to show through my own film.
The group therapy session scene, for example, could be very long and tedious, and for some viewers it might be something that they cannot emotionally relate to, because they came to see a narrative film, not documentary. Despite that, I felt I had to convey it.
Regarding the crackdown scene, some of it appears through archival footage shot from a distance. But as someone making a fiction film, I also have a responsibility to convey Ho-seok’s subjective memory cinematically. So you could say within the narrative structure of Ye-ji’s documentary, multiple layers of roles and goals co-exist.
What are some notes you received from your American movie executives that felt unique to working in the American system versus Korean?
I didn’t feel that at all. From pre-production through post-production, Netflix, as the investor, never once interfered or offered unsolicited notes. Of course, I can’t generalize from that. I haven’t asked everyone else. But I had none of that. In that sense they absolutely guaranteed my independence and freedom as a director.
Now the film is finished and we are promoting it, and in particular part of what we call the Oscar campaign. I probably wouldn’t have gotten this kind of help without Netflix, that’s clear.
Possible Love was released in select US theaters October 23rd and will be available on Netflix globally on November 6th.

title: Golden Arms gets support from Shoe Fabriek ahead of World Armwrestling Championship
body: Ghana’s national armwrestling team, the Golden Arms, has received a boost ahead of the 2026 World Armwrestling Championship in India, following a footwear sponsorship from Ghanaian manufacturer Shoe Fabriek GH Ltd. The company presented specially designed Ghana-branded sneakers to the Ghana Armwrestling Federation (GAF) for the Golden Arms on Friday, October 23, 2026, as part of efforts to support the team ahead of the international competition. The sneakers were presented by Shoe Fabriek’s General Manager, Mrs Adelaide A. Abbiw-Williams, and received on behalf of the Federation by its President, Mr Charles Osei-Asibey. The sponsorship is expected to complement the team’s official uniforms and kits, giving the athletes a coordinated appearance as they prepare to represent Ghana on the world stage. Speaking at the presentation, Mrs Abbiw-Williams said the gesture reflected the company’s commitment to supporting Ghanaian talent and promoting national pride through locally manufactured products. “As a proudly Ghanaian footwear manufacturer, we are delighted to celebrate this important milestone with the Ghana Armwrestling Federation. Ten years of building a sporting discipline, nurturing talent and creating opportunities for Ghanaian athletes to compete internationally is an achievement worth recognising,” she said. She added that the company’s support went beyond the provision of footwear, stressing the importance of corporate Ghana backing athletes who carry the country’s flag at international competitions. “As the team heads to India, we want them to step onto the international stage with confidence, pride and the knowledge that corporate Ghana is behind them. We wish the entire contingent every success,” she added. The Golden Arms will be seeking to make Ghana proud at the World Armwrestling Championship in New Delhi, India, where the country’s athletes will compete against some of the best arm wrestlers from across the world. Shoe Fabriek GH Ltd, based in Akropong-Akuapem in the Eastern Region, specialises in the manufacture of footwear for institutional, industrial and consumer markets, including security boots, safety footwear, school shoes, sandals and casual shoes. The partnership highlights the role of Ghanaian businesses in supporting sports development and demonstrates how local industries can contribute to the success of national teams competing internationally. For the Golden Arms, the footwear sponsorship represents an additional show of confidence and support as they prepare to fly Ghana’s flag at the global championship.

title: IRGC spox reacts to rising oil prices with an image
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 24 (MNA) – IRGC spokesman Brigadier General Hossein Mohebbi posted an image of a burning oil tanker depicting Brent crude prices rising from $116 to $117 per barrel.
Mohebi shared the image on his account on X on Friday night, October 23. The image featured the words “Brent Oil Price” alongside the price increase from $116 to $117 per barrel.
The post came as vessel traffic through unauthorized routes in the Strait of Hormuz has been accompanied by incidents in recent weeks, including naval mine strikes, explosions and fires aboard ships.
Meanwhile, global Brent crude prices have continued to rise. These developments come as the United States maintains its naval blockade of Iran, while military tensions and insecurity across the region continue to weigh on global energy markets.

title: Jigawa police arrest 3 over cable vandalism, theft
body: The Jigawa State Police Command has arrested three suspects over alleged vandalism and theft of electrical cables in Guri and Dutse Local Government Areas of the state. The command also recovered a high-tension cable from one of the suspects arrested in Guri, while two others were apprehended over the alleged theft of armoured cables at the Manpower Development Institute (MDI), Dutse. The Police Public Relations Officer, SP Shiisu Lawan Adam, disclosed this in a statement issued on Saturday, October 24, 2026 in Dutse. According to the statement, police operatives attached to Guri Division arrested a 23-year-old suspect, Abdullahi Maina, of Fulatari Quarters, Nguru Local Government Area of Yobe State, on October 21 at about 9:30am. Bandits killed as hunters repel attack in Katsina Gunmen invade Taraba community, kill residents, cart away motorcycles The suspect was reportedly found in possession of a high-tension cable concealed in a sack. The police said the recovered cable had been taken into custody for further investigation, adding that efforts were ongoing to arrest the suspect’s alleged accomplices. In a related development, operatives attached to Dutse Division arrested two other suspects, identified as Ahmed Garba, 20, and Abdullahi Garba, 25, both residents of Jigawar Tsada town in Dutse Local Government Area. The duo were arrested at the Manpower Development Institute, Dutse, at about 3:00am on the same day. The statement alleged that the suspects conspired, trespassed into the institute’s premises and stole armoured cables. The three suspects are currently in police custody, with investigations ongoing to establish the circumstances surrounding the incidents and determine whether other individuals were involved. The command said the suspects would be arraigned before a court of competent jurisdiction upon the completion of investigations at the State Criminal Investigation Department (SCID) in Dutse. The Commissioner of Police, Jigawa State Command, CP Tijjani Murtala, reiterated the command’s commitment to protecting public infrastructure and combating vandalism and theft across the state. He urged members of the public to remain vigilant and promptly report suspicious activities to the nearest police station. The police advised residents to support security agencies in safeguarding public facilities and essential infrastructure against criminal activities.

body:

title: Moscow Eyes European Security Overhaul in Talks With US Envoys
body:
As expected, talks on ending Russia’s war against Ukraine have shifted to talks on a new division of Europe.
In his statement on 22 October, Putin said that future negotiations should determine guarantees for Russia as well as the broader rules of European security. According to him, it was Witkoff who proposed widening the agenda.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
Europeans are not yet being invited to the conversation about European security. Peskov specified that representatives of Ukraine, Russia and the US will meet in Abu Dhabi. He acknowledged that European countries cannot be left out going forward, but tied their participation to the position they take (whether they behave themselves).
Some Russian experts have a quite concrete picture of what the coming talks should cover. Valdai Club expert Stanislav Tkachenko speaks openly of a return to the demands of December 2021: limiting NATO’s military presence to pre-enlargement levels, removing new bases and military facilities from the Baltic states and Eastern Europe, and halting further enlargement. To this he adds recognition of territorial seizures, the lifting of sanctions and the return of frozen assets. His reasoning is that Moscow regards the European Union as a losing party as well, and therefore expects concessions from it too. Tkachenko even suggests new claims on Odesa, Mykolaiv and Kharkiv, arguing that Putin’s references to “historical territories” leave room for them.
At the same time, it is possible to negotiate and continue the war.
Dmitri Trenin, president of the Russian International Affairs Council, believes that freezing hostilities along the current front line does not suit Russia. Talking to the US is nevertheless worthwhile, since it is already producing some results. He notes that Moscow has agreed to discuss, first and foremost, the future post-war security system. The fighting itself, he predicts, may continue into 2027. He links the concrete terms of any agreement to the situation on the battlefield: talks can happen now, while decisions will depend on military outcomes.
Explanations for the case that negotiations once again lead nowhere are also already being prepared. Fyodor Lukyanov interprets the new Ukrainian proposals as Zelensky’s attempt to ease pressure from Trump. He suggests that Kyiv may walk away from agreements already reached, with the Europeans backing it. For that reason, in his view, Witkoff’s arrival with new ideas does not yet mean anything.
Meanwhile, Moscow is finding reasons to celebrate even before any deal. Duma deputy Oleg Matveychev considers it a success in itself that the US talks to Russia as an equal and discusses a wide range of global issues with it. A concrete outcome of the meeting is not even necessary for this assessment. He takes the comparison of a possible Putin–Trump–Xi meeting with “Yalta-2” as recognition of Russia’s special status: it is once again among the states that shape the future order.
Practical gains are added to the symbolic success. Duma deputy Leonid Slutsky calls the meeting with Witkoff a diplomatic “master class” by Putin and points to sanctions relief and the diesel deal with the US. For him, this is already evidence of a successful restoration of relations with Washington. He envisions further negotiations taking Russia’s interests fully into account.
Trump is also seen as a partner for exerting influence on Ukraine and Europe. Political commentator Gevorg Mirzayan suggests that Moscow and Washington are discussing a coordinated policy towards them. In his view, Trump wants to show voters a foreign-policy success, bring the Europeans back into greater obedience, and establish energy cooperation with Russia.
The rush ahead of the US elections is also viewed as an opportunity for Russia. Boris Mezhuev openly calls Trump an ally on the question of a settlement. He believes the US president needs a peace plan he can present to voters, even if it has not yet been signed. Russia can help him secure such a political result while advancing its own demands.
And yet there are still some in Moscow who remain dissatisfied, such as Dugin, Malofeev and Karaganov, united by a shared mental disorder: a passion for using nuclear weapons. In their latest interviews and publications, they openly call on Putin to use nuclear weapons against Ukraine and Europe.
Reprinted with the author’s permission from his X page. See the original here.
Anton Gerashchenko is a current official advisor and a former deputy minister at the Ukrainian Ministry of Internal Affairs. He is a former member of the Ukrainian parliament from 2014 to 2019.

title: Indonesia Pakistan Qatar Turkey Sign Defense Cooperation MoU
body:
Indonesia, Pakistan, Qatar and Turkey have signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) on defense cooperation under the Badr Project, an initiative to strengthen national defense capabilities and expand collaboration across their defense industries.
The agreement was signed on October 22 during a quadrilateral meeting in Doha, with Indonesia represented by Air Marshal Yusuf Jauhari, Deputy Minister of Defense for Logistics, Defense Industry and Technology.
The MoU establishes three main areas of cooperation: research and development and technology transfer; industrial collaboration and manufacturing; and human resource development. It also covers defense engineering, financing, investment, workforce training and supply-chain resilience.
Jauhari praised Qatar for facilitating the partnership, describing it as a commitment to mutual trust, equality, reciprocity and shared interests. He emphasized that cooperation would respect each country's sovereignty, national priorities and legal and regulatory frameworks.
The four countries described the agreement as a milestone in defense-industrial cooperation, with an emphasis on sustainable development and investment opportunities. However, the announcement did not specify project budgets, production targets, weapons systems or binding procurement commitments.
As an implementation measure, the parties agreed to hold periodic Defense Industry Meetings. After the first three months of implementation, the forum is expected to explore opportunities for extending defense cooperation to other partner countries.
The Badr Project's impact will depend on whether the four countries translate the framework into concrete technology-sharing agreements, investments and joint manufacturing projects.

title: Insults can’t stop growing rejection of your party, ADC replies APC
body: The Presidential Campaign Council of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) says no amount of insult can conceal the growing rejection that Nigerians have for the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC). Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Campaign Council, said this while reacting to a statement issued by Dele Alake, spokesman of the APC Campaign Council. Alake had accused former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, Presidential Candidate of the ADC, of spreading falsehood against the ruling party and its candidate in next year’s election. He also claimed that supporters of ADC were circulating a false document on the expenditure made for the kick-off of the APC Presidential Campaign in Kaduna. Kaduna Govt Debunks N2.3trn APC Campaign Spending Claim Bauchi guber: APM sues INEC, PRP, deputy candidate But Shaibu hit back at Alake, challenging him to produce evidence that the letter in circulation is fake. “Dele Alake’s statement, issued at dawn today, is a desperate and hollow smokescreen from a campaign terrified of its own record.” “He accuses Atiku Abubakar and the ADC of a “devious plan,” AI manipulation and deepfakes, yet offers no evidence linking them to the alleged letter or any fabricated video. This is the APC’s familiar script: make a reckless accusation, dress it up as certainty, then hope Nigerians stop asking questions. Alake should produce the evidence: names, dates and forensic findings. Until then, his “fake news alert” is an empty political stunt. “No conspiracy is needed to expose the APC. Its own failures are visible in every market, filling station and household. Petrol is around ₦1,400 a litre; diesel has topped ₦2,000; food inflation remains close to 20 per cent. More than half of Nigerians were living in poverty last year, according to the World Bank estimate reported by Reuters. These are the brutal consequences of an incompetent, callous and ruinous economic course. They are not fake news. “Bola calls the vehicle near an APC billboard a “routine patrol.” Nigerians can still ask why a campaign billboard needed protection. He can dismiss the images, but he cannot dismiss the reports of supporters brought in from distant states and left sleeping on Kaduna’s streets. More troubling still, reports have emerged of an accident involving APC supporters travelling from Sokoto and also from Abuja to the rally. Details remain unconfirmed, and the APC must urgently account for the passengers’ safety. “Making citizens endure long, hazardous journeys and sleep outdoors simply to create rally optics is political exploitation, not leadership. The APC cares more about the appearance of a crowd than the safety and dignity of the people it transports. “Perhaps this also explains why Tinubu is campaigning in only 12 states. The same supporters must be moved from one rally to the next, along roads his government has left in disrepair. Those journeys will consume meaningful time. Tinubu knows what happens if the crowd fails to reach the next destination: he may be left addressing empty seats—or, as the saying goes, talking to the birds. A campaign that must transport its audience from state to state cannot pass off that audience as spontaneous nationwide support. “You can hire buses, assemble a crowd and plaster the streets with billboards. You cannot hire consent. Nigerians have endured the APC’s punishing prices, shrinking incomes and broken promises. No parade, press statement or insult can conceal their growing rejection of this record. “The APC’s failures are sweeping, painful and indefensible. Its boastful promises have collapsed into a miserable reality of expensive food, unaffordable transport and families forced to make do with less. Alake’s attack on Atiku will not reduce the cost of a meal by one naira. “The real desperados are those clinging to power while the country burns. At the polls, Nigerians will reject this discredited record and defeat the APC. No volume of propaganda can talk the party out of the reckoning it has earned. Bola made life expensive; Atiku will make Nigeria affordable again!”

title: Zelensky Enacts Sanctions Targeting Russian Ballistics and Drones Makers
body:
President Volodymyr Zelensky has signed decrees enacting decisions by the National Security and Defense Council (NSDC) to impose sanctions on Russian entities and individuals involved in manufacturing ballistic missiles and supplying critical components to Moscow’s military-industrial complex, the Office of the President of Ukraine announced .
The statutory measures target Russian enterprises and executive leadership providing raw materials, specialized machine tools, precision optics, and electronic modules required to produce standoff strike systems – such as Iskander, Kalibr, Kh-101, and Kinzhal missiles – alongside military aviation, armored vehicles, and unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs).
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
“We are systematically identifying and imposing sanctions on enterprises involved in the production of Russian ballistic missiles and other strike weapons,” said Presidential Advisor and Commissioner for Sanctions Policy Vladyslav Vlasiuk.
“We are working to coordinate these sanctions with other international jurisdictions. Cumulatively, this should significantly degrade the Russian defense sector’s capacity to manufacture weapons.”
The primary sanctions list targets 51 individuals and 44 corporate entities directly linked to the development and serial production of Russian ballistic and cruise missiles deployed against Ukrainian civilian settlements and municipal life-support systems.
Key institutions designated under the presidential decrees include the Petrov Plastics Institute, identified as the sole manufacturer in Russia of specialized composite polymer components supplied to defense, aerospace, aviation, and naval shipyards.
The measures also target the Komet Corporation of Special Purpose Space Systems, the lead enterprise of a scientific and production consortium manufacturing surface-to-air missile systems, radar equipment, and airborne avionics suites, alongside VitaReaktiv, an industrial enterprise specializing in chemical raw materials integrated into ballistic missile propulsion systems and warheads.
Additional designations focus on research bodies and high-technology developers.
Among them are Promenergo, a defense contractor that develops optical, laser, and optoelectronic targeting systems alongside avionics testing facilities; the Kirov Biochemical Plant, engaged in the chemical synthesis and technical modernization of military armaments; and the Mendeleev All-Russian Research Institute of Metrology, a national scientific body that provides metrological research, precision measurement systems, and software architectures for military equipment.
A second decree enacts sanctions against an additional 32 Russian citizens and 35 commercial entities embedded in supply chains for precision machine tools, microelectronics, and tactical communication components.
The measures target Gagaring, a commercial enterprise specializing in communications hardware and flight controllers for first-person view (FPV) strike drones; Virgin-EK, which procures foreign electronic components for the Russian armed forces; and the Pressmash Machine Tool Association, a wholesale distributor of metalworking machinery that supplies factories producing Kh-101 and Kh-59 cruise missiles alongside Orion medium-altitude UAVs.
The sanctions package also designates corporate entities belonging to the Russian metals group RUSAL. According to Ukrainian government data, between April 2024 and March 2025, United Company RUSAL Trading House and the RUSAL Taishet Aluminum Smelter imported aluminum oxide valued at nearly 150 million rubles ($1.6 million) into Russia.
Ukrainian authorities confirmed that these raw materials were diverted into manufacturing pipelines for military aircraft, armored combat vehicles, missile systems, and loitering munitions.
The enactment of domestic sanctions follows recurring Russian ballistic missile barrages against Ukrainian regional infrastructure ahead of the winter season.
On Monday, Oct. 19, Russian forces launched 16 ballistic missiles at Kyiv and surrounding districts without advance radar notification, damaging over 10 energy facilities and cutting electricity to at least 550,000 households. The strike underscored operational risks amid conflicting accounts between Washington and Kyiv over early-warning missile tracking feeds.
President Zelensky previously stated that Ukraine receives roughly 12 Patriot PAC-2 and PAC-3 interceptors per month – approximately one-quarter of the volume delivered under the Biden administration – despite paid commitments through NATO’s Prioritized Ukraine Requirements List (PURL) and calculated domestic operational requirements of 350 interceptors monthly.
The Ukrainian sanctions push also unfolds amid transatlantic friction over economic deterrence. On Oct. 16, US President Donald Trump issued an executive order invoking Section 115 of the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 202 6 to waive mandatory statutory penalties , including 500 percent tariffs on Russian imports and 100 percent duties on third-party petroleum purchasers.
EU leaders expressed regret over the suspension of US energy penalties during their Brussels summit, pledging to maintain European sanctions and expand coordination with Kyiv to close secondary procurement loopholes underwriting Moscow’s defense manufacturing base.
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

title: Biden and Trump administrations earlier asked SpaceX to enable or disable Starlink – media
body:
The administrations of current U.S. President Donald Trump and his predecessor, Joseph Biden, on several occasions requested that Elon Musk’s company, SpaceX, enable or disable the Starlink satellite communication service in various countries—long before access was restricted for the Ukrainian military in October of this year. This is reported by Reuters, citing sources among former high-ranking U.S. officials who requested anonymity.
“During the presidency of Joe Biden, the requests included switching off the service to prevent Iranian proxy militias in Yemen and Lebanon from using Starlink to communicate, and activating the service to provide ‌internet access inside Iran and in Ukraine to support its military, said four of the former officials. Similarly, President Donald Trump's administration asked Musk, who is CEO of SpaceX, to make the service available in Iran following US-Israeli strikes in 2025 and 2026, in hopes it would bolster internet access and communications for anti-government protesters,” the message reads.
According to the publication’s sources, the Biden administration at times relied on Musk to help implement policy: Biden officials coordinated with SpaceX to thwart US adversaries by ​cutting the service, and to help allies by expanding Starlink’s availability. In their turn, they several times shared intelligence with SpaceX that indicated that the Houthis and Hezbollah were using diverted Starlink terminals — hardware that made its way to the militants through intermediaries. The administration contacted ​SpaceX and asked it to identify the ⁠terminals and shut them off. At least some of the terminals were deactivated.
Shortly after Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, officials in the Biden administration urged SpaceX to expand the Ukrainian armed forces' use of Starlink. At the same time, however, as noted in the report, Musk was already taking steps to limit Ukraine’s access to the Starlink network. Specifically, in 2022, he ordered SpaceX employees to restrict Starlink coverage in areas that Ukraine was attempting to liberate from Russian occupation—a move that came as a surprise to White House officials. Musk also publicly stated that he had rejected a request from Ukraine in 2022 to activate his satellite network in occupied Sevastopol.
In a 2024 submission to the US Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security, SpaceX said it works closely with US government agencies to secure export authorizations where required and to safeguard technology in support of US national security objectives and foreign policy goals.
Reuters reported that SpaceX did not respond to its requests for comment, although Musk noted in a social media post earlier this week that “Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the US government. Any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately (by the president of the United States).”
The publication emphasizes that the Biden-era and Trump requests to Musk show a close relationship in which US administrations rely to “an unprecedented degree on a private-sector company to help implement foreign policy.”
Earlier on Saturday, sources within the Ukrainian Ministry of Defense told Interfax-Ukraine that the Ukrainian Defense Forces and the Ministry had observed the restoration of Starlink—as well as its military version, Starshield—at speeds exceeding 161 km/h, following an outage that had lasted several days. Ukrainian Defense Minister Yevhen Khmara later reported that the terminals were observed functioning at speeds of over 400 km/h. "The connection is stable. This is yet another example of how direct dialogue and the persistent stance taken by the President of Ukraine at the highest level yield results. And this outcome is, above all, vital for our front line, for our military personnel, for the operation of drones, and for logistics and communications," he said.

title: Ukraine sanctions Russian arms suppliers as Moscow ramps up attacks
body:
President Volodymyr Zelensky imposed new sanctions on Russian citizens and companies helping produce ballistic missiles, aircraft, armored vehicles, and drones, the President’s Office announced on Oct. 24.
Included in the first sanctions list are 51 Russian citizens and 44 businesses producing and supplying raw materials, equipment, and tools used in long-range weapons like Iskander, Kalibr, Kh-101, and Kinzhal missiles.
A second sanctions list targets 32 Russian citizens and 35 companies involved in the production and supply chains of equipment and components used in Russia’s military-industrial complex.
"We are systematically identifying and imposing sanctions on enterprises involved in producing Russian ballistic missiles and other weapons. We are working to extend these sanctions to other jurisdictions," said Ukraine’s sanctions chief, Vladyslav Vlasiuk.
"Together, these measures should significantly weaken the Russian military-industrial complex's ability to produce weapons."
In particular, Ukraine targeted Russia's RUSAL Group, a key company involved in the production of military aircraft, armored vehicles, missile weapons, and drones. The company imported 150 million rubles ($1.8 million) worth of aluminum oxide between April 2024 and March 2025, which supplied Russia's military-industrial complex, the President's Office said.
The sanctions come as Russia ramps up its production of missiles and drones. Ukrainian intelligence (HUR) told Ukrainian media earlier this week that Russia produces some 10,000 drones per month and is currently stockpiling 700 ballistic missiles.
As Russia scales up arms production, attacks on Ukrainian cities, particularly Kyiv, have reached unprecedented levels. Civilian casualties are currently at levels not seen in over four years.
Last month, Russia killed at least 328 civilians and injured 2,105 — the deadliest September since the start of the full-scale invasion, and 85% higher than September 2025, the United Nations Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine reported on Oct. 15.

title: 2027: Jigawa APC unveils campaign structure, names Namadi chairman
body: ‎ By Muhammad Inuwa ,Dutse ‎ The All Progressives Congress (APC) in Jigawa State has unveiled its campaign structure for the 2027 general elections, appointing Governor Umar Namadi as chairman and former governors Ali Sa’adu Birnin Kudu and Ibrahim Saminu Turaki as deputy chairmen. ‎ The structure is designed to coordinate campaign activities, strengthen party structures and mobilise grassroots support across the state’s 27 local government areas ahead of the elections. ‎ The appointments were announced in a statement dated October 22, 2026, and signed by the state APC chairman, Hon. Ahmed Garba. ‎ According to the statement, the party’s State Working Committee approved the composition of the campaign council following consultations with party leaders and stakeholders across the state. ‎ The council has six vice chairmen representing the three senatorial districts, with two representatives from each zone to ensure broad participation and effective coordination of campaign activities. ‎ For Jigawa North-East, Senator Muhammad Ibrahim and Senator Ibrahim Hassan Hadejia were appointed Vice Chairmen I and II, respectively. ‎ In Jigawa South-West, the Speaker of the Jigawa State House of Assembly, Rt. Hon. Haruna Aliyu Dangyatin, and Hon. Farouk Adamu Aliyu were named Vice Chairmen I and II. ‎ Similarly, Alhaji Jisa Gerawa and Hajiya Rabi Ishaq were appointed Vice Chairmen I and II for Jigawa North-West Senatorial District. ‎ The party also named Alhaji Lawan Yau Roni as director-general of the campaign council, responsible for coordinating its day-to-day activities and implementing campaign programmes. ‎ The council is expected to provide strategic direction, coordinate campaign operations and strengthen engagement with party leaders, members and supporters ahead of the 2027 general elections. ‎ Garba urged members of the council, party leaders and supporters to demonstrate unity, discipline, loyalty and commitment to the party’s electoral objectives. ‎ He reaffirmed the APC’s commitment to progressive governance, democratic development and advancing the interests of the people of Jigawa State, while calling on members to work together towards the party’s success in the forthcoming elections. The post 2027: Jigawa APC unveils campaign structure, names Namadi chairman appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Agitation at Bimbilla NDC elections as police arrest delegates over ballot photos
body: Police have arrested some delegates at the Bimbilla constituency election centre for allegedly photographing their ballot papers during the National Democratic Congress (NDC) constituency elections. The arrests triggered agitation at the polling centre as officers moved to prevent delegates from taking photographs of their votes. The incident occurred as delegates voted to elect constituency executives for the governing party, raising concerns about maintaining order and calm during the exercise. A total of 60 aspirants are contesting 17 executive positions in Bimbilla, with 1,764 delegates expected to cast their ballots. The Bimbilla elections form part of the NDC’s nationwide constituency polls scheduled for October 24 and 25, 2026, across the party’s 276 constituencies.

title: Kaduna Govt Debunks N2.3trn APC Campaign Spending Claim
body: The Kaduna State Government has debunked claims that Governor Uba Sani approved and released N2.3 trillion for the flag-off of the All Progressives Congress (APC) 2027 presidential campaign in the state. The government described a letter circulating on social media, which allegedly indicated the approval, as fake, saying the governor neither authored nor authorised the document. The Commissioner for Information and Culture, Malam Ahmed Maiyaki, stated this in a statement issued on Saturday in Kaduna. He said the purported letter, dated October 18, 2026, and titled “Notification for Preparations for the Grand Rally Flag Off,” falsely claimed that the governor released N2.3 trillion for the APC presidential campaign flag-off scheduled for Saturday, October 24. Remi Tinubu: I Want To Leave Aso Rock In 2031 Bauchi guber: APM sues INEC, PRP, deputy candidate The letter was allegedly addressed to Senator Abdulazeez Yari, Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council. Maiyaki said the claim was not only false but financially implausible, considering that the entire 2026 Kaduna State budget stood at N985.92 billion. He said the alleged campaign expenditure was more than twice the state’s annual budget and was not supported by any authentic appropriation, approval or expenditure records. “The Kaduna State Government categorically disowns this document. Governor Uba Sani neither authored nor authorised the purported letter, and no N2.3 trillion was budgeted, approved or released for the presidential campaign flag-off,” the commissioner said. He described the allegation as fictitious and a deliberate attempt to mislead the public. Maiyaki also identified inconsistencies in the purported letter, including the misspelling of the governor’s surname as “Uba Sai” and discrepancies in its presentation. He further raised concerns over the apparent unauthorised reproduction of the governor’s signature, saying the irregularities cast doubt on the document’s credibility. The commissioner said the administration had remained committed to fiscal discipline, transparency, accountability and prudent management of public resources since Governor Uba Sani assumed office on May 29, 2023. He listed investments in security, infrastructure, education, healthcare, agriculture and social protection as priorities of the administration. According to him, the government’s financial management approach is reflected in its infrastructure programme, increased agricultural investment, rehabilitation of public institutions, settlement of inherited pension liabilities and expansion of social protection interventions. Maiyaki expressed concern over what he described as an emerging pattern of misinformation aimed at discrediting the governor and his administration ahead of the 2027 general elections. He warned that the fabrication of official correspondence and circulation of false financial claims could attract criminal sanctions. “Political competition must be conducted within the bounds of truth, decency and the law. The fabrication of government correspondence and circulation of false financial claims cannot be justified as legitimate political criticism. “Those seeking to hold government accountable must do so through credible evidence, not manufactured documents,” he said. The commissioner disclosed that the government was taking steps to establish the origin of the purported letter. He called on security and investigative agencies to examine the document and ensure that anyone found culpable in forgery or impersonation was brought to justice in accordance with the law. Maiyaki also urged media organisations and members of the public to exercise caution in circulating unverified documents, stressing that allegations concerning public expenditure should be properly scrutinised before publication. He reaffirmed the administration’s commitment to peace, strengthening public institutions, infrastructure development and improving the welfare of citizens, saying the government would not be distracted from its focus on prudent financial management and sustainable development.

title: Jigawa govt denies giving houses to Kannywood actors
body: ‎ ‎By Muhammad Inuwa, Dutse ‎ ‎Jigawa State Government has dismissed allegations that it allocated houses in the Danmodi Housing Estate in Ringim to popular APC musician Dauda Kahutu Rarara and members of the Triple R group. ‎ ‎Dady Ringim, a new media aide to Governor Umar Namadi, described the allegation as false and lacking factual basis while reacting to the controversy on social media. ‎ ‎The controversy followed a viral video in which Rarara and members of Triple R allegedly claimed that the governor had allocated houses to them”. The video has triggered reactions from opposition figures and other social media users in the state. ‎Among those who criticised the alleged allocation was Zakari Kafin Hausa, a former aide to Governor Namadi and a prominent critic of his administration and ADC Candidate for Auyo/Kafin Hausa House of Representatives in the 2027 election. ‎ ‎In his Facebook post, Kafin Hausa questioned the reported allocation of the houses, particularly as the housing project was allegedly financed with public funds. ‎ ‎ “There are certain decisions taken by this administration that I am wondering whether it is the Umar Namadi we have always known making them or he has been replaced with ‘Jibrin from Sudan.’” ‎ ‎He also questioned why public housing projects should be allocated in such a manner. ‎ ‎However, reacting to the criticism, Ringim accused Kafin Hausa of overlooking the governor’s achievements, arguing that Namadi’s projects and policies were strengthening his popularity and re-election prospects. According to him, “The Triple R statement does not mean the Governor has gift them Houses, they are trying to establish the fact that the Governor has constructed the affordable Housing Estate for the People of the state. “The Danmodi Housing Estate was constructed across the whole 27 Local Government of the state and are available for the citizens whoever meet the requirements” he said. “What they are doing are doing it to advertise the good work of Governor Umar Namadi, not only Housing Estate including Tsangaya, Roads, Health, Agriculture among other.” ‎He said the governor’s achievements were making a lasting impression on the people, adding that “politics is not built on rhetoric alone; it requires action and the trust of the people.” ‎ ‎Ringim expressed confidence that voters would determine the state’s political future, insisting that the administration’s performance was helping to build a lasting legacy, particularly among young people. ‎ ‎He urged political actors to verify information before making public allegations, warning that political differences should not be allowed to encourage the spread of misinformation. ‎ ‎The controversy has generated debate on social media over the alleged allocation of the houses and the management of publicly funded housing projects in Jigawa State. The post Jigawa govt denies giving houses to Kannywood actors appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: 7 dead, 40 wounded after gunmen open fire at funeral in Jordan
body:
JERUSALEM (AP) — Gunmen opened fire during a funeral at a church in Jordan on Friday, killing seven people and wounding 40 others, authorities said.
The shooting took place at a Greek Orthodox church in Karak, about 90 kilometers (55 miles) south of the capital, Amman.
Footage broadcast on Jordanian state television showed two gunmen who appear to be holding pistols approaching the church and firing shots. A third man who appears to be holding a semiautomatic rifle then approaches and opens fire, and all three then run toward the church.
Video footage taken by witnesses shows broken glass and pools of blood on the floor of the church.
Dorgham Halasa, who was among the mourners inside the church, said intense gunfire erupted 15 minutes after the funeral had started, and then people started running. “It was a weird situation, and heavy gunfire,” Halasa said.
He did not see the gunmen, but said other people reported seeing four of them. The Associated Press could not independently verify the number of assailants, and Jordan’s security services did not immediately release details.
A government statement said that the attack was “carried out by unknown assailants,” but didn’t say whether any gunmen were captured or killed. It said that “investigations are underway at full speed.”
Jordan declared three days of national mourning, according to the kingdom’s Petra News Agency.
Karak is home to a minority Christian population.
In 2016, gunmen ambushed police in a series of attacks in Karak, including at a Crusader castle popular with tourists, killing 10 people, including seven officers, and wounding dozens. Jordanian security forces killed those gunmen after a long standoff.
Jordan’s Health Minister Ibrahim al-Budour said two of those wounded are in critical condition.
King Abdullah II said on X that Jordan “will confront the terrorist act that targeted Karak with the harshest penalties” and offered his “deepest condolences to the families of the martyrs, and our wishes for recovery to the wounded.”
Jordan’s Prime Minister Jafar Hassan said during a security meeting in Karak on Friday evening that the attack was a result of terrorist ideology and blind extremism. He said the assailants will be punished and legal measures taken against those who seek to introduce extremism.
Condemnation of the slayings came from around the region, including from Lebanon, Syria, Egypt and Oman.
Ahmed al-Tayeb in Cairo, the grand imam of Al-Azhar, the Sunni Muslim world’s foremost religious institution, offered his condolences to the families of victims in Friday’s shooting, calling it a “heinous terrorist attack.”
Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein called his Jordanian counterpart and “affirmed Iraq’s solidarity with Jordan in the face of terrorism,” Hussein’s office said in a statement.
U.N. Secretary-General Antonio Guterres condemned the attack during a funeral as “especially heinous,” spokesman Stephane Dujarric said. “The secretary-general also calls for all those responsible to be found and to be held to account.”

title: Pezeshkian stresses moving beyond ‘neither war nor peace’
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 24 (MNA) – Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian has emphasized that the country must move beyond the situation of "neither war nor peace" so that his administration can plan within a transparent and predictable atmosphere.
He made the remarks at the venue of Plan and Budget Organization (PBO) on Saturday during a ceremony of Population and Housing Census in 2026.
To begin with his speech, Pezeshkian commemorated the name and memory of founder of the Islamic Revolution Imam Khomeini (RA), martyred Leader of the Islamic Revolution Ayatollah Seyyed Ali Khamenei, and those who were killed by the terrorist US and criminal Zionist regime during the 12-, and 40-day wars imposed against the country, highlighting, “Effective steps must be taken to move the country beyond ‘neither war not peace’.
Pezeshkian described the utilization of modern, smart knowledge and technologies as essential for service delivery and the prevention of disputes and conflicts, emphasizing that by making service delivery "smart," potential violations can be preempted in a timely manner.
The Iranian president described the register-based census as an effective measure for intelligent management, oversight, and evaluation—grounded in the principles of justice and fairness, noting, "This is a significant and valuable undertaking. Move forward with determination, and by collecting accurate data, lay the groundwork for the realization of justice throughout the country. In this way, the cost-effectiveness of operational plans can be enhanced, and productivity increased."

title: HMS Protector towed home after propulsion defects
body: The Royal Navy’s ice patrol ship HMS Protector could not sail from Teesside to Devonport under her own power this month because of propulsion defects, and was towed instead so that engineers can work out what to do with her, according to an answer given in Parliament. Ben Obese-Jecty, the Conservative member for Huntingdon, asked why the ship was unable to make the passage. Luke Pollard, Minister of State for Defence Readiness and Industry, said: “HMS Protector was unable to sail to Devonport under her own power due to propulsion defects. She has been towed to Devonport to enable further technical work to determine the most effective future course of action for the ship.” Answering a second question from Obese-Jecty on why the ship missed the Antarctic season, Pollard said: “HMS Protector did not deploy to the 2025 to 2026 southern summer season due to undergoing a period of prolonged essential and mandatory maintenance to ensure the viability of the vessel into the future.” Protector is the Royal Navy’s only ice patrol ship and carries out the United Kingdom’s survey and inspection commitments in the Antarctic under the Antarctic Treaty. She was bought in 2011, originally built as the Norwegian vessel Polarbjørn, and was taken on initially as a short-term replacement for HMS Endurance, which was crippled by flooding in 2008 and never returned to service. The post HMS Protector towed home after propulsion defects first appeared on UK Defence Journal .

title: It’s time to find a new browser
body:
Hi, friends! Welcome to Installer No. 149, your guide to the best and Verge-iest stuff in the world. (If you’re new here, welcome, happy It Actually Feels Like Fall Now At Least In My Neighborhood), and also you can read all the old editions at the Installer homepage.)
This week, I’ve been reading about Demis Hassabis and computer chips and permafrost, enjoying the first episodes of Machine Gods, filming the next season of Version History (pet season!), seeing You Can See Everything and then reading and listening to absolutely everything about it, painstakingly updating all the stuff in my 1Password, making tiny documents with Tiny Little Office, watching Conan O’Brien own Subway Takes the way he once owned Hot Ones, finally getting properly good at CapCut, and blasting the soundtrack to The Mandalorian and Grogu all workday long.
I also have for you a new AI assistant, the most Duo-y new app for the iPhone Duo, my hunt for the next great browser, and much more. Let’s do this.
(As always, the best part of Installer is your ideas and tips. What are you playing / reading / watching / listening to / modding with Claude this week? Tell me everything: installer@theverge.com. And if you know someone else who might enjoy Installer, forward it to them and tell them to subscribe here.)
The Drop
* Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4. Obviously, Grand Theft Auto VI is the biggest game release of the year, but a new COD is always a big deal. This one doesn’t sound like some grand reinvention of the form, but rather an even more playable, even more powerful version of what works. I was particularly excited to hear that the campaign mode is a huge improvement this time.
* The Blink Mini 4K. Ring cameras get a lot more shine, but Amazon’s cheaper brand also makes some pretty good stuff. This one’s part of a whole new lineup of devices, but $80 for a 4K camera with two-way audio and plenty of smart security features? Not a bad deal.
* JustWatch TV. As streaming services get incessantly more expensive, I’m starting to bail on some paid services and spend more time on the free ones. JustWatch’s new service is surprisingly well-stocked out of the gate — I suspect they’ve been watching what people search for, and making some smart content bets.
* Claude Duet. Here’s Anthropic’s answer to Muse, Instinct, and Dots. Duet seems to be focused on helping you get stuff done at work by making to-do lists, coordinating meetings, and compiling data for you. Still waitlist-only right now, but it’ll be interesting to see if it’s as thirsty for attention as Muse is.
* Wildwood. Before you see this gorgeous, by all accounts excellent stop-motion movie, read everything you can about how it was made. Not a pixel of generative AI in sight, just an unbelievable amount of hard work and human creativity. Humans rock, artists rock, this movie rocks.
* The Teenage Engineering EP-35. When you go to buy this thing, it’s technically called “Life is fantastic!” Which, sure. This thing is a battery powered, multi-input, multi-instrument amp with lots of effects. As always, it is extremely cool-looking. I have no use for it, and I want it quite badly.
* Nintendo Switch Sports Resort. Nintendo basically hasn’t changed the formula here since Wii Sports from two decades ago, and I have absolutely no problem with that. Anything that gives me that super-active tennis and bowling (plus volleyball, boxing, thumb wrestling, and more) is a win in my book.
* Delta 2.0. The next couple of weeks are going to be full of interesting app updates as developers try to figure out what to make of Apple’s foldable phone. But one of the best is already available; Delta can now pretty successfully cosplay as any handheld console ever. (Plus the Sega Genesis!)
* Kindle Plus. This is mostly just a rebranding of Kindle Unlimited, but Amazon put a couple of interesting new features in its $12 monthly reading subscription, including AI-narrated audiobooks. I am dubious of those, but excited about expanding access to audiobooks. We’ll see.
Spotlight
The worst news of the week here in the Installerverse is that Arc is going away. This was obviously coming: The Browser Company bailed on Arc two years ago in favor of the more AI-centric Dia, and Arc has been in maintenance mode ever since. But now it’s not just being ignored, it’s going away. By Christmas, you won’t even be able to use the app anymore.
So now a lot of us are stuck looking for another browser. There are a million new ones out there, many of them somewhere between “heavily inspired by Arc” and “a direct copy of Arc I made in Codex this morning.” I need to test a lot of them. I don’t know exactly where I’ll land yet, but I figured I’d share a bunch of the ones I’m looking at:
* Dia. It has recently gotten a lot of Arc’s best features, and some of the AI stuff is pretty cool. (And mercifully easy to turn off.) The Browser Company’s attention to aesthetic detail remains the best in the biz, so I’m starting here.
* Zen. A total ripoff of Arc, and I mean that as a compliment. Zen runs on Mozilla’s Gecko engine rather than Chromium, which is a win for anyone looking for a little less Google influence in their lives. Last time I tried Zen it was a little buggy and unpolished, but I’ve heard it’s come a long way.
* Orion. I am a dedicated and very happy Kagi user, and I’ve heard good things about how simple and resource-friendly the company’s browser is. Given the seamless Kagi integration, I sort of hope this one wins for me.
* Vivaldi. I used Vivaldi for a while, and I love how customizable it is. I eventually got it set up exactly the way I wanted it. But right next to all that customization is just a feeling of fiddliness, and I couldn’t quite get comfortable in the browser. Might try again.
* Helium. The opposite of Vivaldi, this is a super minimalist, no-frills browser. It’s probably what I need, honestly.
* Firefox. Its confusing stance on AI aside, I like a lot of the recent design and feature choices Firefox has made. I’m also intrigued by some of the Firefox forks, like Waterfox and Floorp, which give it even more customization options.
* Brave. Brave has always felt too heavy to me, and like it’s always trying to convince me to use more of its own proprietary (and often underpowered) features. But it seems to always win in privacy comparisons, so I might need to give it a go again.
On mobile, it’s easy. Quiche is my favorite iOS browser by a mile. Arc was never great on Android, so I’m betting most of us never switched there in the first place.
There are also the default browsers, of course, like Chrome, Safari, and Edge. But each of those browsers continues to fail me in one way or another, and so my search continues. If you’ve found your browser of the future, tell me all about it! Otherwise, I’ll report back here periodically through my journey.
Crowdsourced
Here’s what the Installer community is into this week. I want to know what you’re into right now as well! Email installer@theverge.com or message me on Signal — @davidpierce.11 — with your recommendations for anything and everything, and we’ll feature some of our favorites here every week. For even more great recommendations, check out the replies to this post on Threads and this post on Bluesky.
“Youth is an absolute SCREAM on HBO Max at the moment.” — Jonathan
“Todoist has a stellar integration with Siri AI that has finally made me fully commit to just using it If you delete Reminders, Todoist becomes the default on Siri AI and you can add a to-do to any project with tag AND location support (using Apple Maps saved locations like home and work!). The best part is that it all works WITHOUT having to say ‘... in todoist’ at the end of each query!” — Sajishnu
“Apple added Sound Glow to existing HomePod models and it’s just kinda fun to watch the light on top of HomePod glow and flash. So I’m doing that with some of my favorite playlists.” — Connor
“I’m reading a book called How to Read a Book by Mortimer J. Adler because I want to get better at analysis and reading for understanding vs. absorbing basic information.” — Rhoades
“My girlfriend took a train ride up the west coast and reported that no less than four different people asked her if her 2024 Samsung Galaxy Z-Flip 6 was the new iPhone Duo.” — Nicholas
“I recently read Bodies of Magic by Freya Marske, and it was excellent. What if med school was magical, but everyone was still sleeping with each other and stressing over student loans? Then an unexpected dead body shows up during finals.” — Emmett
“I got a Framework Laptop 13 Pro running Ubuntu last month, and I’m really happy with it. (I haven’t done anything with Linux in maybe 20 years — it’s come a long way!) So now I’m trying to see if I can replace Capture One with Darktable. If I can, that would break my last tie to macOS, and I’ll replace my iMac with a Framework Desktop.” — Morgan
“Exploring the new Nektropos Castle dungeon in EverQuest Legends. The game has been such a nostalgia trip back to 1999, but new content in an ancient game is a bizarre delight.” — Alex
“Setting up Navidrome and having Claude build me a definitive ‘Songs From the Black Hole’ playlist from my Weezer MP3 collection. (It’s harder than first appears: is ‘Lisa’ track 12 or not!?)” — Micheal
“Best Buy had a pretty insane deal on a Bambu A1 Mini, so we got my 12 year old son a 3D printer for his birthday. It’s amazing how easy it was to put out a seemingly perfectly accurate PLA print, compared to horror stories from older printers.” — Jeff
Signing off
Last week, my wife and I went car shopping. Our plan was just to drive a bunch of cars — we knew we needed something with three rows, and really had no experience with any of them — and then go home. Somehow, a few hours later, we were the proud and slightly bewildered owners of a new Kia Carnival.
So far the car has been great, but wow are there a lot of weird tech ideas in cars now. I’m good with CarPlay and Android Auto. I hate how much everything has become a touchscreen. But I’m most thrown by how many features of my car now exist in a companion app. How do we feel about this? I almost miss when I had no idea what to do about the check engine light.
Anyway, I’m a minivan dad now. I think I’m okay with it. Send car tips! Send minivan tips! Send help! See you next week!

title: Laika has spent 20 years building up to Wildwood
body:
Across several decades in Hollywood, Caleb Deschanel has seen a lot. He served as cinematographer on films like The Passion of the Christ and The Patriot, worked on sequences in The Godfather and Titanic, and directed a few episodes of Twin Peaks. Even still, nothing could quite prepare him for his first stop-motion project: working as the cinematographer on Wildwood, the latest release from Coraline studio Laika. While he knew that stop-motion was a long and involved process, he was still surprised by just how much work went into these movies. “When I started I thought it was one thing, and then I quickly found out that it was another thing,” Deschanel says. “It was much more complicated than I expected.”
Wildwood has been a long time coming. Laika CEO Travis Knight originally optioned the rights for the book of the same name, written by Decemberists frontman Colin Meloy, in 2011. But production didn’t begin until a decade later. “I’ve been working on it in some form or another for 16 years,” Knight, who also directed Wildwood, says. “The reason why I stuck with it, the reason why I had to make this movie no matter what, is because of what it meant to me personally. Underneath it all, it’s a story about love and loss and grief, it’s about the impossible things that love asks of us, and that meant something to me personally in a very profound way.”
It’s also the biggest production Laika has ever undertaken. Wildwood tells the story of a young girl named Prue who has to venture into the “impassable wilderness” that surrounds Portland in order to find her baby brother. When she enters the forest she discovers a fantasy realm reminiscent of Narnia, with magical spells, talking animals, and warring factions. It required nearly 50 animators and more than 200 puppets to pull it off, and the film is full of ambitious sequences, like a 12-minute battle with dozens of soldiers and a chase scene through a bustling Portland, where Prue’s brother is carried away by a gigantic murder of crows.
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/26848892-9741-11f1-ad63-72f37b66ec04_wwd.bts_.00083.rgb_.approved-copy.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/f9a99bb0-9744-11f1-a125-ce84cd5b2caf_wwd.bts_.00326.rgb_.approved-copy.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
According to head of animation Brad Schiff, the studio’s ethos involves mixing “old-school craft with modern technology.” With each project, he says, Laika develops new techniques. If something works well, they then push the idea even further on the next project. For instance, on Laika’s previous film, Missing Link, the main character was outfitted with a diaphragm so that when an animator turned a screw on the puppet’s back, the diaphragm could expand or contract, creating the illusion that it was breathing. This has since become the standard for puppets in Laika’s films.
These may sound like small details, but over the years they add up. For costume designer Deb Cook, there wasn’t a single innovation on Wildwood that stood out to her, but rather the sheer number of tools she had at her disposal. “Over time we’ve gathered together a library of techniques that we’ve been able to put into practice on this movie,” she says. This was especially important on Wildwood, which features a huge range of costumes; in the city sequences everyone is dressed in modern clothing, whereas in the forest characters have more fantastical looks.
For Wildwood, many of the advancements came down to materials. The costumes made use of more flexible fabrics, for example, and the team also engineered a new process for creating silicone that’s lighter and more durable than what they previously used. “We’ve done this so we can wean ourselves off of foam latex, which is stinky and it shrinks over time, and five years later it kind of just crumbles,” says Oliver Jones, head of characters and practical effects. “There are advantages to rethinking a lot of these materials that were our go-to probably since King Kong.”
The scale of Wildwood has also forced the studio to adopt another seemingly much more boring practice: being better organized. “They’ve been misplaced,” Cook says, when asked if she’s ever lost a puppet. “There’s now a very sophisticated tracking system because there are so many moving parts, and so many stages around the studio.”
And while much has been said about the large and elaborate sequences in the film — Knight says the epic battle scene is “probably the most technically challenging thing that we’ve ever done” — all of these techniques are designed to imbue more humanity into characters that are portrayed by puppets. In that regard, small details like the flow of fabric or the impression of breathing are vitally important.
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/2f80b4c0-9741-11f1-9111-de501831d785_wwd.bts_.00093.rgb_.approved-copy.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/1acddd60-9745-11f1-99f0-f61ab3b9ac56_wwd.bts_.00350.rgb_.approved-copy.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
“We also have really subtle and intimate scenes, quiet scenes that don’t have a lot of flash, that have virtually no sound design or music, where the only thing that you’re experiencing is the grief of a father talking about a secret that he’s been holding on to for 15 years, or a quiet moment of a woman grieving the loss of her son,” Knight explains. “These are moments where you have nowhere to hide and the performances of these little puppets — these little assemblages of steel and silicon and fabric that have no life of their own — completely spring to life because of the hand and the artistry of the human behind it. Those are the moments that I’m most proud of.”
In this way, the long road to Wildwood hitting theaters makes a lot of sense. Laika has been around for just over 20 years, and over the course of each film the studio has innovated to steadily push its craft forward. Knight may have been thinking about the film for 16 years, but creating the version that is coming out in 2026 wouldn’t have been possible without all of the learnings spread across films like ParaNorman and Kubo and the Two Strings.
For Knight, it’s been especially gratifying to bring it to life with a team of both Laika veterans and newcomers, including not only Deschanel but also a handful of young animators for whom Wildwood was their first feature film project. Some were young enough that Coraline, Laika’s very first film, was what inspired them to get into the field in the first place. “I was really moved by that,” says Knight. “It also made me feel old as shit.”
Wildwood is in theaters now.

title: Perspective: The next James Bond
body:
Scottish actor Sean Connery on location in Amsterdam for James Bond film 'Diamonds are Forever.' Jack Kay/Getty Images/Hulton Archive hide caption
This weekend, perhaps even as we speak, auditions are being held in London to cast the next Bond.
Deadline reports that at least three actors will be screen tested: Jack Lowden, Josh O' Connor, and Callum Turner, who are all fine, experienced British actors and...how do I say this? Hunks.
The Bond selected by Amazon MGM Studios will succeed Daniel Craig, who has owned the role since Casino Royale in 2006, following a parade of other fine, hunky British actors stretching way back to Sean Connery, who starred in Dr. No in 1962.
The literary Bond — a name poached from Dr. James Bond, an American ornithologist who wrote the field guide, Birds of the West Indies , when author Ian Fleming was living in Jamaica — was a Cold War creation. Fleming wrote Casino Royale in 1953, when Great Britain was feeling diminished. Brits had won World War II, with pluck and skill, but were losing their empire. British agents (Guy Burgess, Kim Philby) kept slipping out to Moscow with official secrets before British intelligence could discover they were spies.
It was all damaging to Britain, and embarrassing. But then James Bond strode into the pages of popular culture, dapper and deft. The Soviets and their allies might have sophisticated weaponry and boundless barbarity. But did they drink their martinis shaken, or stirred?
The great espionage novels of Graham Greene and John LeCarre depicted spycraft as a grimy, compromising business. But Fleming's 007, and the onscreen Bonds who played out those stories, dispatched danger in exotic locales, and without rumpling the pleats on their dinner jackets.
Of course ogres and adversaries can shift shapes over decades. I find myself more curious about what forces will next threaten the world when James Bond, whoever plays him, returns to film. So many devices can now listen to, watch, and track our lives second by second, and feed us information they hope will steer our opinions. It may make you think of a line in Dr. No , where Bond tells the scientist who believes he can control the world with his inventions, "Our asylums are full of people who think they're Napoleon. Or God."
