title: ₦278m Paid To Retired Judges, Kogi Pension Commission Replies Adebayo
body: The Kogi State Pension Commission has disclosed that ₦278.07 million has been paid to 15 retired judicial officers who are yet to receive their full gratuity entitlements, while challenging allegations concerning the handling of retirement benefits in the state. The Commission, in a press statement issued on Saturday and signed by its Director-General, Hajia Mariam Ozioma Abedo, said the payments were made from January to date in line with verified entitlements and available government resources. The statement was a response to a publication dated October 23, 2026, attributed to Mutalubi Ojo Adebayo, a Senior Advocate of Nigeria and former Attorney-General of Oyo State, concerning the retirement entitlements of retired judicial officers in Kogi State. While affirming the right of citizens and legal practitioners to demand accountability and advocate the payment of legitimate retirement benefits, the Commission faulted what it described as offensive language, sweeping allegations and personal attacks against Governor Ahmed Usman Ododo, his predecessor, Alhaji Yahaya Bello, and other public officials. The Commission maintained that legitimate retirement benefits are obligations of government and that the administration recognises the contributions of retired judicial officers to the administration of justice and the protection of citizens’ rights. It said outstanding gratuity balances should not be interpreted as evidence that the government is hostile to the judiciary or unwilling to fulfil its obligations. “The rank of Senior Advocate of Nigeria is a mark of professional distinction that carries commensurate responsibilities. It is no licence to insult public office holders, speculate about their motives or substitute provocative language for verifiable evidence,” the statement said. The Commission urged Adebayo to identify any specific beneficiary or category of entitlement he believes has been wrongly handled and seek clarification from the appropriate authorities. It explained that the state government must balance its obligations to retirees with the funding of salaries, pensions, roads, schools, hospitals, security and other essential public services. The statement also rejected descriptions allegedly used against Governor Ododo, including “puppet”, “effigy”, “pawn”, “toy” and “breastfeeding” Governor, arguing that such expressions do not establish whether any retirement entitlement has been wrongly withheld or any payment decision improperly influenced. On the allegation that former Governor Yahaya Bello controls the incumbent Governor and would prevent the payment of judicial officers’ entitlements, the Commission challenged Mr. Adebayo to provide credible evidence. “If Mr. Adebayo possesses credible evidence that a particular payment decision has been improperly influenced, he should identify that evidence and present it through the appropriate channels. Serious allegations demand serious evidence,” the statement added. The Commission stressed that Governor Ododo’s administration remains open to legitimate public scrutiny but insisted that criticism should be grounded in verifiable facts and reasoned arguments. It called on Adebayo to withdraw the alleged abusive descriptions and unsupported personal allegations against Governor Ododo and former Governor Yahaya Bello within 24 hours of the publication of its rejoinder, publish an unequivocal apology through the same channels used to circulate the original publication, and correct the categorical assertion that no payments had been made to retired judicial officers. The Commission warned that failure to comply within the stipulated period would prompt it to submit formal petitions against Adebayo to the Legal Practitioners Disciplinary Committee and the Legal Practitioners Privileges Committee for consideration. It said the language and personal allegations in the publication raised concerns about the standards of restraint, dignity and professional responsibility expected of a legal practitioner, particularly one who has attained the rank of Senior Advocate of Nigeria. The Commission reaffirmed its commitment to engaging with retired judicial officers and other pensioners over their verified entitlements, adding that the government would continue to pursue its obligations through responsible administration, proper financial management and constructive engagement. “The public deserves accurate information. Retired judicial officers deserve dignity and the settlement of their legitimate entitlements. Public discourse deserves the discipline of evidence, the strength of reasoned argument and respect for the responsibilities that accompany professional distinction,” the statement concluded. The post ₦278m Paid To Retired Judges, Kogi Pension Commission Replies Adebayo appeared first on Channels Television .

title: First U.S. Navy Destroyer Enters Phase Two of DDG MOD 2.0 Modernization
body: USS Pinckney becomes the first U.S. Navy destroyer to enter Phase Two of the DDG MOD 2.0 program, adding advanced SPY-6 radars to counter growing global threats. San Diego-based USS Pinckney (DDG 91) began its second phase of DDG MOD 2.0 at a General Dynamics NASSCO drydock following its eight-and-a-half month deployment to the Middle East and Pacific, setting up the first of a series of ships slated to receive Raytheon’s AN/SPY-6(V)4 radars and associated equipment. During its deployment Pinckney proved a number of advanced warfare capabilities, according to the U.S. Navy. The work, part of a $149.6 million contract awarded to General Dynamics, is expected to wrap up by September 2028. “ The collective effort by all stakeholders has finally brought us to the point of execution. Upon Depot Modernization Period completion, USS Pinckney will rejoin the Fleet equipped with the most comprehensive multi-spectral integrated sensor suite designed to maintain maritime superiority for decades to come ,” said Capt. Tim Moore, program manager, DDG MOD 2.0 in a media release . DDG MOD 2.0 is one of the U.S. Navy’s major modernization efforts for Arleigh Burke-class guided missile destroyers, equipping a series of four ships with the distinct-looking SLQ-32(V)7 Surface Electronic Warfare Improvement Program (SEWIP) Block III in phase one, prior to a later refit with the new radars. The ships are also being upgraded with Lockheed Martin’s Aegis Baseline 10, a core component of the radar upgrade that will enable simultaneous air and ballistic missile defense. USS Pinckney (DDG 91), USS Chung-Hoon (DDG 93), USS James E. Williams (DDG 95), and USS Halsey (DDG 97) have all already completed major milestones or Depot Modernization Periods under the program. USS Chung-Hoon (DDG-93) departs Naval Base San Diego for sea trials on April 20 after completing its Depot Modernization Period as part of the DDG Modernization 2.0 program, which focuses on vital mid-life capability enhancements. (Courtesy Photo) These four ships are serving as a trial for future MOD 2.0 installations that will eventually combine both upgrades into a single shipyard availability, starting with USS Sterett (DDG 104), according to Moore. The shift to a single modernization period is intended to reduce the amount of time destroyers spend out of service for major upgrades, allowing the Navy to install both the electronic warfare suite and new radar during the same shipyard availability rather than requiring ships to return for a second round of work. The upgrades come as the Navy faces growing demands on its surface fleet, particularly in the Indo-Pacific and Middle East, where destroyers have increasingly been tasked with defending carrier strike groups, commercial shipping and other naval assets against increasingly sophisticated missile and drone threats. Recent combat operations in the Middle East have severely tested these defenses against unique anti-ship weapons, including one instance where a drone came within a mile of striking a deployed ship off the coast of Israel . The post First U.S. Navy Destroyer Enters Phase Two of DDG MOD 2.0 Modernization appeared first on Naval News .

title: Russia Says Drone Attack Damages Tolyatti Facilities, Ukraine Says Petrochemical Plant Hit
body:
Several industrial facilities were damaged in a drone attack on the Russia n city of Tolyatti on Saturday, local authorities said, while Ukraine said it had struck a major petrochemical plant there.
Togliatti Mayor Ilya Sukhikh said preliminary reports indicated no fatalities or injuries. He did not specify which facilities had been hit.
Ukraine's General Staff said it had struck the Tolyattikauchuk petrochemical plant, one of Russia 's largest producers of synthetic rubber.
The General Staff also reported a strike on the Proton electronics plant in Russia 's Oryol region, which Kyiv says manufactures components for cruise and ballistic missiles.
Oryol regional Governor Andrei Klychkov said three people were killed on Friday in a Ukrainian missile strike on an unspecified civilian facility in the region.
Ukraine's military also reported hitting an aircraft at the Yeysk airfield in southern Russia . Local authorities confirmed an attack in the area but said it caused only minor damage to two apartment buildings.
Russia 's Defense Ministry said on Saturday that air defenses had destroyed 1,297 drones, one French-made SCALP cruise missile and four Ukrainian Neptune missiles over the previous 24 hours.

title: Gunmen open fire at a church during a funeral in Jordan, killing 7 and wounding 40
body:
A man looks through a gap in a stone wall toward a Greek Orthodox church where gunmen opened fire during a funeral hours earlier in Hamoud village, in Jordan's Karak governorate on Friday. AP Photo/AP hide caption
JERUSALEM — Gunmen opened fire during a funeral at a church in Jordan on Friday, killing seven people and wounding 40 others, authorities said.
The shooting took place at a Greek Orthodox church in Karak, about 90 kilometers (55 miles) south of the capital, Amman.
Footage broadcast on Jordanian state television showed two gunmen who appear to be holding pistols approaching the church and firing shots. A third man who appears to be holding a semiautomatic rifle then approaches and opens fire, and all three then run toward the church.
Video footage taken by witnesses shows broken glass and pools of blood on the floor of the church.
Dorgham Halasa, who was among the mourners inside the church, said intense gunfire erupted 15 minutes after the funeral had started, and then people started running. "It was a weird situation, and heavy gunfire," Halasa said.
He did not see the gunmen, but said other people reported seeing four of them. The Associated Press could not independently verify the number of assailants, and Jordan's security services did not immediately release details.
A government statement said that the attack was "carried out by unknown assailants," but didn't say whether any gunmen were captured or killed. It said that "investigations are underway at full speed."
Jordan declared three days of national mourning, according to the kingdom's Petra News Agency.
Soldiers and security officers hold back residents outside Prince Ali Military Hospital during King Abdullah II's visit to people wounded when gunmen opened fire during a funeral at a Greek Orthodox church hours earlier, in Karak, Jordan on Friday. AP Photo/AP hide caption
Karak is home to a minority Christian population.
In 2016, gunmen ambushed police in a series of attacks in Karak, including at a Crusader castle popular with tourists, killing 10 people, including seven officers, and wounding dozens. Jordanian security forces killed those gunmen after a long standoff.
Jordan's Health Minister Ibrahim al-Budour said two of those wounded are in critical condition.
King Abdullah II said on X that Jordan "will confront the terrorist act that targeted Karak with the harshest penalties" and offered his "deepest condolences to the families of the martyrs, and our wishes for recovery to the wounded."
Jordan's Prime Minister Jafar Hassan said during a security meeting in Karak on Friday evening that the attack was a result of terrorist ideology and blind extremism. He said the assailants will be punished and legal measures taken against those who seek to introduce extremism.
Condemnation of the slayings came from around the region, including from Lebanon, Syria, Egypt and Oman.
Ahmed al-Tayeb in Cairo, the grand imam of Al-Azhar, the Sunni Muslim world's foremost religious institution, offered his condolences to the families of victims in Friday's shooting, calling it a "heinous terrorist attack."
Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein called his Jordanian counterpart and "affirmed Iraq's solidarity with Jordan in the face of terrorism," Hussein's office said in a statement.
U.N. Secretary-General Antonio Guterres condemned the attack during a funeral as "especially heinous," spokesman Stephane Dujarric said. "The secretary-general also calls for all those responsible to be found and to be held to account."

title: Zelensky on his relationship with Trump: “I don't play games with him”
body:
He made these remarks in an interview with ABC News , according to Ukrinform.
Zelensky confirmed that Ukraine is ready to end the war as soon as possible, specifically by freezing hostilities along the current front line. According to him, Russia currently controls more than 19% of the Donbas region, but Kyiv is not prepared to cede additional territories in order to end the war.
Zelensky noted that he does not feel betrayed by the United States, but regrets the lack of U.S. aid.
“I feel what I feel. This is not support,” he said.
The president also acknowledged that he does not know why relations between U.S. President Donald Trump and Kremlin leader Vladimir Putin have noticeably warmed. At the same time, he emphasized that the U.S. president’s decision to maintain a personal relationship with the Russian leader is his own choice.
“I don’t know if it’s wrong or not, because it’s his personal decision— to be friends with Putin or not,” Zelensky said, adding that, in his opinion, the two leaders have “quite good relations.”
The head of state also reported that over the past three months, Ukraine has received only 24 interceptor missiles for its Patriot systems from the U.S., although its needs are significantly greater. According to Zelensky, 30 ballistic missiles were fired at Kyiv on Thursday evening alone. He noted that Ukraine needs an average of 350 Patriot interceptors per month.
Despite this, the president emphasized that he remains grateful to the U.S. for its partnership in countering Russian aggression. He also acknowledged that he does not always behave “politely,” explaining this by the need to firmly defend the country’s interests.
“Ukraine cannot have a weak president right now. Of course, I’m an normal person—just a human— maybe not such big humanitarian as Putin, of course,” Zelensky said.
He added that in his relationship with Trump, he tries to be candid and avoid manipulation.
“Between friends like in the family. You have to be honest not to play games. I don't play games with Trump. This is my difference between me and Putin. I don't play with him any games. I'm direct honest,” the president emphasized.
When asked if he believed that Putin had asked Trump to stop the exchange of intelligence between the U.S. and Ukraine, Zelensky replied: “I don’t know. I hope—and I believe and hope—that God will bless us and say no.”
As reported by Ukrinform, U.S. President Donald Trump said that every time he speaks with Russian leader Vladimir Putin, he tells him that it is time to stop and end the war against Ukraine.

title: 10 killed as armed bandits raid Taraba community, loot food stores
body: By Femi Bolaji, Jalingo No fewer than ten residents were reportedly gunned down on Friday afternoon when a large gang of heavily armed bandits invaded Binnari village in Taraba State, unleashing intense gunfire and looting food supplies from shops. According to a police statement issued by the Taraba State Police Command Public Relations Officer, ASP Victor Mshelizah, the tragic attack occurred on Friday, October 23, 2026, at about 3:00 p.m., shortly after residents concluded Jumu’ah prayers. The assailants, numbering in their dozens, threw the rural community into pandemonium as they shot indiscriminately before pillaging food items and provision stores. Operatives attached to the Binnari police station, upon receiving distress calls, mobilised to the scene alongside community volunteers, recovering ten corpses bearing fatal gunshot wounds. The victims have since been handed over to their respective families and buried in accordance with Islamic rites. Reacting to the carnage, the State Commissioner of Police, CP Edwin Ogbeghagha, placed security formations across the area on red alert and ordered the immediate deployment of joint tactical teams comprising the Nigeria Police Force, Police Mobile Force (PMF), and the Nigerian Army to comb the surrounding terrain. The command urged residents of Binnari and neighbouring settlements to remain calm, avoid panic peddling, and cooperate with security operatives by sharing actionable intelligence that will lead to the apprehension of the fleeing attackers. title: Zelensky Ready for Immediate Peace Deal, Expresses Regret Over US Aid
body:
President Volodymyr Zelensky stated in an interview broadcast on ABC News that Ukraine is prepared to conclude a peace agreement with the Russia immediately if achievable, while expressing regret over the contraction of US military assistance.
Speaking in the interview, the president confirmed that Kyiv is prepared to halt hostilities as quickly as possible, reiterating Ukraine’s readiness to freeze combat operations along the existing line of contact.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
Zelensky clarified that while Russian forces currently occupy over 19 percent of Ukrainian territory in the Donbas , Kyiv is unwilling to cede additional land to secure an end to the war.
Addressing the state of bilateral relations with Washington , Zelensky stated that while he does not feel betrayed by the US, he regrets the decline in American defense support.
“I feel what I feel. This is not support,” Zelensky remarked regarding the reduced flow of military supplies.
Zelensky acknowledged an apparent warming of relations between US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin , observing that the nature of Trump’s personal engagement with the Kremlin leader represents an autonomous presidential prerogative.
“I don’t know whether it’s wrong or not, because it’s his personal decision whether to be friends with Putin or not,” Zelensky said, adding that, in his view, the two leaders maintain “quite good relations.”
When asked whether he believes Putin asked Trump to halt intelligence sharing between the US and Ukraine, Zelensky responded: “I don’t know. I hope, I believe and hope, God bless, no.”
Zelensky addressed his own diplomatic style, explaining that defending Ukraine’s sovereign interests during wartime requires an unyielding posture rather than diplomatic deference.
“There cannot be a weak president in Ukraine right now,” Zelensky stated. “Of course, I am an ordinary person, I’m just human, though perhaps not such a great ‘humanist’ as Putin, of course.”
The president stressed that his communication with Trump remains candid and transparent, rejecting tactical pretense.
“As between friends, as in a family, you have to be honest, not play games. I don’t play games with Trump. That is my difference from Putin. I don’t play any games with him. I am direct, honest,” Zelensky said.
The Ukrainian head of state reiterated the acute disparity between domestic air defense requirements and recent munition transfers from the US.
Zelensky confirmed that over the past three months, Ukraine received only 24 surface-to-air interceptors for its Patriot air defense batteries from the US, contrasting the delivery with Ukraine’s calculated operational requirement of roughly 350 Patriot interceptors per month.
Highlighting the scale of Russian standoff strikes, Zelensky noted that on Thursday evening alone, Russian forces launched 30 ballistic missiles toward Kyiv.
Despite the munition deficit, Zelensky emphasized that he remains grateful to the US for its strategic partnership in countering Russian aggression.

title: Kaduna Presidential Rally: Atiku is butterfly thinking itself a bird – Keyamo
body: Festus Keyamo, Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, has described Atiku Abubakar as a butterfly that thinks it is a bird, given his “blistering online attack against the APC (All Progressives Congress), particularly in the North”. The APC is scheduled to flag off its presidential campaign in Kaduna on Saturday. According to Keyamo, Atiku Abubakar, the presidential candidate of African Democratic Congress, ADC, was banking on the bulk of Northern votes to see him through in 2027, knowing that he has no inroads at all into the South. Therefore, Keyamo said in a statement, Atiku has taken to the “common but cheap tactic” of positioning cameras then get people to tear down the posters of President Bola Tinubu, and then post the videos online. “The other tactic is to disseminate disinformation claiming that any support the President is seen to receive in the North is procured only through the massive deployment of financial resources. “Hence the fake letter alleging a N2.3 trillion deployment for the Kaduna rally. The intention is to generate a hoopla that will create a groundswell of public opinion that President Tinubu has been ‘massively rejected’ in the North.” Keyamo said given the mood of the country, the South deserves to complete eight years in the presidency. Also, he added, in 2023, Atiku lost across the Middle Belt, all southern states, except Osun State. Projecting on 2027 votes, Keyamo said with the APC structures in the North backing Tinubu, Atiku Abubakar has seen that his demographic calculation for the 2027 elections regarding northern votes is evaporating. Therefore, he noted, Atiku resorted to desperate tactics. “He knows that even if he wins in some parts of the North and the President comes a close second, the election is as good as over, because those differences would be wiped out by his heavy defeat in the Middle Belt and the South. “Atiku Abubakar thinks he is the Buhari of 2015, who swept the Northern votes. He thinks that was a display of ethnic support. He fails to realise that his past puts him poles apart from a Muhammadu Buhari,” Keyamo said. title: Up to 70,000 police mobilized to curb violence at France protests
body:
PARIS (AP) — France deployed thousands of police Saturday for fresh protests over school funding and soaring living costs, seeking to prevent another weekend of looting, burned cars and attacks on public buildings. In Paris, authorities restricted the main march to the city’s southeastern edge, keeping it away from the center.
Thousands of people were already marching Saturday afternoon in Orléans, south of Paris, in a separate protest against the far right as Marine Le Pen’s National Rally held a two-day congress in the city.
Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said up to 70,000 officers would be deployed nationwide, backed by helicopters, armored vehicles and water cannons.
What began last month as a protest over staff shortages at one high school southeast of Paris has grown into a national movement. Students demanding better schools and workers seeking higher wages and pensions have brought anger over living standards into the final months of President Emmanuel Macron’s presidency.
Macron met high school representatives Friday. They said he had promised to overhaul university admissions, but called for protests to continue until concrete measures are announced.
More than half a million people took to the streets last Saturday. Some 3,000 shops across France were damaged or looted over the weekend.
Ahead of the new protests, Paris landmarks closed, shopkeepers boarded up storefronts and gendarmes stood guard beneath the Arc de Triomphe.
Gendarmes stood guard beneath the Arc de Triomphe as shopkeepers boarded up storefronts across Paris. Near the Saint-Lazare train station Saturday, Akram Ahmed, a 34-year-old contractor, was boarding up an optician’s shop.
“I got the call last night,” he said. “The owner seemed desperate. He said I was saving his life.” Major museums, including the Louvre, Orsay Museum, Picasso Museum and Grand Palais — where a major Cézanne exhibit is on display — were shuttered Saturday.
Art Basel, one of the world’s most prestigious contemporary art fairs, opened to the public Friday, but only for the day, with the threat of unrest prompting organizers to cancel the weekend program. Some protests have been banned
Police changed the Paris route Friday, replacing the planned Bastille-to-Nation march with a route between Porte d’Italie and Porte de Vincennes. At Bastille, the original starting point, police used a megaphone to tell people to leave or face a 135-euro fine.
Protest marches are scheduled in Paris and Marseille, but some other rallies, including in Lyon, Nice and Montpellier, have been banned by local authorities. In Lyon, French media reported that police used tear gas Saturday morning.
Trade unions have criticized the bans, calling them violations of freedom of expression, which is protected by the constitution.
Macron, a centrist, has entered the crisis in the final stretches of his term, with his popularity at its lowest since he took office in 2017. He has said that the measures are needed to protect city centers, businesses and public buildings.
Nuñez acknowledged Monday that police had lost control in some cities during last weekend’s unrest. He offered to resign, but Macron refused.
In Orléans, about 110 kilometers (70 miles) south of Paris, thousands of people took to the streets for an anti-far-right protest. It was organized on the sidelines of a meeting of Le Pen’s nationalist, anti-immigration party ahead of next spring’s presidential election.
Student groups want 250,000 more places in higher education and an end to selection through Parcoursup, the national admissions system.
Their joint 10-point plan also calls for more teachers and repairs to schools and universities. They are also seeking help with everyday costs: an extra 200 euros a month in student grants and a rent freeze in public student housing.
“The money is now concentrated in the hands of very few people,” said Victoria Ambrosini, an art critic and art teacher at Saint-Denis University. “And it’s not possible anymore.”
– Associated Press writer Tom Nouvian contributed to this report.

title: Call of the Wilde: Jacob Fowler shines again in a convincing win for the Montreal Canadiens in Chicago
body:
The streak is over at 546 straight games played for Nick Suzuki. The Montreal Canadiens captain is out of the lineup for two to four weeks with a finger injury after blocking a shot on Tuesday night.
The challenge is on for the Canadiens to rise above losing their best player. Night one was in Chicago and it was an impressive one for the Montreal Canadiens beating the Blackhawks 4-1.
The Canadiens needed someone to step up. Enter, if you can believe it, Jake Evans. The same Evans who hadn’t scored all season. In the first period, his line put together an exquisite passing play to count. It was Owen Beck, quickly to Kirby Dach who fed it in front to Evans who went far side.
In the second period, the Canadiens took far too many penalties, but not only did they kill them, they scored shorthanded. Kaiden Guhle won the puck in front of his own net, and somehow, after that, all the Hawks disappeared. Evans and Guhle led a two-on-one with Evans ripping a shot into the top corner over the shoulder of Spencer Knight.
The unlikely pair combined again late in the second period. It was Evans feeding Guhle at the point, and he fired through a maze of bodies his first goal of the season. That’s a three point night for Evans. The line with Beck and Dach had their best game of the season.
Mike Matheson added an empty netter in his first game back. He had a solid game paired with Lane Hutson.
The most important goaltending statistic in the new era is Goals Saved Above Expected. The best goalie in the playoffs last season was Jakub Dobes in this statistic. He was phenomenal. This season… not so much. Out of 68 goalies in the net this NHL season, Dobes ranks 66th.
Jacob Fowler is 15th in GSAE this season. He’s the goalie that the Canadiens need to rely on to in the crease right now. Fowler is technically sound. For what he lacks in size compared to Dobes, he wins in technical ability. He tracks the puck so calmly. He is prepared for rebounds in a perfect position after the initial shot.
Fowler received high praise from Carey Price recently. Price said that the goalie that reminds him of his style the most is Fowler. That’s some high praise.
Fowler put in a 1.16 GSAE in this one. He held the Canadiens in when they struggled in the opening period. St. Louis said earlier this week that he doesn’t like one of his goalies to sit too long. He may have to rethink that considering there is such a disparity between the two goalies presently.
After the loss to the Sharks, St. Louis commented that players have to understand what the game needs from them. He was speaking to penalties taken, and odd man rushes allowed while leading. He mentioned that his team had the puck in the offensive zone when the comeback started.
The head coach wants his team to understand that up 3-1, they need to shut the game down, not keep it wide open looking for a fourth goal. They learned the lesson. Looking to give it everything they had, Chicago got only four shots on net in the third period.
It’s impossible to replace a number one line with a 64 per cent Expected Goals this season. The first attempt at centre in between Cole Caufield and Juraj Slafkovsky was given to Oliver Kapanen. Head Coach Martin St. Louis didn’t want to ruin the chemistry of a couple secondary lines, so he kept those lines together.
It’s hard to describe how valuable Suzuki is to the team sometimes, but when two wingers have a 64 per cent xG, then Kapanen moves to the line and the xG drops to three per cent for 40 minutes, the perfect description has been found.
With the other lines doing well, it’s hard to imagine what St. Louis will do. He can’t have a number one line destroyed, but he doesn’t have a better alternative either. He’ll need to be patient.
They need a little time to develop some chemistry. In fact, late in the second period, they started to turn it around, and deserve another look to see if they’re figuring it out. The line finished with a 37 Expected Goals share thanks to a terrific third period.
The only goat has an undercurrent of a developing positive. Nothing but praise for a team that finally held a 3-1 lead.
It’s hard to believe, but the knives are out right now for General Manager Kent Hughes because he didn’t get a second line centre in the off-season. However, it should always be remembered that the goal of a GM isn’t to win a championship in October, but to create an open window for a title for seven to ten seasons.
There is absolutely no doubt that Hughes could have acquired a second line centre last June, but at a cost that was so high, that only this season would be better than the rest of the seasons to come. The solution for Hughes has to work in the short and the long term.
To acquire a strong 34 year old centre giving up talented 20 year olds only to have the 34 year old retire next season while the 20 year olds puts in 15 seasons on other teams is not good management. If there was a deal to be made, Hughes would have made it.
It’s going to be a difficult month without Nick Suzuki, but then it will be December, and barring a catastrophic next 13 games, the club will survive. At the trading deadline, Hughes may get another opportunity to make a smart trade for the future, and load up for the playoffs.
Michael Hage is coming soon as well. He may come as soon as this season after he finishes the the NCAA college playoffs. Michigan is the top team in the country. If the Wolverines advance to the Frozen Four, then Hage will arrive mid-April. If they fail to advance, Hage will arrive for the final push in the regular season.
Right now, Oliver Kapanen trying to fill in as Suzuki is obviously a tall order, but the wise see a long horizon while the foolish can only see past their nose.
Brian Wilde, a Montreal-based sportswriter, brings you Call of the Wilde on globalnews.ca after each Canadiens game.

title: One man killed, two others hospitalized following missile strike on Lozova – Synehubov
body:
Russian occupiers launched a missile strike on the city of Lozova in Kharkiv region on Saturday, sparking a fire at a warehouse facility and resulting in one death and several injuries, reported Oleh Synehubov, head of Kharkiv Regional Military Administration.

"A strike was recorded on a warehouse building, which subsequently caught fire... As a result of the shelling, a 26-year-old man and a 43-year-old man sustained injuries. The victims have been hospitalized. Sadly, a 45-year-old man died from his severe injuries," Synehubov wrote on his Telegram channel.

title: Enugu socialite killed during police raid of birthday party
body: By Anayo Okoli A birthday celebration organised by a famous Enugu socialite, Nnaji Izuchukwu, popularly known as Stone, at a hotel in the Asata area of Enugu turned fatal, leading to his death. Reports said the celebration turned chaotic after a misunderstanding among attendees, which allegedly led the hotel management to invite the police from the Anti-Cultism Section. The celebrant, Izuchukwu Nnaji, allegedly died from gunshot injuries he sustained during the ensuing police operation. The exact circumstances surrounding the shooting remained unclear. Still, it was said that in the ensuing confusion following the police raid, he allegedly attempted to escape through a window with another person before he sustained gunshot injuries. The Enugu State Police Command has confirmed the death and ordered an investigation into the incident. Enugu police orders thorough investigation into the death A statement by the command’s spokesman, SP Daniel Ndukwe, said: “The Commissioner of Police, Enugu State Command, CP Mamman Bitrus Giwa, has ordered a thorough investigation into the circumstances surrounding the death of Nnaji Izuchukwu (male) during an intelligence-led operation by operatives of the Anti-Cultism Section of the Violent Crime Response Unit (VCRU). “He has directed the Assistant Commissioner of Police in charge of the State Intelligence Department (SID) to establish the facts of the incident and determine whether the operation and use of firearms complied with established operational standards and extant laws. “Preliminary findings indicate that operatives, acting on credible intelligence, raided Bull Hotel, Asata, Enugu, where Nworie Chidera Kelvin, a.k.a. “Akidi,” an alleged notorious drug peddler and Vikings Confraternity member, was lodged with associates. Akidi is allegedly linked to multiple cases involving unlawful firearm possession and cultism, including one in which he was charged in absentia. He was also suspected of keeping the gang’s firearms and other criminal tools. “The operation led to the arrest of Akidi and nine other suspects, comprising males and females aged 17–28. “Quantities of dried weeds suspected to be “loud” cannabis, a weighing scale suspected to be used for measuring illicit drugs, and ₦43,400 in various denominations were recovered. “During the operation, Nnaji and another suspect jumped through a window in an attempt to escape. While pursuing them, an operative was confronted by both suspects, who allegedly attempted to disarm him. In the ensuing struggle, the firearm discharged, leaving Nnaji with gunshot injuries, while the other suspect escaped. “Nnaji was rushed to hospital, where he was later confirmed dead. His remains have been deposited in a mortuary for preservation and autopsy. “CP Giwa has urged the deceased’s family, associates and other concerned persons to remain calm, assuring them that the circumstances surrounding the incident will be thoroughly investigated and that any officer found culpable will face appropriate disciplinary action. “He reiterated that professionalism, ethical conduct and strict adherence to operational standards, particularly those governing the use of firearms, must never be compromised in any police operation.” The post Enugu socialite killed during police raid of birthday party appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Russian Strike Hits Lozova Warehouse, Killing 1, Injuring 2
body:
A Russian missile struck a commercial warehouse in the city of Lozova in the Kharkiv region on Saturday, Oct. 24, killing a 45-year-old man and injuring two others, regional authorities reported.
Head of the Kharkiv Regional Military Administration Oleh Syniehubov confirmed that emergency medical teams attempted to resuscitate the 45-year-old victim, but he succumbed to critical injuries sustained in the blast.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
Two other men, aged 26 and 43, sustained wounds and were transported to regional medical facilities for inpatient treatment.
The missile impact ignited a fire across the storage facility, prompting specialized firefighting units and civil defense crews from the State Emergency Service of Ukraine (DSNS) to deploy to extinguish the blaze and clear structural debris.
“Medics fought for the life of the victim, but the injuries proved fatal,” Syniehubov stated in an official dispatch.
Concurrently on Saturday, Russian forces launched an aerial attack targeting an infrastructure facility in the southern city of Zaporizhzhia , regional officials confirmed.
According to preliminary assessments released by Mykhailo Semikin of the Zaporizhzhia Regional Military Administration, the strike wounded two civilians and damaged civilian vehicles parked in the vicinity of the impact zone.
The daylight strikes on Lozova and Zaporizhzhia followed an extensive overnight air assault launched by Russian forces between 6:00 p.m. on Friday, Oct. 23, and Saturday morning, Oct. 24.
Early Saturday morning, a Russian aerial attack struck a private residential home in Kyiv’s northern Obolonskyi district , injuring two civilians after capital air defense units engaged high-speed turbojet-powered strike drones over the metropolitan area around 3:42 a.m.
According to the Ukrainian Air Force Command, Russian forces launched 126 strike and decoy unmanned aerial systems against Ukrainian territory overnight.
The incoming wave included 61 high-speed turbojet-powered Shahed variants, alongside S-8000 Banderol and Dan-T compact cruise systems, Gerbera drones, and Parodiya decoy platforms staged from seven locations across the Russian Federation and occupied territories.
By 8:00 a.m. on Saturday, Ukrainian air defenses had shot down or electronically suppressed 101 aerial targets nationwide, including 50 turbojet-powered Shahed munitions, while registering impacts across 14 distinct locations and falling debris at five sites.

title: Ukraine and Russia eye new peace talks but steep obstacles remain
body:
KYIV, Ukraine (AP) — Ukraine and Russia have signaled their willingness to resume U.S.-brokered peace talks and are backing a humanitarian mission led by First lady Melania Trump. But deep disagreements over territory and security guarantees that re-emerged this week underscore obstacles to ending the war.
The new diplomatic push comes after more than four and a half years of fighting, bringing with it a surprise announcement on Friday: Kyiv and Moscow have agreed to a local ceasefire to allow aid next week into a stranded town in Ukraine’s southern war-divided region of Kherson, following secret consultations between Melania Trump and civilian negotiators from Russia and Ukraine.
While the initiative raised hopes of similar humanitarian missions in the future, there were few indications that any of the key positions have shifted. Russia continues to demand Ukrainian territory it does not fully control, while Kyiv insists any agreement must include ironclad guarantees against another invasion.
Within hours of Russian President Vladimir Putin saying he agreed “in principle” to restart talks, Russia launched a deadly barrage of ballistic missiles and drones on Kyiv. Moscow on the same day said it had destroyed more than 800 Ukrainian drones heading toward its cities.
Here’s a look at where the two countries stand as potential negotiations loom.
U.S. presidential envoy Steve Witkoff secured the latest commitment to talks after shuttling between Oslo, Norway, and St. Petersburg, Russia, this week to meet Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and Putin.
A new round of negotiations would be the fourth brokered by the Trump administration, following the most recent round in Geneva in February.
A Kremlin spokesman said that the next round of talks is likely to be held in Abu Dhabi, the capital of the United Arab Emirates, around mid-November. Western governments backing the peace initiative are seeking a new formula to break the impasse while acknowledging that territorial and security questions remain unresolved.
U.S. President Donald Trump’s ties with Zelenskyy, meanwhile, have sunk to a new low. Moscow has been bolstered by Trump’s deal for Russia to supply the U.S. with diesel and his recent rejection of new Russia sanctions.
Kyiv has been undermined by disruptions in satellite support for its drones after rejecting a call by the U.S. president to halt strikes on Russian oil infrastructure. Ukrainian leaders fear the moves will embolden Putin, giving him little incentive to compromise at the negotiating table.
As Trump increased pressure on Zelenskyy, accusing him of being an obstacle to peace, Witkoff secured the release of an American who had been jailed for more than four years on charges of fighting as a mercenary in Ukraine. The envoy described the Russian leader as a “humanitarian” at their meeting in St. Petersburg — a remark met with consternation in Ukraine.
While both sides back calls for new talks, Russia and Ukraine are still far apart on their terms for a settlement, while their armies remain locked on the battlefield and they pummel each other with daily long-range strikes.
Central to Russia’s demands is full control of four Ukrainian regions it illegally annexed months after the start of the full-scale invasion in 2022: Donetsk, Luhansk, Zaporizhzhia and Kherson, in addition to Crimea, which Moscow seized in 2014.
Russia currently occupies about 20% of Ukraine but has failed to capture all the territory in the regions over which it claims sovereignty.
In a long list of demands, Moscow also wants Ukraine to withdraw forces from all four annexed regions, renounce its bid to join NATO, reduce the size of its military and drop restrictions against the Russian language and a Moscow-affiliated branch of the Orthodox Church.
Speaking on state television late Thursday, Putin said Moscow remains “ready to negotiate and seek solutions to this difficult, complex situation,” before adding: “But if some prefer a different path, so be it.
In any case, all the objectives of the special military operation will be achieved.”
Zelenskyy — who for months has publicly advocated for peace talks — argues that giving up land would leave Ukraine more vulnerable to future attacks. Kyiv views security guarantees as essential to prevent Russia from restarting the war in the future.
The Ukrainian president has reaffirmed support for a ceasefire that would freeze front-line positions, followed by talks on conditions for ending the war. Moscow has rejected a break in hostilities until a comprehensive agreement on its terms is reached.
While Kyiv and Moscow have maintained limited contact to organize prisoner exchanges and the return of fallen soldiers, previous talks have made no progress on the security arrangements needed to sustain a peace deal.
Ukraine believes security guarantees backed by Western allies are essential to any future settlement, ideally in the form of NATO membership — an option Vladimir Putin has rejected. Ukraine expects to heavily rely on its own army as the main security guarantee with financial backing from its allies.
Other elements of security guarantees being discussed range from NATO membership, which the U.S. administration has currently ruled out, direct guarantees from the United States in what Zelenskyy has described as an “Article 5-like format” and backing by the European-led 30-country alliance known as the Coalition of the Willing.
Article 5 of the NATO charter contains the alliance’s mutual-defense guarantee, which establishes that an attack on one is an attack on all.
“All of these guarantees are possible on the basis of a strong Ukrainian army — in terms of both numbers and quality — with clear funding, and not a small amount. Our colleagues in Europe and America know this,” Zelenskyy told reporters Thursday at a briefing.
Following the massive attacks on Kyiv and other cities this week, he argued that only increased Western pressure on Moscow would change its calculations about future peace talks.
“It is important to keep trying to find the right solutions to end this war,” Zelenskyy wrote in an online post. “But when Russia responds to negotiations with ballistic missiles, real pressure on Russia is needed to bring about different steps — steps toward ending the killing.”

title: Cuban ambassadors ask Canada to renew rejection of U.S. embargo and fuel blockade
body:
Havana is urging Ottawa not to drop its public opposition to the decades-long U.S. embargo as Washington ramps up pressure on countries supporting Cuba.
“We are confident that Canada will stay with us, as they have done in the past,” Cuban Ambassador to Canada Rodrigo Malmierca Diaz told The Canadian Press.
“The blockade and this intensification is, in practice, killing people.”
The United Nations is set to vote next week on a motion Cuba has put forward nearly every year since 1992. It calls for the termination of “the economic, commercial and financial embargo imposed by the United States of America against Cuba.”
Canada has voted in favour of this motion multiple times.
U.S. President Donald Trump’s administration has been trying to overthrow Cuba’s Communist government through a de facto oil blockade. Washington cut off Venezuelan shipments in January and has threatened to impose tariffs on countries that sell oil to the island nation.
Washington claims Cuba poses a national security threat to the United States. Malmierca said the Caribbean nation is being collectively punished by an American pressure campaign that is harming the health and education of Cubans.
An economic crisis has gripped Cuba since 2020, triggering critical shortages and severe blackouts that peaked after January’s fuel blockade.
Havana insists its economic struggles stem from six decades of American sanctions, but critics point to the inefficiency of its Communist regime. Human Rights Watch and Amnesty International say Cuba’s government engages in arbitrary arrests, tortures political prisoners and limits media and political parties.
Cuba produces only 40 per cent of the fuel it needs. Shortages have led to frequent blackouts that have threatened health care systems and crippled the island’s economy. Air Canada and other airlines cancelled flights to Cuba in February because of shortages of aviation fuel.
Ottawa has pledged to distribute $13 million in humanitarian aid for Cubans through international organizations — not the Cuban government. Past Canadian development funding has gone to things like solar panels aimed at making the island less reliant on foreign fuel.
“The people are resisting because we are convinced that the most valuable thing we have is the independence, the sovereignty of Cuba. And we are not going to surrender that,” Malmierca said.
“We would like to have a normal relationship with the U.S. We are ready for dialogue.” Malmierca said countries that have supported Cuba have told Havana they’re being warned by Washington their access to American trade or aid could be curbed if they continue supporting UN motions to end the blockade.
He said Cuba is “not naive” and knows Canada is facing its own economic pressure from the Trump administration.
“This year is a particular moment because of all this aggressivity of the U.S. government against Cuba,” he said. “They are in a kind of offensive with other countries, trying to exercise influence for them to change their votes. We know they are using threats.”
The Canadian Press asked the U.S. State Department for comment but didn’t receive a response.
U.S. Ambassador to the UN Mike Waltz this week urged countries to vote against the motion, dismissing it as a product of “70 years of propaganda” meant to distract from corruption in Havana. He said Washington has been lobbying European countries to vote against the motion.
“Do not let them abuse your vote for their oppression,” he said at a Monday event he hosted. “Do not give in to this lie.”
In a statement, Global Affairs Canada said it is still pondering how it will vote on the UN motion next week.
“As with all UN resolutions, Canada’s voting position is being considered in advance of the vote,” wrote spokesperson Thida Ith.
“Canada continues to call for the Cuban government to implement needed reforms to respect the political and economic rights of the Cuban people, and to release all political prisoners.”
In July, Havana called for a UN debate on the American embargo in the context of the island’s fuel crisis. Washington suggested it was a waste of resources to debate a motion that had already been debated nine months prior, and insisted that the decision to hold a debate be put to a recorded vote.
The vote passed and a debate was held. Canada was among 30 countries that abstained from the motion on holding a debate.
Civil society groups such as the Canadian Network on Cuba said they fear Ottawa may be pulling back from Cuba.
A document The Canadian Press obtained through a freedom-of-information request shows Ottawa had frank exchanges with Cuba about its liquidity crisis before Trump ramped up pressure on the Communist government.
The document — a briefing book prepared by Global Affairs for its deputy minister — shows the deputy minister met with three Canadian firms during a visit to Havana in February 2023 to discuss their Cuban clients’ unpaid bills.
The document says the aim of the meeting was to reassure the three firms that Ottawa “has their back … without unduly encouraging new investors and traders who risk not being paid for their goods/services.”
The companies mentioned in the document are the National Bank, mining firm Sherritt and hotel chain Blue Diamond, now called Royalton. None of the companies responded to The Canadian Press when asked whether they still have accounts in arrears in Cuba.
Sherritt and Royalton have both ceased operations in Cuba. Havana has blamed their withdrawal on American pressure tactics.
The briefing book for the deputy minister reveals some of the nature of Canada’s discussions with Cuba, with Ottawa pushing for details on small and medium-sized enterprises and Havana requesting more aid.
“Canadian firms are facing mounting payment arrears with Cuban buyers. Many Canadian firms in Cuba are SMEs and the situation is threatening their sustainability,” reads the February 2023 document for the deputy minister.
“We sought bilateral meetings for you, that would allow you, for example, to engage on human rights and new economic actors (private sector SMEs and entrepreneurs). The Cuban side wanted rather to talk to you about new tourism initiatives and more Canadian international development projects.”
The briefing book proposed that Canada “leverage Cuba’s desire for increased assistance in our dialogue on other priorities (e.g. human rights)” — but added that the cheapest and most effective things Canada could offer would be technical help with reforming the agriculture sector and rules for smaller businesses.
Malmierca said Cuba is implementing 176 reform measures which came out of parliamentary and public consultations. He said these measures will allow a larger role for the private sector, foreign investment incentives and municipal autonomy.
“In Cuba, we work according to the rule of law,” he said. “Cuba is a society that is continuously trying to improve.”
He said a trade fair in Havana next month is going largely virtual due to the current electricity shortages, and Cuba will hold an event in Toronto ahead of time to drum up interest from Canadian entrepreneurs.
“We can maintain not only the economic relationship, but we can increase it in better conditions in the near future.”

title: Obuasi SHTS scandal: GES Director-General must resign – Former GNAT General Secretary
body: Former General Secretary of the Ghana National Association of Teachers (GNAT), David Ofori Acheampong, has called for the resignation of the Director-General of the Ghana Education Service (GES) over the handling of sexual abuse allegations involving the headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School. Speaking on Asempa FM’s Kukurantumi show on Saturday, October 24, Mr Ofori Acheampong argued that the GES leadership must take responsibility for the situation, which has raised serious concerns about student safety and accountability within the education sector. “In my opinion, the Director-General of GES must resign and take responsibility for this situation,” he stated. He also questioned the response of the headmaster, who has reportedly claimed that eight teachers at the school conspired against him amid allegations of sexual misconduct involving 19 female students. “How can a headmaster claim that eight teachers have plotted against him when he is facing allegations of having sexual relations with 19 female students?” he questioned. Mr Ofori Acheampong further expressed concern about the motivation of some individuals entering the teaching profession, arguing that teaching should be regarded as a calling rather than merely an employment opportunity. According to him, the limited availability of jobs in Ghana has compelled many people to pursue teaching primarily as a means of escaping unemployment, rather than out of a genuine commitment to educating and protecting children. He maintained that teaching requires dedication, professionalism and a strong sense of responsibility towards students, particularly those entrusted to the care of school authorities. His comments follow allegations of sexual abuse involving 19 female students at Obuasi Senior High Technical School, brought to public attention through an investigative documentary by journalist Manasseh Azure Awuni.

title: 2 linked to espionage services nabbed in Kermanshah
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 24 (MNA) – Iran’s Ministry of Intelligence in cooperation with the Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps (IRGC) Ground Force arrested two espionage operatives in western Iranian province of Kermanshah.
The arrests came after round-the-clock efforts made by Intelligence Ministry’s agents and the Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps (IRGC) Ground Force commandos.
During the intelligence operation, security forces seized 10 Starlink satellite internet devices, 10 AK-47 rifles, and 5,200 rounds of ammunition for pistols and G3 rifles.
The operation was part of ongoing intelligence efforts to identify and counter activities by individuals affiliated with foreign espionage services and prevent actions that could threaten Iran’s security.

title: Chelsea vs Tottenham: Preview, team news, possible line-ups
body: Chelsea will look to extend their winning run in the Premier League when they host Tottenham Hotspur at Stamford Bridge on Saturday in a London derby that could have significant implications for both sides. Chelsea have won four, drawn one and lost two of their opening seven league matches, leaving them in the top four. Their recent results have also boosted confidence, with a 5-1 victory over Bournemouth followed by a 2-0 win away to Everton last weekend. Pedro Neto scored twice against Everton as Chelsea ended a run of 22 Premier League matches without a clean sheet. The Blues will now attempt to record three consecutive league victories for the first time since February. The West London club have won their last six league meetings with Tottenham. Another victory on Saturday would set a new club record for consecutive league wins against their London rivals. Tottenham, meanwhile, ended a six-game winless start to the league campaign with a 3-1 victory over Coventry. James Maddison, Omar Marmoush and Ben Davies scored to give Roberto De Zerbi’s side a much-needed result. The win was Tottenham’s fourth Premier League victory in 2026 and the first time in 36 top-flight matches that they had scored more than twice. Despite the result, Spurs remain 16th in the table, although they are only three points behind the top nine. They will need to improve their away record against Chelsea to secure another positive result. Tottenham have won only once in their last 34 Premier League visits to Stamford Bridge, recording 11 draws and 24 defeats. Their most recent victory there came in the 2017-18 season, when Mauricio Pochettino guided them to a 3-1 win. Spurs have also lost their last six London derbies in the league and will be keen to avoid extending that run. Team news Chelsea goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez is set to miss the match after undergoing surgery for a fractured jaw sustained during the win over Everton. He joins Reece James, Jamie Gittens, Pep Chavarria and Emmanuel Emegha on the injury list. Malo Gusto, however, is available again after recovering from illness. Mike Penders is expected to start in goal in Martinez’s absence. The 21-year-old could become Chelsea’s youngest goalkeeper to start a Premier League match. For Tottenham, Rodrigo Bentancur remains suspended and will serve the second match of his three-game ban. Xavi Simons, Wilson Odobert, Lucas Bergvall and Destiny Udogie are also sidelined with knee injuries, while Savio is unavailable because of a muscle problem. Mykhaylo Mudryk, who is on loan from Chelsea, is ineligible to face his parent club and is also recovering from an ankle injury. Tosin Adarabioyo is a doubt with a calf problem, but Pedro Porro, Omar Marmoush and Andrew Robertson have been passed fit to play. Possible line-ups Chelsea: Penders; Acheampong, Lacroix, Colwill; Neto, Caicedo, Henderson, Hato; Palmer, Rogers; Pedro. Tottenham Hotspur: Kinsky; Gray, Van Hecke, Van de Ven, Robertson; Gallagher, Tonali, Maddison; Kudus and other attacking options to be confirmed. The post Chelsea vs Tottenham: Preview, team news, possible line-ups appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Aggrieved NDC delegates invoke curses on party executives over alleged bloated register in Atwima Kwanwoma Constituency
body: Some aggrieved delegates of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) in the Atwima Kwanwoma Constituency of the Ashanti Region, who allege that their names have been removed from the party’s electoral register, have invoked curses on party executives over what they describe as their failure to address the issue. Tension is mounting at Twedie, where the NDC constituency elections are taking place. Some aggrieved delegates allege that the names of qualified delegates have been removed from the electoral register and replaced with those of persons they consider unqualified, purportedly to favour certain candidates in the elections. The aggrieved delegates say they have repeatedly reported the matter to the party’s regional executives for resolution, but their concerns have allegedly not been addressed. They claim the failure of the executives to intervene has left them with no option but to invoke the Antoa deity, calling for spiritual retribution against anyone found culpable in the alleged manipulation. “We have poured libation and slaughtered sheep while invoking Antoa Nyamaa and other river deities to deal with those allegedly responsible for the disputed changes,” they said. Speaking to the media, one of the aggrieved delegates, Gifty Kobbina, expressed frustration over the development, insisting that their sacrifices and commitment to the party should not be undermined by what they describe as an attempt to disenfranchise legitimate delegates. “We have suffered for this party, and we will not allow anyone to cheat us. We are calling on Antoa to strike anyone who has a hand in this album manipulation,” she alleged. The aggrieved delegates have warned that failure to resolve their concerns could undermine the credibility of the constituency elections and deepen divisions among party members.

title: Remi Tinubu: I Want To Leave Aso Rock In 2031
body: First Lady Oluremi Tinubu has expressed the desire to leave the Presidential Villa in Abuja by 2031. She said this at the inauguration of the Abuja headquarters of the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement. The movement is a grassroots mobilisation group campaigning for the president’s return to office in 2027. “I want to leave Aso Rock, in 2031, by the grace of God, and enter a Nigeria that me as a 70-something-year-old woman will enjoy,” she said. Insults can’t stop growing rejection of your party, ADC replies APC Bandits killed as hunters repel attack in Katsina Mrs Tinubu cited “improvements” in the country’s airports as evidence of progress. She said she wanted to be able to travel more conveniently. “I want to get to the airport. I want to travel, you know, so quickly. And you can see our airports too are changing,” she said. At the event, the First Lady commissioned the movement’s Abuja headquarters and dedicated the facility to the president’s anticipated victory in the 2027 election. “So to the glory of God, and for the victory of Mr President come 2027, I hereby formally commission the PBAT door-to-door movement campaign headquarters Abuja,” she said. Mrs Tinubu also expressed support for the All Progressives Congress (APC) and Government Ekpemupolo, popularly known as Tompolo, the movement’s convener. Daily Trust reports that her remarks reflect a pattern of public defence of her husband’s leadership that predates his presidency and has continued amid mounting debate over the impact of his policies. In October 2022, while Tinubu was seeking the presidency, the then Lagos Central senator expressed confidence that his experience in Lagos would help him address Nigeria’s problems. “Don’t worry, we (Tinubu’s administration) will fix it, that’s all I can tell you,” she said in an interview with AIT. She argued that the foundations laid in Lagos could guide his plans for the country. After he assumed office in May 2023, she urged Nigerians to be patient, saying her husband could not resolve the country’s problems instantly. At an Independence Day church service in October 2023, she said the administration had inherited longstanding challenges and was committed to addressing them rather than blaming previous governments. “My husband is not a magician. He is going to work and I believe and hope that we will have peace in this country. The best is yet to come to us,” she said. As economic difficulties persisted, Mrs Tinubu continued to defend the administration’s approach. In February 2024, she described the hardship being experienced by Nigerians as temporary and expressed hope that conditions would improve. Eight months later, she rejected the suggestion that her husband was responsible for the economic hardship. And said the government was trying to secure the country’s future. “We are just 18 months into our administration, we are not the cause of the current situation, we are trying to fix it and secure the future,” she said in October 2024 during a visit to the palace of the Ooni of Ife, Oba Adeyeye Ogunwusi. Her latest comments come as political mobilisation gathers pace ahead of the 2027 general election. In January 2026, she described her husband as “the architect of modern Nigeria” in a social media post that attracted mixed reactions, including criticism from Nigerians who questioned the administration’s record. In September, she appealed to voters in the South-East to support Tinubu’s re-election, telling a women’s empowerment gathering in Imo State: “Make una vote for Mr President, we go work for una and Nigeria go better.”

title: Britain and Germany review joint strike programme
body: Luke Pollard hosted the German State Secretary for Armament and Innovation at Lancaster House for talks covering Deep Precision Strike and wider defence industrial cooperation, with both countries reviewing joint capability programmes under the Trinity House Agreement, according to the Ministry of Defence. Pollard, the Minister for Defence Readiness and Industry, met Jens Plötner on 15 October under the United Kingdom and Germany Ministerial Group on Equipment and Capability Cooperation. He described Germany as “one of our closest and most valued defence partners.” Senior officials and military leaders from both countries attended, including Rupert Pearce, the National Armaments Director, and Vice Admiral Carsten Stawitzki, his German counterpart. A panel discussion at the German Embassy followed, with Philipp Kerth of Hypersonica and Katherine Williams of Rolls-Royce taking part alongside officials. Deep Precision Strike is the joint effort to field a long-range strike capability with a reach beyond two thousand kilometres, committed to in the Trinity House Agreement signed in October 2024. That agreement covers air, land, maritime, cyber and space cooperation and now sits under the Kensington Treaty signed in July 2025. The talks followed the Prime Minister’s visit to Berlin on 8 October, where the two countries agreed to deepen space cooperation and to establish a Counter-Hybrid Partnership aimed at grey zone threats. Trinity House has produced more concrete activity than most bilateral defence agreements manage in two years. German P-8 Poseidon crews have operated from Lossiemouth, the two countries have worked together on uncrewed systems, and Rheinmetall has expanded its British footprint, with the barrel factory at Telford announced under the agreement. The post Britain and Germany review joint strike programme first appeared on UK Defence Journal .

title: Is David Warner right in questioning Test cricket's supremacy over poor crowd attendance?
body: The warning signs were there by the time the first ball was bowled in the first Test between South Africa and Australia in Durban earlier this month. The reigning and previous world Test champions were facing off once again, with wounds from the ball-tampering saga from the previous visit still not full healed. And yet, barely anyone turned up for the opening Test. Or for the second match in Gqeberha. Former Australia opener, and a central figure in the ball-tampering scandal of 2018, David Warner put it rather bluntly. "We keep hearing how important Test cricket is, but where are the fans in South Africa? Empty stands, no atmosphere, and we’re supposed to believe the format is thriving? You can’t keep calling Test cricket the pinnacle of the game if no one turns up to watch it. Harsh reality, but someone has to say it. Pathetic," Warner posted on social media. We keep hearing how important Test cricket is, but where are the fans in South Africa? Empty stands, no atmosphere, and we’re supposed to believe the format is thriving? You can’t keep calling Test cricket the pinnacle of the game if no one turns up to watch it. Harsh reality,… — David Warner (@davidwarner31) October 20, 2026 Warner was a batter who started his career almost exclusively as a T20 batter, and then forced his way into Test cricket. He ended up playing over 100 Tests. A lot of it got taken away from him after the sandpaper saga, with Warner losing any hopes of a future leadership position. He knows how high the stakes are for players. And what it means if there is no one to witness their battles. After the opening Test, a Cricket South Africa official said they will look into the reasons for low attendance for a marquee home series. "A Test match of this quality, featuring the Proteas and Australia, deserved greater support in the stands," Heinrich Strydom, chief executive of KwaZulu-Natal Cricket Union, said in a statement. "While we recognise that supporters face competing demands on their time and finances, we must also understand better what influences their decisions to attend and what more we can do to make live cricket an attractive and worthwhile experience. "This is something we will reflect on through a thorough internal review." Former South Africa batter Daryll Cullinan had already warned that the series had many factors going against it. In his piece for Cricinfo, Cullinan said that hosting a series in South Africa in October, when heavy rains are commonplace, and on underprepared surfaces was inviting trouble. Test Cricket in places that struggle for crowds should make it FREE to enter! Boards should make their money off their franchise tournaments. There is no way that Durban and PE have made enough money off ticket sales to justify no one there watching. — Kevin Pietersen🦏 (@KP24) October 21, 2026 Fewer patrons The situation is grim in most parts of the cricket world, barring England, Australia and a handful of centres in India. Most cricket boards simply can't afford to host Test matches as broadcasters are not queueing up to show them in the first place. A majority of Test series now are two-game affairs, just to meet minimum requirements. T20 cricket now bankrolls the entire system, first via franchise leagues and then internationals. Everything else feeds off it. Test matches in England are still viewed by a full crowd while Australia too boasts healthy attendances for five-day matches. In India, places such as Mumbai, Delhi, Kolkata, Chennai and Bengaluru get good crowds but they are not always allowed to host Tests due to rotation of venues. And how long will even the traditional Test centres continue to attract good crowds? Test patrons are not getting any younger. The next generation simply does not consume cricket the way Test cricket serves its fares. When a 112-Test veteran like Warner spells it out as clearly as that, there is no hiding from it - Test cricket is being propped up and will continue to require support. The moment you are at the mercy of the elements, one can't complain if the wind changes direction. For now, franchise leagues and T20s are pumping in money, allowing most cricket boards to pay the bills and keep the ball rolling at the domestic level. If some cricket boards decide Test cricket does not make financial sense, don't hold it against them. If you feel passionately about Test cricket, make sure to attend next time a match is held at a venue near you.

title: Why some Ontario voters are turning to AI chatbots for 2026 municipal elections
body:
Eric Apps had an inkling of who would get his vote in Toronto’s municipal election , but the lawyer wanted a second opinion before making his final decision.
In Parkdale-High Park, his usual safe choice in longtime councillor Gord Perks was taken away when the 63-year-old decided to retire. The race for the city’s west-end ward has ballooned to 10 candidates — none of whom Apps is familiar with.
He turned to a system he was familiar with: Claude, Anthropic’s artificial intelligence chatbot. Apps asked the bot for the top five polling candidates in his ward and their policies on issues such as bike lanes, housing and property taxes.
“It laid them all out in a very easily digestible format,” he said.
Apps is not the only one turning to AI for election information. During Quebec’s provincial election earlier this month, an estimated 40 per cent of the province’s voters turned to AI chatbots and received false and outdated information about the election, according to McGill University researchers. Many Quebec news outlets don’t allow chatbots to access their websites, so their reports cannot be mined for users’ queries.
Experts say this marks a troubling shift in the democratic process, where citizen engagement and human judgment is superseded by some algorithms that could be providing false information.
There were a few gaps in Apps’ own search, he noted. The chatbot could not provide much information on candidates who weren’t as widely reported on by news outlets or who didn’t have very active online presences. He acknowledged that some of the gaps could be related to the parameters of his questions.
“The blind spots are probably in the eyes of the beholders,” Apps said. “If you have your point of view going into it, then it probably is going to be giving back information that is not necessarily going to focus on opening your eyes.”
Alissa Centivany, an associate professor of Information and media studies at Western University, said artificial intelligence bots have replaced traditional search engines, such as Google, and reliable media platforms, such as news organizations’ websites.
For some voters, chatbots have become their main method of seeking information.
For AI researchers like Centivany, it remains unclear what an AI chatbot’s “technical process” is as it scrapes the internet for information. Centivany notes that the quality of information AI chatbots can compile is often lower than she would hope for, especially in the context of political elections.
One concerning element, she said, is that the mishmash of information it gathers can include user-generated content from social media sites like Reddit. Centivany said researchers are starting to see evidence of how a bot will compile information based on what they think a user will want to hear, based on past queries, as opposed to objective facts.
“A lot of it is opinion, a lot of it is untrue, a lot of it is inflammatory,” she said. “And it’s being used as a source of information.”
As he asked Claude more questions about candidates in his ward, Apps said he was also keenly aware of its limitations, especially with the influx of content on social media platforms, such as TikTok and Instagram.
“You have to take your AI engine with a grain of salt,” he said. “It gave me the basic information and then it puts it back to the viewer.”
The accessibility of the AI platforms made political participation easier, Apps said. While he considers himself somewhat politically aware, he said the chatbot acted as an information “refresher.”
“You ask it a question and it gives you an answer,” he said. “It’s not giving you glossy videos with clickbait-ish headlines.”
Anthropic said Claude uses web search to find up-to-date information and shows its sourcing so users can “judge their credibility for themselves.”
“Claude is trained to note when claims are disputed, when sources conflict, or when a source may be inaccurate or have an agenda,” the company said in a statement to The Canadian Press.
Earlier this month, Anthropic announced new updates to its usage policies, which included a “refocusing” of their elections section and political content restrictions.
“We’ve further sharpened our section on elections, focusing it specifically on disallowing the use of Claude to deceive voters or disrupt elections (for instance, by spreading false information about candidates or how to vote, impersonating candidates or election officials, or trying to suppress turnout),” the company’s news release read.
Alex Marland, a professor of Canadian politics and the Jarislowsky Chair in Trust and Political Leadership at Acadia University, said it makes sense that voters would turn to an accessible tool such as AI for information about candidates in elections.
Typically, people might vote for the political party they most align with, but candidates in Ontario municipal elections are not affiliated with a party.
“What ends up happening is you have to invest a lot more time to try to understand, ‘What are my choices and what do these people stand for?'” Marland said.
It’s a positive sign that voters want to get engaged in municipal politics, Marland said, since Ontario’s last municipal election had record-low voter turnout. According to the Association of Municipalities of Ontario, the average voter turnout in the 2022 was almost 33 per cent, compared to roughly 38 per cent in 2018.
But it’s up to users to be vigilant in fact-checking the information they’re receiving, Marland added.
“This is a piece of information that is going in with other pieces of information.”

title: In the Shadow of the Front
body:
Beyond a checkpoint north of Kharkiv, an old road sign puts the Russian city of Belgorod about 70 kilometers (43 miles) away. Yet the nearest Russian soldiers are much closer.
Leaving the city behind, the road winds through a belt of villages well in range of the front’s danger. Russian troops occupied these settlements early in the full-scale invasion, before Ukrainian forces reclaimed them in stages from spring to September 2022.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
A military quad bike travels beneath protective netting stretched over the road and along its sides to obstruct approaching attack drones. (Photo by Korbinian Leo Kramer) Advertisement
A military quad bike travels beneath protective netting stretched over the road and along its sides to obstruct approaching attack drones. (Photo by Korbinian Leo Kramer)
Beside the road, deep anti-tank ditches and wire obstacles now guard against a renewed Russian advance. While Kharkiv’s parks are still meticulously tended, sustaining its reputation as Ukraine’s cleanest city, the defenses beyond it have thickened since the beginning of the year. Military pickups appear more frequently, moving fast between the villages and Ukrainian positions holding the line beyond Lyptsi, toward Hlyboke and Lukyantsi.
Coils of defensive concertina razor wire fill a deep ditch cutting through farmland north of Kharkiv, part of the fortifications protecting the approaches to the city. (Photo by Korbinian Leo Kramer) Other Topics of Interest Moldova Expels Russian Diplomat After Drone Crash Moldova has declared a Russian diplomat persona non grata after an explosive Geran drone crashed near family homes and an energy site.
Coils of defensive concertina razor wire fill a deep ditch cutting through farmland north of Kharkiv, part of the fortifications protecting the approaches to the city. (Photo by Korbinian Leo Kramer)
Roofless houses stand among overgrown gardens and ruins as protective netting follows the dips and rises of the countryside. Smoke hovers above the fields, though the frontline trenches remain out of sight.
Vegetation grows through the exposed steel frame of a ruined hall. Torn roof panels hang above debris, while daylight filters through holes in the surviving metal sheets. (Photo by Korbinian Leo Kramer) Advertisement
Vegetation grows through the exposed steel frame of a ruined hall. Torn roof panels hang above debris, while daylight filters through holes in the surviving metal sheets. (Photo by Korbinian Leo Kramer)
Rain sets in along the route. A wrecked bridge leaves little prospect of getting through, forcing the car to turn back. Nearby, an older woman in a green poncho is making her way through the downpour on crutches.
