Officers seized a mobile phone, computers, a hard drive and a folder containing Pizza Fan tax and statistical documents. They also recovered a black case containing four vintage lighters and two gold-coloured pocket watches. Searches at other properties uncovered additional evidence, including diaries containing notes covering the years 2023 to 2026. Across all locations, authorities seized €1,288,732.60 in cash, 52 computer units, six luxury cars, three motorcycles, mobile phones, laptops, storage devices and other digital evidence. Authorities will transfer the cash to the Deposits and Loans Fund, while forensic specialists will examine the digital evidence. Special software allegedly enabled sales without receipts According to the police investigation, the organisation had operated an alleged revenue-concealment mechanism since 2016, using specialised software that allowed restaurants to complete orders without issuing the legally required receipts. Investigators say the system relied on a function known as kerasma , meaning “treat” or “complimentary item”. The software recorded and processed orders normally but allowed selected transactions to be completed without generating receipts. The transactions remained in the central system, which allegedly enabled the network to track actual turnover and calculate the revenue concealed from tax authorities. The case file describes distinct roles among the alleged members, including management, financial administration, software support and coordination of individual stores. Some individuals allegedly collected and transferred money generated by undeclared transactions. Authorities are also examining reports that members received warnings about impending tax inspections. Investigators examine financial flows and overseas company links As part of the financial investigation, authorities examined the company’s corporate structure and the involvement of a company based abroad. Investigators are tracing financial flows and the movement of funds allegedly generated by the network. Authorities have also initiated proceedings to freeze assets belonging to individuals and legal entities, following a request from the Directorate for Combating Organised Crime to the Authority for the Prevention of Money Laundering. Investigators prepared 108 audit reports covering 2023, 2024, 2025 and 2026 and forwarded them to Greece’s Independent Authority for Public Revenue (AADE) to determine the taxes allegedly evaded. The arrested individuals appeared before the competent prosecutor. The investigation remains ongoing, and the allegations must be established through the judicial process. Former franchise owner alleges pressure and threats A former franchise owner, who operated a store for approximately three to four years, has described alleged pressure he experienced after refusing to follow practices he said others demanded of him. “I did not agree with what was happening. I wanted to leave. I did not want to do it. They pressured us through intimidation. There was intimidation in general. ‘If you don’t do what I tell you, I’ll shut your shop down,’” he said. He added that franchise operators who had experienced similar pressure should not be held responsible for the alleged scheme. Cash stored in plastic bags found at alleged deputy leader’s home Images broadcast by SKAI television’s Report at 10 programme showed cash stored in plastic bags, reportedly discovered during a search of the home of a person described in the case file as the alleged organisation’s deputy leader. The images add to the evidence seized during the operation, which included more than €1.28 million in cash, 92 luxury watches, jewellery, electronic devices and other items. title: Ukraine continues to receive intelligence from CIA, despite strained relations between Trump and Zelenskyy – media
body:
The U.S. intelligence community continues to assist Ukraine in defending itself against Russian aggression—notably by providing early warnings of incoming missiles and drones—even as relations between President Donald Trump and President Volodymyr Zelenskyy remain poor, reports The Atlantic.
Citing an unnamed high-ranking officer who frequently visits Ukraine, the publication notes that the CIA plays a leading role among American personnel in the country. The source also remarked that, with the CIA’s help, Ukrainians have become very adept at carrying out strikes against Russia.
Another intelligence official based in the Baltic states, who works closely with the USA to counter Russian influence, told the publication that CIA operations are currently much more aggressive than they were during the administration of former President Joe Biden, though you would never know it from Trump’s rhetoric.
“The administration’s policy is deeply conflicted, and perhaps no one understands that better than John Ratcliffe, the director of the Central Intelligence Agency. He has a foot in two worlds: advising a president who’s continuously at odds with Ukraine’s leadership, and running an agency that’s essential to Ukraine’s war for survival … ,” the article says.
Ukrainians do not view Ratcliffe as their defender. They know that he works for an unpredictable boss and that, should Trump carry out his recent threat to cut off intelligence support unless Ukraine stops attacking Russian oil refineries, Ratcliffe will follow that order, The Atlantic added.
Sources familiar with the matter describe Ratcliffe as someone who clearly understands the threat that the Russian Federation poses not only to Ukraine but also to the United States and its allies. The same can be said of U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth, both of whom have now aligned themselves with Trump’s rhetoric.
According to the report, the CIA Director has likely advised Ukrainian President Zelenskyy on how to engage with Trump.
Commenting on disruptions to the Starlink satellite network and American early-warning systems, the publication notes that the USA has not yet officially cut off the flow of intelligence, though Trump could take such measures at any moment. The ezine says that should Trump decide to do so, those who have worked with Ratcliffe say he would not attempt to persuade the president to change his mind even despite concerns within CIA headquarters.

title: APC accuses Atiku, ADC of plot to discredit Kaduna rally
body: The All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council has accused former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar and his African Democratic Congress (ADC) of plotting to discredit its presidential campaign flag-off in Kaduna. The council alleged that the opposition planned to deploy fake news, artificial intelligence-generated content and deepfake videos to undermine the rally, President Bola Tinubu, Kaduna State Governor Uba Sani and APC leaders. This is contained in a statement by Mr Dele Alake, spokesperson of the council, on Saturday, ahead of the campaign flag-off in Kaduna. “We have uncovered a well-orchestrated, devious plan by former Vice President Atiku Abubakar and his party to discredit the APC presidential campaign flag-off in Kaduna today (Saturday),” he said. Insults can’t stop growing rejection of your party, ADC replies APC Kaduna Govt Debunks N2.3trn APC Campaign Spending Claim Alake alleged that the opposition had used misleading narratives and manipulated reports to influence public opinion and portray the APC rally negatively. He cited the circulation of a photograph showing a security vehicle on routine patrol near an APC campaign billboard in Kaduna metropolis. According to him, the opposition allegedly misrepresents the photograph as evidence that security personnel are deployed to protect APC billboards. The APC presidential campaign council spokesman also accused the opposition of circulating a purported letter from the Kaduna state governor to Sen. Abdulaziz Yari, Director-General of the campaign council. The alleged letter claims that the state government has released N2.3 trillion to host the rally. “We are still at a loss as to how anyone can imagine and concoct this senseless and utterly baseless lie that defies logic and basic common sense,” he said. He argued that the amount was inconsistent with the state’s annual budgets, noting that the Kaduna state budgets for 2024, 2025 and 2026 totalled less than N2.3 trillion. He puts the budgets at N458.271 billion for 2024, N790.439 billion for 2025 and N985.9 billion for 2026. Alake further alleged that the opposition planned to circulate old, doctored and deepfake videos during the rally to create a false impression of public resentment. “We hereby use this opportunity to alert the general public about this malicious and ignoble plan,” he added. He described Atiku and the ADC’s alleged actions as attempts to undermine the APC’s electoral prospects and urged Nigerians to reject what it called disinformation. He also called on the public to remain vigilant against misleading content circulating online and in the media.

title: Zelensky imposes sanctions on Russian ballistic weapons makers and defense industry component suppliers
body:
According to Ukrinform, this was reported by the Office of the President.
“Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky signed decrees enacting the decision of the National Security and Defense Council of Ukraine to impose sanctions against Russian entities and individuals who assist in the production of Russian ballistic missiles, as well as those who supply the Russian defense industry with equipment and components for military aircraft, armored vehicles, missile systems, and drones,” the statement reads.
The first sanctions list includes 51 individuals and 44 entities involved in the manufacture of ballistic missiles, which Russia uses to attack critical and civilian infrastructure, shell Ukrainian cities and communities, and kill people. These are key enterprises that produce and supply raw materials, equipment, and tools for the creation of long-range weapons such as the “Iskander,” “Kalibr,” Kh-101, and “Kinzhal.”
The sanctions package specifically targets the following enterprises and their executives: “G. S. Petrov Institute of Plastics”—Russia’s sole manufacturer of a range of components for composite materials supplied to plants in the defense, aerospace, aviation, and shipbuilding sectors; “Kometa Special-Purpose Space Systems Corporation”—the lead enterprise of a research and production group that manufactures anti-aircraft missile systems, radar equipment, and avionics systems; “VitaReaktiv” is a company specializing in chemical raw materials and involved in the production of ballistic missile weapons; “Promenergo” develops optical, laser, and optoelectronic devices, as well as information and targeting systems, and conducts testing of onboard equipment; “Kirov Biochemical Plant” is involved in the production and modernization of weapons and military equipment; “D. I. Mendeleev All-Russian Scientific Research Institute of Metrology” conducts scientific research, manufactures measuring equipment, and develops software for weapons and military equipment.
Sanctions have also been imposed on 32 Russian citizens and 35 Russian companies. Among them are enterprises involved in the production and supply chains of high-precision industrial equipment, tools, and components, as well as electronics and raw materials for entities serving the Russian defense-industrial complex.
These include: “Gagaring,” which specializes in the sale of communications and control hardware for FPV drones; “Virgin-EK,” which supplies foreign electronic components to Russian invaders; the “Pressmash” Machine Tool Association, which specializes in the wholesale trade of metal-cutting machine tools supplied to factories involved in the production of the Kh-101 and Kh-59 missiles and the “Orion” UAV.
Sanctions have also been imposed on enterprises within the Russian industrial group “RUSAL” that are of critical importance to the aggressor country and are involved in the manufacture of military aircraft, armored vehicles, missile systems, drones, and other military products. From April 2024 to March 2025, “RUSAL Trading House” and “RUSAL Taishet Aluminum Plant” alone imported nearly 150 million rubles worth of aluminum oxide into Russia. Supplies of this raw material were used to manufacture military aircraft, missile systems, armored vehicles, and drones.
“We are systematically identifying and imposing sanctions on companies involved in the production of Russian ballistic missiles and other weapons systems. We are working to extend these sanctions to other jurisdictions. Collectively, this should significantly weaken the Russian defense industry’s ability to produce weapons,” said Vladyslav Vlasiuk, the President’s Special Advisor on Sanctions Policy.
As reported by Ukrinform, in September, the Main Intelligence Directorate of the Ukrainian Ministry of Defense released information on 23 Russian enterprises involved in production cooperation to develop 95Ya6 anti-aircraft guided missiles for the “Pantsir” anti-aircraft missile and gun systems.

title: Sexual abuse should trigger police investigations, not community intervention – Felicity Nelson
body: The Deputy Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Tourism Development Company, Felicity Nelson, has called for an end to the practice of traditional and religious leaders intervening to seek private settlements in sexual abuse cases instead of allowing the police to investigate. Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, October 24, Ms Nelson said the practice of elders, chiefs, queen mothers, pastors and imams pleading on behalf of alleged perpetrators of sexual offences undermines accountability and must be discouraged. Her comments follow allegations of sexual abuse involving female students at Obuasi Senior High Technical School, which have raised concerns about child protection and the handling of complaints within educational institutions. “We have to look culturally as Ghanaians and say this idea that when someone commits a crime, especially of a sexual nature, where elders, church leaders, imams, chiefs and queen mothers go and beg on their behalf needs to stop,” she stated. “If it was even my wish, we need to criminalise it,” she added. Ms Nelson stressed that allegations of sexual abuse must be subjected to thorough investigations rather than resolved through informal interventions, while safeguarding the rights of all parties involved. She also urged authorities to prioritise the welfare of the alleged victims by ensuring they receive adequate psychological, emotional and medical support. “Of course, all allegations must be investigated. As it stands now, these still remain allegations, so we are still saying yes, let’s investigate. However, I want us to prioritise the victims in this case, their wants, their needs,” she said. “We need to ensure that they are fine. We need to ensure that psychologically they are okay, emotionally they are fine. In terms of health, we need to do those checks,” she emphasised. Highlighting the broader problem of sexual abuse in Ghana, Ms Nelson cited UNICEF reports which, according to her, indicated that 22 per cent of adolescent girls had experienced some form of sexual abuse, while another report suggested that 51 per cent of girls in secondary schools experienced sexual abuse between 2019 and 2021. She described the situation as endemic, warning that the allegations at Obuasi Senior High Technical School reflect a wider national concern, with many incidents going unreported. “This is endemic, it’s a serious issue. Inasmuch as we are talking about Obuasi, we need to be mindful of the fact that this is not just happening at Obuasi,” she noted. The Deputy CEO further called for stronger safeguarding systems to protect children, ensure complaints are appropriately handled and prevent alleged perpetrators from escaping scrutiny through community interventions.

title: Type 31 costs rising in labour and the supply chain
body: Inflation is pushing up the cost of the Type 31 frigate programme across labour and the wider supply chain, and the Ministry of Defence is assessing what that does to the affordability of the programme as a whole, according to an answer given in Parliament. Ben Obese-Jecty, the Conservative member for Huntingdon, had asked ministers to set out which areas of the programme are under inflationary pressure, following up an answer given on 6 October. Luke Pollard, Minister of State for Defence Readiness and Industry, said: “The Type 31 programme is experiencing inflationary pressures across a number of areas, including labour and the wider supply chain. The Ministry of Defence continues to assess the effect of these pressures on the programme and its overall affordability.” Babcock is building five Type 31 frigates at Rosyth under a contract awarded in 2019 worth around £1.25 billion, based on the Iver Huitfeldt design, with the first of class named HMS Venturer. The programme supports around two and a half thousand skilled jobs across Scotland and the wider United Kingdom supply chain, including four hundred apprenticeships. Ministers told Parliament earlier this month that they were monitoring the schedule for the class alongside Babcock. Norway has since selected the Type 26 design for its own frigate programme, and the Defence Investment Plan sets out further orders for crewed warships alongside the hybrid Navy of uncrewed and autonomous systems. The post Type 31 costs rising in labour and the supply chain first appeared on UK Defence Journal .

title: Abeiku Santana raises concerns over access to GTA CEO Maame Efua Houadjeto
body: Deputy Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Tourism Authority (GTA) in charge of Marketing and Special Duties, Gilbert Abeiku Aggrey aka Santana, has asked the Tourism Minister to intervene in recurring difficulties accessing the Authority’s CEO, Maame Efua Houadjeto, for urgent consultations. In a letter dated Thursday, 22nd October 2026, and addressed to the Minister of Tourism, Culture and Creative Arts, Abla Dzifa Gomashie, Abeiku said the challenge was affecting his ability to obtain timely guidance, approvals and decisions needed to carry out his responsibilities, particularly in domestic tourism, special events and marketing. “On several occasions, I have had to request meetings through the CEO’s secretary or personal assistant, only to be informed that she is unavailable,” he stated. He acknowledged the demands on the CEO’s schedule but said the situation had made it difficult for him to perform his duties effectively. “This situation sometimes causes delays in operations, stakeholder engagements, and the implementation of key assignments,” Mr Aggrey wrote. He also stressed that his concerns were not intended as a personal complaint but were aimed at addressing what he considers a communication gap within the institution. “My intention is not to make a personal complaint, but to highlight a communication gap that needs to be addressed in the interest of effective management and institutional efficiency,” he said. Abeiku has consequently asked the Minister to intervene to help establish a more effective arrangement for communication and consultation between himself and the CEO, particularly on urgent official matters. “I therefore respectfully seek your intervention, with the knowledge of the Board Chairperson, to help establish a more effective communication and consultation arrangement between the CEO and my office, especially on urgent official matters,” he stated. Despite the concerns raised, Mr Aggrey reaffirmed his commitment to working with the CEO and the Authority’s management team. “I remain committed to working professionally with the CEO and the entire management team to achieve the Ministry’s objectives and strengthen the performance of the Ghana Tourism Authority,” he said. Abeiku’s Appointment President John Dramani Mahama appointed Abeiku Santana as Deputy Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Tourism Authority in February 2025 after the National Democratic Congress assumed office on 7th January 2025. Abeiku Santana is a broadcaster, tourism advocate and entrepreneur with experience in media, marketing, travel and hospitality. He is the Chief Executive Officer of Kaya Tours Ghana Limited and holds a master’s degree in Tourism Management from the University of Cape Coast and a master’s degree in Marketing Strategy from the University of Ghana Business School.

title: Gendarmerie armored vehicles deployed to Paris streets ahead of mass protests
body:
PARIS, October 24. /TASS /. Armored vehicles of the French Gendarmerie have appeared on the streets of Paris ahead of scheduled mass demonstrations, a TASS correspondent reported.
Several armored vehicles are stationed near the Elysee Palace, where the security perimeter has been expanded beyond its usual size. Law enforcement officers have blocked access to streets adjacent to the French leader’s residence using vans and metal barriers.
Additional armored vehicles, along with a large number of police officers and gendarmes, are deployed near the National Assembly (the lower house of parliament). Numerous police and Gendarmerie vehicles are also parked along streets near major tourist attractions, including the Champs-Elysees, the Eiffel Tower, the Arc de Triomphe, and various other locations throughout the city.
A mass demonstration involving trade unions and student movements is expected in Paris on Saturday. The Paris Prefecture rejected the organizers' requested route from the Place de la Bastille to the Place de la Nation, authorizing instead a march on the city's periphery from the Porte d'Italie metro station to the Porte de Vincennes metro station. Following the riots and looting that marred demonstrations last Saturday, October 17, the French Interior Ministry pledged to significantly bolster security measures, increasing the number of police and Gendarmerie personnel deployed to maintain order from 10,000 to 70,000. Up to 500,000 people are expected to take part in protests across France on October 24.

title: Trump makes Alaska the latest frontier in his election power grab
body: President Donald Trump is escalating his crusade to exert control of America’s elections as his party barrels towards a potentially bruising midterm. The Justice Department has already filed lawsuits in nearly every state to try and gain access to voter files. Trump revisited his longstanding bid to restrict mail voting, sparking a legal battle that reached the Supreme Court. He sought to make anti-terrorism funds for state and local governments contingent on how they administer elections. He has threatened to withhold federal election funding from states that refuse to change voter registration forms and sparred with Republican lawmakers over a bill to overhaul elections. But with most of those efforts stalling, on Thursday, just 12 days before Election Day, the DOJ took things even further: In an extraordinary move, it asked a court to preemptively block Alaska’s Senate results if Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan loses, stunning current and former election officials in both parties. “Boy, they are scraping the bottom of the barrel. It feels like a real desperation play to me, because it has got zero basis in the law,” said Ben Ginsberg, a veteran Republican election law expert who was counsel to George W. Bush’s 2000 and 2004 presidential campaigns. At virtually every corner, courts have rebuffed Trump’s efforts, and legal experts expect the latest DOJ maneuver to have the same outcome. The requests for voter rolls were blocked repeatedly by members of Trump’s own party and struck down in court . The attempt to restrict mail voting was ultimately blocked by the Supreme Court. Federal judges blocked both the anti-terrorism and election funding efforts. The SAVE Act, which would require voters to provide proof of citizenship at the polls, has stalled in the Senate. But Trump keeps pushing, telling reporters Friday that he had personally green-lit the Alaska lawsuit: “I'm the one that said 'Do it.’” The gambit is another sign that Trump is once again ramping up his efforts to exert greater control over how elections are administered — with officials bracing for what may come next. “I think there is an attempt to lay a foundation to say, ‘If we had won these lawsuits, we would have won the election,’” Gabriel Sterling, a Republican and former senior Georgia elections official who sparred with Trump over his false claims of fraud in the state in 2020, said of the Alaska lawsuit. “So, for them, filing and losing for them is the same difference, tactically speaking, potentially.” Trump has been claiming elections were being stolen from him since the 2016 primaries , and his wide-ranging legal and political attempts to overturn his 2020 election loss sparked a riot at the U.S. Capitol in January 2021, even as some in his party want him to move on . “The federal government is his company, and he gets to call all the shots of his company, and that's just never how it's been done before,” said Stephen Richer, Maricopa County, Arizona’s former GOP chief election official. POLITICO reached out to the offices of every Republican statewide election official in America for a response to the DOJ’s action in Alaska. Four declined to comment, and the rest did not respond. Their silence shows just how powerful Trump remains in the party, and how few are willing to cross him just days before November’s midterms. "The survival rate politically of people who oppose Donald Trump on this issue is not great if you're Republican,” said Richer, who was ousted by a more conservative Republican in a 2024 primary after defending the county’s 2020 election results against a yearslong campaign from Trump and his allies to try to prove they were rigged . Arizona Democratic Secretary of State Adrian Fontes railed against the DOJ’s lawsuit, accusing the department of “working as the president's lawyers.” “The Department of Justice is acting in a monstrously political way, and it's purely inappropriate, and they lose a lot of credibility by putting their thumb on the scales,” Fontes said in an interview Friday afternoon. “This attempt in Alaska, if it comes to Arizona, will also fail.” The Justice Department, in a statement posted on social media , said "claims that DOJ is trying to stop Alaska’s election are FALSE." Instead, the DOJ argued it was "seeking to protect election integrity, consistent with the National Voter Registration Act (enacted by Congress) and ensure the will of Alaska voters is respected." Washington state Attorney General Nick Brown, a Democrat, described the legal filing in Alaska as “part of a concerted effort to control the election and to try to dictate the outcome in Donald Trump and the Republican Party’s favor.” Brown said he worried the administration would contest the results of the midterms. “That is not hypothetical,” Brown said. “This is what the president has done for years now, and he has the entire power of government, and most importantly, the Department of Justice around elections, acting at his request.” Sterling predicted the effort would backfire on the GOP. “By talking about stolen elections, by talking about cheating, they're suppressing their own vote and they're encouraging the votes of their opponents,” he said. “So tactically, I think it's politically moronic.” The DOJ lawsuit in Alaska comes less than two weeks before a midterm election cycle in which Republicans are bracing for losses across the map . And the Trump administration’s increasing interventions are raising questions about how far his administration intends to go in trying to assert federal authority over elections that by law are run by state and local officials. A current Georgia Republican election official, granted anonymity to discuss internal deliberations around the Alaska lawsuit, said they are prepared to forcefully push back on any action from the federal government. “Bring it on,” the official said. “I think there's zero credible way for any entity, much less the DOJ, to say that the election results in Georgia are suspect.” The lawsuit is the culmination of years of escalating tensions between the federal government and state election officials over election proceedings. In February , a typically staid gathering of the nation’s top election officials turned fiery when Utah Lt. Gov. Deidre Henderson, a Republican and her state’s chief election official, confronted a senior White House aide over the DOJ’s voter roll push. The DOJ “pretty much slandered all of us to publicly claim that secretaries of state are not doing our jobs and that the federal government has to do it for us. Not OK,” Henderson said to White House Deputy Director of Intergovernmental Affairs Jared Borg, as her colleagues and reporters looked on. On Wednesday, Henderson’s office received a letter from the Justice Department informing her that election monitors will be sent to her state. Her office responded the next day by distributing instructions to poll workers noting that the DOJ observers “must not interfere with voting” and giving guidance in case “a situation arises involving law enforcement or legal demands.” Henderson was unsparing in a recent interview with CBS News . "In the past two elections that I oversaw as lieutenant governor the threats were all external," she said. "But now we also have threats coming from within our own government." Lisa Kashinsky contributed to this report.

title: U-17 WWC: Busari reveals how Flamingos recovered from Poland shock
body:
Nigeria’s Flamingos head coach Akeem Busari has praised his players for their resilience and determination after they bounced back from their defeat to Poland to stun defending champions North Korea 3-1 in their final Group B fixture at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup .
The victory marked a significant response from the Nigerian side, who had suffered a disappointing 2-1 loss to Poland before recovering with a 2-0 win over Puerto Rico and an impressive performance against the North Koreans.
Busari, who took charge of the team in April, reflected on the progress made under his leadership, the disappointment of losing to Poland, and the need for his players to maintain their belief as they pursue their ambitions at the tournament.
The coach explained that the defeat to Poland was a rare setback for a team that had enjoyed an encouraging run of results in preparation for the competition.
“Like I said to somebody while we were talking, the Poland game was the first game we had lost since I took over the team in April this year. We have played a series of about 20-something friendlies,” Busari said.
“During the qualification, we played four games and won all of them, while at WAFU-B, we won all five games. Poland was a shocker to us, but we just had to let it go. We had to restrategise and look at ourselves.
“We had to ask ourselves if that was really what we saw within ourselves. We needed to come back, and this victory was one of the fights for that comeback.”
The Flamingos coach also addressed the role of officiating in football, acknowledging that mistakes can happen while insisting that his players must respect decisions made by match officials and remain focused on their own performance.
Busari stressed that resilience, self-belief and discipline were essential qualities for any team hoping to compete for a major title.
“Human errors happen. Referees are human beings, and they can make mistakes, just as we can as humans,” he said.
“But nevertheless, it is a game in which they are in charge. We just have to respect whatever decisions come. We cannot be a team or even champions without perseverance and self-belief. These are part of the discipline required of a good team with a good culture.
“Whatever they are doing to us, they are balancing it with the other team as well.”
The coach also pointed to fatigue and lapses in concentration as factors that affected his players during the match, explaining that the technical crew attempted to manage the game through substitutions and other tactical adjustments.
According to Busari, the Flamingos had to work hard to preserve their energy as the contest progressed, but the opposition continued to introduce fresh players.
“For our girls, it was a loss of concentration at that moment. You could see that we tried to slow things down with substitutions and do everything possible to manage what we had,” he explained.
“But they kept introducing players, and endurance was really beginning to tell on our girls. Nevertheless, the players kept fighting.”
The victory over North Korea will provide the Flamingos with renewed confidence as they continue their campaign, but Busari’s message remains clear: Nigeria must maintain its discipline, learn from its setbacks and keep believing in its ability to compete with the best.
Flamingos midfielder Rodiat Yusuf was equally delighted after Nigeria’s impressive victory, describing the result as the product of teamwork, determination and the players’ commitment to carrying out their coach’s instructions.
Yusuf, who was named Player of the Match, said the team approached the encounter determined to secure the result they needed and was pleased that their collective effort delivered the desired outcome.
“I feel so excited because we were determined to get the result we wanted, and we achieved it through hard work, consistency and working as a team,” Yusuf said.
“With the help of the coach’s instructions, we were able to get the result. It is a good moment for me, scoring my first goal this March.”
Reflecting on the personal significance of her performance, Yusuf described the experience as a special memory while urging her teammates to maintain their focus and continue giving their best in every match.
“It is a good thing for me. It is a remarkable memory for me, and I am so excited. We got the win we wanted,” she said.
“We should just keep our heads up. This game has been played and it is gone. We just have to keep doing our best every time, in every match. We should give our 100 per cent and always get our maximum result.”
Yusuf’s comments reflect the determination within the Flamingos camp to move beyond individual achievements and concentrate on the bigger objective of progressing further in the tournament.
Meanwhile, Kemi Adegbuyi, who scored Nigeria’s opening goal against North Korea, expressed her gratitude after helping the Flamingos secure a memorable victory over the defending champions.
The forward credited God for the achievement and said the team entered the match with a clear objective: to win and collect all three points.
“I feel very, very happy, and I am very, very grateful to God because it is not by our power. It is God, yes,” Adegbuyi said.
Explaining how she found the net, the Nigerian forward said her quick reaction and determination to reach the ball ahead of the opposition helped her convert the opportunity.
“I think I was faster to the ball, and that made me score the goal. I was faster to the ball; I was quicker,” she explained.
“Our plan was to win, so our plan was to get the three points. We came out fully to play so we could get the three points.”
Adegbuyi also expressed confidence in Nigeria’s ability to challenge for the trophy, insisting that the Flamingos would continue to work towards their ultimate ambition.
“I believe we can win this tournament by His grace,” she added.
With Busari demanding perseverance, Yusuf emphasising consistency and Adegbuyi expressing belief in the team’s title ambitions, the Flamingos will hope their victory over North Korea becomes a turning point in their campaign.
After recovering from the disappointment against Poland, Nigeria have shown they can respond under pressure. The challenge now is to build on that performance, maintain their momentum and turn their renewed confidence into further progress at the U-17 Women’s World Cup.
Based on their last performance? No one would bet against that happening.

title: Turkey Calls on Greece to Recognise Elected Muftis in Thrace
body: Turkey has called on Greece to recognise muftis elected by the Muslim minority in Western Thrace, accusing Athens of violating religious freedoms and referring to the community as a “Turkish minority”. Education Minister Sofia Zacharaki and Didymoteicho Mufti Emin Serif (File photo) In a statement issued on October 24, 2026, Turkey’s Foreign Ministry criticised Greece’s appointment process for muftis in Komotini and Xanthi, arguing that it disregards fundamental rights protected by the 1923 Treaty of Lausanne and other international agreements. “The institution of the mufti is an integral part of the religious, social and cultural identity of the Turkish Minority of Western Thrace,” the Turkish Foreign Ministry said. The statement claimed that Greece ignores the community’s will and religious freedom by refusing to recognise the muftis it elects, and accused Athens of violating rights protected by international agreements. “We call on the Greek authorities to recognise the legitimate muftis elected by the Minority and to abandon efforts to impose appointed muftis,” the ministry concluded. Turkey’s statement reiterates Ankara’s position that the Muslim minority in Western Thrace constitutes a Turkish minority, a description that Greece does not officially recognise. The dispute centres on the appointment of religious leaders and the interpretation of minority rights under the Treaty of Lausanne. title: Russian Border Strikes and EU EES Challenge Checkpoints
body:
Russian strikes on border crossing infrastructure along Ukraine’s western frontiers, coupled with the EU’s rollout of its Entry/Exit System (EES), have introduced logistical complications, but border authorities are adapting to ensure stable movement, a senior Ukrainian border official said.
According to Ukrinform , Andrii Ivanskyi, deputy head of the administrative jurisdiction department of the State Border Guard Service of Ukraine (DPSU), outlined the compound operational pressures facing crossing points.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
“Despite the difficult conditions of war, Ukrainian border guards continue to protect the border, ensure proper crossing procedures on the western border with European Union countries, and carry out combat missions as part of the Defense Forces of Ukraine,” Ivanskyi said.
Ivanskyi explained that Russian forces have deliberately targeted border checkpoints since late August, attempting to disrupt civilian transport and commercial supply chains along Ukraine’s borders with Moldova , Romania , and Poland .
According to the DPSU representative, the physical bombardment of customs facilities and approach corridors is paired with an expanding spectrum of Russian hybrid operations engineered to generate disruption and psychological stress at checkpoints.
“The enemy uses hybrid threats – such as false bomb threats, power disruptions, and interference with operational databases – to increase the psychological pressure on checkpoint operations,” Ivanskyi noted.
Ivanskyi observed that recent months demonstrate how the war directly affects Ukraine’s western border, which also functions as the external border of the EU. He added that European partner nations have responded to Russian strikes in proximity to the frontier in accordance with their own national security protocols and sovereign interests.
“There is an understanding that this is the result of external aggression, rather than the consequence of our own actions or shortcomings,” Ivanskyi stated.
The logistical strain on western crossing points coincides with the EU’s implementation of the Entry/Exit System (EES), an automated digital framework registering non-EU citizens crossing external Schengen borders. The system requires biometric data collection – including facial scans and fingerprints – which can introduce procedural delays during initial processing phases.
Ivanskyi stated that Ukrainian border detachments are adjusting to the new regulatory requirements and explaining the procedural adjustments to departing citizens to mitigate congestion.
Despite ongoing Russian strikes on transit corridors, the overall volume of passenger crossings has remained stable, Ivanskyi reported. Border units process between 35 million and 37 million individual border crossings – covering both arrivals and departures – annually.
Ivanskyi recalled the initial days of the full-scale invasion in 2022, when Ukraine experienced the largest displaced population movement in Europe since World War II.
On March 9, 2022, a record 120,000 individuals crossed the frontier in a single 24-hour cycle, with over 5 million people exiting the country during the first 100 days of active conflict, enabled by emergency clearance procedures enacted by Poland, Hungary , Slovakia , and Romania.
Addressing unlawful border crossings, Ivanskyi confirmed that attempts to evade state controls persist – including by men subject to military mobilization – though the overall volume of such attempts has declined.
“We strive to ensure border security and remain reliable partners of the European Union,” Ivanskyi emphasized. “If foreign nationals cross the border illegally and are detained within EU territory, we cooperate with our partners, particularly through readmission procedures, to return these individuals to their countries of origin.
The relevant bilateral agreements are functional, protocols are signed, and institutional cooperation continues.”
Ivanskyi pointed to Poland’s operational framework in countering migration pressure, noting that Warsaw’s experience managing migration flows along its frontier with Belarus between 2020 and 2022 enabled Polish border authorities to establish rapid response and containment protocols.
The DPSU official emphasized that Ukraine is standardizing its border administration procedures to align with European Union accession benchmarks.
“We operate in accordance with the principles declared by Ukraine on its path to European integration, adopting European approaches to border management and adapting best practices to our operational realities,” Ivanskyi concluded.
“This applies to service organization at external frontiers, the standardization of internal procedures, and their practical implementation across all operational echelons.”

title: Dubai chocolate brand hailed by Sheikh Hamdan after clinching UAE award win in honour of global success
body: The home-grown brand behind the Dubai chocolate confectionery craze has enjoyed more sweet success after scooping a major UAE award. Fix Dessert, led by husband and wife team Sarah Hamouda and Yezen Alani, rose to global prominence in 2024 thanks to its Can’t Get Knafeh of It bar – a pistachio, knafeh and tahini-filled treat. The company has now been honoured for its remarkable foodie feats after being named as a winner in the inaugural Dubai-it prize, earning the accolade in the business projects category. Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed, Crown Prince of Dubai, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Defence, hailed the chocolate maker for its worldwide impact. "Sarah Hamouda and Yezen Alani transformed a home-based business in Dubai into a global success," Sheikh Hamdan said in a post on X. "Sales of Dubai-style chocolate surged by 1,234 per cent in one year, and today, these products are sold in markets around the world and at more than 100 airports. We announce that the Dubai-it Award for Projects in the Business Category goes to FIX Dessert, which introduced ‘Dubai Chocolate’ to the world. Sarah Hamouda and Yezen Alani transformed a home-based business in Dubai into a global success. Sales of Dubai-style chocolate surged by… pic.twitter.com/yKWxEVAAN2 — Hamdan bin Mohammed (@HamdanMohammed) October 24, 2026 "This is the spirit of Dubai-it: transforming a simple home-based business into a global success. Congratulations to the Fix Dessert team." Since launching online in 2021, the brand has grown to include two stores in Dubai International Airport, one at Singapore's Changi Airport and a concession at Harrods in London . They have also hosted several pop-ups in the UAE. It now offers a collection of 10 dessert bars, with seasonal and limited-edition creations also part of the selection. What is the Dubai-it prize? Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid , Vice President and Ruler of Dubai, unveiled the Dubai-it strategy in June in an effort to spread the emirate's culture of excellence among companies, institutions and future generations in the emirate. He said it would serve as a launchpad for future success and ensure ambitions were set high, stating that Dubai's accomplishments over the years had been built on "achieving exceptional results in record time, with precision and excellence". The award was subsequently launched to celebrate the innovation, enterprise and expertise of individuals and businesses across the city. Earlier this month, SWS Board Technology was named as the winner of the economy category of the awards. The Dubai-based manufacturer has grown to produce nearly half the world's kiteboards and wakeboards.

title: France U A E Sign MoU on Rafale F5 Standard
body:
France and the United Arab Emirates have signed an intergovernmental agreement on cooperation involving the Dassault Rafale F5 fighter standard, as both countries seek to strengthen defense ties amid regional tensions following the war with Iran.
According to The National News, the agreement was signed during French President Emmanuel Macron’s Gulf tour. It covers cooperation within the French and Emirati Rafale program and technical and financial arrangements for industrial cooperation in future combat aviation.
Financial terms and technology-sharing provisions remain undisclosed. Earlier negotiations reportedly involved a proposed Emirati contribution of €3.5 billion towards an estimated €5 billion development program, but it remains unclear whether that commitment has been reinstated or what access Abu Dhabi will receive to sensitive technologies.
The Rafale F5 is planned to feature an RBE2-XG radar, upgraded electronic warfare and communications systems, an uprated M88 T-REX engine, and the ability to operate alongside a future unmanned combat aircraft. Qualification is expected around 2033, with exports projected to follow later.
The agreement builds on the U.A.E.’s December 2021 contract for 80 Rafale F4 aircraft in a package valued at more than €16 billion. Initial deliveries are reportedly scheduled for the end of 2026.
Broader defense agreements cover military interoperability, industrial resilience, artificial intelligence and space. Macron also visited EDGE Group, the U.A.E. defense conglomerate comprising more than 35 companies, as Abu Dhabi seeks to localize manufacturing and reduce dependence on foreign suppliers.
France has supported Gulf partners against Iranian attacks and French Rafales reportedly intercepted around 100 drones and missiles during the conflict.
The visit also produced agreements on artificial intelligence, advanced technology and energy. Three agreements involving French start-up AMI Labs cover cooperation with Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence, G42 and Analog in AI research, cloud computing, AI models and robotics. ADNOC Gas and Schneider Electric agreed to assess energy technologies, while ADNOC Refining and Technip Energies signed contracts covering refinery capacity enhancement and sustainable aviation fuel.
More than 600 French companies operate in the U.A.E., and French exports to the country are valued at approximately $4 billion annually.

title: Occupiers attack three towns, four villages in Donetsk region over past 24 hours: 2 people killed, 18 wounded
body:
Two civilians were killed and 18 others, including three children, were wounded as a result of shelling in Donetsk region by Russian occupiers over the past 24 hours, Donetsk Region Police communications department reported on Saturday morning.
"The Russians attacked Sloviansk with a UAB-250 aerial bomb and drones, killing one person and wounding four others. One private house, three apartment buildings, two shops, a gas station, and 29 vehicles were damaged. In Kramatorsk, enemy strikes killed one civilian and injured 14 others, including three children. Six private houses, 26 apartment buildings, two educational institutions, a shop, two medical facilities, and two vehicles were damaged," the message says.
In addition to Kramatorsk and Sloviansk, the town of Druzhkivka and the villages of Iverske, Novodonetske, Novostepanivka, and Stepanivka also came under fire. A total of 105 civilian objects were damaged, including 57 residential homes.
"In Novodonetske, the shelling damaged 20 residential homes, a shop, a bus stop, and a garage cooperative. In Iverske and Stepanivka, one private house was damaged in each village," the police reported.
Over the past 24 hours, on October 23, the police recorded 1,991 strikes along the front line and in residential areas of the region.
The police and the SBU have initiated criminal proceedings under Article 438 (war crimes) of the Criminal Code of Ukraine.

title: APC accuses Atiku, ADC of plot to discredit Tinubu’s Kaduna campaign flag-off
body:
The All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council has accused the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, f ormer Vice President Atiku Abubakar, o f planning to discredit the ruling party’s presidential campaign flag-off in Kaduna today.
The allegation was contained in a statement signed by Dele Alake, spokesperson for the APC Presidential Campaign Council.
The council alleged that Atiku and the ADC had deployed what it described as “fake news operations,” including artificial intelligence-generated content, deepfake videos and counterfeit documents, to discredit President Bola Tinubu, Kaduna State Governor Uba Sani and other APC leaders.
The council said the alleged campaign began with the circulation of a photograph showing a security vehicle stationed near an APC campaign billboard in Kaduna.
According to the APC, the photograph was presented as evidence that security agents had been deployed to protect the party’s billboards.
The council also alleged that a purported letter from Mr Sani to the Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Abdulaziz Yari, claiming that the Kaduna State Government released N2.3 trillion to host the rally, was fabricated.
The APC described the claim as “utterly baseless,” noting that Kaduna State’s budgets for 2024, 2025 and 2026 amounted to less than N2.3 trillion.
“We are still at a loss as to how anyone can imagine and concoct this senseless and utterly baseless lie that defies logic and basic common sense. How much is the entire annual revenue of Kaduna State, or any state, for that matter, that a state would spend N2.3 trillion to host a rally?
“The N2.3 trillion that Atiku and his hirelings are circulating online is more than Kaduna State’s annual budget for three years,” the statement said.
The APC alleged that the figures were intended to create a negative impression about the cost of hosting the rally.
It further accused the opposition of planning to circulate “old, doctored and deepfake videos” during the rally to create the impression that residents were opposed to the APC campaign.
“We hereby use this opportunity to alert the general public about this malicious and ignoble plan,” the council said.
The APC also urged Nigerians to be vigilant and reject what it described as attempts to manipulate public opinion ahead of the 2027 general elections.
The allegations were made as the APC begins its presidential campaign for the 2027 election with a flag-off rally in Kaduna today.
President Bola Tinubu is expected to attend the rally at the Kaduna Township Stadium, where the party is expected to mobilise supporters from across the country. The APC had earlier announced Kaduna as the starting point of its nationwide campaign programme.
The Kaduna APC has said it is targeting a large turnout for the event, while a support group, Arewa for Asiwaju, said it plans to mobilise 10,000 supporters from the 19 northern states and the Federal Capital Territory.
The party’s campaign council has said the Kaduna rally will mark the formal commencement of its drive to secure Mr Tinubu’s re-election in 2027, with subsequent presidential rallies scheduled across the country.
The APC’s proposed itinerary includes rallies in Rivers State on 7 November, Plateau on 14 November, Oyo on 21 November, Borno on 25 November, Enugu on 28 November and Bauchi on 29 November, among other states.

title: Bauchi guber: APM sues INEC, PRP, deputy candidate
body: The Allied Peoples Movement (APM) has filed a suit at the Federal High Court in Bauchi, challenging the eligibility of Tijjani Aliyu Mohammed, the Peoples Redemption Party (PRP) deputy governorship candidate, to contest the 2027 Bauchi State governorship election. The party argued that Tijjani Aliyu’s name was not included in the list of members the PRP submitted to the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) before the commission’s deadline for submission of party membership registers. The APM’s legal adviser, Barrister Jidauna Tula, told reporters in Bauchi that the suit, numbered FHC/BAU/CS/70/2026, was filed to seek the court’s interpretation of the electoral law regarding Tijjani Aliyu Mohammed’s candidacy in the interest of justice and fairness. Tula said the suit sought the enforcement of Sections 77(4), 77(5) and 77(6) of the Electoral Act 2026. ‎PHOTOS: APC presidential campaign kicks off in Kaduna Remi Tinubu: I Want To Leave Aso Rock In 2031 He said the case was instituted against INEC, Tijjani Aliyu Mohammed and the PRP following the publication of Tijjani Aliyu’s name by the electoral body as the party’s deputy governorship candidate for the 2027 election. According to him, the APM asked the court to determine whether the publication of Tijjani Aliyu’s name as the PRP deputy governorship candidate was lawful, having regard to the combined provisions of Sections 177(c) and 187(2) of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999 (as amended). Tula said the party asked the court to determine “whether the publication by the electoral body, on the 10th of October 2026, displaying the name of Tijjani Aliyu as the running mate/Deputy Governorship candidate of the 3rd Defendant for the 2027 Bauchi State Governorship Election is lawful, having regards to the combined provisions of Sections 77(4), 77(5) and 77(6) of the Electoral Act 2026”. He said the party also asked the court to determine “whether having regards to Section 77(5) of the Electoral Act 2026, the name of Tijjani Aliyu was lawfully published by INEC on the 10th day of October 2026 as the running mate/Deputy Governorship candidate of the PRP in the 2027 Bauchi State Governorship election, when the Tijjani Aliyu Mohammed’s name was not present on the 3rd Defendant’s register of members submitted by the PRP to INEC”. Tula said the APM had further asked the court to determine “whether the INEC lawfully published the name of the Tijjani Aliyu on the 10th day of October 2026 as the running mate/Deputy Governorship candidate of the PRP in the 2027 Bauchi State Governorship election given the 2nd Defendant’s continued membership of the All Progressives Congress (APC) as at the 10th day of May 2026 when PRP submitted its register of members to INEC”. The legal adviser said the party also sought the court’s determination on “whether INEC lawfully published the name of Tijjani on the 10th day of October 2026 as the running mate/Deputy Governorship candidate of the 3rd Defendant in the 2027 Bauchi State Governorship election, the 3rd Defendant having failed to comply with the provisions of Section 77(4) of the Electoral Act, 2026 when it submitted her register of members to the INEC on the 10th of May, 2026, and held its primary election on the 25th day of May 2026”. Last week, the APM filed another suit challenging the eligibility of the PRP governorship candidate, Senator Shehu Buba Umar, to contest the 2027 Bauchi State governorship election. However, Buba’s legal team argued that his candidacy was lawful.

title: Patras Historic Apollo Theatre Set for €20 Million Restoration
body: Greece’s Ministry of Culture has approved the tender documents for the €20.84 million restoration and reopening of the historic Apollo Theatre in Patras, paving the way for work on the landmark building 155 years after construction began in 1871. The project has a budget of €20,839,903, with the Western Greece Region contributing approximately €17 million through the Western Greece 2021–2027 programme and the Ministry of Culture providing a further €3.7 million, according to regional governor Nektarios Farmakis. The restoration aims to preserve the theatre’s architectural and historical significance while returning it to active use as a modern performance venue for theatre productions, concerts and other cultural events. According to the tender published on the Ministry of Culture’s Diavgeia transparency portal, the project will address extensive deterioration caused by years of use, as well as alterations introduced during earlier repair and renovation works between 1956 and 1970, when builders added reinforced concrete structures. Extensive restoration and modernisation The restoration programme covers both the Apollo Theatre and the neighbouring Mansion of Literature and Arts. Planned works include cleaning and repairing the exterior façades, treating cracks, renewing finishes and strengthening the masonry. Contractors will replace the existing roofs, restore the original geometry of the stage tower’s roof and install new timber roof structures with tiled coverings. They will also replace exterior windows and doors to match the theatre’s original design and reinforce both buildings to meet structural safety requirements. The project will introduce several improvements to the theatre’s facilities and accessibility, including: Accessible routes and facilities for people with disabilities. An internal corridor connecting the theatre with the Mansion of Literature and Arts, which will accommodate the foyer and ticketing and information areas. Expanded dressing rooms and backstage facilities. New technical control rooms, equipment areas, access galleries, lifts and staircases for performers and staff. Restoration of the orchestra pit to its original position. New administrative offices, maintenance facilities, storage areas and sanitary facilities for audiences, performers and staff. Modern electromechanical installations, including fire-protection equipment, air-conditioning systems and a heat pump. The works will also provide a new theatre stage built to modern standards, updated theatrical lighting, a redesigned auditorium seating layout and a new passenger lift. A landmark of Patras’ cultural identity Located in central Patras at Georgiou Square, the Apollo Theatre is a defining landmark of the city’s cultural heritage. Designed by German architect Ernst Ziller, the building stands as a notable example of 19th-century neoclassical architecture and is often described as a miniature version of Milan’s La Scala opera house. Construction began in 1871, and the theatre hosted its first performance on 10 October 1872. The Ministry of Culture has designated the building as a property requiring special protection. It serves as the permanent home of the Municipal and Regional Theatre of Patras and also hosts concerts and other cultural events. Western Greece Regional Governor Nektarios Farmakis welcomed the tender announcement, describing the theatre as a living part of Patras’ history that belongs to both its past and its future. “It is a part of the soul of Patras, and its place is once again at the centre of the city’s cultural life,” he said. Patras Mayor Kostas Peletidis also welcomed the announcement, calling the tender a vindication of the city’s efforts to restore its historic landmark and return it to full operation. He said the project followed years of persistent and systematic work by the municipal administration, which began pursuing European funding for the restoration in 2015 under the 2014–2020 funding programme. title: Greek MS Patient Launches Platform to Combat Misinformation
body: A 47-year-old Greek man who has lived with multiple sclerosis for 18 years has launched an independent online platform to track scientific research and emerging treatments for the disease, separating evidence-based findings from exaggerated claims and medical misinformation. Tasos Fokas created MyelinWatch (myelinwatch.com), a bilingual platform in Greek and English that began operating in September 2026. It provides updates on major research developments, a treatment guide, information on experimental approaches to myelin repair, and details of scientific studies and research programmes. The website also features a dedicated section for Greece. Fokas, an audiovisual producer who works with the Centre for Combating Disinformation, told the Athens-Macedonian News Agency (AMNA) that he established the platform as a private initiative to catalogue scientific studies and emerging treatments for multiple sclerosis (MS). “The issue that concerns the community is reversing symptoms, as there is no definitive cure for the disease,” he said. According to Fokas, MyelinWatch operates independently and receives no institutional funding. Although the website accepts voluntary donations through a QR code, he personally covers its operating costs. The platform serves exclusively as an information resource and does not provide medical services or medical advice. Tackling misinformation about experimental treatments Fokas said widespread misinformation about experimental treatments motivated him to establish the platform. “In recent years, we have repeatedly seen misinformation on this subject. Everything that gets announced, even in social media posts, is presented as the treatment that will cure everyone. The truth is very different,” he said. He explained that existing treatments can reduce relapses and slow disease progression, while other interventions help manage symptoms, but none constitutes a definitive cure. “The misinformation surrounding the disease prompted me to create MyelinWatch,” he added. Artificial intelligence combined with human oversight MyelinWatch uses artificial intelligence (AI) to identify and process new scientific publications. Fokas employs different AI models as supporting tools, while cross-checking information against original sources. Every morning, an automated system searches scientific databases, including PubMed and Europe PMC, clinical trial registries such as ClinicalTrials.gov, and announcements from universities, research teams, companies and regulatory authorities. However, automation does not replace human oversight. Before publishing information, Fokas examines the original source, the announcement’s content and the evidence supporting the findings. He also compares new information with studies already recorded on the platform to establish whether it represents further developments in existing research or a new discovery. The system suggests potential additions, removals and new entries, but Fokas makes the final decisions and publishes the material manually. MyelinWatch tracks research from early laboratory experiments through clinical trials and the potential approval of treatments. It distinguishes preclinical findings from results obtained in human studies and records cases in which initial expectations have not been confirmed. “The existence of a study or a promising laboratory discovery does not, in itself, prove that a treatment is effective in patients,” Fokas said. Personal experience drives the initiative Fokas’s work on multiple sclerosis information stems directly from his own experience with the disease. He said his first neurological episode occurred in 2005, when he was 26. He experienced paralysis in his left arm and leg, along with speech difficulties, but doctors took approximately three years to diagnose his condition. He subsequently tried different treatments, encountering side effects and difficulties administering injections himself. These experiences also highlighted the importance of practical support for people living with MS. His work with the Centre for Combating Disinformation further exposed him to tactics used to spread misleading health claims. “I have seen the techniques used to mislead people and make money at the expense of patients,” he said. Fokas referred to claims that present scientific findings outside their proper context, exploiting fear and creating false expectations about treatments that do not exist. Through MyelinWatch, he aims to provide a reliable resource that helps people with multiple sclerosis, their families and the wider public distinguish credible scientific progress from unsupported promises.
