title: Situation near DPRK embassy in Beijing calm
body:
BEIJING, October 24. /TASS/. No heightened security measures are in place near the DPRK Embassy in the Beijing, a TASS correspondent reported.
Earlier, some Western media outlets reported, citing their own sources, that North Korean leader Kim Jong Un had arrived in China for a visit.
No police patrols or other security personnel were spotted near the diplomatic mission, which is located near the Chinese Foreign Ministry. Members of the People’s Armed Police guarding the embassy requested that passersby refrain from taking photographs of the gates and the building.
Renovation work is underway on one of the buildings within the diplomatic compound, with scaffolding visible near the southwestern wing.
The Chinese Foreign Ministry has not yet responded to a TASS request for comment on the reports.
Kim Jong Un paid an official visit to China in September 2025 to participate in commemorative events marking the 80th anniversary of the end of World War II. Prior to that, the North Korean leader visited China in 2019.

title: Two more Lockheed Martin F-35A Lightning II fighters arrive in Rovaniemi, Finland
body: Before JF-509 and JF-511 can be used for training, they must pass airworthiness and acceptance inspections carried out by Air Force and Defence Forces Logistics Command personnel. Each aircraft needs its own airworthiness certificate. The new arrivals follow JF-510 and JF-512, Finland’s first F-35s, which landed on Sept. 18. At a ceremony in Rovaniemi on Oct. 1, a Finnish pilot flew an F-35 in Finland for the first time. The Finnish Defence Forces’ F-35A fighter jets JF-509 and JF-511 arrived at the Lapland Air Wing in Rovaniemi on 23 October at 5:56 pm. This marks the 2nd delivery of new fighter jets to Finland. A total of four 🇫🇮 F-35s have now arrived in Finland. ➡️ https://t.co/JkvImOJkAH https://t.co/A0dt0C7Vc2 — Ilmavoimat (@FinnishAirForce) October 23, 2026 Maintenance training is set to start in Rovaniemi later this year. Finnish personnel who have completed initial training in the United States will work as instructors alongside U.S., Norwegian and Danish instructors and specialists. As of the Finnish Air Force’s Oct. 1 update, the first eight aircraft built for Finland were being used for training in the United States. The first groups of Finnish personnel have already finished their U.S. courses, but initial training there will continue until early 2028. Finland expects to reach initial operational capability in early 2028, by which point Lapland Air Wing will fly only F-35s. Karelia Air Wing is due to get its first jets the same year. Deliveries will run until the end of 2030, when the fleet is scheduled to reach full operational capability. Until then, Finland will operate its F/A-18 Hornets and F-35s side by side. JF-509 left Lockheed Martin’s factory in Fort Worth, Texas, on Oct. 20 and stopped at Lajes Air Base in the Azores. There it was joined by JF-511, which had been held in the Azores since September with a minor avionics fault. The @FinnishAirForce’s new F-35s on home soil, opening a new chapter for Finnish airpower. ✈️🇫🇮 https://t.co/VS7wi2KmSq — Lockheed Martin Europe (@LMEuropeNews) October 23, 2026 Ferry flights are planned and carried out by the United States under the Foreign Military Sales process. Finland takes ownership of each aircraft at factory acceptance but only assumes control once it arrives in the country. Finland is also getting ready to share aircraft, personnel and weapons with other European F-35 operators. In 2025, it signed the “Capacity on Call” memorandum with Norway, Denmark, the Netherlands and Belgium, and U.S. Air Forces in Europe takes part under a separate arrangement. On Sept. 17, a Finnish pilot flew a Norwegian F-35 at Ørland Air Base, the first time a Finn had flown the type in Europe. The Air Force expects this cooperation to become routine and to strengthen logistics and security of supply as the fleet enters service.

title: Israel's opposition weighs minority coalition as Bennett, Liberman reject Arab support
body: Israel's anti-Netanyahu bloc is preparing for the possibility of forming a minority government after the upcoming elections, despite opposition from Avigdor Liberman and Naftali Bennett, while a broad agreement is emerging among the parties to replace Knesset Speaker Amir Ohana even before a coalition deal is reached.In most polls, the anti-Netanyahu camp holds an advantage over the outgoing coalition bloc, but the Zionist parties seeking political change fall short of the majority needed to form a government based on their current agreements.Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his allies are far from securing a majority in many polls, although some surveys give the right-wing bloc enough seats to form a government. The electoral threshold could change the distribution of Knesset seats, and a relatively small number of votes could determine whether Israel forms a new government or enters another round of political turmoil.There is broad agreement within the camp seeking to replace Netanyahu on the need for a change of government. The disagreement begins over how to form that government if the Zionist parties in the bloc fail to win a combined 61 seats.Gadi Eisenkot wants to lead the bloc and become its main candidate for forming the next government. He firmly rejects the possibility of serving under Netanyahu, even in a rotation government, and has raised the possibility of establishing a minority government if the parties seeking political change secure 58 or 59 seats.The idea is to swear in a government that wins a majority in a confidence vote, even without the permanent support of 61 MKs, and subsequently attempt to broaden its parliamentary base.Eisenkot has made no secret of his ambition to achieve a much stronger electoral result, one that would allow him to form a Zionist government without relying on political actors outside his camp.Relying on 58 or 59 seats, however, would require detailed agreements with his partners, particularly Bennett and Liberman, who oppose establishing a government dependent on the support or abstention of the Arab parties.Eisenkot himself has not ruled out the possibility of outside support from Ra'am. In recent discussions and interviews, he has sought to project confidence that progress could be made in stages, but no agreed formula has yet been presented that would allow the plan to be implemented.From a legal standpoint, swearing in a government does not require 61 votes in favor, but rather a majority in the confidence vote. Abstentions by MKs could allow a government to take office without an absolute majority.By contrast, a constructive vote of no confidence, intended to replace an incumbent government, requires the support of 61 MKs for an alternative government.Eisenkot's minority-government scenario could therefore be relevant during the process of forming a government, but it would not allow the anti-Netanyahu bloc to remove an incumbent Netanyahu government through a simple majority vote.The political difficulty remains: Who would agree to serve in such a government, who would abstain in the vote, and how would the government survive after being sworn in?Liberman rejects minority government, insists on Zionist majorityAvigdor Liberman categorically rejects this possibility. He has made clear that he would not support a minority government, even for a transitional period, and insists on a government backed by a Zionist majority.A unity government with Netanyahu is also unacceptable to him. From his perspective, if a suitable majority cannot be found, another election would be preferable to establishing a government that fails to meet the conditions he has set.Liberman has raised another possibility: bringing Likud MKs into a government without Netanyahu, or creating a Zionist majority through a change in the composition of the political blocs after the elections.He has even claimed that some Likud MKs would be willing to take such a step. Liberman has not named them, and at this stage there are no public negotiations with Likud MKs about joining such a government.Eisenkot wants to establish a government even with a partial majority and attempt to expand it later. Liberman is unwilling to join such a government and demands a Zionist majority from the moment it is formed.Bennett and Yair Lapid, who head the Beyachad list, are also demanding a Zionist government and are unwilling to base its formation on the votes or abstentions of the Arab parties.By contrast, Democrats chairman Yair Golan has not ruled out cooperation with Ra'am.The disagreement among the party leaders could intensify when they are required to decide whether to support the swearing-in of a government that lacks a Zionist majority in the Knesset.The meeting between Eisenkot and Liberman this week ended with a joint statement emphasizing the need to increase voter turnout. It did not resolve their disagreement over a minority government.Internal competition for leadership also continues. Eisenkot wants to emerge from the elections as the leader of the largest party, believing such a result would strengthen his position during consultations at the President's Residence.Bennett sees himself as a natural candidate to lead the anti-Netanyahu camp because of his experience as prime minister, while Liberman insists on withholding any commitment that could enable the formation of a government contrary to his positions.Each party leader is seeking to increase his political strength, even though the transfer of Knesset seats between parties in the same camp does not necessarily increase the bloc's overall representation.After the elections, they will also need to agree on the identity of the next prime minister, the composition of the coalition, and the conditions for establishing it.Anti-Netanyahu parties seek agreement on replacing Knesset speakerWithin the anti-Netanyahu bloc, broad agreement is emerging on a step that could be attempted even before the question of forming a government is settled: replacing Knesset Speaker Amir Ohana.The move is intended to give the camp opposing Netanyahu control over the parliamentary agenda, even if Netanyahu remains in office as head of a caretaker government.Electing the Knesset speaker is among the first steps taken by a newly elected Knesset, and the vote is public.To replace Ohana, the bloc would need to assemble a majority around an agreed candidate. It could also rely on votes from MKs representing the Arab parties.The move would not require a prior agreement on the composition of the next government.Among the names raised as possible candidates are Chili Tropper, Matan Kahana, and Elazar Stern from Eisenkot's list; Meirav Ben-Ari and Eitan Ginzburg from the Bennett-Lapid list; Efrat Rayten from the Democrats; and attorney Oded Forer from Yisrael Beytenu.No consensus candidate has yet been announced.Liberman estimated this week that MKs from the outgoing coalition would also support replacing Ohana, suggesting that as many as one-third of them could vote against him.If such MKs are indeed prepared to take that step, they would have to do so publicly.Opposition parties prepare legislative agenda for new KnessetThe anti-Netanyahu bloc is seeking to advance a state commission of inquiry into the events of October 7, changes to military conscription legislation, limits on the prime minister's tenure, and the repeal of some of the changes promoted by the outgoing government to the judicial system.Liberman also wants to advance legislation that would prevent a person facing criminal charges from serving as prime minister.The parties have not yet reached a binding agreement on all the details of the proposed legislation or the order in which it would be advanced.Teams representing the parties have already held meetings to coordinate their first steps in the new Knesset.The idea is to use the first weeks after the elections to advance legislation before coalition negotiations deepen the disagreements between the parties.The experience of the Bennett-Lapid government also looms in the background. Laws promised when that government was formed were not completed before it collapsed.This time, the anti-Netanyahu bloc wants to move quickly, but there are concerns that MKs with differing political views will not support every item on the shared agenda.Replacing the Knesset speaker would not automatically provide a legislative majority, and not all members of the bloc agree on every proposed judicial change.Legislation effectively targeting Netanyahu would likely encounter constitutional and legal difficulties, including questions of applicability and legislation directed at a specific individual.Nor would a state commission of inquiry be established automatically simply because the Knesset elected a new speaker.If the move succeeds, Netanyahu could remain in office as head of a caretaker government while a newly elected Knesset, in which his opponents hold a majority, works to advance an agenda contrary to that of his government.

title: Senator Schiff criticizes Trump’s diesel fuel deal with Russia, citing weakened Ukrainian defense and concessions on sanctions
body:
U.S. Democratic Senator Adam Schiff has criticized agreements reached between U.S. President Donald Trump and the Russian side regarding the export of diesel fuel. Schiff pointed to a significant easing of sanction pressure on the Kremlin and a weakening of Ukraine’s defensive capabilities, noting that the deal offers no tangible economic benefit to American consumers.
“Trump's art of the Russian deal. Putin gets massive sanctions relief. Ukraine gets its defenses crippled. And the United States gets less than one day's worth of diesel and no meaningful relief at the pump,” the American legislator said on X.
According to the senator, these agreements between the White House and Kremlin leader Vladimir Putin have failed to produce any real reduction in fuel prices at American gas stations—a result of the fact that the volume of Russian product contracted for is negligible compared to daily U.S. consumption—while, at the same time, Russia has secured significant concessions regarding sanctions, all against the backdrop of a weakening in Ukraine’s defense capabilities.
Earlier, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio rejected criticism that the agreement concerning Russian diesel fuel and the delay in imposing new sanctions against Russia amounted to free concessions to Putin.

title: Stefanchuk discusses bilateral cooperation with Hungarian partners
body:
According to Ukrinform, Stefanchuk reported this on Facebook .
“These meetings marked an important step toward further deepening the partnership between our countries and developing dialogue at all levels,” Stefanchuk noted.
According to him, the Ukrainian-Hungarian dialogue is characterized by active momentum and is taking on new meaning.
“I appreciate the openness and sincerity of our communication with our Hungarian partners. We had the opportunity to discuss important issues of bilateral cooperation directly, align our positions, and outline plans. There are specific areas where it is important to build on this positive momentum. First and foremost—further advancing Ukraine’s path toward EU membership, intensifying interparliamentary cooperation, and strengthening good-neighborly relations,” Stefanchuk emphasized.
According to Stefanchuk, “The willingness to remember and honor the difficult chapters of our shared history is of particular importance. I am convinced that respect for historical truth and memory should help our peoples find common ground.”

I thank my Hungarian colleagues for the substantive meetings, openness, and hospitality. This was a true visit of solidarity and mutual understanding,” emphasized the Speaker of the Verkhovna Rada.

title: US-Ukraine-Russia Talks Slated for Abu Dhabi or Switzerland
body:
The next round of trilateral discussions between negotiating delegations from the US , Ukraine, and the Russia could take place in Abu Dhabi or Switzerland within the coming weeks, Sky News reported, citing a US official.
Speaking on condition of anonymity, the official stated that the discussions are projected to take place in “a couple of weeks.”
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
The primary objective of the working-level consultations is to establish foundations for a potential leader-level summit between the heads of state, though the official stressed that significant preparatory work remains before high-level meetings can materialize.
“The goal would be to build to a leader-level meeting eventually, but much work remains to be done before that happens,” the official explained.
The prospective diplomatic encounter follows preliminary discussions held across European and regional diplomatic hubs, including previous engagements in Oslo and Saint Petersburg.
The report aligns with disclosures delivered by President Volodymyr Zelensky , who previously identified Abu Dhabi, the capital of the United Arab Emirates , as a primary proposed venue for three-way consultations in early or mid-November.
Addressing international security specialists at Washington’s Hudson Institute on Friday, Oct. 23, Zelensky said that any viable diplomatic framework requires verifiable security guarantees and sustained international defense commitments.
The president outlined three prerequisites for an enduring settlement : an immediate, enforceable ceasefire, binding international defense commitments, and minimum ten-year international funding to sustain a large standing military capable of deterring future aggression.
“We need not just peace. Peace which has to be fair and strong,” Zelensky told the institute via video link. “We need a big, big strong army, minimum ten years.”
Zelensky emphasized that Ukraine’s war-affected economy cannot independently maintain the required defensive force structure without continuous outside financing.
He added that while Kyiv maintains its pursuit of NATO membership, bilateral US security guarantees modeled after NATO’s Article 5 and ratified by the US Congress could serve as an interim defense architecture.
The president also cautioned against Western concessions to Moscow – including the lifting of statutory sanctions or releasing frozen Russian state assets – without binding reciprocal safeguards, stressing that an armistice must serve as “point number one” before comprehensive political agreements can be concluded.
“We are ready to meet any day, even tomorrow, but it all depends on the Russians,” Zelensky noted, observing that Moscow had previously delayed planned diplomatic sessions by raising procedural obstacles.
The planning for trilateral talks arrives as Kyiv articulates its operational parameters regarding prospective ceasefires.
In an interview with ABC News, Zelensky stated that Ukraine is prepared to halt combat operations along existing front lines to stop casualties as quickly as possible, while firmly ruling out the formal surrender of sovereign territory.
“Yes, we are ready to put an end to this war as quickly as possible... To freeze the front line,” Zelensky said.
Addressing public speculation suggesting that Ukraine might cede 25 percent of its sovereign territory, Zelensky clarified that Russian forces currently occupy 19.3 percent of the country. He explained that reaching a 25 percent threshold would require surrendering the unoccupied portions of the Donbas , a condition Kyiv unconditionally rejects.
“When someone speaks about 25 percent, it implies that we would have to surrender the entire Donbas, and only then would the Russians control 25 percent. Right now, they control 19.3 percent,” Zelensky explained.
The president reiterated that while Ukraine is open to freezing active frontline maneuvers along the active line of contact, Kyiv will never grant legal recognition to occupied lands as Russian sovereign territory.
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

title: Gunmen invade Taraba community, kill residents, cart away motorcycles
body: Several residents, including women and children, were killed when gunmen attacked Binnari town in Karim-Lamido Local Government Area of Taraba State on Friday evening. Daily Trust learnt that the gunmen, riding on motorcycles, invaded the town at about 3pm and opened fire in different directions, killing many residents and wounding several others. A community leader in the area, Alhaji Tanko Andami, who spoke with Daily Trust by telephone, said the attackers invaded the town on Friday, which is a market day, and began shooting at residents. He said the gunmen arrived on about 50 motorcycles, with two men on each motorcycle. Tinubu’s northern test begins Insecurity spreads in Sokoto Andami said the attackers, after killing residents, looted shops and carted away cash, foodstuffs and other provisions. He added that the gunmen also took away new motorcycles whose owners abandoned them while fleeing the attack. According to him, the attackers were among the bandits who had taken control of several communities in the area and were operating around the Plateau and Bauchi borders with Taraba State. “We are going to conduct the burial of those killed in the attack this morning. “We appeal to the Taraba State governor and security agencies to pay special attention to Karim-Lamido Local Government Area because many communities are under the control of bandits who operate around the Plateau and Bauchi border areas with Taraba State,” he said. Another resident of Binnari, Yahuza Binnari, who fled to a nearby village, said the attackers invaded the town shortly after Friday prayers, when the market was crowded. He said the attackers blocked the entrances to the town, while others moved into the market, which was busy because it was a market day, and started shooting in different directions. “There was total confusion in the town as people ran in different directions. “When the attackers left, we counted more than 18 dead bodies, while several others were still missing. “We are going to conduct the burial of those killed and search for the missing people,” he said. When contacted, the Police Public Relations Officer of the Taraba State Command, ASP Victor Mshelizah, confirmed the attack. He, however, said 10 people were killed in the incident and that police personnel had been deployed to the affected area.

title: Army seeks new ways to power troops on the battlefield
body: UK Defence Innovation has opened a Tactical Power Challenge worth £2.45 million seeking better ways to generate, store, distribute and manage electrical power for deployed forces, run on behalf of the British Army with support from the Defence Science and Technology Laboratory, according to UK Defence Innovation. The competition is being delivered in partnership with Australia’s Advanced Strategic Capabilities Accelerator and closes at noon on 10 November. Further detail is available on the government’s competition page . The organisation said the challenge seeks innovative solutions to improve the generation, storage, distribution and management of electrical power for deployed forces. Power has become one of the quieter constraints on how the Army fights. A dismounted section now carries radios, electronic warfare detectors, night vision, counter-drone equipment, tablets and the batteries for all of it, and the weight of those batteries competes directly with water and ammunition. At formation level the problem scales up into generators, fuel convoys and the thermal and acoustic signature that a diesel generator park produces for anyone looking. Ukraine has made the point sharply over the past four years, because units operating dispersed and under constant observation cannot run a visible generator, and the fuel resupply that a traditional headquarters depends on is one of the easiest things for a drone operator to find and hit. Silent generation, solar and battery hybrids, and power management that lets one source feed several systems have all moved from convenience to survivability. The Australian partnership places the competition inside a wider pattern of British and Australian innovation work, with the Advanced Strategic Capabilities Accelerator performing a similar function to UK Defence Innovation. Running a challenge jointly gives a successful supplier two potential customers and gives both armies a chance of fielding compatible equipment, which matters more as the two countries work together under AUKUS Pillar Two on autonomy, artificial intelligence and electronic warfare. UK Defence Innovation was established to replace the Defence and Security Accelerator and to put a single organisation in charge of pulling new technology into the department at pace, with a budget ringfenced under the Strategic Defence Review. Competitions of this kind are its main instrument, offering a defined sum against a defined problem on a short timetable. title: Typhoon Rosal exits PAR; ITCZ bringing scattered rain
body: MANILA, Philippines – Typhoon Rosal (Champi) exited the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR) on Saturday morning, October 24, then left the weather bureau’s monitoring domain in the afternoon. At the time of its exit from PAR, Rosal’s maximum sustained winds were already down to 120 kilometers per hour. During its peak, it was a super typhoon with maximum sustained winds of 215 km/h. Rosal did not make landfall in the Philippines, but it affected parts of Northern Luzon, especially the northernmost province of Batanes. It brought moderate to intense rain, as well as winds up to Signal No. 2 . The trough or extension of the tropical cyclone has also affected various areas in Luzon, the Visayas, and even Mindanao in the past days. On Saturday afternoon, the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical, and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) said scattered rain and thunderstorms due to Rosal’s trough will only be confined to Batanes, Ilocos Norte, Apayao, and Babuyan Islands in the coming hours. Rosal entered PAR last Tuesday, October 20, becoming the Philippines’ 18th tropical cyclone for 2026, and the first for October. PAGASA earlier estimated the country may have one or two tropical cyclones during the month. So far, no new low pressure areas or potential tropical cyclones are being monitored inside or outside PAR. Meanwhile, the intertropical convergence zone (ITCZ) is bringing scattered rain and thunderstorms to the Visayas, Mindanao, Sorsogon, Masbate, and Palawan on Saturday evening. Flash floods and landslides are possible. The ITCZ is a belt near the equator where the trade winds of the Northern Hemisphere and the Southern Hemisphere meet. The Philippines is currently in a transition period to the northeast monsoon or amihan, following the end of the southwest monsoon or habagat , which was announced last October 5. The northeast monsoon typically brings surges of cold temperatures, but the upcoming amihan period could be warmer as the existing strong El Niño in the tropical Pacific Ocean is predicted to become very strong in the fourth quarter of 2026. – Rappler.com

title: Future of UAE’s ODI cricket and captain Harpreet Bhatia in doubt as end of League Two looms
body: The UAE have four matches left in the Cricket World Cup League Two. Let’s be honest, it can’t end soon enough. The national team have endured a miserable three years in one-day international cricket. So much so that the privilege of playing it at all is now on the line. They are bottom of the CWCL2 table, having lost 21 of their 32 matches so far. With two games each against Oman and the Netherlands in Dubai over the next two weeks, it is doubtful how many wins they will be able to add to their tally. It means they will now have to play to retain their status at the Cricket World Cup Qualifier Play-off in Nepal in December. The ICC haven’t announced the criteria for having official ODI privileges in the next four-year cycle. UAE lose to Scotland – in pictures It has been speculated that the game’s governing body might be about to extend the number of countries who play ODIs. Although where the funding will come from to keep sides like the UAE – who have had regular ODI status for the past 11 years – in the matter to which they have become accustomed is anyone’s guess. After all, the ICC traditionally prefer a conservative approach to things like this, rather than an expansionist one. But the UAE are working on the assumption they need to finish in the top four of that eight-team play-off in Kathmandu to safeguard their status. That should be doable, but it is far from a foregone conclusion given the opposition. Namibia, who will in all likelihood be involved, and Nepal have had the UAE’s measure for some time now. Canada have hit a dip at just the wrong time for them, with the UAE beating them when they met in Scotland in the summer. The national team have been adept at punching down when it comes to sides lower ranked than them in the recent past. But the four sides coming up from the Challenge League – Italy, Uganda, Jersey and probably Kuwait – will be far from easy beats. At their best, the UAE should have no concerns. But they are so infrequently in that condition, and the team continues to be in a state of flux. Just six players in the squad for the final tri-series were part of the XI for the first CWCL2 match, which was a loss to Canada in Dubai in 2024. Having been out the ODI side for some time, Muhammad Waseem has been recalled for UAE’s triseries against Oman and Ned If he retains his place for the subsequent qualifier playoff, he won’t be able to take up his TWO-HUNDRED AND TEN THOUSAND DOLLAR ILT20 contract 🤯 pic.twitter.com/OP3GaJdqvb — Paul Radley (@PaulRadley) October 22, 2026 And four of those – Basil Hameed, Aayan Khan, Muhammad Waseem and Tanish Suri – have spent long periods out of the team in the intervening time. The side have been undermined by the constant change, and it has shown in results. Young players on whom the future should have been built – such as Ali Naseer, Alishan Sharafu, Ethan D’Souza and Vriitya Aravind – have been tried and discarded. Even the captaincy has been tossed around with liberal abandon. Four people have led over the course of the three year competition, with some – such as Rahul Chopra, who is back at the helm now – being dispensed then recalled. The league campaign started with Waseem in charge. Tellingly, he was missing the chance to take up a contract in the Pakistan Super League to play in that first tri-series. Now he has been recalled to the side. If he is retained for the play-off, he will have to forego a large chunk of the $210,000 deal he landed to play in the DP World ILT20. They seemed to have finally settled on a captain who had the faith of coach Lalchand Rajput when Harpreet Bhatia ascended to the role this year, just a few months into being in the country. Now his future, too, is in doubt. Harpreet will miss the games against Oman and the Netherlands as he is on an indefinite break from cricket on compassionate grounds. The Emirates Cricket Board announced this week he would be returning to India as his mother is ill. “I am grateful to the [ECB] for accepting my request of taking a break from cricket, as well as all the support the board has given me in recent days and months,” Bhatia said. “For now, my full focus is my mother’s health and well-being. I wish the team the very best for their upcoming fixtures.” The ECB in turn said it “offers its full support to Harpreet and his family in this difficult time”. “The board is fully committed to the mental health and well-being of all its players and support staff especially when they have challenges pertaining to their families,” the ECB wrote. “We thank Harpreet for his professionalism and commitment to the ECB and the UAE men’s national cricket team. We are all praying for his mother and wish her a full recovery at the earliest.” The UAE start their CWCL2 tri-series when they face Oman at the ICC Academy in Dubai Sports City on Sunday.

title: Stateful Agentic Engineering Copilots with Letta: Core Memory, Shared State, Semantic Retrieval, Custom Tools, Streaming, and Portable Agent Workflows

In this tutorial, we build a stateful engineering copilot with Letta that demonstrates how agentic memory extends beyond conventional prompt-based conversations. We begin by creating inspectable core memory blocks that the agent can autonomously update, then expose those blocks for programmatic state synchronization and shared access across multiple agents. We further extend the architecture with archival vector memory for semantic retrieval, a custom server-side tool for deterministic risk estimation, streaming for observing agent execution, server-side message history for persistent conversations, and .af export for portability. Together, these components demonstrate a practical memory architecture in which persistent state, retrieval, tools, multi-agent collaboration, and execution traces work as an integrated agentic system. Also remember we already tried bumping " "session.timeout.ms and it did nothing — don't suggest that again.") dump_memory(copilot.id, "core memory after 2 turns (note what moved where)") hr("3. Your code writes into the context window") live = get_block(copilot.id, "project_state") set_block(copilot.id, "project_state", (live.value or "") + "
[CI 09:41Z] main is RED: integration/kafka_rebalance_test failing (flaky x3).") chat(copilot.id, "Anything I should know before I start the day?") hr("4. Shared memory between two agents") policies = client.blocks.create( label="policies", description="Non-negotiable engineering policies. Read-only: obey, never edit.", value="1. No direct pushes to main.
2. Every fix ships with a regression test.

Customer data never leaves EU regions.", limit=2000, read_only=True, ) scratchpad = client.blocks.create( label="team_scratchpad", description="Shared working notes between the copilot and the reviewer agent. I look for the failure mode " "everyone else skipped, and I cite the team policies by number."}], ) print("reviewer id:", reviewer.id) chat(copilot.id, "Write your proposed fix for the rebalance issue into the team_scratchpad " "block so the reviewer can see it. Keep it to 4 lines.") print("

agents attached to this block:", [a.name for a in flex(lambda: client.blocks.agents.list(block_id=scratchpad.id), lambda: client.blocks.agents.list(scratchpad.id), label="blocks.agents.list")]) We demonstrate self-editing memory by providing the copilot with durable information about the engineer, project, decisions, and known failure modes. We also update project state directly from application code and create shared read-only and writable blocks for multi-agent collaboration. We then connect a reviewer agent to the shared memory and observe how both agents exchange persistent working context. Copy Code Copied Use a different Browser hr("5. Archival memory: bulk-load knowledge, then let the agent retrieve it") KNOWLEDGE = [ ("Postmortem 2024-08-02: Halo dropped 1.2M events when the consumer group rebalanced during a " "deploy. Root cause: commits inside the poll loop blocked past max.poll.interval.ms.", ["postmortem", "kafka", "halo"]), ("ADR-017: Halo uses at-least-once delivery with idempotent writes keyed on (tenant_id, event_id). " "Exactly-once via Kafka transactions was rejected for throughput reasons.", ["adr", "architecture", "halo"]), ("Runbook: to drain a Halo node, set DRAIN=1, wait for lag<1000, then SIGTERM. Never SIGKILL — " "in-flight batches are only checkpointed on graceful shutdown.", ["runbook", "ops", "halo"]), ("Benchmark 2025-01: rdkafka 2.3 with 8 partitions sustained 240k events/s at p99 32ms on " "c6i.4xlarge; the bottleneck was JSON parsing, not the network.", ["benchmark", "performance"]), ("Priya's preference on file layout: one module per bounded context, integration tests live " "next to the module, no tests/ mega-directory.", ["preference", "style"]), ("Incident 2025-03-19: an EU tenant's payload was mirrored to us-east-1 for 40 minutes. This is why policy 3 exists.", ["incident", "compliance"]), ] def archive(agent_id, content, tags): return flex( lambda: client.agents.passages.insert(agent_id=agent_id, content=content, tags=tags), lambda: client.agents.passages.create(agent_id=agent_id, text=content, tags=tags), lambda: client.agents.passages.create(agent_id=agent_id, text=content), label="agents.passages.insert", ) for content, tags in KNOWLEDGE: archive(copilot.id, content, tags) print(f"inserted {len(KNOWLEDGE)} passages") hits = flex( lambda: client.agents.passages.search(agent_id=copilot.id, query="losing messages during a deploy"), lambda: client.agents.passages.list(agent_id=copilot.id, search="losing messages during a deploy"), label="agents.passages.search", ) print("
 programmatic semantic search for 'losing messages during a deploy':") for h in list(hits)[:3]: print(" •", textwrap.shorten(getattr(h, "content", None) or getattr(h, "text", ""), 150)) chat(copilot.id, "Before I restart a node tonight: is there anything in our history I should " "worry about, and what's the safe procedure?") hr("6. Give the agent a custom tool") def estimate_release_risk(open_bugs: int, days_to_deadline: int, test_coverage: float) -> str: """Estimate the risk of shipping a release on time. Args: open_bugs (int): Number of open P0/P1 bugs. days_to_deadline (int): Calendar days left before the ship date. test_coverage (float): Line coverage as a fraction between 0.0 and 1.0. Returns: str: A risk score from 0-100 and a verdict. """ import math pressure = open_bugs / max(days_to_deadline, 1) score = max(0.0, min(100.0, 100 * (1 - math.exp(-1.4 * pressure)) * (1.3 - test_coverage))) verdict = "SHIP" if score < 35 else ("SLIP ONE WEEK" if score < 70 else "DO NOT SHIP") return f"risk_score={score:.1f} verdict={verdict}" tool = flex( lambda: client.tools.upsert_from_function(func=estimate_release_risk), lambda: client.tools.create_from_function(func=estimate_release_risk), label="tools.upsert_from_function", ) flex(lambda: client.agents.tools.attach(agent_id=copilot.id, tool_id=tool.id), lambda: client.agents.tools.attach(copilot.id, tool.id), label="agents.tools.attach") print("attached tool:", tool.name, "| agent tools:", [t.name for t in flex(lambda: client.agents.tools.list(agent_id=copilot.id), lambda: client.agents.tools.list(copilot.id), label="agents.tools.list")]) chat(copilot.id, "We have 9 open P0/P1 bugs, 12 days to the Nov 14 date, coverage is 0.61. " "Score the risk with the tool, then record the verdict in project_state.") We populate archival memory with tagged engineering knowledge and use semantic search to retrieve relevant information without relying on exact keyword matches. We then allow the agent to query this archival knowledge autonomously when answering an operational question. Finally, we create and attach a custom server-side release-risk tool so the agent can perform deterministic calculations and record the resulting decision in memory. Streaming the agent's steps") def stream_chat(agent_id, text): print(f" user : {text}") s = flex( lambda: client.agents.messages.stream(agent_id=agent_id, input=text), lambda: client.agents.messages.stream(agent_id=agent_id, messages=[{"role": "user", "content": text}]), lambda: client.agents.messages.create_stream(agent_id=agent_id, messages=[{"role": "user", "content": text}]), label="messages.stream", ) for chunk in s: kind = getattr(chunk, "message_type", None) or getattr(chunk, "type", "") if kind == "reasoning_message": print(" ", textwrap.shorten(getattr(chunk, "reasoning", "") or "", 160)) elif kind == "tool_call_message": print(" ", getattr(getattr(chunk, "tool_call", None), "name", "?")) elif kind == "assistant_message": print(" ", as_text(getattr(chunk, "content", ""))) try: stream_chat(copilot.id, "One-line status of Halo, from memory only. No tools.") except Exception as e: print("streaming unavailable on this SDK version:", e) hr("8. Server-side conversation history") hist = flex(lambda: client.agents.messages.list(agent_id=copilot.id, limit=8), lambda: client.agents.messages.list(copilot.id, limit=8), label="agents.messages.list") for m in hist: kind = getattr(m, "message_type", "?") body = as_text(getattr(m, "content", "")) or getattr(m, "reasoning", "") or "" print(f" [{kind:<24}] {textwrap.shorten(str(body), 110)}") print("
 reconnect from a fresh process with just the id:") print(" client.agents.messages.create(agent_id='%s', input='...')" % copilot.id) We use Letta’s streaming interface to observe reasoning, tool calls, and assistant responses as the agent executes a task. We then inspect server-side conversation history to verify that the interaction state persists independently of the local Python process. We also demonstrate how the agent can be reconnected from a fresh process using only its persistent identifier. Copy Code Copied Use a different Browser hr("9. Export / import the agent") try: dump = flex(lambda: client.agents.export_file(agent_id=copilot.id), lambda: client.agents.export_file(copilot.id), label="agents.export_file") blob = dump if isinstance(dump, (str, bytes)) else json.dumps(dump, default=str) path = "/content/copilot.af" if os.path.isdir("/content") else "copilot.af" with open(path, "wb" if isinstance(blob, bytes) else "w") as f: f.write(blob) print(f"exported → {path} ({len(blob)} bytes) — memory, tools and history travel with it.") print("re-import later with: client.agents.import_file(file=open(path,'rb'))") except Exception as e: print("export not available on this SDK/deployment:", e) CLEANUP = False if CLEANUP: for aid in (copilot.id, reviewer.id): try: client.agents.delete(aid) except Exception as e: print("agent delete:", e) for bid in (policies.id, scratchpad.id): try: client.blocks.delete(bid) except Exception as e: print("block delete:", e) print("deleted.") else: hr("Done") print(f"copilot : {copilot.id}
reviewer : {reviewer.id}") print("Inspect them visually in the ADE at https://app.letta.com") We export the complete agent state to an .af file, providing a portable representation of the agent’s memory, tools, and conversation state. We then include optional cleanup logic that removes the agents and shared blocks created during the tutorial. We finish by displaying the persistent agent identifiers and the Letta ADE location for further inspection. In conclusion, we now have a complete view of how Letta supports persistent, inspectable agent workflows rather than treating every interaction as an isolated prompt. We saw how core memory maintains high-value state in context, archival memory provides scalable retrieval, shared and read-only blocks coordinate multiple agents, and application code can directly synchronize external state. We also used custom tools and streaming to extend and observe agent behavior while server-side history and agent export provide persistence and portability. Through this workflow, we established a practical foundation for building engineering copilots that continuously retain context, reason over accumulated knowledge, collaborate across agents, and operate with explicit, controllable memory. title: Israelis warned to exercise caution in France ahead of renewed violence, protests
body: Israel's Foreign Ministry issued an advisory on Friday urging Israelis currently in France or planning to visit the country to exercise heightened caution.The advisory follows violent demonstrations and riots that took place in several locations across France on October 17, amid concerns that protests could resume in the coming days. The Foreign Ministry highlighted two dates in particular: October 24 and November 5.The ministry advised Israelis to avoid demonstrations, protests, and large gatherings, even when they appear peaceful, warning that such events could escalate suddenly. Anyone who finds themselves near a confrontation is urged to leave the area immediately rather than stopping to watch or film the incident.Israelis planning to travel to France in the coming days are urged to assess conditions in the areas they intend to visit before departure and remain aware that the situation could change at short notice.Luxury stores in France board windows, increase security ahead of fresh protestsLuxury boutiques in France boarded up their normally glitzy windows and added guards ahead of fresh protests on Saturday, with some planning to stay closed after rioters looted shops across the country last weekend.France, the most visited country in the world, draws large numbers of overseas shoppers seeking Chanel handbags and Hermes scarves, an important source of revenue for brands facing slowing demand.But some decided staying open was too risky after last week's events, when rioters smashed and looted hundreds of shops in Paris, Marseille, and Bordeaux.A Rolex retailer and a De Beers store near the capital's famous Place Vendome will remain closed on Saturday, staff said, while managers at stores including Richemont-owned IWC Schaffhausen said they would decide whether to close early depending on the intensity of the protests.Groups including France's main student union UNEF and the Yellow Vest group, which emerged as a potent anti-establishment movement in 2018, plan to march through central Paris later on Saturday to protest against high living costs and cuts to public services.France mounts huge security operation as protesters prepare to marchFrench security forces fanned out across Paris on Saturday ahead of protests that authorities fear could turn violent, with Interior Minister Laurent Nunez urging police to be "hyper-reactive" against troublemakers and looters.Soldiers from an anti-terrorism military unit patrolled the Champs-Elysees avenue while police vans circled the Arc de Triomphe, looking to protect some of the capital's most famous sites from any repeat of the unrest that shook France last week.Nunez has mobilized 70,000 police nationwide for Saturday's demonstrations, 10,000 more than on October 17, when a wave of vandalism and looting raised questions about the government's ability to maintain order.Anger over living costs and strained public services has drawn students, workers and unions onto the streets in recent weeks, but authorities say radical militants and bands of young looters have exploited the protests to sow chaos.Speaking to police in Paris, Nunez warned officers that they would face attempts to target shops, public institutions and security forces."We have to be ultra, ultra responsive. We have significant calls for disruption from political groups and quite simply from criminals," he said. "It is going to be a long day."But staff at LVMH brands Louis Vuitton, Dior and Bulgari said they weren't taking any chances and security at their stores near Place Vendome had been increased for the day. Additional private security to supplement the police presence in the neighborhood is also planned.Nearby department store Printemps also increased its security staff, carried out safety repairs and added security measures to reinforce shop windows and entrances, a spokesperson for the store said.Hermès finance chief Eric du Halgouet said this week the company had increased security measures at its French stores, adding it was too early to say how much impact recent events would have on business.Demonstration in Orleans against far rightAuthorities have sharply restricted demonstrations across much of France. Marseille reversed an earlier ban and authorized a union march, while protests remain restricted in central Lyon. Union rallies will also go ahead in Strasbourg, but bans remain in force in several other cities including Nancy, Metz, Besancon, Belfort, Rouen, Le Havre, Toulon and Limoges.The first authorized march began mid-morning in Orleans, about 120 km (75 miles) south of Paris, to protest against Marine Le Pen's far-right National Rally, which is holding a congress in the city this weekend."We have come to tell the far right, face to face, that we are not afraid," said Bally Bagayoko, the mayor of Saint-Denis and a member of the hard-left France Unbowed (LFI) party.Tensions were heightened by a shooting west of Paris on Friday in which a gunman suspected of acting out of Islamophobic hatred killed one person and wounded four others, including a 12-year-old girl.

title: Obuasi SHTS sexual abuse: FIDA Ghana calls offence first-degree felony, says it’s not bailable
body: The President of the International Federation of Women Lawyers (FIDA) Ghana, Gloria Ofori-Boadu, has described the alleged sexual abuse involving the headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School as a “first degree felony” and argued that the offence should not be bailable. Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, October 24, she said the seriousness of the allegations and the potential danger to society should be considered in decisions regarding bail. “Secondly, we want to see the charge sheets, the bill of indictment. This is an indictable offence because it’s, I’ll call it a first degree felony. It’s so bad,” she said. She added that although bail decisions depend on the discretion of the court, the alleged conduct should be considered when assessing whether the accused poses a danger to society. “We want to see how it translates into prosecution, the trial, right from the beginning to the final decision of the court. And even if there’s a jail sentence, we want to see him entering the jail place,” she said. Madam Ofori-Boadu said FIDA Ghana wanted to follow the case through every stage of the justice process, from the charges filed by the police to the trial and the court’s final decision. “We even believe that this is not a bailable offence because at the end of the day, even though bail depends on the discretion of the court and all that, there’s a need to look at the danger to society that this person has, seems to always indicate that he’s dangerous,” she added. The FIDA Ghana president also criticised the Ghana Education Service (GES), arguing that its policies on how teachers accused of sexual assault are handled require review. She said the organisation had already issued a statement on the matter and had been engaging the media to educate the public on the issue. According to her, the GES must account to taxpayers for its handling of cases involving teachers accused of sexual misconduct, particularly where disciplinary measures such as interdiction, dismissal, transfer or promotion have been applied. Madam Ofori-Boadu said the organisation was also concerned about the wider cost of sexual abuse to victims and the country, particularly its impact on the mental and physical well-being of those affected. “The cost to the nation of depriving the mental health and physical wellbeing of one citizen is very huge,” she said. She urged the media to help monitor the case by seeking information on the charges and the prosecution process to ensure that the matter is followed through to its conclusion.

title: Jordan Tightens Security After Deadly Attack on Greek Orthodox Church
body: Jordan has increased security around shopping centres, foreign embassies and other locations after a gun attack on a Greek Orthodox church killed seven people and injured dozens during a funeral. Security has been stepped up across Jordan following a deadly shooting at a Greek Orthodox church in the southern governorate of Karak, which authorities have condemned as a terrorist attack. The US Embassy in Amman announced the heightened security measures after gunmen opened fire during a funeral on Friday, October 23, killing seven people and injuring dozens more, according to Jordan’s Public Security Directorate. Authorities are continuing to search for the attackers. No group has claimed responsibility, and officials have not confirmed whether the suspects have links to Islamist militant organisations operating inside or outside Jordan. Jordanian leaders condemn attack Jordanian Prime Minister Jafar Hassan condemned the violence, blaming terrorist ideology and extremism. “We will not allow society to go down this path,” Hassan said in a statement posted on social media. King Abdullah II visited Karak following the attack and vowed that those responsible would face severe consequences, warning they would be punished with an “iron fist”. The attack has raised concerns over security in a country where such incidents are considered rare. Jordanian authorities have previously said they foiled attempted attacks by Islamist militants. Christians among Jordan’s minority communities Christians make up a minority of Jordan’s population, which is predominantly Muslim. The country is home to significant Christian communities and numerous biblical sites visited by pilgrims from around the world. The shooting at the Greek Orthodox church has prompted renewed concern for the safety of Christian worshippers and religious communities in the region. The US Embassy’s warning highlights the increased security measures now in place following the attack, although authorities have not publicly identified a confirmed motive or established links to any particular militant group.
