title: Obuasi SHTS scandal: Prioritise victims’ welfare, not just investigations – Felicity Nelson
body: The Deputy Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Tourism Development Company, Felicity Nelson, has called for the psychological, emotional and physical well-being of alleged victims to be prioritised as investigations continue into sexual abuse allegations involving the headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School. Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, October 24, she stressed that although the allegations must be thoroughly investigated, equal attention should be given to ensuring that the affected students receive appropriate medical care, counselling and emotional support. “Of course, all allegations must be investigated. As it stands now, these still remain allegations, so we are still saying yes, let’s investigate. However, I want us to prioritise the victims in this case, their wants, their needs. We need to ensure that they are fine,” she stated. “We need to ensure that psychologically they are okay, emotionally they are fine. In terms of health, we need to do those checks,” she added. Ms Nelson further expressed concern about the prevalence of sexual abuse among adolescent girls in Ghana, citing UNICEF reports which, according to her, indicated that 22 per cent of adolescent girls had experienced some form of sexual abuse. She also referenced another UNICEF report which she said showed that 51 per cent of girls in secondary schools experienced some form of sexual abuse between 2019 and 2021. Describing the situation as a widespread national problem, she cautioned against treating the Obuasi allegations as an isolated incident, noting that many cases of sexual abuse remain unreported. “This is endemic, it’s a serious issue. Inasmuch as we are talking about Obuasi, we need to be mindful of the fact that this is not just happening at Obuasi,” she said. Ms Nelson also criticised the cultural practice of influential community figures intervening to seek forgiveness or private settlements on behalf of individuals accused of sexual offences. She argued that interventions by traditional authorities, religious leaders and other influential personalities could undermine accountability, particularly when they discourage victims from pursuing formal complaints. “We have to look culturally as Ghanaians and say this idea that when someone commits a crime, especially of a sexual nature, where elders, church leaders, imams, chiefs and queen mothers go and beg on their behalf needs to stop,” she stated. “If it was even my wish, we need to criminalise it,” she added. The Deputy CEO further called for a review of safeguarding systems to strengthen the protection of children and ensure that allegations of sexual abuse are appropriately handled. Her comments follow allegations of sexual abuse involving female students at Obuasi Senior High Technical School, brought to public attention through an investigative documentary by journalist Manasseh Azure Awuni. The headmaster has denied wrongdoing, and the allegations remain subject to investigation. Ms Nelson maintained that beyond establishing the facts and ensuring accountability, protecting the welfare and dignity of affected students must remain central to the response.

title: Philip Lustre Jr. arrest a ‘sad day for journalism in the Philippines’ – lawyer
body: MANILA, Philippines – The arrest of Philip Lustre Jr. is an attack on press freedom in the Philippines, the veteran journalist’s lawyer Dino De Leon said. Lustre was arrested at a restaurant in Quezon City on Saturday, October 24, for alleged cyber libel. He was served an arrest warrant issued by Branch 10 of Davao City’s Regional Trial Court. The 72-year-old is the author behind Kill, Kill, Kill: Extrajudicial Killings in the Philippines , which documents former president Rodrigo Duterte’s deadly war on drugs. Must Read Veteran journalist Philip Lustre Jr. arrested for alleged cyber libel “This is a sad day for journalism in the Philippines,” De Leon said in an ambush interview on the same day of Lustre’s arrest, as seen in a video by Bilyonaryo News Channel. “Nararamdaman na naman natin ‘yung pag-atake sa mga members ng media. This is reminiscent of the Duterte administration na nanggaling sa Davao City again ‘yung complainant .” (We are again witnessing the attacks on members of the media. This is reminiscent of the Duterte administration, where the complainant is from Davao City.) Lustre had earlier mentioned that he did not know who the complainant was, and was also unaware that there was a complaint being lodged against him. ‘Laws protecting reputation must never be used to harass journalists’ The Presidential Task Force on Media Security (PTFOMS), meanwhile, expressed support for Lustre’s welfare, access to legal counsel, communication with his family, and medical assistance, given that he is a senior citizen. “We urge the prompt handling of any application for bail in accordance with applicable rules, with due consideration for his age and welfare. His reported lack of prior knowledge of the complaint also warrants clarification through the appropriate legal processes,” PTFOMS said in its statement. With Lustre’s arrest coming just a day after Davao City 1st District Representative Paolo “Pulong” Duterte filed a cyber libel complaint against several GMA Network journalists, PTFOMS also stressed that “laws protecting reputation must never be used to harass journalists, suppress legitimate criticism, or obstruct the public’s access to information.” “The threat of arrest, prolonged litigation, and substantial legal expenses can discourage journalists from pursuing important stories even before a complaint is resolved,” it said. It also said that it will coordinate with De Leon and the concerned authorities to gather official information on Lustre’s arrest. – Rappler.com

title: NDC goofed with initial Obuasi school sexual abuse statement; I’m glad we corrected it – Felicity Nelson
body: The Deputy Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Tourism Development Company, Felicity Nelson, has admitted that the National Democratic Congress (NDC) erred in its initial statement on the sexual abuse allegations involving the headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School. Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, October 24, Ms Nelson disclosed that she strongly disagreed with the party’s initial response and publicly criticised it immediately after its release. “I just want to admit that yes, our party goofed. Instantly, the minute they issued that statement, I wrote against it,” she stated. According to her, although the allegations remain unproven, the party should have prioritised the welfare of the children involved rather than allowing political considerations to overshadow the need for justice. She stressed that political parties have a responsibility to demonstrate compassion and support for children, particularly when serious allegations of sexual abuse emerge. “The idea that these are allegations, but as a party, we must always ensure that when we are talking about children, we must ensure that we care, and we support children,” she said. Ms Nelson maintained that while the political career of an individual facing such allegations could be put on hold, efforts to protect children and pursue justice must not be delayed. “So even though they still stand as allegations, his political career, he can put that on hold, but we cannot put the justice we need to seek for the children on hold,” she emphasised. She further questioned the message the party’s initial response sent to children and parents across the country. “What message are we sending to the kids out there and all the mothers, all the fathers, all the parents out there?” she asked. Despite her criticism, Ms Nelson welcomed the party’s subsequent decision to revise its position, describing the correction as a positive step. “So I feel like we did goof. I admit that we goofed, but I am glad to see that we went back and corrected that,” she added. Her comments follow public controversy surrounding allegations of sexual abuse involving female students at Obuasi Senior High Technical School, brought to light through an investigative documentary by journalist Manasseh Azure Awuni. The school’s headmaster, Zakaria Abdulai, has denied wrongdoing, and the allegations remain subject to investigation. Ms Nelson’s remarks highlight her position that the protection of children and the pursuit of justice must take precedence over political loyalty, while respecting the presumption of innocence of individuals facing allegations.

title: Israeli green card holder charged with illegal voting in 2024 US presidential election
body: Israeli citizen Yehuda Peer was one of nine Pennsylvania residents charged with illegally voting in the 2024 US election, the US Department of Justice announced on Friday. Peer, a lawful permanent US resident but not a US citizen, has been charged with one count of voting by an alien. Citizens of Poland, Cuba, Kenya, Russia, Greece, and the Netherlands have also been charged with voting in the 2024 and 2022 elections.  If convicted, they face a maximum possible sentence of a fine, one year in prison, or both.  Illegal voting affront to principles of democratic republic, US attorney says“These cases are important because the crime of illegal voting undermines the integrity of our elections and harms citizens by stealing the power of our votes,” said Brian Miller, United States Attorney for the Middle District of Pennsylvania.“Illegal voting is not a victimless crime but a serious affront to the principles of our democratic republic,” he added.  “Illegally casting a ballot in a federal election corrupts the electoral process and diminishes the voice of every lawful voter. These alleged violations undermine public confidence in our democratic institutions and harm the citizens whose votes are entitled to determine our nation's future,” said Homeland Security Investigations Philadelphia Special Agent in Charge Nathan Abel.

title: Ukraine receives only 24 Patriot missiles from USA over past three months - Zelenskyy
body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that Ukraine has received only 24 interceptor missiles for its U.S.-made Patriot air defense systems over the last three months—a quantity far short of what is actually needed.
In an interview with ABC News on Friday, he noted that 30 ballistic missiles were fired at Kyiv just this past Thursday evening.
According to Zelenskyy’s estimates, Ukraine requires an average of 350 Patriot interceptor missiles per month.
Asked if he believes Putin requested that Trump to turn off intelligence-sharing between the U.S. and Ukraine, Zelenskyy responded, "I don't know. I hope, I trust and I hope God bless. No."
The President of Ukraine noted that he does not feel betrayed by the United States, but expressed regret over the lack of American aid. "I feel what I feel. It's not supportive," Zelenskyy said.
He emphasized that he is grateful for the partnership in the war against the Russian Federation, but suggested that, at times, he may not be as "polite" as other partners expect him to be. "Of course I'm a normal person, I'm just human, maybe not such a big humanitarian as Putin, of course … Like between friends, like in the family, you have to be honest, not to play games. I don't play games with Trump. This is my difference between me and Putin. I don't play with him any games. I'm direct, honest," Zelenskyy said.
The Ukrainian head of state believes that this is Trump’s personal decision “to be friends with Putin or not," but suggested that “they're in quite very good relations.”
Zelenskyy stated that the Ukrainian side is "ready to stop this war as quick as possible," but noted that the Russian Federation currently controls more than 19% of Ukrainian territory, and that Ukraine is not prepared to cede any further territory for the sake of ending the war.
As earlier reported, by June 2025, the U.S. military will likely have used up to two-thirds of its stockpile of missile-defense interceptors, even as American defense companies ramp up production. Specifically, Lockheed Martin is working to increase its annual production capacity for advanced PAC-3 interceptors, used in Patriot missile systems, from approximately 600 to 2,000 units. According to Bloomberg, the shortage in missile stockpiles has already affected supplies to other U.S. allies.
German authorities are seeking permission from the USA to assemble an advanced version of the Patriot interceptor missiles at facilities in Germany, stated German Defense Minister Boris Pistorius.
Zelenskyy has stated that Ukraine is not the top priority for suppliers of American PAC-2 and PAC-3 missiles for Patriot air defense systems, as the majority of these have long been directed to the Middle East. According to the president, Ukraine is also working with European and other nations around the world to secure additional missile supplies to protect its population.
According to him, Ukraine received 675 missiles throughout 2023, and 364 in 2025—yet the number of Russian missile strikes has increased during this period. For 2026, the delivery of 264 PAC-3 and PAC-2 missiles was planned. The PAC-3 missiles are supplied by the United States through the PURL program. "All our partners—both Americans and Europeans—are aware of the sums they are contributing and know exactly how many missiles they are providing us. There are also separate bilateral agreements with various European nations and countries in the Middle East. But, unfortunately, you can see a downward trend, and this depends primarily on the American side," Zelenskyy stated in August of this year.
On October 21, Ukrainian Minister of Defence Yevhen Khmara and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of Ukraine Mykhailo Drapaty met with a delegation from the American defence company Lockheed Martin, led by Orlando Sanchez Jr., President of Lockheed Martin Aeronautics. The discussions focused on the importance of stable arms supplies and future cooperation. In particular, the parties addressed increasing the delivery of PAC-3 interceptor missiles to counter the threat of strikes by Russian ballistic missiles.

title: Russia running sabotage campaign across Europe
body: Russia is conducting a campaign of hybrid attacks and sabotage across Europe, and Britain is working with the United States to deter and contest activity that threatens Euro-Atlantic security, according to an answer given in Parliament. Jim Shannon, the Democratic Unionist Party member for Strangford, had asked what steps are being taken to work with the United States to reduce the Russian threat to both home territories. Louise Sandher-Jones, the Minister for the Armed Forces, said: “As our closest defence and security partner, we engage and collaborate with the US regularly on a range of issues. We know Russia is conducting a campaign of hybrid attacks and sabotage across Europe. The UK does not seek confrontation with Russia, but we will continue to deter and contest activity that threatens Euro-Atlantic security.” Answering a separate question from Shannon on support for Poland and Lithuania, Sandher-Jones said: “The UK stands ready to defend every inch of Allied territory, with NATO remaining the cornerstone of the UK’s defence and security. This is reflected in our commitment to reach NATO’s defence spending target of 3.5% of GDP by 2035. Article 5 of the North Atlantic Treaty makes clear that an armed attack against one NATO Ally is considered an attack against the entire NATO Alliance. “As the third-largest cash spender on defence in NATO, the UK contributes significantly towards the security of NATO’s eastern flank, which includes Poland and Lithuania. This is demonstrated through rotational air policing, troop deployments, and joint exercises, including maritime surveillance in the Baltic region. NATO is a defensive alliance and does not seek confrontation with Russia, but Russia should understand that any attack on a NATO ally would be a grave miscalculation.” Wes Streeting told the Defence Committee this month that hybrid activity of this kind amounts to state backed terrorism. European governments have attributed arson, parcel bombs, rail sabotage, cable damage and drone incursions over airports and military sites to Russian intelligence services or to proxies recruited through messaging apps. The post Russia running sabotage campaign across Europe first appeared on UK Defence Journal .

title: Campaign Turns Ugly As Israeli Election Nears
body: Days ahead of close-fought Israeli elections, campaigns have gone into overdrive with poor-taste jibes and inflammatory attacks against candidates, sometimes crossing red lines. Fuelled in part by a boom in AI-generated images flooding social media, candidates and activists are seeking to portray their opponents as weak, untrustworthy or damaging for the country as they play on stereotypes and fears to sway public opinion. The electioneering has at times turned personal, with some candidates who lost loved ones in the wars following Hamas’s October 7, 2023 attack even having their bereavement dragged into the campaign. Ahead of Tuesday’s vote, polls show Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc neck and neck with that of his main centre-right rival Gadi Eisenkot. On Wednesday, Eisenkot posted a video on X wishing Netanyahu a happy 77th birthday that featured a slate of AI-generated characters including a Hamas member speaking from a tunnel. “What can we wish for the person who has been protecting us for 20 years?” the militant says, evoking theories that the premier has deliberately helped the Islamist movement stay in power in Gaza, charges vehemently denied by Netanyahu. Soon after, an AI depiction of Iran’s supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei pops up, telling Netanyahu: “One more round without victory and I’ll make you a bomb as a present.” Netanyahu has also liberally weaponised AI-generated content against his rival. In July, he posted a video depicting Eisenkot rejecting a hug from a young man wearing a T-shirt with the slogan “Israel unity” and instead embracing Arab-Israeli candidate Mansour Abbas. The clip sparked widespread outrage over claims the young man had been made to resemble Eisenkot’s son, who was killed fighting in Gaza in 2023, something Netanyahu’s party denied. In an interview broadcast by Channel 13, Eisenkot said he had felt “deep contempt for Netanyahu and his entourage” after watching the video. Netanyahu’s camp has used AI throughout the campaign to stoke fears over a possible opposition coalition including Arab-Israeli parties. Clips have ranged from Jewish opposition politicians taking off masks to reveal Arab-Israeli candidates underneath, to Arabs looming over what appears to be a crumbling parliament building. Billboards for Netanyahu’s Likud party with the phrase “The Right or Palestine” alongside the faces of Arab-Israeli politicians have also sprung up across the country. “It’s incitement, especially from Prime Minister Netanyahu’s camp,” said Thair Abu Ras, head of the Forum for Regional Thinking at the Van Leer Jerusalem Institute. “This whole notion of having an Arab party in the coalition is illegitimate in the eyes of the right wing, and they’re trying to enforce that kind of way of thinking on the Eisenkot coalition as well,” he told AFP. Apparently racialised comments have been levelled at Eisenkot, the son of Moroccan Jews. This month, a senior commentator on the pro-Netanyahu Channel 14 television station described him as “a monkey”. While the term is not necessarily a racial slur in Hebrew, the remark drew widespread condemnation from opposition politicians and from Netanyahu himself. This picture taken on October 14, 2026 shows supporters of Itamar Ben Gvir, Israel’s national security minister and head of the far-right Otzma Yehudit (Jewish Power) party, shouting slogans as he tours a market during a meet-and-greet as part of his campaign ahead of Israel’s legislative election, in Ramle. ‘Disgusting’ Social Media Comments The election is the first since Hamas’s October 2023 attack. Some candidates are people whose lives were transformed that day or in the wars that followed, but trauma or bereavement have not spared them from personal attacks. Laly Derai, whose son was killed fighting in Gaza in 2024, is running for the new far-right Amcha Israel party, which advocates universal conscription into the Israeli military — an increasingly contentious issue due to exemptions for religious students. She says she has faced a coordinated smear campaign against her, which has at times invoked her son’s death and accusations that she is betraying his memory. Arab-led Joint List political alliance candidates Ahmad Tibi (centre, R), Yousef Jabareen (C), and Sami Abu Shehadeh (centre, L) attend a meeting of the Arab-led Joint List party as part of the campaign ahead of Israel’s legislative election, in Ara in northern Israel on October 23, 2026. Posters calling for her to withdraw her candidacy so as not to “put the country in danger” have sprung up in the area around the settlement where she lives in the occupied West Bank. “They’re trying to break me but, paradoxically or not, this campaign has reinforced my decision to enter politics precisely to put an end to this hate-filled rhetoric,” she told AFP. Speaking to public broadcaster KAN, she said she had received “phone calls at all hours of the day and night, disgusting comments on social media, signs posted in our towns, including near our children’s school buses — all of this just because we dared to propose something new.” Relatives of hostages formerly held by Hamas have also been caught in the crosshairs. On an unofficial Facebook page for supporters of Netanyahu’s Likud party, an image was posted on Tuesday pitting one mother of a former hostage against another. One mother, Likud candidate Talik Gvili, looks calm against the backdrop of an Israeli flag, while Einav Zangauker — a vocal critic of Netanyahu — looks frenzied around protesters tinted in red. “It is us or them,” the caption reads. AFP The post Campaign Turns Ugly As Israeli Election Nears appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Sinai Monastery Agreement Reached as Archbishop Symeon Prepares to Sign Deal with Egypt
body: Archbishop Symeon says an agreement with the Egyptian government will help safeguard the historic Holy Monastery of Saint Catherine at Mount Sinai, following months of negotiations and support from Orthodox Churches. The future of the historic Holy Monastery of Saint Catherine at Mount Sinai has taken a significant step towards resolution, with Archbishop Symeon announcing his intention to sign an agreement with the Egyptian state. In a statement released on Saturday, October 24, the Archbishop said the agreement would help resolve outstanding issues surrounding the monastery’s legal status and protect its historic and legal rights. The announcement follows more than a year of negotiations between the monastery and the Egyptian government, amid legal proceedings that raised concerns about the future of one of Christianity’s oldest monastic communities. Archbishop Symeon said he would proceed with signing the agreement as soon as his health permits. A specific date will be determined in consultation with the monastery’s brotherhood and the Egyptian government. Orthodox Churches unite behind the agreement The Archbishop highlighted the support received from the Ecumenical Patriarchate, the Patriarchate of Jerusalem, the Patriarchate of Alexandria, and the Churches of Greece and Cyprus. According to his statement, the Orthodox Churches expressed their unanimous support for signing the agreement, hoping it would provide a secure resolution to the outstanding issues while safeguarding the monastery’s longstanding rights. Archbishop Symeon described the development as an expression of unity among the Orthodox Churches of the East, emphasising the importance of their collective support for the monastery. He also acknowledged the assistance of the Greek state and supporters of the monastery around the world during the negotiations. Legal uncertainty surrounding the monastery The negotiations followed a ruling by the Ismailia Court of Appeal on May 28, 2025, which preceded Archbishop Symeon’s election. The monastery subsequently received a draft agreement from the Egyptian government intended to clarify aspects of the court ruling and establish how it would be implemented. According to the Archbishop, the proposed agreement sought to preserve the monastery’s centuries-old traditions and uninterrupted monastic life while clarifying its position within Egypt’s modern legal framework. The monastery requested additional time to examine the proposal, submit amendments and prepare documentation concerning its historical status and the properties under discussion. Archbishop Symeon said the Egyptian government, under President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi, had allowed the dialogue to continue for more than a year. He expressed confidence that the announcement of the agreement removed the grounds for issuing an expected decision by Egypt’s Court of Cassation on October 24. The precise legal implications of the announcement will depend on the agreement’s final terms and implementation. A historic centre of Orthodox Christianity The Holy Monastery of Saint Catherine stands at the foot of Mount Sinai in Egypt’s Sinai Peninsula. Dating back to the sixth century, it is one of the most significant centres of Christian monasticism and holds exceptional importance for the Orthodox Christian world. The monastery has maintained a distinctive ecclesiastical tradition and a spiritual presence in the region for approximately 1,500 years. Its future has attracted international attention because of its religious significance, historical legacy and longstanding relationship with both Egypt and the wider Orthodox Christian community. Archbishop Symeon said the monastery would continue its religious mission, with its monks welcoming pilgrims, visitors and travellers. He also expressed gratitude to the Orthodox Church leaders who supported the agreement, attributing the unity surrounding the negotiations to the intercession of Saint Catherine, the monastery’s patron saint. The announcement marks an important development in efforts to secure the monastery’s future, although the agreement is still to be formally signed. title: RAF Typhoons join French nuclear exercise for first time, escorting Rafale strike mission
body: The UK Defence Nuclear Enterprise described the exercise as “a landmark moment” in Franco-British defence relations. In a social media post, it said the exercise marked a significant advance in coordination between Europe’s only two nuclear powers. The Rafales took off from Saint-Dizier Air Base in eastern France, with the British jets flying as escorts. The UK Ministry of Defence said no nuclear weapons were involved. According to the ministry, the aim was to improve how the two air forces work together, and the exercise showed they are ready to respond jointly to serious threats. “This exercise marks a new chapter in the defence nuclear relationship between the United Kingdom and France,” said Defence Secretary Wes Streeting. “As Europe’s nuclear powers, we have a shared responsibility to contribute to the security and stability of the Euro-Atlantic region. Paris was keen to stress that working more closely with London does not mean giving up control of its own nuclear forces. “Having independent nuclear forces does not exclude coordination,” said Catherine Vautrin, France’s Minister of the Armed Forces and Veterans. “Our nuclear cooperation with the United Kingdom keeps deepening: on Tuesday night, UK Typhoons participated for the very first time [in] a French nuclear exercise alongside Rafales.” Streeting said the exercise showed both the depth of the partnership and the credibility of the two countries’ deterrents. The Defence Nuclear Enterprise linked it to a shared commitment to European security, collective defence and credible deterrence at a time of growing threats. The UK has committed £63 billion over four years to nuclear defence, covering the Dreadnought and SSN-AUKUS submarine programmes, a new warhead and other work. It also plans to buy 12 F-35A jets and join NATO’s nuclear mission. More broadly, UK-French defence ties are governed by the refreshed Lancaster House Agreement, which provides for a larger joint deployable force, deeper nuclear cooperation and joint work on next-generation weapons.

title: I want my Wednesday back
body:
Freelance dev/devops/security. Click here to learn more about my background and the services I offer.
Or, why we’re not seeing mass-exploitation of php2shell yet.
Update 2026-10-25: three days after the patch was available, the first public evidence appeared of exploitation in the wild. This was a honeypot, presumably a low-traffic sensor. As far as I can tell, the technique matches my description below. So seems likely that at this point, mass-exploitation of low-traffic sites has begun. The constraints making exploitation of mid/high traffic websites unlikely, to my knowledge, still stand.
Update 2026-10-25: regarding high-traffic sites, a public $2k bounty on stealmybitcoin.com has not yet been claimed. However, Dan Guido of Trail of Bits, claims they have a reliable exploit that works under load. If so, that’s faster than I expected. I have not seen public confirmation, or what they mean by “under load.”
Update 2026-10-25: discussions on lobste.rs and reddit .
Update 2026-10-26: stealmybitcoin.com was not vulnerable the first 20 hours, then got hacked within hours using this PoC . It uses a different technique: send one producer request, then consumer requests for all workers, and pipeline them to reduce chances of random other requests interfering. It does require that the final request ends up at the same worker, and the PoC README notes that the technique depends on knowing the exact worker count.
When multiple containers are behind a loadbalancer, each with their own ASLR layout, I don’t think this exploit would work. Possibly if you use number_of_workers * number_of_containers (assuming you somehow determine both) and keep hammering until you get very lucky and all requests of all stages end up in the same container. Session stickiness could change that, but is not a default for common load balancers and uncommon in mid/high traffic websites. In my experience HTTP pipelining also won’t force common load balancers to send all requests to the same container.
With what is currently known, I maintain that this was a critical vulnerability that should be patched asap, but recommending downtime was an overreaction for mid/high traffic websites. That response would be appropriate for a shellshock/heartbleed style vulnerability where the complexity is low, and mass exploitation can begin almost immediately after the patch is released. I’m concerned that if recommending downtime becomes normal for critical but complex vulnerabilities, the advice will get ignored when the next heartbleed or shellshock is found.
But if more information comes out, I’ll be happy to follow-up that I no longer want my Wednesday back.
I saw wildly varying opinions on whether php2shell is serious, or if they cried wolf. Got curious, started digging into the PoCs. I’m not an exploit dev and maybe there were other factors, so take with a grain of salt. Egg on my face if mass exploitation starts right as I hit publish.
Best PoC of php2shell I’ve found: https://github.com/9bie/php2shell-bypass-aslr-exp (and a fork with all docs translated to english )
To exploit, you need to do four consecutive (correction: some of the requests need to be consecutive, not all four) requests to the same php worker process . And you need to know the exact php build (php version, OS version, architecture), or try exploits for every possible build.
What this PoC does is take a docker image that uses the default mod_php number of workers, which is 150. Then it opens 149 connections that send half a request to keep the other workers busy, and does the four exploit requests against the 150th worker.
Even a moderately popular production website will have multiple web VMs/containers running multiple php workers behind a load balancer and constant bot traffic. That means you would have to try a wide range of number of connections to open. On top of that you likely won’t know the exact build version, so you would have to try exploits for every combination out there.
Let’s say you try this for the 50 most popular php/OS combinations, and any number of workers between 10 and 1010. That’s 50k attempts. But against constant background traffic, you would need to try each combination a number of times. Each of these attempts involves opening a whole lot of connections, so they each take some time. The PoC runs against localhost and takes 3-4 seconds, so let’s optimistically call it 10 seconds on the internet.
You can only do one attempt at a time, so that means multiple days of bruteforcing in a way that is essentially a DoS, since a large part of that range will exhaust the maximum number of connections. At this point the person running the site will likely notice, start blocking IP addresses or adding a WAF.
Most high-traffic websites already run WAFs/rate-limiting to deal with bot traffic, so you would need to run this attack from a great many IPs, and preferably clean ones that are harder to come by. But running this from many IPs also increases the chances that your timing will be off, reducing the number of plausible attempts even further.
That’s assuming the WAF doesn’t block your attempts entirely, because the easiest ways to exploit these vulnerabilities were known at the time of the announcement.
I’m sure people and agents will come up with clever techniques to reduce the required number of attempts eventually. But that has nothing to do with “this will get mass-exploited within 15 minutes.”
Against very low-traffic websites that do not have any bot protection, leak information about their version, running close to stock configuration, you might get lucky.
So sure, it’s a critical vulnerability, deserves attention, should be patched ASAP. Maybe even put in the announcement that if you’re running low-traffic sites, be extra sure to patch fast.
But to the AI security vendors who promoted this as THE GATES OF HELL WILL OPEN YOU HAVE TO PATCH WITHIN 15 MINUTES OR DIE? I want my Wednesday back.
Oh and the claims of it being exploited in the wild? At time of writing, they’re referring to exploitation attempts . In fact, HoneyLabs so far hasn’t seen a single exploit attempt that could even run successfully.

title: US Senators Threaten Nomination Block Over Ukraine Starlink Curbs
body:
A bipartisan group of US senators is preparing to block the confirmation of US President Donald Trump’s nominees for federal posts until the White House ensures the restoration of full Starlink functionality for the Ukrainian military, The New York Times reported.
Citing three people familiar with the matter, the report noted that the planned holds could intensify an escalating conflict between Capitol Hill and the executive branch over the administration’s foreign policy approach toward Russia .
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
The legislative standoff is anticipated to unfold during the lame-duck congressional session following the Nov. 3 midterm elections , when Republican leaders are expected to seek floor confirmations for dozens of executive and judicial nominees before the conclusion of the 119th Congress.
The procedural pushback underscores widening resistance within Congress to the administration’s recent accommodations toward Moscow , with senior Republicans increasingly joining Democrats to challenge executive decisions regarding security assistance and sanctions policy.
Lawmakers from both chambers have linked recent operational curbs on Ukrainian defense communications directly to shifting policies in Washington.
Republican Representative Brian Fitzpatrick of Pennsylvania stated that he would seek the dismissal of federal officials responsible for disrupting Starlink services in Ukraine, alongside appropriations cuts for their respective agencies.
Fitzpatrick, a former FBI supervisory special agent who worked on Russian counterintelligence matters in Kyiv, questioned claims that the technical restrictions were coincidental amid public criticism directed by Trump toward President Volodymyr Zelensky .
“I personally don’t believe in the coincidence theory,” Fitzpatrick said.
The disruptions were also addressed during a secure telephone consultation between Zelensky and a bipartisan group of senators organized by Democrat Richard Blumenthal of Connecticut and Republican Thom Tillis of North Carolina. According to the lawmakers, the Ukrainian president reported that vital satellite services remained subjected to operational limitations.
“Funding the Russian war machine, cutting off Ukraine’s satellite communications , and degrading its air defenses all stand in the way of peace,” Blumenthal and Tillis stated in a joint communique.
A Senate aide confirmed that while the Senate Foreign Relations Committee previously approved the transfer of multiple tranches of air defense interceptors to Ukraine, the munitions have not yet reached Ukrainian military inventories.
The aide added that congressional committees are exploring a formal investigation into SpaceX regarding service disruptions in Ukraine and have instructed commercial entities involved in Russian diesel transactions to retain records for future oversight inquiries.
The congressional backlash coincides with disclosures detailing repeated interventions by both the Biden and Trump administrations requesting SpaceX founder Elon Musk to adjust Starlink coverage parameters across international conflict zones, Reuters reported, citing six former senior US officials.
According to former officials, Washington has sought both to constrain access in specific geographic areas to deny connectivity to hostile paramilitary networks and to expand coverage to support allied military operations or anti-government demonstrators.
Under the Biden administration, US authorities asked SpaceX to deactivate Starlink coverage in sectors of Yemen and southern Lebanon to prevent misuse by Iran -aligned armed groups.
In October 2023, amid combat engagements between Israeli forces and Hezbollah in southern Lebanon, US intelligence alerted the White House to reports that individuals linked to the militant movement possessed satellite terminals.
Similar precautions were raised in 2024 regarding Yemen’s Houthi movement during American air operations.
Conversely, the Biden administration coordinated with SpaceX to activate Starlink in Iran following civil protests in September 2022 that erupted after the custodial death of Mahsa Amini, with US agencies helping facilitate the transport of satellite terminals into the country.
Immediately following the launch of Russia’s February 2022 full-scale invasion of Ukraine , US officials also pressed for the rapid expansion of Starlink access for Ukrainian defense forces.
The Trump administration similarly approached Musk to ensure Starlink operations across Iran following joint US- Israeli military strikes in 2025 and 2026, aiming to facilitate communications for anti-government demonstrations.
The revelations mark the first detailed public accounting of formal executive branch requests directing the operational footprint of commercial satellite communications in foreign operational theaters.
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

title: AI will not replace human musicians as it lacks originality, Sennheiser boss says
body: Artificial intelligence will be unable to replace human craft in the music industry because it lacks the ability to create original work, the chairman of German audio major Sennheiser has said. While AI can be used as a tool to support the creation of music, the booming technology is largely only able to produce output based on what it has been trained on, raising questions about actual creativity, Daniel Sennheiser said. "AI is a calculation of probability ... it comes out with basically everything that it knows, but it cannot create something new," Mr Sennheiser, who is also co-chief executive of the Wedemark-based company, told The National in an interview in Dubai. "Therefore, if you make your own music, if you create something, you're always going to be safe. AI can support you in your creative process and actually even inspire you ... but it will never replace a [musician]." Several industries have grown concerned with the growth of AI, as the technology becomes more powerful and is able to create works in music, film, arts and other endeavours that have relied on human skill and talent. Music artists and unions have been protesting against copyright infringement and the overall lack of originality when it comes to AI-generated music. Even streaming services are taking action. This week, Spotify said it had removed about 50 million songs it deemed as AI slop over the past year. Generative AI in music, however, is growing to become big business: revenue in the market is projected to hit almost $2.8 billion by 2030, nearly triple the estimated $960.4 million this year, data from Grand View Research shows. "Like with every new technology, initially you're very afraid of the substitution that it's doing. And, yes, [AI] is creating some what I call background music, which you can do very well with AI today," said Mr Sennheiser, the third-generation leader of the company founded in 1945. "AI tools are allowing much more people to be creative with music ... it's more of a support than anything else." Supply chains and UAE focus Mr Sennheiser said the current supply chain disruptions, as a result of geopolitical conflicts and tariff battles, have not directly affected the company, owing to in-house operations and third-party relationships. For instance, Sennheiser has its own assembly line for surface-mount devices, or those that place electronic components on circuit boards. The company is also not affected by shortages in chips and critical minerals such as neodymium, as the audio industry does not use those components on a broad scale unlike manufacturers of smartphones and computers. It also helps that Sennheiser is based in Germany, considered the manufacturing hub of Europe that is home to key industries such as car making, chemicals, engineering and technology. "We were always able to deliver more or less every product ... we find our way around those shortages," Mr Sennsheiser said. He did acknowledge, however, that Sennheiser raises prices based on the costs of raw materials, transport and manufacturing, which includes energy. "We look at what is available in the market and what is sustainable, so we have a regular schedule of increasing prices based on the realities that are there," Mr Sennheiser said. The company will also continue to invest in the Middle East, especially in the UAE, where its Dubai office serves the wider region, including CIS countries. The company does not divulge market share numbers. Mr Sennheiser, however, noted that while the brand is underrepresented in some markets, they have a "fair share" in others, including the UAE. "I see the market growing and that's why I want to invest in this region," he said, without providing details.

title: U.S. birth rate drops to record low, but older women are having more babies
body:
Fewer women in their 20s are choosing to become mothers, leading to an overall birthrate decline in the U.S. But the birth rate among U.S. women age 30-45 is rising according to the latest federal data. Charly Triballeau/AFP hide caption
Sarah Harris was 36 years old when she gave birth to her daughter Bridget last year. She describes motherhood as equal parts joy and exhaustion. "When you have a baby in your mid-30s, what you gain in wisdom and experience you also lose in terms of energy," Harris says with a laugh.
Harris, who lives in Vermont, was laid off from a job four months after Bridget was born. She says she's still figuring out what her career and her life will look like with a child. Harris thinks a lot of women are like her. They're wrestling with financial uncertainty and waiting much later to choose pregnancy.
There's also the high cost of raising a child, which Harris said convinced her that one is enough. "I think in another era or another life or another scenario, I might have had more children," Harris says. "I think we're in a difficult societal moment and so that's absolutely affecting people's reproductive choices."
Harris is, in fact, part of a slow revolution in what motherhood and parenting look like in the United States The latest report from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention found the general fertility rate for women fell by 1% to a new record low in 2025. That continues a two-decade trend toward fewer children.
The one-year drop for 20-somethings was even more eye-catching. "Certainly the 6% decline in the birthrate for women age 20 to 24 is noteworthy," said Brady Hamilton, a demographer at the CDC's National Center for Health Statistics who co-authored the report. He noted that teenagers also saw a 7% decline.
A separate study released last month by the Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta found Gen Z women twenties, "are dramatically less likely to want children" compared with U.S. women of previous generations.
"Several factors have been identified as contributing to this lower desire to have children, such as increased labor market opportunities and agency among women, rising financial costs, changing priorities, and [concerns about] maternal mortality," the study found.
Dr. Tanise Branche, medical director of labor and delivery at Temple Health, a health, research and training network in Philadelphia, told NPR more of her younger women patients are following a different life script.
"They're starting to focus not necessarily just on what they can bring to kids, but what's going to be best for them," she says.
Meanwhile, the latest CDC data shows a small but significant increase in older women, ages 30 to 45, who are choosing to become pregnant.
Branche says more women, including herself, are building careers and stable lives before becoming mothers.
Branche is currently pregnant with her fourth child. "I will be 43 with my last delivery and I started this reproductive journey at 37," she said. "I see the net positive being that we have a choice."
As a consequence of this shift, there are fewer children now in the U.S. The population under age 18 is falling steadily, according to the U.S. Census Bureau, dropping by more than 1 million from 2010 to 2020 .
Some experts also believe women would choose to have more kids if they could afford them and had proper supports that include affordable housing, daycare and health insurance.
"The fact that there are a lot of people who still say they want families, but don't feel like they're able to have them [is a concern]," says Anna Louie Sussman, author of a new book on parenting choices called Inconceivable . "Young people say, I can barely take care of myself I can't imagine taking care of someone else."
Sussman herself is part of the trend toward delayed motherhood. Because of her own concerns about affordability and her career, she froze her eggs and waited to have her child until she was in her early 40s.
"I do feel lucky that I'm a little further along professionally than I would have been in my 20s or even 30s," she said.
As women build different lives and birthrates keep falling, the U.S. is changing. The median age is rising rapidly, reaching 39.4 years old in 2025 . More states, including Vermont where Sarah Harris lives, are seeing actual population decline, according to the Census Bureau .
"I think about it a lot because I live in a very small place where we're hoping to keep the doors of our elementary school open for as long as we can," she says.
Editor's note: An earlier version of this story cited U.S. data for falling birthrates among individuals age 15 to 19, describing them as women. The reference has been changed to describe the group as teenagers. Nov. 1, 2026
A previous version of this story mistakenly stated Sarah Harris’ age as 37 when she gave birth to her first child. She was 36.

title: Is your Medicare Advantage plan ending next year? Here's what to know
body:
Medicare chief Dr. Mehmet Oz speaks at an event announcing the artificial intelligence website, America.gov in Washington, D.C., last month. Jim Watson/AFP via Getty Images hide caption
A slew of Medicare Advantage plans are disappearing for next year, leaving seniors in many areas with fewer options. In 193 counties across the country, no plans are offered at all.
Medicare's annual open enrollment period kicked off October 15 and runs until December 7, and seniors enrolled in those privatized Medicare plans that are closing in certain markets should carefully review their options.
Medicare Advantage means private insurers run Medicare for older Americans who choose it over traditional Medicare, where the federal government itself administers the program. More than half of the 70 million Americans in Medicare choose Medicare Advantage. It's popular because it covers services like vision and dental, often with lower premiums than traditional Medicare. It also often folds in the "Part D" drug benefit, simplifying that decision.
But a downside of Medicare Advantage is that companies can pick and choose where they offer plans. If a certain community is not profitable, a company can leave that market. And that has been happening on an increasingly large scale the last three years, according to research published in JAMA.
Big swaths of rural America are losing Medicare Advantage choices and so are some major metro areas.
Last year, 2.9 million seniors were in Medicare Advantage plans that closed up shop, according to JAMA. This year, an analysis of insurance company announcements by An Arm and A Leg podcast, shows at least 2 million people will be affected. Other preliminary estimates range from 3.2 million to 5 million seniors. About 35 million people are enrolled in Medicare Advantage.
According to an analysis of federal data by the health policy research organization KFF, the 193 counties that will have zero Medicare Advantage plans are mostly rural. Last year that number was about 120 counties without a plan offered.
KFF's numbers also show that there will be far fewer plans offered in some metro areas. Dallas, Minneapolis, Seattle, Houston and Portland all have between a quarter and a third fewer Medicare Advantage plans for seniors.
If your plan is ending, and you don't choose another, the insurance company will assign you to another Medicare Advantage plan or the government will enroll you in traditional Medicare — but without a supplemental or drug plan.
If you want to switch from Medicare Advantage to traditional Medicare and your plan is ending, you can enroll in a Medicare supplemental plan — also known as Medigap — without the same restrictions that you would normally have. If you have a pre-existing condition that has prevented you from enrolling in Medigap before, that could be good news.
Another wrinkle this year is that insurance companies can cap enrollments on some of the Medicare Advantage plans that they do offer.
Which means: If you wait to sign up, a plan you want might already be full.
The companies are supposed to enroll people on a first-come, first-serve basis — and not cherry-pick customers based on health conditions, age, or demographics.
Another reason not to delay is that with so many people on the hunt for new plans, it may take longer than usual to get help.
Here are some tips for navigating Medicare open enrollment this year:

title: Edo Govt, NLC Resolve Dispute As NUEE Moves To Restore Electricity
body: Electricity supply is set to be restored in Edo State after Governor Monday Okpebholo and leaders of organised labour settled the dispute over recognition of the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) caretaker committee in the state. According to a Press Release by the Chief Press Secretary to the governor, Patrick Ebojele, the agreement was reached at a closed-door meeting in Abuja convened by the Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), Senator George Akume. Also present were NLC President, Comrade Joe Ajaero; Minister of Labour and Employment, Dr Muhammad Maigari Dingyadi; and former Edo State Governor and ex-NLC President, Senator Adams Oshiomhole. Speaking to journalists after the meeting, Governor Okpebholo said the parties had resolved the matter. According to him, the state government would recognise the caretaker committee and work with labour leaders on arrangements for a substantive election. “There is no issue actually, and we have resolved the issues that border the NLC caretaker committee in Edo,” he said. The Governor of Edo State, Monday Okpebholo, the Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), Senator George Akume, NLC President, Comrade Joe Ajaero, Minister of Labour and Employment, Dr Muhammad Maigari Dingyadi, former Edo State Governor and ex-NLC President, Senator Adams Oshiomhole and others at the settlement meeting in Abuja. Ajaero confirmed the agreement and thanked the Governor, Akume, Dingyadi and Oshiomhole for their roles. He said labour had agreed to work with the state government on recognising the caretaker committee, organising a substantive election, and addressing the rights and privileges due to the committee. “Consequently, power will be restored in Edo,” Ajaero said. Oshiomhole described the dispute as a communication gap, which he said had now been resolved. He said the reason for continuing the action no longer existed. He also noted the Governor’s offer to rebuild trust between the Edo State Government and organised labour, and said renewed cooperation was needed to maintain industrial harmony. Dingyadi said the parties had agreed to work together for the peace and progress of Edo State and Nigeria. He said the NLC would conduct a substantive election in Edo within three to six months. “The principal issue, which is electricity, is going to be restored immediately,” the minister said. Akume commended the participants for their willingness to settle the matter through dialogue. The power outage followed two related but separate disputes. The first was an industrial disagreement between BEDC Electricity Plc and the National Union of Electricity Employees (NUEE) over workers’ pay and welfare. The second was a leadership dispute with the Edo State NLC, led by Joseph Igbafe, over recognition of its caretaker committee. The post Edo Govt, NLC Resolve Dispute As NUEE Moves To Restore Electricity appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Talking your language: UAE unveils AI tool designed to master Arabic dialects
body: A cutting-edge Abu Dhabi university has unveiled an Arabic AI tool designed to decode a variety of regional dialects and respond to rapid shifts in language. Jais 3 – built by the Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence, in partnership with Abu Dhabi's Inception42 – is able to field queries and carry out tasks such as transcribing conversations and creating documents and presentations. It features Jais speech, a voice recognition model for the Arabic language and its varying dialects from across the Gulf and North Africa. The advanced AI platform was developed through the university's Institute of Foundation Models (IFM) with the goal of keeping pace with the nuances of a language spoken by more than 400 million people around the world. The tech is also able to deal with code-switching, which refers to when a bilingual person alternates from one language to another. "Arabic AI needs to understand the language in its everyday context, which varies by geography and across generations," said Haonan Li, senior research scientist at IFM. "For example, we need to account for the many nuances in spoken Arabic, including when speakers slip into English or French mid-sentence and back again. We built Jais 3 for Arabic as it's really used." High-tech training Jais Speech transcribes Modern Standard Arabic and dialects spoken across 19 Arab countries. It follows speakers as they switch between Arabic and languages such as English or French, keeping those words in their original script. It also identifies the dialect being spoken and can add Arabic vowel marks to a transcript. Paired with the language models, Jais Speech enables Jais 3 to take spoken instructions in Arabic or English and act on them. Mr Li said the team worked extensively to ensure strong representation of the many forms of Arabic spoken in the region and beyond. “One of the key challenges was ensuring broad and balanced representation across regional dialects," he said. "For Gulf dialects, this involved working with a more limited pool of existing open data and addressing the tendency of open models to default to Modern Standard Arabic rather than maintaining the requested dialect when generating synthetic data. "This required additional work in data synthesis and filtering to ensure the quality and relevance of the resulting data set." A similar challenge was faced by the Jais 3 team for Morocco, where available data tended to be heavily weighted towards Moroccan Darija, leaving other dialects in the region less represented. Embracing technology Richard Morton, vice president and executive director of IFM, said the launch of Jais 3 showed the importance of investing in rapidly evolving technology. "Jais has shown what the UAE's long-term investment in open AI research can deliver for the Arabic-speaking world," he said. "With Jais 3, we are extending that foundation into speech and agents at a time when the UAE is putting AI to work across government and society – reflecting MBZUAI's commitment to the UAE National AI Strategy 2031 and to building the research capability and national talent that will carry it forward." IFM and Inception42 evaluated the models on an audited suite of 24 Arabic benchmarks, which they are releasing publicly alongside the models. The results showed the largest Jais 3 model leads open models on agentic tasks and matches the strongest on Arabic understanding. Jais Speech recorded the lowest average word and character error rates among all models compared, while the seven billion and 32 billion-parameter models earned the highest average Arabic scores among open models of comparable sizes. "Jais 3 makes Arabic AI more practical for business use," said Dr Larry Murray, senior vice president of Applied Science at Inception42. "Stronger reasoning and instruction following, combined with tool use, provide a foundation for multi-step agentic workflows. With open models across a range of sizes, organisations can match these capabilities to their computing budgets and deployment needs."
