title: Russian air defenses down 1,297 drones over past 24 hours
body:
MOSCOW, October 24. /TASS/. Russian air defense systems downed a SCALP air-launched cruise missile, four Neptune long-range cruise missiles, and 1,297 Ukrainian fixed-wing drones over the past 24 hours, the Russian Defense Ministry reported.
"Air defense systems have shot down a French-made SCALP air-launched cruise missile, four Neptune long-range cruise missiles, and 1,297 fixed-wing unmanned aerial vehicles," the ministry said in a statement.
The Ukrainian armed forces have lost approximately 1,190 troops over the past 24 hours as a result of actions by Russian armed forces in the special military operation zone, the Russian Defense Ministry reported. According to the ministry, the enemy lost over 200 personnel in the area of responsibility of the Battlegroup North, over 215 due to the actions of the Battlegroup West; up to 180 in the sector of the Battlegroup South, over 350 in the Battlegroup Center’s sector, over 205 in the area of responsibility of the Battlegroup East and up to 40 in the sector of the Battlegroup Dnepr.
Russian forces have struck energy and transport infrastructure facilities used to support the Ukrainian military. "Operational-tactical aviation, attack drones, missile forces, and artillery of the Russian armed forces struck energy and transport infrastructure facilities used by the Ukrainian military, as well as storage and launch sites for long-range unmanned aerial vehicles. Additionally, temporary deployment points for Ukrainian armed formations and foreign mercenaries were hit across 147 areas," the ministry said in a statement.

title: HURIWA urges NASS to withdraw nutritionists’ council bill
body:
The Human Rights Writers Association of Nigeria (HURIWA) has urged the National Assembly to withdraw a proposed bill seeking to establish the Nutritionists Registration Council of Nigeria, warning that it could marginalise indigenous food knowledge and create legal uncertainty around traditional nutritional practices.
HURIWA said the bill, sponsored by Chike Okafor, a member of the House of Representatives representing Ehime Mbano/Ihitte Uboma/Obowo Federal Constituency, requires a fundamental reconsideration because of its proposed regulatory powers and the absence of adequate safeguards for traditional and family-based nutritional knowledge.
The association made the call in a statement issued on Friday by its National Coordinator, Emmanuel Onwubiko.
Mr Onwubiko said the bill should be withdrawn pending transparent and inclusive consultations involving nutrition experts, traditional knowledge holders, farmers, public health professionals, civil society organisations and affected communities.
He said Nigerian communities had developed extensive knowledge of local foods, seasonal diets, food preservation, fermentation, medicinal plants, breastfeeding and complementary feeding long before the emergence of formal nutritional science.
The national coordinator argued that the bill does not adequately protect these practices or clearly distinguish professional nutritional services from ordinary family guidance and the transmission of traditional knowledge.
“HURIWA considers the Bill, in its present form, a deeply troubling legislative proposal that threatens to place Nigeria’s indigenous food knowledge, traditional nutritional practices and community-based systems of learning under the shadow of an overcentralised statutory regulator,” Mr Onwubiko said.
He called for the immediate withdrawal of the bill pending a comprehensive national consultation involving relevant professionals and communities.
Mr Onwubiko said the association was not opposed to professional standards, scientific research or the regulation of qualified nutrition practitioners.
However, he argued that the proposed legislation could create an overcentralised regulatory structure that undermines Nigeria’s indigenous food heritage.
“This is not a rejection of professional standards, scientific research or the legitimate regulation of qualified nutrition practitioners. It is a principled rejection of legislation that seeks to establish sweeping regulatory powers over nutrition without first guaranteeing the protection of Nigeria’s cultural heritage, indigenous knowledge systems and the everyday food practices through which generations of Nigerians have sustained their families and communities,” he added.
HURIWA also called for greater transparency regarding provisions of the bill covering international collaboration, recognition of foreign qualifications, approval of training institutions outside Nigeria, and the receipt of grants, endowments and donations by the proposed council.
The association specifically identified Sections 3, 14, 17 and 32 as requiring more scrutiny, stating that the bill should contain stronger safeguards for transparency and public oversight of external funding.
However, it cautioned against treating international cooperation or foreign funding as evidence of wrongdoing.
HURIWA urged the bill’s sponsors to disclose the consultations and research that informed the proposal and clarify whether foreign organisations, donors or commercial interests participated in developing or promoting the proposed regulatory framework.
The association maintained that Nigerians were entitled to understand the evidence underpinning the proposed regulatory structure and the measures intended to prevent potential conflicts of interest.
The opposition to the bill is the second public rejection of the proposed regulatory framework by groups concerned about its implications for nutrition practice in Nigeria.
The Dietitians Council of Nigeria had previously opposed the proposal, raising concerns about its implications for the regulation of nutrition-related professions and the existing framework governing dietetic practice.
HURIWA’s position highlights the need to clarify the distinction between dietitians and nutritionists, their respective professional responsibilities and the regulatory arrangements governing their practice.
While dietitians are trained to provide medical nutrition therapy and manage diet-related health conditions, nutritionists generally focus on nutrition education, dietary guidance and public health nutrition, although their roles may overlap depending on their training and specialisation.

title: Russian attacks kill 4, injure 78 across Ukraine over past day, as drone strikes Kyiv residential building in the morning
body:
Russian attacks over the last day killed four people and injured 78 across Ukraine over the past day, as Moscow strikes at Kyiv in the morning of Oct. 24, local authorities report.
In the early hours of Oct. 24, a Russian drone struck a residential building in Kyiv’s Obolon District, injuring two people, and cauing a fire, the Kyiv City Military Administration reported .
On Oct. 23, Russian forces attacked the city of Chernihiv in Chernihiv Oblast during the day, killing one man and injuring at least 25 people, local authorities said.
An air raid alert was declared in Chernihiv at around 1:40 p.m. local time due to a missile threat. Minutes later, Ukraine's Air Force reported drones and a Banderol low-cost cruise missile heading toward the city.
Chernihiv City Council said two private businesses were targeted in the Russian attack but provided no further details.
In Donetsk Oblast , Russian shelling of a residential area in the front-line city of Kramatorsk killed one person and injured six more, including three children, the Donetsk Oblast Prosecutor's Office reported on Oct. 23.
In Sloviansk , another front-line town in Donetsk Oblast, Russian attacks throughout the previous day killed one 62-year-old woman and injured four people, Sloviansk Mayor Vadym Lyakh wrote on Oct. 24.
In Dnipropetrovsk Oblast , a Russian attack on the city of Dnipro killed one and injured eight people, while three more people were injured in the Pidhorodnenska community, according to regional governor Oleksandr Hanzha .
In Zhytomyr Oblast , a Russian drone attack in the city of Zhytomyr injured nine people on Oct. 23, including two children, Ukraine’s police force reported .
In Kharkiv Oblast , Russian forces injured seven people, including a 12-year-old girl and a 13-year-old boy, Kharkiv Oblast Governor Oleh Synehubov said. Homes, businesses, and gas stations were also damaged or destroyed in the strikes, he added.
In Kherson Oblast , Russian forces struck residential areas across the region, injuring six people on Oct. 23, the Kherson Oblast Military Administration reported.
In Ukraine's southern Odesa Oblast , three people were injured in Russian attacks over the past day, as Russia struck a recreational building, an administrative building, and a warehouse, said regional governor Oleh Kiper .
In Sumy Oblast , Russia carried out 40 attacks on 25 settlements, injuring five people in several communities over the past day, the regional military administration said. In total, the air alert sounded for more than 18 hours, the administration added.
Overnight, Russian forces launched 126 drones, 61 of which were jet-powered, Ukraine’s Air Force reported . Ukraine managed to suppress 101 drones, including 50 jet-powered drones, the Air Force said. Russia ramped up production of jet-powered drones this year, which are much harder to shoot down than their propeller powered predecessors, while Ukraine has managed to improve the interception rate over the last month.

title: Zoom Versus The Hague: Anatomy of a Russian Sleight of Hand
body:
Before 2022, Izium was an ordinary town in Kharkiv region. It had more than 46,000 people, the Siverskyi Donets River, Kremenets Hill, factories, schools, hospitals and markets.
Oleshky, on the left bank of the Dnipro River opposite Kherson, was home to around 24,000. Enerhodar depended on its nuclear power plant, the largest in Europe. That life ended when Russia came.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
Russian troops seized Izium in the spring of 2022 and held it until Sept. 10, 2022. After liberation, about 10,000 people remained in the town, roughly a fifth of its pre-war population. Local officials estimated that around 80 percent of the town had been destroyed. In a forest on the outskirts, investigators found a mass burial site: 447 bodies, most of them civilians, many bearing signs of torture.
Oleshky has been under occupation since the first days of the full-scale invasion. After the destruction of the Kakhovka dam in June 2023, around 90 percent of the town was flooded. The occupation authorities did not evacuate residents.
Today, about 1,700 people remain in the town center. According to the UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine, no food supplies have reached Oleshky since May 26, 2026. At the end of August, Russian checkpoints blocked all civilian movement and declared the town a “grey zone.”
The approach roads are mined, and humanitarian organizations have no access. For months, Ukrainian forces have been delivering food to residents by drone, in repeated runs; One night alone brought in four tonnes.
On Oct. 15, the Kharkiv Regional Prosecutor’s Office screened the documentary “Evidence” at Filmhuis Den Haag. Journalist Veronika Marchenko made it together with the prosecutors, with support from the GIDNA project of the Future for Ukraine foundation and from Project Expedite Justice.
GIDNA, led by clinical psychologist Anna Hruba, provides free and anonymous support to women who have survived conflict-related sexual violence. The team’s ongoing work is supported by the Defense Intelligence of Ukraine (HUR).
The director had access to official investigation files and closed interrogations. The film covers torture, sexual violence, unlawful detention and executions. It tells the story of a girl who lost her parents and grandmother when a Russian airstrike hit a residential building, and follows the investigation into the killing of a local forensic expert with a disability. It also shows the work of prosecutors and investigators after liberation: exhumations, forensic examinations, identification of specific perpetrators.
After the screening, the coordinator of the Ukraine accountability cluster at the Dutch Ministry of Foreign Affairs moderated a discussion. The audience included Ukraine’s Ambassador to the Netherlands Andriy Kostin, diplomats from other countries, international journalists, and representatives of the Kharkiv Regional Prosecutor’s Office and the International Criminal Court.
The hall was full. The film was later shown to the Ukrainian community in Amsterdam.
Kyrylo Budanov, head of the Office of the President of Ukraine, noted that Russia is trying to prevent information about its crimes from spreading internationally, but despite provocations and attempts to disrupt them, the screenings went ahead.
A week later, Moscow responded with a group video call.
The so-called international “telebridge,” titled “Zaporizhzhia Region: Escalation of the Ukrainian Armed Forces’ Terrorist War,” was initiated by the Russian delegation to the Vienna negotiations on military security together with Rodion Miroshnik, ambassador-at-large of the Russian foreign ministry.
It was moderated by the head of the delegation, Yulia Zhdanova. Rossotrudnichestvo and its network of “Russian Houses” handled the organization.
HUR made the purpose of the operation public before it began. The aim was to divert attention from Russia’s war crimes, above all the catastrophe in Oleshky, to discredit the Ukrainian military and to weaken partners’ support for Kyiv.
Moscow had no answer to the evidence shown in The Hague. So it staged its own show. It responded to Izium by talking about Zaporizhzhia, and said nothing at all about Oleshky.
The main speaker was Miroshnik. He is a former press secretary to Ukraine’s ousted president, Viktor Yanukovych, and a former Party of Regions member of the Luhansk regional council. Since 2014, he has served in the occupation structures in the Luhansk region, and he is under sanctions.
Alongside him spoke the occupation “governor” of Zaporizhzhia region Yevhen Balytskyi, the “head” of Enerhodar Maksym Pukhov, reserve Major General Mykola Plotnikov, and Yuri Chernichuk, appointed by Russia as director of the occupied Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant.
Viewers were also shown “witnesses” and “victims” prepared in advance for the broadcast.
The announcements promised diplomats from 80 countries and representatives of the UN, the OSCE, BRICS and the CIS. The actual line-up: staff of Russian embassies, Rossotrudnichestvo branches in Zambia, Kuwait, Uzbekistan, Nigeria, Bulgaria, Venezuela, Mongolia and Malaysia, and propagandists from Russia Today.
Simultaneous interpretation into three languages was meant to create the impression of an international format. No discussion was planned.
The occupation “governor” and the “head” of Enerhodar explained how Ukrainian forces were supposedly violating the rights of civilians in occupied territory that they themselves control.
The script was predictable. Miroshnik produced casualty figures for the occupied part of Zaporizhzhia region: 508 civilians killed since February 2022. He tied a supposed three- to fourfold rise in strikes to the EU’s €90 billion loan. Chernichuk spoke of a “blockade” of the nuclear plant.
All of it came from the occupation authorities themselves. The territory is closed to independent investigators, journalists and international missions. After Izium was liberated, prosecutors, forensic experts and international journalists worked on the ground, and every body from the mass grave underwent forensic examination.
The link to the European loan has a clear addressee. Moscow is speaking to the Western taxpayer: Your money is killing civilians. The goal is to split support for Ukraine at a time when funding for 2026 and 2027 has already been approved and is being disbursed.
Oleshky has gone months without proper food, water or medical care. Moscow has not explained why. It held a Zoom call about “Ukrainian crimes” in a neighboring region instead. It gave no answer to what was shown in The Hague either, only its own staff and witnesses prepared in advance.
Russian channels and Rossotrudnichestvo websites will now circulate recordings of the call. They will be presented as a “broad international discussion.” No one will check how many people actually joined or who they were. For the domestic audience and for Moscow-friendly countries of the Global South, what matters is the picture: diplomats, interpretation, “witnesses,” numbers.
In The Hague, the audience saw material from criminal proceedings, forensic findings and testimony from people who survived occupation and found the courage to speak. The film was shown in the city that hosts the International Criminal Court, to lawyers, diplomats and journalists free to ask any question. Every episode can be tested in court.
The Russian telebridge was built from statements by the people who run the occupation and from “testimony” prepared for broadcast. It was shown in a closed video call to Russia’s own staff. Nothing in it can be verified, and no one intended it to be.
In liberated Izium, investigators found a mass grave. Oleshky is still occupied, and food is not allowed in. Moscow answered with a video call among its own people. Russia could open these territories to independent investigators and let food into Oleshky today. It chose another Zoom.
The views expressed in this opinion article are the author’s and not necessarily those of Kyiv Post.
Oleksandr Antonyuk is a political consultant and military serviceman. He was born in Lviv and graduated from Lviv Polytechnic National University. He has previously worked at the radio stations Lvivska Khvylia, Radio Man, and Army FM, and has participated in projects for the ICTV and Rada TV channels.
He also worked in the Apparatus of the Verkhovna Rada of Ukraine and is a co-author of its communication strategy.

title: Vincent Kompany 'stable' in hospital after collapsing at Bayern Munich training
body: Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany is in a stable condition in hospital after collapsing while watching the German club's reserve team train on Friday. Kompany had been unwell during the week with reports suggesting he had struggling with a virus and the 40-year-old missed Bayern's pre-match media conference ahead of their Uefa Champions League draw with Arsenal. Kompany was on the touchline at the Allianz Arena on Wednesday despite the pouring rain as the match ended 2-2, with Alphonso Davies and Harry Kane on target as the German and English champions settled for a point each. Bayern's next game is away to Freiburg on Sunday which the former Belgium and Manchester City captain will now miss as he undergoes more tests at hospital. “The good news is he's stable ,” said Bayern's director of sport Max Eberl, who had assistant coach Aaron Danks alongside him in Saturday's press conference ahead of the Freiburg match. “I spoke with him last night, with his wife too. 🗣️ 𝗠𝗮𝘅 𝗘𝗯𝗲𝗿𝗹 𝗼𝗻 𝗩𝗶𝗻𝗰𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗞𝗼𝗺𝗽𝗮𝗻𝘆'𝘀 𝗰𝗼𝗻𝗱𝗶𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 “The good news is he's stable. I spoke with him last night, with his wife too. It wasn't a nice moment for all of us, he collapsed on the pitch yesterday and will spend a few more days in hospital… pic.twitter.com/kbrAC7LhH6 — FC Bayern (@FCBayernEN) October 24, 2026 “It wasn't a nice moment for all of us, he collapsed on the pitch yesterday and will spend a few more days in hospital until everything is checked over. “It shows again how health is the most important thing in life – not football. So, all of us send our best well-wishes. We as FC Bayern stand together. The most important thing is that the cause is established and he gets fit again. He'll only come back when he's fit. “They’ve been investigating the cause all along. He’d already been having minor problems last week. The doctors are doing nothing but trying to find out what it is. “The tests have already yielded some results, but further results are needed to determine exactly what it is and how long it will take for him to recover. I’m not a doctor. But we can support him with energy and love.” Eberl admitted he did not know how long Kompany would be missing for but made clear he get “all the time” he needs. “We’re not going to start setting any time frames,” he said. “We need to find out what the issue is, and then it’s a question of what the recovery time will be. We're not talking in terms of days, but weeks. We’re all clear on that. And we have such a fantastic coaching staff, led by Vinnie. “But our success is down to an outstanding team behind the scenes. There’s absolutely no thought of changing anything. All the guys here are outstanding – and so, in the spirit of Vinnie, which everyone carries within them, we can all tackle the coming weeks.” Everyone at Manchester City is wishing a speedy recovery to our former captain and Club legend, Vincent Kompany. Get well soon, Vinny 🩵 https://t.co/RYUP7DjYkj pic.twitter.com/fozzCkHGQl — Manchester City (@ManCity) October 23, 2026 Erbl also admitted that some of the young players who watched their manager's collapse had been “a bit overwhelmed” by what they witnessed. “For the U23s, it happened while they were training, so they experienced it first-hand,” he added. “For 17- and 18-year-old boys, that's quite something – many of them haven’t had to deal with anything negative before. Some things just happen. The boys were a bit overwhelmed; that’s only human. “Everyone looks out for one another; that’s what defines FC Bayern. We’re there for each other and for everyone else who’s affected by this. That’s Bayern Munich – it’s not just empty words, but it’s what truly sets us apart. The fact that we go through this together and are there for one another really strengthens the family, which is the most important thing.” Bayern are currently top of the Bundesliga on 14 points from six games, albeit only ahead of Borussia Dortmund on goal difference. In the Champions League, they are in 14th spot having won one and drawn two so far, leaving them one point outside automatic qualification spots for the knockout stages. Kopmany took over as manager in 2024 guiding the club to successive Bundesliga titles, one German Cup and two German Super Cups.

title: Petraeus says U.S. can’t be ‘held hostage’ on aluminum as domestic smelting revives
body: “We can’t be held hostage to others having the sole capability to provide critical minerals and strategics, including aluminum,” Petraeus said at an Oct. 16 event hosted by the American Primary Aluminum Association (APAA) at the National Press Club in Washington. “The fact is, we have allowed China to achieve at least oligopolistic control over many of the strategic and rare earth mineral categories and processing in particular and that should make us very, very uncomfortable.” APAA has since released a video of the fireside chat, which also featured Century Aluminum CEO Jesse Gary, Magnitude 7 Metals owner David Kaplan and research economist Adam Hersh. Smelters restart, new plant planned The industry group pointed to Century Aluminum’s Mt. Holly smelter in South Carolina, which has returned to full production, and to the restart of Magnitude 7 Metals’ plant in Missouri. According to APAA, the Missouri restart alone will raise U.S. primary aluminum output by 20% by the end of 2026. APAA also cited Century’s planned smelter in Inola, Oklahoma, which it says would double U.S. production capacity. If built, it would be the first new primary aluminum smelter in the country in nearly 50 years, the association said. APAA argues that more domestic smelting would strengthen the industrial base that defense manufacturers depend on, since aluminum is used across a wide range of military and civilian products. Industry credits tariffs APAA President Mark Duffy said rebuilding primary production would cut U.S. reliance on aluminum from China, Russia and the Middle East. He attributed the recent wave of investment to the 50% Section 232 tariff on aluminum imports and urged the administration to keep it in place with no exceptions or exemptions. Petraeus also credited the administration. “Aluminum is in just about everything and we should have our own supply of this,” he said. “This is one [of] the areas in which I think the current administration has really done quite good work.”

title: About 15,000 aspirants set for executive NDC positions across all constituencies
body: The National Democratic Congress (NDC) is proceeding with its constituency executive elections nationwide despite a court injunction restraining the party from conducting the polls in Nkwanta North in the Oti Region. The party’s Acting Director of IT and Elections, Mahdi Jibrill, says preparations for the Nkwanta North elections are continuing because the party has not been formally served with the court order. Speaking on Accra-based CitiNews on Thursday, October 22, he maintained that the constituency polls would take place as scheduled. “The Nkwanta North election will come on this weekend. From what I have in the data as we speak, we have no injunction on us. Nobody has served us, and party headquarters, the general secretary, is running the election of the constituency. So for us, we know the election will go on,” he said. The High Court in Dambai issued an interlocutory injunction restraining the NDC from conducting the elections in Nkwanta North. The order also barred the party from using or relying on a register of branch executives compiled after elections held in June and July 2026. The nationwide constituency executive elections are scheduled for Saturday, October 24, and Sunday, October 25, as part of the party’s reorganisation programme ahead of the 2028 general elections. About 15,000 aspirants are expected to contest various executive positions across the NDC’s 276 constituencies, according to information from the party’s elections leadership. The positions include constituency chairman, vice-chairman, secretary, treasurer, organiser, deputy organiser, communications officer, women’s organiser and youth organiser, among others. The successful candidates will be responsible for coordinating party activities, mobilising members, managing local structures and implementing the party’s programmes within their respective constituencies. The elections form a key part of the NDC’s preparations for the 2028 general elections, as constituency executives are expected to play an important role in grassroots mobilisation and voter engagement. The exercise is being conducted by the Electoral Commission in collaboration with the party’s election committees in the constituencies, while the Ghana Police Service is responsible for security during the polls.

title: Ukraine’s ex-PM Warns Against ‘Sham’ Trump-Putin Diplomacy
body:
Ukraine must not be sacrificed in a great-power deal between US President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese leader Xi Jinping, warns Ukraine’s former Prime Minister Arseniy Yatsenyuk, accusing Moscow of seeking to carve up Europe.
Speaking to TVP World at the Freedom Games conference in Łódź, Yatsenyuk described the prospect of a summit involving the three leaders without Ukraine as “a sham talk”.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
He warned that such a meeting risked repeating the great-power bargains of the 1938 Munich Agreement and the 1945 Yalta Conference.
“He wants to partition Europe,” Yatsenyuk said of Putin.
Although Moscow has signalled a willingness to resume talks with Ukrainian representatives, Yatsenyuk accused the Kremlin of using diplomacy to buy time. He insisted that neither Ukraine’s future nor Europe’s security could be negotiated without those directly affected.
Yatsenyuk also criticised Trump’s decision to permit Russian diesel imports and waive fresh sanctions under a law named after the late Senator Lindsey Graham.
The move has drawn criticism from lawmakers in both US parties, who argue that it eases pressure on Moscow as its invasion of Ukraine continues.
Calling the deal “unprecedented”, Yatsenyuk rejected Trump’s suggestion that Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries were chiefly responsible for rising US fuel prices. He pointed instead to the war in Iran and questioned whether Russian diesel shipments could significantly lower prices.
Yatsenyuk warned that Ukraine faces an immediate threat as Russia intensifies strikes on energy infrastructure ahead of winter. He estimated that Moscow could launch 70 to 120 ballistic missiles a month and said Kyiv needed at least 120 interceptors monthly to protect its cities.
“And as of now, we have practically zero in our stockpiles,” he said.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has also appealed to European allies for 300 Patriot interceptor missiles ahead of the cold season.
Despite his criticism of Washington’s Russia policy, Yatsenyuk urged Kyiv to preserve bipartisan support in the United States.
American intelligence, Patriot missiles and other equipment purchased with European funds remain crucial to Ukraine’s defence.
“We need Americans in, but not out,” he said.

title: Lebanon's Aoun vows end to neglect of Tripoli in first presidential visit to city in 15 years
body: Lebanon's President Joseph Aoun vowed on Saturday to end decades of neglect in Tripoli during the first presidential visit to the northern city in 15 years, a move aimed at restoring public trust in state institutions and services. Mr Aoun was received with a hero's welcome in Lebanon's second-largest city, which is home to some of the country's wealthiest politicians but remains among its most marginalised and impoverished areas. Speaking at the Tripoli Serail, he said the "time has come to put an end to neglect" in the city and to address the socioeconomic challenges facing its residents. "My visit is to tell the people of Tripoli that the state is present and always stands by your side," Mr Aoun said. "To restore trust, we must provide citizens with services. Human dignity requires the state to deliver services and ensure they are accessible to everyone. This is how we rebuild trust." He said projects were being planned to create jobs for residents. "It is our duty to serve the people," he added. Tripoli Mayor Abdel Hamid Karimeh described Mr Aoun's visit as historic, saying it follows years of state neglect. The last reported visit to the city by a sitting Lebanese president was in November 2011. Mr Aoun's itinerary included stops at the Palace of Justice, Tripoli Port, the special economic zone and the Rachid Karami International Fair, sites considered important to the city's economic development. Speaking at the Palace of Justice, Mr Aoun said tackling corruption was a national priority and stressed the importance of an independent judiciary. Mr Aoun was accompanied by Interior Minister Ahmad Hajjar and Justice Minister Adel Nassar, along with senior security officials. Mr Hajjar said the presidential visit demonstrated the state's commitment to Tripoli and he expressed hope that it would help strengthen security and economic activity in the city. He also warned that deteriorating economic conditions could undermine stability. Meanwhile, Mr Nassar said the visit was significant and showed the government's commitment to developing Tripoli. "The city has an essential role and we will do everything necessary to develop it," he said.

title: Russia launches 126 UAVs at Ukraine; 101 neutralized
body:
Overnight into Saturday, Russian occupation forces launched 126 drones of various types at Ukraine, including 61 jet-powered UAVs, as well as Banderol loitering munitions and decoy drones. Ukraine’s air defense forces shot down or neutralized 101 of these, including 50 jet-powered drones, the Air Force of the Armed Forces of Ukraine reported.

"Hits by enemy aerial weapons were recorded at 14 locations, while debris from intercepted drones fell at five other locations," the Air Force stated on its Telegram channel.

The aerial attack was countered by Ukrainian aviation, anti-aircraft missile units, electronic warfare and unmanned systems units, and mobile fire groups of the Ukrainian Defense Forces.

As of the time of the announcement, the attack was still ongoing, with Russian strike drones remaining in Ukrainian airspace.

Consequently, the effectiveness of Ukraine’s air defense overnight exceeded 80%; specifically, the interception rate for jet-powered drones reached 82%.

title: Security has ramped up in Jordan after deadly terror attack on church killed seven, US embassy says
body: The US embassy in Amman said security had been stepped up at malls, foreign embassies and other locations across Jordan after Friday's attack on a church in Jordan that authorities described as a terrorist act by extremists.Seven people were killed and dozens were injured when gunmen opened fire ​during a funeral at a Greek Orthodox church in Karak governorate, the head of Jordan's Public Security Directorate said.There was no immediate claim of responsibility.Such attacks are extremely rare in Jordan, though authorities in the US ally say that in recent years they have repeatedly foiled attempted attacks by Islamist militants.Jordanian officials have not yet confirmed links to Islamist groupsAuthorities said they are still searching for the attackers, adding it was too early to determine whether they had links to known groups inside or outside Jordan."This is a result of a terrorist ideology and blind extremism and we will not allow society to go down this path," Prime Minister Jafar Hassan said in a post on X/Twitter hours after the violence.Jordan's King Abdullah, a major US partner in the fight against militant Islamist groups, visited Karak hours after the attack and said the perpetrators would be punished "with an iron fist."Christians make up a minority of Jordan's population. The country is home to several biblical sites that attract Christian pilgrims from around the world.Jordan has been among US allies in the region to be hit by Iranian attacks this year after the US and Israel launched strikes against Iran in February.

title: Kobakhidze Attends Events Marking Anti-Soviet Uprising Anniversary in Budapest
body: Georgian Dream Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze was in Budapest on October 23 to attend events marking the 70th anniversary of the Hungarian anti-Soviet uprising, in his first visit to the Hungarian capital since Georgian Dream’s close ally Viktor Orbán lost power to Péter Magyar’s party in the April elections. Georgian government’s official press releases showed Kobakhidze alongside Magyar and other European leaders and officials, attending a series of events commemorating the revolutionary events of 1956 that, after initial success, ended with the Soviet Red Army brutally suppressing the uprising. Guests included European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen, European Council President Antonio Costa, Moldovan President Maia Sandu, Ukrainian Parliamentary Speaker Ruslan Stefanchuk, former NATO Secretary-General Jens Stoltenberg, and officials and delegations from different countries. However, the media reported that many leaders of European countries were also absent despite invitations. The commemorative events attended by Kobakhidze included a gala concert and an official reception hosted by Magyar, according to the Georgian government’s press release. Hungary under Viktor Orbán has in recent years been the closest European partner of the Georgian Dream government amid Tbilisi’s isolation from the country’s traditional Western partners. Budapest has remained among the few European destinations for Georgian Dream officials’ trips, including to take part in the Conservative Political Action Conference (CPAC) of far-right leaders. Orbán’s Hungary was also repeatedly reported to have used its veto power to block more resolute measures by Brussels, including sanctions, in response to Tbilisi’s anti-democratic actions. Following the change of government after the landslide victory by the Tisza Party, Magyar pledged to continue what he called “good relations” with Georgia. title: Seven people, incl children, injured in shelling of Kharkiv region over past 24 hours
body:
Over the past 24 hours, Russian occupation forces launched strikes on the city of Kharkiv and 15 other settlements in the region, leaving seven people injured, including two children, reported Oleh Synehubov, head of Kharkiv Regional Military Administration.

"In the city of Kharkiv, a 12-year-old girl sustained injuries, while two women, aged 46 and 37, and a 13-year-old boy experienced acute stress reactions. In the village of Cherkaski Tyshky (Tsyrkuny community), men aged 57 and 52 were injured. In the urban-type settlement of Blyzniuky, a 39-year-old woman experienced an acute stress reaction," Synehubov wrote on his Telegram channel.

title: Plateau Govt Moves To Close AI Gap, Trains Executives For Digital Governance
body: The Plateau State Government has called on public sector executives to embrace Artificial Intelligence (AI) to improve productivity, strengthen accountability and enhance service delivery, as it steps up efforts to align governance with global digital trends. The call was made at a training programme themed “Closing the AI Gap for Executive Excellence: Strengthening Leadership, Productivity and Accountability,” organised by the state government to equip officials with the knowledge and skills to apply AI responsibly in public administration. The training brought together the Secretary to the State Government, Arch. Samuel Jatau; Commissioner for Information, Joyce Ramnap; Permanent Secretary, Policy and General Services, Gayi Timothy; and other government officials. Speaking at the programme, Jatau, who represented Governor Caleb Mutfwang, said understanding Artificial Intelligence had become essential for a government seeking to digitise its operations and align its policies with global best practices. He described AI as a double-edged sword that could improve efficiency when properly used but also pose risks if applied irresponsibly. “AI is a double-edged sword which has the good side and the bad side, and that is the reason why we are here today, so that we can know which edge of the sword we should use,” he said. The Secretary to the State Government urged public officials to understand how to use AI tools, identify AI-generated documents and exercise caution when sharing official information with such platforms. He noted that AI could reduce workloads and improve the quality of official output, but stressed the need for government employees to understand its limitations and potential risks. Also speaking, the Permanent Secretary, Policy and General Services, Gayi Timothy, said the training was designed to bridge the gap between the opportunities offered by AI and the capacity of government institutions to deploy the technology effectively. According to him, AI could help public servants streamline administrative processes, analyse data, prepare reports, improve planning and monitor institutional performance. He, however, emphasised that the technology must be deployed with human oversight, data protection and adherence to ethical and professional standards. “The success of this programme will ultimately be measured not merely by what we learn, but by how effectively we apply that knowledge to improve institutional performance and the quality of services delivered to our citizens,” Timothy said. The Commissioner for Information, Joyce Ramnap, said adopting AI was particularly important for government communication, noting that the technology could strengthen the gathering and dissemination of information across Plateau State. “We must key into this if we must work as employees of government and chief executive officers. I’m hoping that this training will be able to equip us better on how to gather data and also disseminate information,” she said. Ramnap urged participants to take advantage of the training to improve how government information is collected, processed, and communicated to the public. The programme is expected to encourage responsible adoption of emerging technologies across government institutions, with the broader goal of building a more efficient, accountable and citizen-focused public service in Plateau State. The post Plateau Govt Moves To Close AI Gap, Trains Executives For Digital Governance appeared first on Channels Television .

title: UG commissions Alex A. Dadey Centre in honour of Dr Alexander Apau Dadey Snr, Father of KGL Boss
body: The University of Ghana (UG) has commissioned the Alex A. Dadey Centre at its Legon campus in honour of Dr Alexander Apau Dadey Snr., a veteran educationist and administrator whose career spanned teaching, institutional leadership and public service. The facility was commissioned on Friday, October 23, 2026, in a partnership between the University and the University of Ghana Alumni Association (UGAA). To ensure its long-term sustainability, the KGL Foundation has committed to funding the centre for the next 20 years. Speaking at the ceremony, the Vice-Chancellor of the University of Ghana, Professor Nana Aba Appiah Amfo, said Dr Dadey Snr. was a former student of the University who later served on its governing council from 1978 to 1985. She described his service on the Council as a significant part of his contribution to the institution, noting that he had also benefited from the mentorship of distinguished academic Professor Alexander Kwapong during his time as a student. Dr Dadey Snr. also held leadership positions in Ghana’s education sector, serving as National Chairman of the Ghana National Association of Teachers (GNAT) for five years and President of the Conference of Heads of Assisted Secondary Schools (CHASS) for six years. He served as headmaster of Achimota Senior High School and Okuapeman Senior High School. At the ceremony, his son, Alex Apau Dadey, Founder and Executive Chairman of the KGL Group of Companies, described his father as a man of discipline, integrity, humility, intellectual curiosity and commitment to public service. He said his father regarded education not merely as a route to personal success but as a tool for transforming individuals, society and national development. Mr Dadey said his upbringing taught him that success should be measured not only by the wealth accumulated but also by the lives transformed and the institutions strengthened. He also recalled his father’s emphasis on the enduring value of reputation and character, saying the greatest legacy is what remains after a person is gone. Reflecting on the family’s approach to wealth creation and philanthropy, Mr Dadey said giving back to society was a moral responsibility. “As a family, we believe in a moral responsibility to give back to society and the institutions that nurtured us, shaped our character, and provided the foundations for our success,” he said. He said the establishment of the KGL Foundation was rooted in that conviction and in principles passed down by his father. “Wealth creation and wealth distribution are two sides of the same coin,” he said, describing the philosophy the family believes should guide African entrepreneurs and business leaders. He added that successful businesses should create value for shareholders and employees while contributing to the long-term prosperity of the communities in which they operate. The commissioning forms part of the Dadey family’s broader philanthropic activities through the KGL Foundation, which supports education, healthcare, sports and other social development initiatives. The Foundation is scheduled to commission several projects between October and November 2026, including a 250-capacity technology centre at Aburi Girls’ Senior High School and a sports complex for Mfantsipim Senior High School in Cape Coast. It is also partnering with the Ghana Medical Trust Fund to construct a diagnostic centre at the Greater Accra Regional Hospital, popularly known as Ridge Hospital. In Kumasi, the Foundation has partnered with the Eve Medical Foundation to establish the KGL Eve Medical Centre at the KNUST Medical Village. The centre provides women’s wellness, mental health and general medical services. Beyond infrastructure, the KGL Foundation has supported Ghana’s national football teams, juvenile football and the Ghana Football Association, while providing scholarships to thousands of students through its initiatives. The Foundation’s 20-year funding commitment to the Alex A. Dadey Centre is intended to support the facility’s continued operation and maintenance, extending the family’s investment in education and the University of Ghana.

title: U A E s EDGE Reaches Full-Rate Production on Automated 40mm Ammunition Line
body:
EDGE has reached full-rate production on an automated 40×53mm grenade ammunition line operated by LAHAB, its medium- to large-calibre ammunition manufacturer.
Operational since late 2025, the line can produce up to 1.5 million rounds annually, automating component assembly from start to finish without manual intervention.
The system comprises three modules covering cartridge case assembly and filling, projectile filling and assembly, and final assembly and belting. Built to Industry 4.0 standards, it records production data across all three modules and provides real-time dashboard monitoring of throughput, performance and production status, enabling deviations to be identified and corrected during operations.
LAHAB CEO Mohammed Arbabi said automation had reduced manual labor requirements by nearly 60%, while improving efficiency and supporting increased output.
The project forms part of EDGE’s broader smart manufacturing program. The group reported completing more than 68 Industry 4.0 transformation projects across 28 production facilities in 2025, doubling production capacity at 13 entities.
At HALCON, EDGE’s guided-weapons manufacturer, an automated DESERT STING 16 assembly line using 11 industrial robots, more than 300 sensors, six machine-vision stations and automated material handling and inspection increased production volume by 130% and reduced labor content by 23%, according to EDGE.
At CARACAL, its firearms and small-caliber ammunition producer, an automated storage and retrieval system increased storage density by approximately 80% and made storage and retrieval three times faster, eliminating the need for an additional warehouse investment, the company said.

title: Iran needs no permission of any power to defend itself: spox
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 24 (MNA) – In response to the US threatening of renewing war against Iran, Government Spokeswoman Fatemeh Mohajerani emphasized that Iran does not seek permission from any power to defend itself.
In a note published “Iran will not be destroyed by threats.”, the spokeswoman underlined that Iran will not wait for permission of any power to defend itself.
The text of the note is read as follows,
These days, Iran’s enemies speak of a nation’s fate while asserting their capacity to destroy it as if a country could be wiped off the world map, and a civilization erased from the memory of history, with a single command.
American authorities and Israeli officials must understand that Iran’s destiny is not written according to their wishes or will. This nation will not surrender its independence or its right to determine its own future to those who issue threats. Repeating threats does not alter this reality—just as speaking more loudly does not transform a claim into reality.
“We know the suffering caused by war. We understand that behind every act of destruction, lives are disrupted, and behind every lost life, a family is left grieving forever. For this reason, we speak of peace with a sense of responsibility and strive to prevent war. Yet, no one should mistake this sense of responsibility for hesitation in defending Iran. Safeguarding the lives of our people, the territorial integrity, and the independence of the country is a duty in which we shall never falter.”
Iran does not wait for any power’s permission to defend itself. The country’s powerful Armed Forces are tasked with safeguarding this land, and aggressors must realize that a decision to commit an act of aggression will not be without cost or consequence. Any assessment regarding Iran that fails to take into account the nation’s defensive capabilities and the will of its people is fundamentally flawed.

title: Rubio identifies Donbas as key issue in war, emphasizes the need for mutual concessions
body:
The Russia-Ukraine war is essentially centered on 11% of the territory in Donbas—an area Russia has unsuccessfully attempted to seize by military force, and which Ukraine refuses to cede for reasons of sovereignty and long-term security. Consequently, a resolution to the conflict is possible only through diplomatic means, involving mutual compromises at the negotiating table, stated U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio.
"...people keep talking about it’s a war in Ukraine. That war is about Donbas. It’s about one region of the country … It’s – at it’s core, it’s about 11 percent of one part of that country that Russia wants and cannot take militarily and that Ukraine is unwilling to give up. And they have good reasons why they don’t want to do that – for sovereignty and their own security long term," Rubio said.
According to the head of American diplomacy, the conflict has no military solution and will only be resolved through diplomatic means. The Secretary of State noted that the core challenge lies in finding a compromise—one where both sides gain certain benefits while also making concessions to bring an end to the hostilities.
Rubio pointed out that the U.S. President is dedicating a significant amount of time to resolving this complex conflict, and the American team is working daily to bridge the differences between the parties. The Secretary of State added that achieving peace requires both sides to be at the negotiating table, and the United States stands ready to act as a mediator to facilitate such a meeting—a necessary prerequisite for resolving the issue.

title: Ukraine says Starlink and Starshield operating at 400 kilometers per hour after week of throttling
body: KYIV, Ukraine – The Starlink satellite communications system and its military version Starshield are operating again at speeds over 400 km per hour, Kyiv’s defense minister said on Saturday, October 24, after over a week of service restrictions that slowed connections and disrupted military operations. “The Ministry of Defense’s monitoring systems are recording a return to normal speed for Starlink/Starshield. We are recording a speed of over 400 km/h. The connection is stable,” Evhenii Khmara told reporters. The Ukrainian military does not disclose the systems’ maximum operating speeds, and the defense ministry did not say whether service had been fully restored. “Monitoring systems had previously recorded disruptions to the Starlink/Starshield service. The speed metrics have now returned to normal,” the ministry said. The restrictions, first reported on October 14, undermined Ukraine’s ability to intercept Russian attack drones and disrupted frontline communications, Ukrainian officials said. Sources said connection speeds had been reduced to about 160 kph or less. Ukraine’s problems with SpaceX-owned Starlink came after US President Donald Trump announced a deal to buy Russian diesel and waived new sanctions on Moscow while pressing Ukraine to stop striking Russian oil refineries. Neither SpaceX boss Elon Musk nor the US government has acknowledged responsibility for restricting Starlink or Starshield in Ukraine. Both have said publicly that any such decision could only have been taken by the other. Reuters has reported that the order to throttle Starshield came from inside the White House . Trump said on Friday that if problems with access to Starlink communications systems in Ukraine persisted, he would “get it straightened out,” – Rappler.com

title: Defense Forces strike Tolyattikauchuk and Proton-Elektrotex plants, and aircraft at Yeysk airfield in Russia
body:
This was reported by the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine on Facebook , according to Ukrinform.
“Strikes on the main production building of Proton-Elektrotex JSC in the city of Orel, Orel Oblast, Russian Federation, have been confirmed. This complicates the production of components for cruise and ballistic missiles, which the enemy is using to strike Ukrainian cities,” the statement reads.
As noted by the General Staff, JSC “Proton-Elektrotex” is a leading Russian manufacturer of optoelectronic equipment and devices with a full production cycle—from crystals to finished products—including - modules for the S-71 “Kover” air-launched cruise missiles and switch-inverters for the 9M723 “Iskander-M” ballistic missiles. As part of this cooperation, the company is also involved in the production of the “Pantsir-S1” air defense system and its variants.
The “Tolyattikauchuk” plant in the city of Tolyatti, Samara Oblast, Russian Federation, was also struck. An explosion and fire were reported in the vicinity of the plant.
The General Staff added that the plant produces synthetic rubbers, monomers, fractions, and high-octane gasoline additives. Synthetic rubbers, in particular, are used to produce solid rocket propellant for tactical and ballistic missiles.
In addition, an aircraft at the Yeysk airfield in the Krasnodar Krai of the Russian Federation was struck. The extent of the damage is being assessed.
“The Ukrainian Defense Forces are striking targets on enemy territory within the framework of the right to self-defense guaranteed by Article 51 of the UN Charter,” the General Staff concluded.
As reported by Ukrinform, in the Samara Region of the Russian Federation on the night of Saturday, October 24, a drone attack caused a fire at the “Tolyattikauchuk” plant, which produces, among other things, synthetic rubbers used in the manufacture of solid rocket fuel.

title: Obuasi SHTS scandal: Manasseh concerned about political interference, attempts to suppress allegations
body: Investigative journalist Manasseh Azure Awuni has alleged that some political figures in the Ashanti Region interfered in sexual abuse allegations involving the headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School, with attempts allegedly made to settle complaints privately and pressure victims’ families into withdrawing police cases. Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, October 24, Manasseh expressed concern over what he described as the failure of school authorities, education officials and political leaders to ensure that serious allegations of sexual abuse were promptly reported to the police. According to him, the involvement of influential political figures in handling complaints raised questions about efforts to suppress the allegations. He recounted an incident in which the Municipal Chief Executive (MCE) for Obuasi East, Mr. William Kofi Adzowu, popularly known as Biggie, allegedly contacted a housemistress, Stephanie Adwoa Yeboah, after 10 p.m. and instructed her to bring out a female student who had reportedly complained of sexual abuse. Manasseh claimed the MCE subsequently arrived with individuals presented as the girl’s relatives and arranged for her to leave the school for a meeting intended to resolve the matter privately. He questioned why school authorities allowed the student to be taken away at that hour instead of ensuring that the allegations were reported to the police. The investigative journalist disclosed that he personally contacted the MCE, who reportedly acknowledged that the allegations involved a criminal matter but explained that there was insufficient evidence at the time. “And that, for me, is a weak response because your duty is not to gather evidence. The police are trained and have the power to do the investigation. So yours is to just report, but they didn’t report,” he stated. Manasseh further alleged that the MCE justified his intervention on political grounds, reportedly telling him, “As you may be aware, the headmaster is a party person.” He claimed the MCE subsequently involved a local party chairman and another political figure identified as King Zuba, whom he described as the Mampong mayor. According to Manasseh, some of the individuals later met the housemistress at Kofkans Hotel in Kumasi, where discussions were held and money allegedly changed hands. Turning to a separate allegation of rape involving another student, the journalist criticised the school and local Ghana Education Service (GES) officials for allegedly failing to notify the police despite receiving information about the incident. He said even after an intelligence official reportedly collected evidence, including GH¢100 and the student’s underwear, which allegedly contained semen, the school authorities failed to report the matter. Manasseh recounted how the girl’s father encountered difficulties obtaining permission to withdraw his daughter from school, eventually claiming she required traditional treatment for a spiritual illness. According to him, the father took the girl directly to the police station after securing permission for her to leave. He contrasted the difficulties faced by the father with the ease with which a politician allegedly arranged for another student to leave the school late at night. The journalist also alleged that reports of sexual abuse had reached some local authorities as far back as 2025, but appropriate action was not taken. He further disclosed that the father of one alleged victim told JoyNews that a delegation, purportedly acting on behalf of the headmaster, visited his village to apologise and persuade him to withdraw the police complaint. According to the account, the delegation allegedly promised that the headmaster would finance the girl’s university education and help her secure employment afterwards. Manasseh said the delegation subsequently repeated its appeal before the local Odikro, who also confirmed the visit to JoyNews. However, he indicated that the father remained determined to pursue the matter through the police despite the alleged pressure. “So apart from the political interference and the big men coming in, sometimes pressure is also brought to bear on some of the victims and their families,” he said.

title: Fancy harnesses make coding agents more expensive but not better, study finds
body:
Makers tout score gains from new agent harnesses like Claude Code or OpenCode. A study finds that claim doesn't hold up. Swapping harnesses barely moves results more than running the same setup twice, but costs can triple.

A coding agent pairs a language model with a harness, the system prompt, tools, and context management that make the model work inside a code repository. New harnesses ship every day, and leaderboards mix them freely, but two researchers at Shandong University measured how much the harness actually matters when you hold the model constant. The paper's title gives away the answer: "What does a harness buy? Mostly tokens."
Earlier comparisons were measuring noise
Previous studies report gaps of more than 20 points between harnesses, but those numbers almost always come from a single run, according to the authors. Pure reruns of the same setup already vary by up to six points on SWE-bench Verified. Zhipu AI, for example, advertises its own harness with a 2.4-point lead over Claude Code, a margin that falls well within that noise range. Harnesses are also often wired into the benchmark differently, making comparisons even less reliable.

Liu and Han ran five models through three harnesses in their shipped versions: Claude Code, OpenCode, and mini-SWE-agent. mini-SWE-agent gives the model only a Bash tool and skips context management. Claude Code and OpenCode offer specialized file and search tools, long system prompts, and automatic history compression.

The models were Qwen3.6, Qwen3.8, Deepseek-V4-Flash, GLM-5.3-Flash, and HY4-Preview. Claude Opus 5 ran as a reference only in Claude Code. Tests used the 45 hardest tasks from SWE-bench Verified plus a pool of 447 more. Several setups ran twice to measure noise.

All runs happened offline. In early tests with web access, 71 percent of Deepseek and Qwen model attempts pulled the correct fix straight from GitHub instead of solving the task themselves. Claude models almost never did this. The researchers discarded those results and don't claim any maker trained on the test data, but the pattern was strong enough that they cut off web access for all remaining runs.
Swapping harnesses moves results about as much as a rerun
On the larger pool of 447 tasks, Claude Code and mini-SWE-agent, the heaviest and lightest harnesses, sit less than two points apart for both tested models. Within a five-point band, they're statistically equivalent.

[caption id="attachment_63061" align="aligncenter" width="1800"] The three harnesses consume two to three times as many tokens as the leanest option per model, but pass rates stay within measurement uncertainty. Only OpenCode's deficit on the large task pool is statistically significant. | Image: Liu & Han[/caption]

The researchers expected the biggest harness effect on the 45 hardest tasks. Instead, harnesses differ by two to five solved tasks per model, and a simple rerun of the same setup shifts the count by up to three. Sometimes mini-SWE-agent leads, sometimes Claude Code does.

The flip rates tell the same story. Between two reruns, the median outcome changes on 13 percent of tasks. Between two different harnesses, it's also 13 percent. Swapping models pushes that to 22 percent. Which tasks a given harness wins changes from run to run, matching a coin flip. The harness gap behaves like a "fresh draw of the same noise," the authors write.

[caption id="attachment_63059" align="aligncenter" width="1800"] Swapping harnesses flips task-level results about as often as a simple rerun, while swapping models causes much larger shifts. | Image: Liu & Han[/caption]

These small samples also limit what any comparison can detect. With 45 tasks, even a 13-point gap shows up only half the time. With 447 tasks, gaps of about five points become reliably detectable. Zhipu's claimed 2.4-point advantage falls below both thresholds, and so do many other advertised improvements.
All harnesses perform the same, except OpenCode falls behind
The only measurable harness effect is a steady deficit for OpenCode. On the large task pool, it trails the other two by up to nine points. About half of that gap traces back to an output limit. When a model exceeds this limit mid-step during reasoning, Claude Code prompts it to keep going. OpenCode lets the step end there, and the attempt usually fails.

Adding a Claude Code-style continuation prompt to OpenCode didn't help, because the same task rarely triggers the same overflow on a retry. For the rest of the gap, the authors have no explanation, only an observation: under OpenCode, models stop working much sooner. On locally run models, OpenCode also had a much tighter time limit than Claude Code, which the authors flag as an uncontrolled variable.

mini-SWE-agent runs into the context window because it lacks context management, mostly on tasks where the other harnesses also fail. OpenCode's search tools try to download a binary file on first use and break when offline.

[caption id="attachment_63060" align="aligncenter" width="1800"] With Qwen3.8, some OpenCode runs hit the output limit, while mini-SWE-agent without context management more often runs into the context window. | Image: Liu & Han[/caption]
System prompt and tool descriptions set the bill
With the same model, same tasks, and same price list, a single task can cost up to three times more depending on the harness. Tool outputs barely explain the gap. All three harnesses return similar amounts of text per call.

The real difference comes from the system prompt and tool descriptions. They get resent with every step and run about 16,600 tokens for Claude Code, roughly 7,000 for OpenCode, and under 1,000 for mini-SWE-agent. Claude Code also keeps the model's reasoning output in the conversation history, based on the researchers' reverse engineering.

[caption id="attachment_63058" align="aligncenter" width="1800"] Claude Code starts much higher because of its roughly 16,600-token system prompt with tool definitions. After that, context grows at similar rates across all three harnesses. | Image: Liu & Han[/caption]

After that first call, context grows at similar rates across all harnesses. The system prompt size sets the baseline cost, and the number of steps multiplies it. Which factor dominates depends on the model: With GLM-5.3-Flash, Claude Code costs nearly twice as much as mini-SWE-agent. With Deepseek-V4-Flash, mini-SWE-agent needs so many extra steps that the two end up even. Lower prices for cached tokens dampen the gaps but don't change the ranking.

[caption id="attachment_63057" align="aligncenter" width="1800"] With GLM-5.3-Flash, a single trial in Claude Code costs 1.81 yuan versus 0.56 yuan in OpenCode. With DeepSeek-V4-Flash, Claude Code and mini-SWE-agent end up at roughly the same price. | Image: Liu & Han[/caption]
No home-field advantage, open questions around thinking
Deepseek's own harness scores no better with its own model than the other harnesses do, but costs the most. Claude Opus 5 delivered identical results even after the researchers removed tools from Claude Code. A year-old version solves a similar number of tasks at less than half the cost, because Extended Thinking wasn't on by default back then.

Thinking was the only case where the harness choice actually changed the outcome. Without thinking, mini-SWE-agent with Qwen3.6 drops eleven points, while Claude Code and OpenCode stay within noise. HY4-Preview also loses eleven points in Claude Code without thinking. How much an agent depends on reasoning seems tied to the specific model-harness combination. The authors admit their test grid is too small to explain why.

The study relies mainly on one benchmark. A small cross-check on Terminal-Bench 2.1 shows the same pattern. The closed-source top model, Opus 5, ran only in Claude Code. A harness buys " fewer ways to lose a task, and a bill, not pass rate," the authors conclude. They recommend publishing a rerun of the same setup alongside every harness comparison. That's the only way to tell how much of a measured difference is just noise. Data and analysis scripts are available on GitHub.

More effort in the harness rarely pays off in other studies, either. In one, a simple Markdown file beat a complex skill system for AI coding agents. An earlier study already showed that the choice of framework can nearly triple costs for the same model. Harness design gets a lot of attention as a result. Nvidia recently cut nearly half its token costs for coding agents through better agent steering.

title: Spain Develops F110 Frigate Variant with Enhanced Air Missile Defense
body:
The Spanish Navy and shipbuilder Navantia are defining an enhanced version of the F110 frigate , designated F110 IAMD (Integrated Air and Missile Defense), to strengthen Spain’s ability to counter aircraft, cruise missiles, ballistic missiles and emerging threats.
The initiative builds on the F110 program, with five frigates currently under construction, and aligns with future capability requirements outlined in the Spanish Navy’s Armada 2050 document. The proposed ships would complement the existing five-ship program, with final specifications subject to operational requirements and the procurement process involving the Navy, the Ministry of Defense and Navantia.
The F110 IAMD is intended to detect, classify, track and engage multiple threats simultaneously at greater ranges. Planned missions include area air defence, escorting high-value assets and coordinating air defence within naval task groups.
Expanded firepower: Increased vertical launch capacity designed to accommodate different missile types and mission-specific weapons loads.
Advanced combat management: Integration of the cloud-hosted SCOMBA New Generation (NG) system to connect sensors, weapons, onboard systems, autonomous platforms and data links, creating a shared tactical picture.
NATO and EU interoperability: Information exchange and integration into joint, multi-domain naval networks.
Future-ready architecture: An open, scalable and cyber-secure design intended to incorporate new sensors and weapons against next-generation missiles and uncrewed systems.
Multi-mission operations: Retention of anti-submarine, anti-surface, electronic warfare and asymmetric-threat response capabilities, alongside space for mission modules, a second helicopter and uncrewed vehicles.
Greater endurance and availability: Increased speed and endurance, supported by digital-twin technology, condition-based maintenance and integrated platform management to anticipate faults, improve lifecycle support and assist crew training.

title: Trump Signals Possible Follow-On Military Operation Against Iran
body:
US President Donald Trump said that Washington could execute another military strike against the Islamic Republic of Iran , referencing prior combat actions amid ongoing regional hostilities, Reuters reported.
Speaking at a campaign rally in Florida on Friday, Oct. 23, Trump addressed the armed conflict involving American forces and Tehran, suggesting that further kinetic operations remain an active policy option.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
“We may do another little Epic Fury,” Trump told supporters, referencing the operational code name associated with US military actions against Iranian assets.
The remarks were delivered during a broader address focused on international security and commercial trade policy ahead of the Nov. 3 US midterm elections.
Trump’s statements arrive amid persistent transatlantic debate regarding the economic fallout of the conflict in the Middle East, particularly surrounding shipping lanes in the Persian Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz.
In an interview published on Thursday, Oct. 22, on “The Diary of a CEO” podcast, President Volodymyr Zelensky addressed the Trump administration’s foreign policy approach , arguing that energy market volatility stems directly from escalating military engagements in the Middle East rather than Ukrainian defense operations.
Zelensky rejected claims by the US administration asserting that Ukrainian long-range drone interdictions against Russian oil refineries were responsible for driving up domestic US retail diesel benchmarks.
“I think it’s wrong and unacceptable that he pins Russia’s aggression and Russia’s killings on me,” Zelensky said, pointing to disruptions across maritime bottlenecks in the Middle East as the primary source of international fuel benchmark pressures.
Zelensky observed that Kyiv had repeatedly proposed a verified, reciprocal suspension of attacks against energy infrastructure, but noted that Russian President Vladimir Putin had refused to formalize a ceasefire.
Zelensky argued that criticism directed at Ukraine diverted attention from the structural drivers of inflation tied to Middle Eastern instability.
The prospect of expanded US operations against Iran coincides with assessments regarding technical and military cooperation between Moscow and Tehran.
Speaking at a joint press conference in Oslo on Tuesday, Oct. 20, alongside Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre and Finnish President Alexander Stubb, Zelensky stated that Ukrainian defense agencies have identified evidence of Russian drone transfers and intelligence assistance provided to Iran .
“I think that Putin helps Iranians and helped, because we saw different details from the drones which Russia delivered to Iran,” Zelensky stated.
“I think also they shared with them intelligence, I mean from satellites and other information. This is what we know.”
Responding to questions regarding whether the Kremlin is leveraging its ties with Tehran to influence Washington’s foreign policy calculations, Zelensky emphasized that Moscow has aligned itself with Iranian strategic interests.
“I don’t know too much, yes, but I know that Russia stays on the side of Iranians,” Zelensky added.
Ukrainian security authorities previously indicated that Russian electronic warfare units and space-based reconnaissance assets have provided signals intelligence to Iranian command centers , reflecting an expanding axis of bilateral defense cooperation while the US evaluates operational countermeasures across the region.
