title: Turkey rules out combat with Houthis under defence pact as foreign ministers meet in Istanbul
body: Turkey does not expect its troops to engage in combat with the Houthis under a defence pact with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan, Defence Minister Yasar Guler said on Friday, as the countries' foreign ministers met in Istanbul to discuss regional developments. "The main purpose of our possible military support to Saudi Arabia will be to strengthen deterrence . We absolutely do not foresee entering into any conflict with the Houthis," he said. "Our priority is to prevent new tensions from emerging in the region and to contribute to security and stability." Mr Guler said Turkey would assess requests for military support to Saudi Arabia and determine the scope of its assistance once parliament ratified the pact. The Makkah defence agreement, signed in August and submitted to Turkey's parliament for ratification this week, is based on the principle that an attack on one member is considered an attack on all. But Article 2 specifies that countries must assist one another in the event of an attack or military aggression by "another country or a group of countries" , raising questions about whether it would apply to strikes by Yemen's Houthis, who have escalated attacks on Saudi Arabia in recent weeks. Saudi Arabia and Pakistan have ratified the agreement. The two countries' foreign ministers met in Istanbul on Friday on the sidelines of the Regional Four (R4) ministerial meeting, which involved Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Egypt, where they discussed bilateral relations and regional developments, among them the situation in Yemen. Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan and Pakistan's Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar condemned recent Houthi attacks on civilian areas in Saudi Arabia, according to a statement by the kingdom's Foreign Ministry. The bilateral talks took place as Istanbul hosted a wider diplomatic gathering , the first of its kind, which also brought together foreign ministers from the UK, France, Germany and Italy. Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan hosted the meeting to discuss "regional issues of mutual concern", his office said. In a joint statement issued after the meeting, the ministers said they "condemned in the strongest terms the unacceptable escalation by the Houthi militia", including continued strikes on Saudi Arabia targeting civilians and civilian infrastructure, as well as attacks on commercial shipping in the Red Sea and the Bab Al Mandeb strait. They expressed solidarity with the governments of Yemen and Saudi Arabia and called on the Houthis to "immediately cease all military actions, threats and attacks, and to return to the political process in good faith". Saudi Arabia has come under intensified Houthi attacks in recent weeks, including deadly strikes on airports that have disrupted air travel and prompted the cancellation or postponement of major international conferences, diplomatic summits and sporting events in the kingdom. The Houthis have also claimed attacks on Saudi energy and military targets.

title: Node2Shell evolves to HTTP2Shell, blast radius affects many HTTP libs and apps
body:
Unified cloud security with real-time visibility.
in-app runtime defense and threat detection.
Brotli is a lossless compression algorithm and data format developed by Google. It’s a way to make data smaller for storage or sending over the internet. Software then unpacks it to recover the original data. It’s widely used for HTTP compression to compress web content such as HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.
CVE-2026-111497 is an out-of-bounds write in the Google Brotli decoder affecting versions 1.0.3 through 1.2.0 on all platforms. This is the same Brotli decoder flaw behind Node2Shell announced a couple days ago. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can send a crafted Brotli-compressed stream to corrupt memory, leak sensitive data, crash the process, or potentially execute arbitrary code. It carries a CVSS v4.0 score of 9.2 (Critical), and Node.js is affected through its bundled Brotli library.
A bug makes the Brotli decoder keep accepting more bytes when it should reject the data. Those bytes can overflow a small working buffer and damage the program’s memory. An attacker can use that damage to control what runs, such as their own code.
OpenAI's Codex Security team reported this as unauthenticated remote code execution that works in both directions, so a malicious client can take over an unpatched server and a malicious server can take over an unpatched client that accepts compressed responses. The root cause had already been fixed in Brotli's source code on February 27 , but nobody recognized it as a security issue at the time, and no Brotli release included the fix until October 21 .
That means every project that bundles Brotli has to ship its own update.
‍ You can see what we’ve tracked here in Aikido Intel.
As for unaffected software, Apache’s standard mod_brotli does not decode Brotli.
For CVE-2026-111497, update the affected runtime or Brotli library:
Update the affected runtime or Brotli library. For platforms with no vendor fix yet, use an Aikido patched container image (see below), or disable Brotli decoding until a fix is available. Update dependency locks, rebuild affected applications and container images, redeploy, and restart services. Verify that running workloads use the patched components.
Update dependency locks, rebuild affected applications and container images, redeploy, and restart services. Verify that running workloads use the patched components.
These workarounds reduce exposure while you prepare the upgrade:
Changing Accept-Encoding alone is insufficient: a malicious server can send a Brotli response regardless of what the client advertises, and urllib3 selects its decoder from the response’s Content-Encoding header.
Keep these controls in place until affected components are patched and verified. Review coverage as vendors confirm additional affected components or attack paths.
If you can't upgrade every affected component right away, turning off Brotli decoding cuts off the path to the vulnerable decoder. Each tool handles this differently, and blocking Brotli in one place doesn't protect the others.
curl only decodes compressed responses when you pass --compressed . Remove the flag from scripts, aliases, CI jobs, and .curlrc files. Setting an Accept-Encoding header yourself with -H doesn't turn decoding on.
In apps that use libcurl, leave CURLOPT_ACCEPT_ENCODING at its default of NULL, which stops libcurl from decompressing responses. Setting it to a list like "gzip, deflate" won't protect you, because a malicious server can respond with Brotli regardless of what the client asks for.
To check whether your curl build can decode Brotli at all, run curl -V and look for brotli in the Features line.
Where Brotli support is optional, uninstall Brotli and brotlicffi, remove extras such as httpx[brotli] and any other requirements that would reinstall them, regenerate your lockfiles, and rebuild and restart your workloads. Requests, urllib3, and HTTPX keep gzip and deflate support without these packages, but a server that sends Brotli anyway may cause an unreadable response or an application error. Uninstalling the packages also leaves any Brotli decoders bundled into other runtimes, libraries, or products in place.
Reject requests whose Content-Encoding includes br in middleware or at your proxy, before Express 5 or body-parser 2.x decodes the body. fetch() decodes Brotli responses automatically and doesn't offer a standard setting to turn that off, so upgrading the runtime is the only fix for responses your app fetches.
Envoy only decodes Brotli when the Brotli decompressor filter is configured, which Istio doesn't do by default. To find it in your EnvoyFilters, run:
kubectl get envoyfilters -A -o yaml | grep -nE 'compression\.brotli\.decompressor|brotli\.decompressor\.v3\.Brotli'
To check a running sidecar or gateway, run:
istioctl proxy-config listeners <pod> -n <namespace> -o json | grep -nE 'compression\.brotli\.decompressor|brotli\.decompressor\.v3\.Brotli'
If either command returns a match, remove the Brotli decompressor from the EnvoyFilter and run the second command again to confirm it's gone from the live proxy configuration. Using Brotli only to compress responses doesn't trigger the vulnerable code.
mod_brotli compresses responses and doesn't decode them, so a standard Apache setup doesn't run the vulnerable decoder.
Aikido flags vulnerable versions of Brotli and brotlicffi in your repositories, container images , and dependencies, including when they arrive as transitive dependencies. Your dashboard shows which services still run a vulnerable version, so you can upgrade the ones that call outside servers or accept compressed request bodies first.
Once you've upgraded, Aikido checks if the finding is gone. For platforms with no vendor fix yet, Aikido provides patched Node.js and Ubuntu container images, so you can remediate without changing versions.
Wednesday, October 21: Node.js disclosed CVE-2026-111497, dubbed “Node2Shell.” A Node.js process that decompresses attacker-controlled Brotli data can be made to leak memory or run arbitrary code. Users were exposed if their app or a library decompresses bad Brotli data (e.g. the built-in fetch(), body-parser). Node.js released fixes the same day. Google released fixed Brotli versions 1.0.10, 1.1.1 and 1.2.1 the same day.
Thursday, October 22: The maintainers of the Brotli and brotlicffi packages on PyPI shipped fixes for the same flaw, and GitHub published an advisory covering both.
Friday, October 23: It became clear the flaw reaches other languages and services, given how widely the library is integrated downstream. Patches landed for Bun, Envoy and Istio. OpenAI also shared that the root cause had been fixed in Brotli's source code back in February , without anyone flagging it as a security fix.
Saturday, October 24: Java brotli4j shipped a fix, and Amazon published its Amazon Linux 2023 advisory.
Sunday, October 25: Microsoft released out-of-band .NET updates.
Monday, October 26: Debian and Alpine have fixes. Fedora and Red Hat are partly fixed, and Ubuntu, SUSE and the standard RHEL repositories have none yet. Aikido published patched Node.js and Ubuntu container images for platforms with no vendor fix. See the table above for each platform.
Tuesday, October 27: Ubuntu releases fixes
The flaw sits in DecodeBlockTypeAndLength() , which handles block switches, the points where a Brotli stream changes which Huffman tree it uses. In vulnerable versions the function returns a plain boolean, and BROTLI_FALSE can mean either "this stream is malformed" or "I need more input." Callers can't tell the two apart, and on the fast path the decoder discards the return value entirely.
A crafted stream can declare a single block type and then exhaust that block's length, which forces a switch that can't succeed. The decoder then either reports that it needs more input for a stream that's complete, or keeps decoding with the block state it already had. That second path leads to the out-of-bounds write.
The upstream fix, google/brotli commit 0ed4268 , makes the function return an error code and adds a new error, BROTLI_DECODER_ERROR_FORMAT_BLOCK_SWITCH (-17). Decoding now stops on a format error on both the safe and fast paths. OpenSourceMalware diffed the Brotli 1.2.0 and 1.2.1 source distributions and found that 1.2.1 differs only in the version bump and the decoder changes from that commit.
OpenSourceMalware (OSM) did early research into how this flaw reaches Python, including diffing the patched releases and testing the decoder with AddressSanitizer. Their write-up is worth reading for the full details.
The Brotli flaw behind Node2Shell (CVE-2026-111497) affects Python. Two PyPI packages, Brotli and brotlicffi, compile the same vulnerable Brotli decoder that Node.js bundles. GitHub published an advisory for the CVE. Brotli has 82.8 million downloads per month.
You're affected if any Python environment you run has Brotli 1.2.0 or earlier, or brotlicffi 1.2.0.x, installed. Popular HTTP clients such as requests and httpx load these packages automatically when they're present . Some packages automatically install Brotli as a dependency such as Scrapy, while others require explicit mention of it. An attacker can reach the vulnerable decoder by sending a malicious Brotli response to a request your app makes, or by sending your app a request body compressed with Brotli. That means an app can be exposed without importing Brotli anywhere in its own code. It’s a popular transitive dependency, so check your systems.
To fix it, upgrade to the patched releases:
You’re affected if any of your Python environments have one of these packages installed:
Your code doesn’t have to import either package. These HTTP clients advertise Accept-Encoding: br and decode Brotli responses automatically:
Attacker data can reach the decoder through two routes:
The fix is a package upgrade, and it takes four steps:
If your Python Brotli bindings came from a Linux distribution package instead of PyPI, the fix comes through your distribution, so check its security advisory as well.
Python Brotli vulnerability refers to CVE-2026-111497, the Brotli decoder flaw known as Node2Shell , as it affects Python packages on PyPI. The CVE record pairs CWE-252 (unchecked return value) with CWE-787 (out-of-bounds write).
The CVE record gives the flaw a CVSS 4.0 score of 9.2, and Node.js rates it high severity. OSM built Brotli 1.2.0 and 1.2.1 with AddressSanitizer and ran a crafted stream through both. Version 1.2.0 consumed all of the roughly 23 MB stream and kept reporting that it needed more input, whether the stream arrived in one piece or in chunks as small as one byte. Version 1.2.1 rejected the stream with error -17 every time.
OSM didn't pursue memory corruption or code execution in the Python extension. The decoder code is the same code that researchers exploited against an unmodified Node.js 24.22.0 build, as Imperva and others reported. For Node.js, The Hacker News reported no exploitation in the wild as of October 22.
Treat it as urgent anyway. The bug is a memory-safety flaw in a component that handles untrusted network input, and the fix is a routine version bump. Services that call outside servers or accept compressed request bodies should go first.
If you're reproducing the bug from Python, brotli.decompress() raises a generic brotli.error: decoder failed for any error, so you can't see which error code fired. A Decompressor() fed the crafted stream incrementally will never finish on 1.2.0.
‍ Which versions fix CVE-2026-111497 in Python?
Brotli 1.2.1 and brotlicffi 1.2.1.0, along with any newer releases.
An installed package is enough. urllib3, requests, httpx and aiohttp use Brotli or brotlicffi automatically when either is present and decode Brotli responses from any server your app calls.
It should now. pip-audit reads the PyPI advisory database, which includes PYSEC-2026-4322 for Brotli and PYSEC-2026-4323 for brotlicffi, and OSV now maps the GitHub advisory that Dependabot uses to both packages. Aikido also flags both, including when they arrive as transitive dependencies.
Uninstalling Brotli and brotlicffi removes the vulnerable decoder from Python, though a server that sends Brotli anyway may cause errors. Rejecting Brotli-encoded requests at the edge reduces inbound exposure but doesn't protect against Brotli responses your app fetches. For steps covering other tools, see "How to disable Brotli decoding while you patch."

title: Ooni to grace Dokubo-Asari’s coronation in Rivers
body:
The Ooni of Ife, Adeyeye Ogunwusi, has been invited to the coronation of Mujahid Dokubo-Asari, the Amanyanabo of Elem Kalabari in Rivers State , scheduled for 19 December.
Mr Dokubo-Asari extended the invitation during a visit to Mr Ogunwusi at his palace in Ile-Ife, Osun State, according to a statement signed by Sadiq Lawal, the director of media and public affairs at the palace.
The visit also provided an opportunity for both traditional rulers to discuss strengthening cultural, historical and economic relations between Ile-Ife and Elem Kalabari.
“The visit provided an opportunity for the Kalabari monarch to formally invite the Ooni to the forthcoming Se Diye (Coronation) ceremony scheduled for December 19, 2026, in Buguma, Rivers State,” the statement read.
Mr Dokubo-Asari, also known as Da Amakiri Tubo, said traditional institutions remained important to community development, conflict resolution and the preservation of cultural heritage.
He commended the Ooni’s leadership and commitment to peace and unity, describing the meeting as an opportunity to strengthen relationships among traditional institutions across Nigeria.
Responding, Mr Ogunwusi welcomed the visit and invitation, stressing that cooperation among traditional rulers could promote national unity, peaceful coexistence and mutual respect among Nigeria’s diverse cultural communities.
Mr Ogunwusi said he wanted to establish stronger cultural, historical and economic ties between Ile-Ife and Elem Kalabari, adding that sustained engagement between traditional institutions could deepen understanding of Nigeria’s diverse identities and shared heritage.
He also commended Mr Dokubo for what he described as the wisdom and maturity with which he had handled his affairs since ascending the throne, saying “traditional leadership required courage, prudence and commitment to the welfare of the people.”
As a mark of goodwill, Mr Ogunwusi presented Mr Dokubo with a bronze artwork, explaining that it symbolised the importance of the people to a leader.

title: Parts of UAE set for rain, fog and 50kph winds but wait for drop in temperatures goes on
body: Parts of the UAE are braced for rain , high winds and fog in the coming days - but temperatures are set to remain high across the country. The National Centre of Meteorology forecasts wet weather on the horizon in northern and eastern areas of the Emirates until at least Wednesday. The NCM's online weather map shows rainfall is most likely in Ras Al Khaimah and Fujairah on Monday and Tuesday. The weather centre - in its latest five-day buletin - said humid nights were in prospect with fog likely on the morning commute throughout next week. Winds are expected to reach up to 40kph on Sunday and could rise to 50kph from Monday to Wednesday, carrying dust into the air and hampering visibility. The Northern Emirates in particular have experienced unstable weather conditions this month, with heavy rain and hail reported in some areas. Abu Dhabi and Dubai are expected to avoid the wet weather, while the unseasonable autumn heat is set to persist across the Emirates. The weather bureau predicts daytime temperatures will remain in the mid to high 30s in both Abu Dhabi and Dubai over the next five days and could exceed 40°C in Al Ain and remote desert areas of Abu Dhabi. The UAE's average daily temperature in October stands at 29.7°C, according to the NCM's latest monthly weather summary. The mercury has risen this month, however, with the El Nino weather phenomenon playing its part in delaying the typically cooler autumnal weather.

title: Khmara on Starlink: Speed of over 400 km/h recorded, connection stable
body:
Monitoring systems at the Ministry of Defense have recorded the restoration of Starlink/Starshield performance at high speeds, Ukrainian Defense Minister Yevheniy Khmara reported.
"We are recording speeds of over 400 km/h; the connection is stable. This is yet another example of how direct dialogue and the persistent stance taken by the President of Ukraine at the highest level yield results. And this result is, above all, vital for our front line, for our military personnel, for the operation of drones, and for logistics and communications," Khmara commented in response to journalists' questions on Saturday.
He emphasized that the Ministry of Defense continues to monitor and document the performance of Starlink/Starshield.
Earlier on Saturday, sources within the Ministry of Defense told Interfax-Ukraine that the Ukrainian Defense Forces and the Ministry of Defense had observed the restoration of Starlink/Starshield connectivity at speeds exceeding 161 km/h.
According to the Ministry of Defense sources, as of the morning of October 24, Starlink/Starshield was confirmed to be operational at speeds above 161 km/h. The agency continues to monitor its performance, conduct tests at higher speeds, determine upper limits, and assess the full extent to which the service has been restored.
