title: Second Global Rosary Congress convenes in Wa to foster peace and religious tolerance
body: Thousands of Catholics, alongside diverse religious groups and traditional leaders, have convened at the Wa Malik Jaabre Sports Stadium for the second edition of the Global Rosary Congress. The three-day spiritual gathering, aimed at promoting evangelisation and peace, has drawn high-profile clerics and state officials advocating for religious harmony and spiritual renewal. Delivering the keynote address, Bishop of Damango Diocese Peter Paul Yelezuome urged the Christian community to see the Rosary as a powerful tool for evangelisation, not a passive tradition. He challenged the faithful to bear witness to Christ’s teachings in their daily lives to counteract societal vulnerabilities such as poverty, illiteracy, and tribal tensions that threaten the region’s peace. The rosary must be utilised as a weapon of prayer rather than a simple accessory, he stated, urging believers to actively pair their prayers with concrete acts of Christian charity. Founder and Leader of the Global Rosary Network Reverend Father David Obeng Paintsil recounted the origins of the Congress, which evolved from digital prayer sessions held during the 2022 pandemic closures. Highlighting the transformative power of the devotion, he shared a personal testimony of surviving a near-fatal car accident in 2016, attributing his miraculous escape from a burning vehicle to the intervention of the Blessed Virgin Mary. “The doors were opened on their own. No human intervention. The seat belt was released,” he recounted, noting that the incident solidified his dedication to spreading the Rosary. Upper West Regional Minister Charles Lwanga Puozuing expressed the region’s enthusiasm in hosting the monumental event. He emphasised the devotion’s capacity to foster peace and mutual respect across different religious denominations. Pledging his support for the spiritual exercise, the regional minister promised to purchase 50 rosaries for distribution among attendees lacking the prayer beads. The traditional leadership also threw its weight behind the Congress. Representing the Overlord of the Waala Traditional Council Wa Naa Fuseini Seidu Pelpuo IV, Divisional Chief Naa Wayodi Saaka delivered a message underscoring the deep-rooted religious tolerance in the municipality. “Whether Muslim, Christian, or traditionalist, we are all one people under one skin,” he stated, noting that religious diversity in Wa families has always been a source of strength rather than division. The Wa Naa’s representative welcomed the spiritual gathering, affirming the palace’s belief that where prayer goes up, blessings come down.

title: Tinubu’s northern test begins
body: Barring any hitch, the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential candidate, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, will this morning flag off his 2027 presidential campaign in Kaduna, North-West, Nigeria. The main campaign is expected to hold at the Kaduna Township Stadium, with all the seven North-West governors expected to attend, Weekend Trust reports. The event, according to various analyses, is significant in the current bid by not only the ruling party to woo the electorate to vote for its presidential candidate in the 2027 general elections, but more significantly, it would trigger full-fledged campaigns by most of the parties in all the states of the federation. Presidential and National Assembly elections campaign, according to the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), began on Tuesday, 19 August 2026 and is supposed to end on Friday, January 15, 2027. Inside FCT’s education crisis The story of ‘briefcase’ farmers Our correspondents report that the political parties contesting the next presidential elections have not shown much enthusiasm in kick-starting their campaigns since the blast of the whistle, but have been mainly enmeshed in controversies surrounding the naming of their campaign councils. Weekend Trust reports that presidential candidates usually choose the flag-off of the campaigns at regions other than their base. Goodluck Jonathan for instance flagged off his 2011 presidential campaign in Lafia, Nasarawa State, and in 2015 flagged off his re-election campaign at Tafawa Balewa Square (TBS) in Lagos After him, Muhammadu Buhari flagged off his 2015 presidential campaign in Port Harcourt, the capital of Rivers State at the Adokiye Amesiemeka Sports Complex in Igwurita-Ali, Ikwerre Local Government Area and in 2019, took it to the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium in Uyo, the capital of Akwa Ibom State, on December 28, 2018. Tinubu, as the APC presidential candidate had in 2023 chosen Jos, the Plateau State capital in North Central Nigeria, to kick off his campaign with the probable reason being that Jos was the home state of his campaign Director General, Simon Bako Lalong. For the APC currently, the release of the names of members of the campaign council was dogged by controversies until the list was suspended and later reviewed to remove names considered controversial or politically inappropriate. With the indication that the APC is now ready to get down to brass tacks, the concern has shifted to why the party’s apparatchik settled for Kaduna as the place to flag off its campaign given the issues that make the state appear the least likely for such considerations. Issues like the level of insecurity in the state and the charged political atmosphere as an aftermath of the detention of the immediate past governor of the state, Malam Nasir el-Rufai easily resurface to probe this decision. Our correspondents report that there have been chants of ‘Ba ma yi’ in many political gatherings in the North lately due to perceived high cost of living and hardship believed to have been wrought by the current administration led by President Tinubu. There is also the known fact that the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar, when he contested in previous elections on other platforms, always led at the polls in Kaduna State. There are also reservations over the choice of venue, the Kaduna Township Stadium which is considered not spacious enough for a gathering with such an anticipated mass gathering. Weekend Trust, however, gathered that other venues like the Ahmadu Bello stadium is under construction and the Murtala square is hosting a polo tournament. Late President Muhammadu Buhari held his campaign rally at the Ahmadu Bello Stadium located in the state capital. President Buhari was welcomed by Governor Nasir El-Rufai and other top officials of the ruling party. In year 2015, former President Goodluck Jonathan held his campaign rally at Ahmadu Bello Stadium where he was received by party leaders and supporters. Those in the top APC campaign councils, however, share different views. Baffa Babba Dan Agundi, who is the Director-General of the Tinubu Support Group in Kano, explained that Kaduna is strategic because it is the centre of the entire northern Nigeria. He said, “While Mr President will go to other states as well, he is flagging off the North-West campaign in Kaduna because it is very important to him. It is the centre of the region. But it doesn’t matter any state he chooses to do it, be it Kaduna or elsewhere.” On the issue of insecurity, he said, “The simple logic is that the president met this insecurity handed over to him by a northern president, the late Muhammadu Buhari. And with the security architecture then dominated by northern people, the former president could not succeed in ending insurgency in the North. At present also, the structure of our security architecture is dominated by northerners.” He added that for any northerner to say he is not voting for President Tinubu next year “means we are not honest, even to ourselves. It means that northerners are not reliable politically because this is a man who aligned himself with northern Nigeria all his life.” Other public commentators have expressed reservations about choosing Kaduna as the venue of the event, saying the APC is afraid of the reactions of the public; hence they decided to hold the event at a township stadium as against the usual Murtala Muhammad Square. Jalal Falal, a politician and public affairs analyst, said: “The selection of Kaduna State for the flag-off of the APC presidential campaign was deliberate and based on several factors. “As we know, the event is expected to attract APC members from the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory. Kaduna is also the home state of former governor, Nasir el-Rufai, a prominent opposition figure who is currently facing legal proceedings. “The APC may want to use the opportunity to demonstrate its political strength, even in a state associated with an opposition figure. “However, the crowd at the rally may not necessarily reflect the actual level of acceptance of the APC among the people of Kaduna State.” He said Kaduna was strategically located in the North, making it relatively accessible to people travelling from the North-East and North-Central regions to attend the event. This is another possible reason for choosing the state. “Another important factor is Governor Uba Sani’s political activities since assuming office. In my view, he has paid more attention to political engagements than governance. He has attended several political gatherings and party activities across the country, sometimes at the expense of his primary responsibility of governing Kaduna State. “The APC may, therefore, see the campaign flag-off as an opportunity to reciprocate the governor’s support and political commitment to the party. The frequency of State Executive Council meetings since his administration began is one of the issues that should be examined in assessing his approach to governance. “Furthermore, Nigerians, including residents of Kaduna State, are facing economic hardship. The policies of President Bola Tinubu’s administration have increased the burden on many citizens and the effects are being felt across the state. “The APC may, therefore, find it easier to mobilise a crowd for the rally than to secure an enthusiastic reception from residents. “Previously, major political gatherings of this nature were held at the Murtala Mohammed Square in Kaduna, a larger venue capable of accommodating a substantial crowd. This time, however, the party has chosen Kaduna Township Stadium, which has a reported capacity of about 10,000 people. “The choice of venue raises questions about the expected turnout and the security arrangements for the event. The APC may be seeking a location where security personnel can easily manage access and movement around the venue,” he said. A Kaduna-based political analyst, Haruna Ibrahim Nasarawa, described the choice of Kaduna for the campaign flag-off as strategic because of the state’s position in northern politics. According to him, Kaduna is home to people from different ethnic, religious and social backgrounds, making it a meeting point for political interests across the country. He said supporters from other northern states could find it easier to travel to Kaduna than some other destinations in the region. “It is better for the rally to hold in Kaduna than Sokoto, Zamfara or Katsina states because Kaduna is more or less the centre of northern Nigeria and also a bit safe compared to others,” he noted. He added that people from Bauchi, Gombe, Borno and Yobe might prefer to attend a rally in Kaduna because of its location and transport connections. Nasarawa also argued that the state’s concentration of security formations could make it a more suitable location for a large political gathering than some other parts of the North-West. His position reflects the logistical and political considerations behind the choice of Kaduna, adding that Governor Uba Sani has a strong relationship with the president, which might also be the reason for the choice of Kaduna for the flag-off. Nasarawa further suggested that the choice of a smaller venue could be linked to security and the desire to create a visibly full stadium. He said the venue was close to important security facilities, including the police command headquarters and other security establishments. He added that a smaller stadium could appear full, even if the rally did not attract all the supporters expected across the North-West. The APC Kaduna State publicity secretary, Mohammed Sani Haruna, said Kaduna was an important city with emotional and historical connections to people across northern Nigeria and due to its historical significance, national outlook and the relationship between Governor Sani and President Bola Tinubu. He said Kaduna, which formerly served as the capital of the defunct Northern Region, remained a city to which many northerners had strong sentimental attachments. “Kaduna is a city of different colours. First, it is the capital of northern Nigeria and was formerly the capital of the defunct Northern Region. It is a city to which almost everyone in the North has some sentimental or emotional attachment,” he said. Haruna added that Kaduna was home to people from different parts of the country, making it a suitable location for a major national political event. He said the presence of Nigerians from different backgrounds in the state made it representative of the country’s diversity. “In that sense, Kaduna represents the whole of Nigeria. When you bring an event to Kaduna, you are bringing it to almost the entire country because there is hardly any part of Nigeria that is not represented here,” he said. The APC spokesman also cited the longstanding relationship between Governor Uba Sani and President Tinubu, saying the two leaders had worked together as pro-democracy activists during the struggle for the restoration of democracy. According to him, the relationship between the two leaders was another factor that made Kaduna a suitable venue for the campaign flag-off. He acknowledged that Kaduna still faced security challenges but said there had been achievements in efforts to protect residents and communities. He added that since the president could not visit every part of the North at once, Kaduna offered an opportunity to reach people from different parts of the region. On the choice of the Uba Sani Township Stadium as the venue for the event instead of Murtala Square, Haruna said people were entitled to express different opinions about the decision. He said polo tournament was ongoing at the Murtala Square while the ABS is undergoing construction, adding that the Township Stadium is the one available and located within the centre of the city which made it very convenient for an event like this. Campaign promises in 2023 In 2023, Tinubu and his running mate, Kashim Shettima, promised to tackle insecurity, strengthen national security; eliminate terrorism, banditry, kidnapping and other forms of violent extremism. They also promised to recruit, train and equip additional security personnel and establish specialised anti-terrorism units; modernise security equipment and strengthen intelligence gathering, border security and community policing; improve the welfare of security personnel and families of fallen officers and protect critical infrastructure and combat oil theft and pipeline vandalism. They further promised to diversify the economy away from excessive dependence on crude oil exports; create jobs, particularly for young Nigerians, and promote entrepreneurship; encourage domestic manufacturing, exports and private-sector investment; develop industrial hubs across the six geopolitical zones; improve public finance management, reduce government waste and corruption, strengthen revenue generation; review the exchange-rate regime, pursue a stronger and more stable naira. Other pledges included; to tackle inflation by increasing the production and supply of goods, as well as coordinate fiscal and monetary policies to support economic growth and limit foreign-currency borrowing and link new borrowing to revenue-generating projects where possible, among other things; increase electricity generation, transmission and distribution capacity; increase crude oil production to 2.6 million barrels per day by 2027 and four million barrels per day by 2030. They also promised to increase indigenous participation in crude oil production, targeting more than one million barrels per day by 2027; expand gas production and complete critical gas infrastructure projects; combat oil theft and gas flaring through stronger enforcement and technology; rehabilitate refineries and pursue sufficient domestic refining capacity to meet petroleum-product demand; phase out fuel subsidies and redirect the savings towards infrastructure, agriculture and social welfare. The target for 2027 The Director-General of the Arewa for Asiwaju and former Minister of Defence, Muhammad Badaru Abubakar, said the campaign targeted over 10,000 supporters from the 19 northern states and the Federal Capital Territory for the campaign flag-off. In a statement issued by the movement’s head of media relations, Edwin Olofu, Abubakar said the mobilisation would involve the group’s national leadership, state coordinators and grassroots structures. Abubakar said the target reflected the group’s determination to demonstrate its organisational capacity and sustain support for Tinubu. He urged members to intensify mobilisation and ensure that their activities remained peaceful and orderly. The atmosphere in Kaduna Since the APC announced its decision to hold the North-West presidential campaign in Kaduna, the state has been busy. It is also wearing a new look as major streets within the state metropolis have been painted, while President Tinubu’s political posters are at strategic places, including roundabouts, mega billboards and public buildings. The Kaduna State Township Stadium, venue of the campaign flag-off, has been given a facelift. Weekend Trust observed that most of the major roads like the Muhammadu Buhari Way, Sokoto Road from the Government House to NEPA roundabout have been renovated. Also, the 44 Army roundabout was recently constructed and completed by the state government. Streetlights have been installed along major streets. Similarly, the stadium was repainted and decorated with APC flags ahead of the event. A visit to the venue showed that roads leading to the stadium had also been adorned with billboards and posters of President Tinubu, Vice President Kashim Shettima and the Kaduna State governor, Uba Sani. Inside the stadium, the conveniences, pavilion and other facilities have been prepared for guests expected to attend the campaign rally. The venue has also been restricted to the public ahead of the rally, with APC flags flying and the premises decorated with green lawns and campaign posters of the president. Security agencies promise tight arrangements Security is another major issue surrounding Tinubu’s visit. But the Kaduna State police command said personnel from different security agencies had been deployed to provide security before, during and after the rally. The police spokesperson, DSP Mansir Hassan, told Weekend Trust that the command was prepared for the event and urged residents to remain peaceful and obey the law. “We know Kaduna people to be peace-loving and law-abiding citizens. So we are urging them to be law-abiding during and after the rally,” he said. He added that the police were not expecting problems because of the planned deployment of security personnel across the state. Hassan also said some roads leading to the venue would be affected by movement restrictions. The arrangements are intended to protect the president, party leaders, supporters and residents. Their effectiveness will depend on proper coordination among the security agencies and clear information about road closures and alternative routes. From campaign visits to working relationship Before the 2023 general election, Tinubu visited Kaduna at least twice during his presidential campaign period. On October 16, 2022, he attended an interactive session with northern leaders at the Arewa House, Kaduna, where he discussed his plans for the region. He returned to the state in December 2022 when he visited Birnin Gwari to commiserate with residents affected by banditry. He also attended the APC North-West presidential campaign rally at the Ahmadu Bello Stadium on December 13. During the Birnin Gwari visit, Tinubu was accompanied by the then governor, Nasir el-Rufai and Senator Uba Sani as the governorship candidate. He reportedly assured the emir and residents of his commitment to addressing insecurity if elected president. The Emir of Birnin Gwari, Zubairu Jibril Maigwari, also conferred a traditional title on him. Despite the campaign activities, Tinubu lost Kaduna State in the 2023 presidential election to Atiku Abubakar of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP). His relationship with the state government under Senator Uba Sani, however, continued after he assumed office in May 2023. Since then, Tinubu has made three documented visits to Kaduna: on February 10, 2024, for the 60th anniversary of the Nigerian Defence Academy; on June 19, 2025 to inaugurate projects and on September 19, 2025 to attend a wedding of Senator Abdul aziz Yari’s son and visit the family of former President Muhammadu Buhari. The visits have included military, development and social engagements, while Governor Sani has maintained a working relationship with the president. Vice President Kashim Shettima has also represented Tinubu at several official engagements in Kaduna, including activities connected with the resettlement of Tudun Biri residents affected by the December 2023 military drone strike. Shettima also visited the state following the abduction of school children and teachers from Kuriga in March 2024, conveying the president’s concern and assurances that security agencies had been directed to secure the victims’ release. In January 2026, he commissioned completed housing units and supporting facilities under the Tudun Biri resettlement scheme.

title: No single nation can unilaterally rewrite NPT: Iran UN envoy
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 24 (MNA) –Iran’s ambassador to UN has defended his country’s inalienable right to peaceful nuclear energy, accusing US and Israel of waging two wars of aggression waged against Iran, warning no single nation can unilaterally rewrite NPT.
Addressing the UN General Assembly, Ambassador Gholamhossein Darzi pushed back against Western pressure, asserting that Article IV of the NPT (Non-Proliferation Treaty) guarantees all state parties the right to develop peaceful nuclear energy, including the full nuclear fuel cycle.
The following is the full text of the statement which is read:
The Agency’s reporting must remain professional, objective, factual, and free from political influence. Its credibility depends on impartiality and technical integrity.
Nuclear energy is indispensable to development and energy security. Article IV of the NPT affirms the inalienable right of all States Parties to develop research, production, and use of nuclear energy for peaceful purposes, without discrimination and in conformity with Articles I and II. Yet certain States systematically demonize this right and weaponize proliferation concerns to pressure States into abandoning their national nuclear fuel cycles.
The United States, an NPT depositary, openly questions the very existence of States Parties’ right to pursue the full nuclear fuel cycle, including uranium enrichment. Denying States access to this essential technology while claiming to uphold their right to peaceful nuclear energy violates Article IV. No State can unilaterally rewrite the Treaty or impose its own political veto on the legitimate rights of other States Parties.
In response to Iran’s resolute defense of its inalienable rights under the NPT, the United States and the nuclear-armed Israeli regime launched two wars of aggression against Iran in 2025 and 2026, massively targeting its peaceful nuclear facilities under IAEA safeguards.
These aggressions caused immense destruction and killed thousands, including our martyred Leader, whose well-known fatwa rejects nuclear weapons and other weapons of mass destruction. They also violated international law, the UN Charter, the IAEA Statute, relevant IAEA General Conference resolutions, and Security Council resolution 487 (1981).
Neither the IAEA General Conference, the IAEA Board of Governors, nor the Director General has condemned these attacks. The Security Council has likewise failed to do so. The Director General has once again failed to condemn these attacks in his statements delivered today under this agenda item. Instead, pressure is directed against the victim while the aggressors escape accountability.
Certain Western delegations continue to invoke so-called proliferation concerns while refusing to condemn attacks against safeguarded peaceful nuclear facilities. This is not a consistent commitment to non-proliferation; it is the weaponization of non-proliferation for political purposes.
The hypocrisy of this approach is blatant. Iran, an NPT State Party since 1970, has consistently affirmed its commitment to its international obligations and diplomacy. Yet its peaceful nuclear program and safeguarded facilities have been subjected to political pressure and military attacks, while the Secretariat’s withholding of technical cooperation deprives Iran of the benefits of peaceful nuclear development that the Agency is mandated to promote. Meanwhile, the Israeli regime—the region’s sole possessor of nuclear weapons, with unsafeguarded nuclear facilities—continues to enjoy impunity. This selective application of non-proliferation standards exposes the political motives behind the pressure on Iran and undermines the credibility of the international non-proliferation regime.
These same delegations demand access for inspectors while military threats persist, disregarding the extraordinary circumstances created by aggression. Let us be clear: Iran has neither abandoned nor formally suspended its safeguards obligations. However, aggression has fundamentally altered the physical and security conditions for their implementation. The Agency’s own reports acknowledge that verification activities ceased and inspectors were withdrawn for safety reasons. Those same safety concerns cannot be ignored when their return is demanded.
The continued existence of safeguards obligations does not eliminate the need to assess whether verification can be performed safely and effectively. No country can reasonably be expected to provide access amid military operations and persistent threats without adequate safety guarantees. Responsibility for creating these circumstances lies with the aggressors, not their victim.
Iran will continue to cooperate with the Agency to the extent circumstances permit. However, such cooperation cannot come at the expense of the safety of its people, facilities, or IAEA inspectors.

title: “Not allow warmongering rulers to distort your protests”
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 24 (MNA) – Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf has told the global protesters, emphasizing, “Don’t allow the warmongering rulers to distort your protests.”
In a post on his account late on Friday, he called on protesters across the world to “not allow warmongering rulers to distort their protests by creating a fake binary” and wrote, “Their post-awakening playbook: shift protest from vertical to horizontal, then shame you for waking up.”
“Hold the line. Signal: Epstein, Gaza, Iran war, corruption, all from same top cabal. Noise: native vs. non-native. Don’t let them change the subject to dodge accountability,” Ghalibaf stressed.

title: Attempt to accuse Russia of disinformation turned against West — envoy
body:
MOSCOW, October 24. /TASS/. Disinformation about alleged fakes in Russia in the Hunter Biden case has turned against the West, said Kirill Dmitriev, Special Representative of the Russian President for Investment and Economic Cooperation with Foreign Countries, and head of the Russian Direct Investment Fund.
"Disinformation about the supposed ‘Russian disinformation’ is exposed. Agents trying to cover up Hunter’s ‘laptop from hell’ story are charged. Russian hoax conspiracy backfires," he wrote on X in response to the news that two FBI agents were arrested in the United States on charges of giving false testimony to Congress regarding the laptop belonging to the son of the former US president.
Hunter Biden’s laptop, which was allegedly handed over by its owner to a workshop in Delaware and left there, contained information that could be used to discredit him. In the autumn of 2020, this information became public, causing a political scandal in the United States. Initially, the US falsely claimed that the data about this computer was Russian disinformation. However, it later turned out that all this information was true.

title: US merely dream of returning to Persian Gulf: Iran's top gen.
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 24 (MNA) – Issuing stark warning to US, the chief of Staff of the Armed Forces and Commander of the Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters has said, “Under no circumstances will we allow rusting US warships to re-enter the Persian Gulf."
The proud and powerful Armed Forces of the Islamic Republic of Iran have rendered the US Navy ineffective — a force that Trump and the US leadership regard as the pinnacle of American power and use to threaten the region and the world — to the extent that it is no longer capable of approaching the waters surrounding the Persian Gulf or Iran’s territorial waters, Major General Ali Abdollahi emphasized.
“Under no circumstances and at no time will we allow US military vessels to enter the Persian Gulf,” he reiterated.
Trump has repeatedly claimed that Iran’s nuclear facilities have been destroyed, while at the same time repeatedly stating that Iran must not possess nuclear weapons. This blatant contradiction appears to have no end, he opined.
If you have destroyed everything, then what is the meaning of repeating this delusion? These completely meaningless, contradictory and repetitive statements are intended to deceive world public opinion, particularly the American people, he said, adding, “If you are certain that you have destroyed all of Iran’s military capabilities and assets, then why do your rusting warships, vessels and cowardly military forces dare not approach the Strait of Hormuz or Iran’s maritime and land borders?”
Undoubtedly, through the firm resolve of Iran's brave and wise Leader, the determination of the resilient Iranian people, the self-sacrificing Armed Forces and the officials of the Islamic Republic, it has been decided that the United States, its illegitimate offspring — the Zionist regime — and your feeble and aggressor armies will be sunk deeper and deeper into the quagmire you have created with your own hands, General Abdollahi continued.
By the grace of God and relying upon the assistance of the God Almighty, Iran’s strategy of strength is to ensure that the longer this confrontation continues, the deeper you will be pushed into the quagmire of death and decline, the chief of staff of Iran's Armed Forces stipulated.

title: German teen arrested on suspicion of murder in connection with US girl's death
body:
The 14-year-old girl was from Fort Wayne, authorities said.
A German teenager has been arrested on suspicion of murder in connection with the death of a 14-year-old girl in the United States, according to the FBI.
The 18-year-old is suspected of manipulating an Indiana teen over a social platform into harming herself and taking her own life, according to prosecutors in Germany.
The FBI said Friday it worked with local Indiana authorities to investigate the teenager's death and shared evidence with German authorities. The suspect was arrested on Thursday, prosecutors in Hamburg said.
The girl was from Fort Wayne, according to the Fort Wayne Police Department, which investigated her death.
"After a thorough criminal investigation, the Homicide Unit identified a suspect who contributed to the juvenile’s death," the police department said in a statement Friday. "Investigators identified him as an adult male residing in Germany and collaborated with federal partners at the Federal Bureau of Investigation and authorities in Germany."
Officials have not publicly identified the girl or the suspect.
Hamburg prosecutors said the German national, who was 17 at the time of the alleged offenses, is suspected of manipulating "a psychologically vulnerable" American girl through the social platform Discord between September and October.
Prosecutors are investigating reports alleging the suspect demanded the girl to inflict severe self-harm and then to take her life on Oct. 2.
Whether the death was recorded on video "remains a subject of the ongoing investigation," Hamburg prosecutors said.
The suspect allegedly tried to obtain footage of the death and "threatened the girl's social circle, stating that he would otherwise publish her personal data as well as compromising images of her," prosecutors said.
Prosecutors believe the suspect sought to use the footage to gain status within or to gain entry to the so-called "NMK" (Nefarious Maniac Kult), which they said is modeled on groups linked to the online "COM network" such as "764."
A Discord spokesperson said in a statement to ABC News on Monday that the company "has been aggressively disrupting the 764 subculture and affiliated groups since 2021, when we first identified these actors."
"We were among the first to share intelligence with law enforcement and alert other major online services, and have since removed thousands of servers, banned users, and filed numerous CyberTip reports with NCMEC [National Center for Missing & Exploited Children] related to 764 and other sadistic harm actors," the statement continued. "We continue to work closely and proactively with law enforcement and industry partners to identify, disrupt and prevent these groups from causing harm."
Last week, authorities in Fort Wayne warned the community about what they called the online extremist network 764 and "splinter groups" that they said target vulnerable teens through social media and gaming websites.
"The most concerning thing that we're seeing is these groups are encouraging these young people that they're targeting to commit self-harm, cutting, carving symbols and words into their bodies," Fort Wayne Police Department Det. Brian Martin said at a news conference on Oct. 14.
"They're encouraging our children to send explicit photos, nude photos of themselves. They're encouraging our young people to commit self-mutilation. They are encouraging to harm family pets, to torture pets," he continued.
He added, "They're such predators that they want this to be video recorded or live streamed to them while they're doing this."
Previously, Discord has said that disrupting the 764 network and affiliate groups "has been among Discord's highest priorities" and that it has taken steps to remove thousands of "servers" and invested in new ways to detect the groups.
ABC News' Jason Volack contributed to this report.

title: UN Exhibition in Astana Highlights 30 Stories of Sustainable Development
body: The Astana Times provides news and information from Kazakhstan and around the world. ASTANA – A young inventor turning air pollution into printer pigments, a teacher inspiring students to rediscover the joy of reading and an entrepreneur harnessing solar energy to extract drinking water from the air are among 30 people featured in a United Nations exhibition that opened in Astana on Oct. 21. A visitor explores the GLOCAL exhibition in Astana. Photo credit: Dariga Bassybayeva / The Astana Times The photography and multimedia exhibition, titled “GLOCAL: Global Goals. Local Lives,” highlights people whose work is helping turn the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) into practical solutions for communities across Kazakhstan. The exhibition, which takes place in the National Museum of Kazakhstan, features stories from Astana, Almaty, Shymkent and Kyzylorda, as well as the Karagandy, Akmola, Turkistan and Mangystau regions. Those profiled include young innovators, educators, health care professionals, environmental activists, entrepreneurs working to address local challenges and expand opportunities for vulnerable communities. From global commitments to global actions Speaking at the opening ceremony, UN Resident Coordinator in Kazakhstan Sarangoo Radnaaragchaa stressed the importance of involving local communities in sustainable development efforts. “Sustainable development is not something we deliver to people. It is something we build with people,” she said. The exhibition focuses on five pillars of the UN’s 2030 agenda — people, planet, prosperity, peace and partnership, highlighting local efforts to address challenges ranging from environmental protection and education to health care and economic opportunity. Yerzhan Ashikbayev, First Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs of Kazakhstan, delivers opening remarks at the GLOCAL exhibition in Astana. Photo credit: Dariga Bassybayeva / The Astana Times “The theme of today’s exhibition underscores the importance of connecting this global agenda with national priorities and action in our regions, cities and rural communities,” said First Deputy Foreign Minister Yerzhan Ashikbayev. Chinwe Ogbonna, United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) country representative in Kazakhstan, said the exhibition underscores the importance of aligning global goals with local priorities. “This event signifies what can happen when we translate global goals to local priorities,” she said, describing the 30 featured stories as examples of transformative change. Ogbonna noted that Kazakhstan has made progress toward the SDGs but emphasized that further work still remains. She highlighted persistent inequalities, climate-related challenges, the need for a more inclusive economy and the importance of strengthening partnerships and peace. “Kazakhstan can do more across each of the five goals that we are demonstrating here today,” she said. Kazakhstan’s work on sustainable development also forms part of its broader agenda at the UN General Assembly , where the country has highlighted priorities ranging from water security to peacekeeping and nuclear disarmament. Kazakhstan’s partnership with the UN The exhibition also reflects the broader cooperation between Kazakhstan and the UN under the UN Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework for 2026–2030. The framework identifies four strategic priorities: empowered people and strong institutions, a resilient and inclusive economy, a sustainable environment, and strengthened social cohesion. Kazakhstan also used the UN General Assembly’s high-level week in September to strengthen international partnerships. The country’s foreign minister held bilateral meetings with international counterparts , discussing cooperation on issues of mutual interest. Ashikbayev also pointed to the establishment of the UN Regional Center for Sustainable Development Goals for Central Asia and Afghanistan in Almaty as an important milestone in cooperation between Kazakhstan and the UN. Water security, he said, remains a priority for the region. Ashikbayev also highlighted the country’s initiative to establish an international water organization under the UN aimed at strengthening coordination in global water governance. These national and regional priorities connect with the exhibition’s central message: sustainable development takes shape through concrete action in people’s everyday lives. The exhibition will run until Nov. 4. The post UN Exhibition in Astana Highlights 30 Stories of Sustainable Development appeared first on The Astana Times .

title: Trump floats possibility of imposing 200% tariffs on Ukraine and Russia to force peace
body:
He made the remarks at a campaign rally in Florida, according to an Ukrinform correspondent.
At the same time, Trump expressed doubts about the effectiveness of such a move, as the United States does not trade enough with the two countries.
He said his tariff policy had helped him end eight wars, with trade restrictions allegedly playing a decisive role in five of them.
"If you continue to fight, we're going to put a 200% tariff on both of you – and, amazingly, they stopped the war," he said, recounting a past experience without specifying which countries he was referring to. "Probably we should do that immediately with Ukraine and Russia. I did not think of it."
However, he acknowledged that this approach might not work in the case of the Russian-Ukrainian war.
"But we don't buy enough to do it for them," Trump said.
Trump has previously claimed on several occasions that he secured a ceasefire between India and Pakistan by threatening to impose 200% tariffs on goods from both countries if the fighting continued. India, however, has denied Washington's role in reaching the agreement and maintains that the ceasefire was negotiated directly by the military leadership of the two countries.

title: What community means for a wine shop along Maginhawa Street
body: MANILA, Philippines – For a business owner, sending customers out the door would normally be the opposite of the goal. But for Rose Abes, owner of La Rosa Vino, sharing customers with her neighbors is part of how she does business. On September 19, La Rosa Vino once again brought guests to walk along Maginhawa Street, Quezon City for its fourth Wine and Food Hop. This year, its day-long event paired wines with signature dishes from six partner restaurants in the neighborhood. For Rose, these partnerships are built on something simple. “A good relationship is very important,” she said, referring to her connection with the Maginhawa Food Community (MFC) and fellow business owners. This is a philosophy that has shaped La Rosa Vino since Rose opened the business in February 2023. What began as her passion for wine came with a goal: to build a community of wine drinkers in Quezon City, where she saw fewer spaces devoted to wine compared with areas like Makati. FOR EVERYONE. Guests of the Wine and Food Hop include previous customers and fellow business owners from the Maginhawa Food Community. Photo from La Rosa Vino But building that community also meant finding her own place in an industry she acknowledges remains largely dominated by men. “I just need to be me,” Rose said in an interview with Rappler. “ Wala akong magagawa (There’s nothing I can do) since it’s really male-dominated. So, I just need to be myself.” Ever since she opened her wine shop, Rose has continuously grown her customer base and has found consistent support from the MFC. Finding her place in wine Before Rose found herself as a wine shop owner, she was working in marketing and events. When the pandemic prompted her to reconsider her career, she decided to turn her passion for wine into a business of her own. Finally, her lockdown-born passion for wine led her to change careers. She decided to take her knowledge, wine and spirit certifications, and dream to create a little nook for wine lovers. While Rose admits that La Rosa Vino is still young, she is also proud to share that she has seen a good increase in wine lovers who now frequent her shop. Beyond selling bottles of wine, Rose has continued introducing activities that encourage customers to explore alcoholic beverages in different ways. “My goal of bringing my customers an experience remains,” she said. In 2025, Rose hosted various activities in her shop partnered with the experience of drinking wine, such as vegan dining, yoga sessions, floral arrangements, and more. This year, Rose leaned more into experiencing the alcoholic beverages themselves — one of which was a whiskey appreciation class. “A lot of my customers showed interest in appreciation classes. It’s a deeper experience compared to what we hosted before, so I thought maybe it would not be a hit. Surprisingly, we were fully booked within two weeks!” she shared. WOMAN-OWNED. Rose Abes (center) joins fellow participants during the Wine and Food Hop. Photo from La Rosa Vino Rose has also noticed that many of La Rosa Vino’s customers and event participants are women, something she believes may reflect their desire for spaces where they can enjoy and feel safe at the same time. “I’m happy that La Rosa Vino is a comfortable space for them to enjoy alcoholic drinks. Like me, maybe they are also looking for a place to be themselves freely,” she explained. “Perhaps the shop being woman-owned adds to that comfort,” she said. But the intimate community Rose has built extends beyond the customers who visit La Rosa Vino. Through the MFC, she has also found support among fellow entrepreneurs navigating the fulfillment and challenges of running their own establishments. Growing with the Maginhawa community While her background in marketing helped her establish La Rosa Vino, Rose admitted that managing a physical business came with its own challenges. Being part of the MFC, however gave her opportunities to collaborate with neighboring restaurants, including through La Rosa Vino’s annual Wine and Food Hop. Formed in 2021, this network of business owners has grown from a small group of restaurant owners into a collective of 70 members. According to its president, Jules Guiang, they started with around five restaurants and initially struggled to establish credibility among restaurant owners. They gradually earned their trust through initiatives involving local government coordination and events such as the Maginhawa Arts and Food Festival. “We advocate for Maginhawa to remain a hub for micro and small businesses, many of which are family-owned,” said Guiang. “The MFC works to bring these concerns to the local government, especially as the area attracts more customers.” He said the group wants to help smaller establishments remain in business and potentially grow, rather than be crowded out by larger brands. LONG-RUNNING. Wadough owner Wado Siman shares his café’s success. Photo from La Rosa Vino One of the MFC’s members is Wadough’s, a pastry shop known for its minimalist cakes, including the viral wedding cake it made for actress Bea Alonzo. The shop was also the third stop on La Rosa Vino’s Wine and Food Hop. “When I opened this café nine years ago, I imagined it as a place where I would sit down with customers and chat with them while having coffee and cake. The goal was that,” said owner Wado Siman, recalling that they never really expected the shop to be famous. Wado believes that most of his shop’s fame is brought by pure luck, especially with the timing of going viral online during the pandemic. This success led him to gain more customers, which naturally brought customers to nearby restaurants too. Making room for more For Rose, the Wine and Food Hop is one way to put that shared goal into practice. By bringing her customers to neighboring establishments, La Rosa Vino helps introduce them to other independent businesses along Maginhawa while giving participating restaurants another opportunity to reach customers. The event also reflects how Rose approaches running her own business. Rather than focusing solely on bringing people into La Rosa Vino, she sees value in encouraging them to explore the neighborhood and discover what other establishments have to offer. “The MFC is very supportive with its business owners, both emotionally and physically,” Rose said, recalling that the collective helped her during her first year running a physical establishment. COMMUNITY. Guests gather around to toast the start of the Wine and Food Hop event. Photo by Elle Guison/Rappler Over time, her fellow business owners have also become her friends. When asked how she found her partner establishments, she replied that they were very casual invitations of “ isasali kita sa next Wine and Food Hop ko, ha? ( I’ll include you in my next Wine and Food Hop, okay?)” For Rose, these relationships have become part of how La Rosa Vino operates. She has always envisioned La Rosa Vino developing a community that includes not only the customers who visit her shop, but also the independent businesses that share Maginhawa Street. After all, she believes that wine is better enjoyed with company. – Rappler.com

title: Who are the key figures in Israel's election and what are their stances on Palestinian statehood?
body: Israelis will head to the polls next week in one of the most important elections in their country's history , with potential implications for the entire region. As international recognition of Palestinian statehood grows, who are the main figures and what have they said about the issue? Benjamin Netanyahu Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has been the most famous, capable and divisive politician in Israel for decades. As with so many recent Israeli elections, Tuesday’s vote is not fundamentally about left versus right. It is about whether Israelis choose to be led by “Bibi” Netanyahu once again. He is not projected to even come close to a majority in mainstream polls – but no one is writing him off. He survived pressure to stand down after the massive security failure of the October 7, 2023, attacks, even though many predicted that his departure was imminent at the time. Many analysts say that he could come into his own in complicated coalition negotiations stages, if Tuesday’s elections result in a stalemate. His supporters, be they fervent or reluctant, say that only he is truly qualified to lead Israel, given his decades-long experience as a statesman, his perfect English and his relationships with world leaders, in particular US President Donald Trump . His opponents say he has driven Israel into global isolation, undermined its security with aimless and endless wars after the disaster of October 7, and empowered the far-right and the ultra-Orthodox, which could put Israel on a path to becoming a theocracy. What he says about the two-state solution : Today, Mr Netanyahu is vehemently opposed to a Palestinian state and regularly says that it has been his life’s work to prevent one. His latest government unleashed a massive wave of illegal settlement in the occupied West Bank. Israeli settlements have long been considered one of the main obstacles in achieving the two-state solution. His coalition partners also want to resettle the Gaza Strip. Gadi Eisenkot A former military chief of staff, Gadi Eisenkot is trying to bring military efficiency to the hapless campaign to unseat Mr Netanyahu. His straightforward brand has propelled him to the top of the opposition, far ahead of much more experienced candidates, including former prime ministers. His party, Yashar, means “honesty” in Hebrew. His brand is more about who he is than his policies. His family are Mizrahi Jews from Morocco, not Ashkenazim from Europe, who typically dominate Israel’s political elites. He lost close family members during the Gaza war. He is from Israel’s periphery, not the posh neighbourhoods of Tel Aviv or West Jerusalem. He says a lot less about his policies and has run a very cautious election campaign. He is not shy when it comes to military force. He pioneered the Dahieh doctrine , the use of disproportionate force in war, including against civilian infrastructure, an approach that shaped Israel’s campaign during the Gaza war. He does not oppose illegal settlement in the occupied West Bank. Nonetheless, his promise for a state commission of inquiry into the October 7 attacks and an end to draft exemptions for ultra-Orthodox Israelis put him at substantial odds at home with Mr Netanyahu, of whom he is just ahead in most polling. What he says about the two-state solution : In August, Mr Eisenkot said in a post on X that no Palestinian state would arise if he was in government. In a post earlier in October, he criticised Mr Netanyahu for speaking “in favour of two states dozens of times”. Itamar Ben-Gvir National Security Minister Ben-Gvir is a convicted criminal who has been in charge of Israel’s police for four years. He is arguably the second most prominent face of Israel’s coalition, after Mr Netanyahu. He regularly gloats about the destruction of Gaza, dramatically worsened conditions for Palestinian prisoners in Israeli jails and the huge rise in illegal settlements. He has growing support from Israel’s increasingly populist right wing, much of which is young and full of political energy. Opponents of Mr Netanyahu often lambast the Prime Minister for giving Mr Ben-Gvir a path to power. They hope that a responsible opposition government can put the Ben-Gvir genie back in the bottle. Even if the Netanyahu bloc that put him in power falls, good polling numbers, a booming brand and a massive social media following mean that he is probably here to stay. What he says about the two-state solution : Mr Ben-Gvir is deeply opposed to a Palestinian state, calling instead for Israeli annexation of the occupied West Bank and resettlement of the Gaza Strip , alongside the expulsion of its Palestinian residents. Last year he said that Palestinian Authority officials should be assassinated if the UN advanced the recognition of a Palestinian state. Naftali Bennett-Yair Lapid Both Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid were prime ministers in the government before Mr Netanyahu’s current coalition. Their steady decline in the polls over recent months after combining forces in April to form the “Together” party sums up why so many of Mr Netanyahu’s opponents feel depressed by the state of Israel’s opposition. Despite a great deal of political experience, neither could drum up inspiration and are now overshadowed by Mr Eisenkot, who says very little, giving the impression that Israel’s opposition is neither dynamic nor energised, but instead a cautious exercise in crisis management. What they say about the two-state solution : Mr Bennett, a former settler leader, is opposed to a Palestinian state. He said in July that if “someone comes along and says that ‘we need to withdraw [from the occupied West Bank]’… they’ll just kill us”. Over his career, Mr Lapid has been more open to the prospect of the two-state solution than his running partner, often speaking of some form of “separation” between Israelis and Palestinians. He has hardened his rhetoric since the October 7 attacks, however, calling the UK, Canada and Australia's recognition of a Palestinian state in 2025 a “diplomatic disaster, a terrible step and a reward for terrorism”. Mansour Abbas He is chairman of the Arab-Israeli Ra’am party and a potential kingmaker. Despite many Jewish-Israeli politicians vowing never to stand with parties that represent Israel’s Palestinian citizens, expectations of higher-than-usual voter turnout in the Arab community could lead to Palestinian politicians commanding an important number of seats in the Knesset. The community has faced a devastating wave of organised and violent crime since Mr Ben-Gvir took over the police. They are frequently attacked by Israel’s growing right wing as a threat to the country. Motivation to go to the polls after very tough times at home, as well as the trauma of seeing what is happening to fellow Palestinians in the occupied West Bank and Gaza, could make leaders such as Mr Abbas a lot more powerful. What he says about the two-state solution : Mr Abbas called on Israel to recognise an “independent Palestinian state” in August. “We want [Israel and the US] to recognise it, and we’ll work to achieve peace, rapprochement and an end to the occupation and conflict,” he added. Yair Golan He has emerged as one of the most important leaders on the country's beleaguered political left, which for years has struggled to have its voice heard by voters in an increasingly religious and right-wing society. He has been the subject of verbal attacks by the current government, including on Friday when Defence Minister Israel Katz attributed any "attack on Israel and all next terrorist attacks" to Mr Lapid, Mr Bennett and Mr Golan. A former deputy chief of the Israeli military, he now leads the Democrats party and last year said he was determined to “save Israel from a messianic and extremist” government. What he says about the two-state solution : He has historically supported the two-state solution, but, like many in Israel, has avoided talking in detail about the subject since the attacks on October 7, 2023. He has spoken about working to actively end the Palestinian-Israeli conflict and reaching a comprehensive agreement, not just managing the crisis. He also advocates uprooting illegal settlements and establishing Palestinian statehood.

title: 13 first-offender inmates discharged from Wa Central Prison under 2026 presidential amnesty
body: Thirteen first-offender inmates have been officially discharged from the Wa Central Prison after benefiting from the 2026 presidential amnesty granted by President John Dramani Mahama. The release ceremony, held on October 23, 2026, marked the discharge and reintegration of these individuals back into society. Upper West Regional Prisons Commander DDP Alhaji Ousmane Tasembedo revealed that 18 names were initially submitted to the prison headquarters for amnesty consideration. Out of this number, 13 were approved by the President in conformity with Article 72(1) of the 1992 Constitution. However, only three inmates were discharged at the ceremony, as the remaining 10 had already gone home through the standard one-third sentence discharge process before the amnesty reached them due to bureaucratic processes. The regional commander emphasised that the amnesty represents an opportunity for transformation and a fresh beginning rather than merely a release from custody. He noted that the Wa Central Prisons has successfully reformed and rehabilitated 34 inmates since 2024. Among the 13 approved amnesty beneficiaries, two acquired vocational skills in smock sewing and tailoring. He assured them that the service would provide them with start-up materials to begin their new lives. Assembly Member for Jonga and Wa Municipal Justice and Security Chairman Daubile Alhassan Ibrahim, representing the Municipal Chief Executive, cautioned the beneficiaries to conduct themselves properly as they reintegrate into society. He clarified that the amnesty does not provide immunity from future prosecution. “It doesn’t mean that when you are granted this amnesty today and you go out there and commit any offense the law will not say oh some time ago the president was granted you amnesty to go home and rest,” he warned. Speaking on behalf of the beneficiaries, 39-year-old Yakubu Anas expressed deep appreciation to the President for the unique opportunity. Anas also extended gratitude to the regional command for the vocational training received during their incarceration, promising to put the acquired skills to good use and maintain good behaviour. Nuokpem Richard, speaking for the families of the beneficiaries, thanked the government and prison officials for the training provided to the inmates. “We are praying that they should go and continue and then achieve their aim at the end of the day they should be somebody in the near future,” he stated.

title: Putin and Modi instruct governments on trade development — ambassador to Russia
body:
MOSCOW, October 24. /TASS/. Russian President Vladimir Putin and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi after the BRICS summit, where they had the opportunity to discuss a full range of Russian-Indian relations, issued instructions to the governments to further develop cooperation between the two states, India’s ambassador to Russia Vinay Kumar said in an interview with TASS after the II Russian·Indian business forum Time.
"One of the concrete results of [the cooperation] was the joint participation of the leaders of our countries in the BRICS business summit, as well as a visit to the Innoprom·India exhibition — the first Russian industrial exhibition held in New Delhi," the diplomat noted. "This allowed the leaders to discuss the entire range of bilateral relations and give instructions to the relevant ministries and agencies on further developing cooperation, including in the areas of trade and commerce."
The II Russian·Indian business forum Time was held in Kazan from October 15 to 16. The event was aimed at developing Russian·Indian trade and economic cooperation. During the forum, participants discussed ways to implement joint initiatives, promising investment projects, and opportunities for technological and economic cooperation. TASS is the forum’s information partner.

title: Xi orders all-out rescue efforts after 7.0-magnitude quake
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 24 (MNA) – Chinese President Xi Jinping has ordered all-out search and rescue efforts for the missing and prompt medical treatment for the injured after a 7.0-magnitude earthquake struck a county in southwest China.
Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, urged in an important instruction every effort to minimize casualties. The earthquake struck Baqen County in Nagqu City, Xizang, at 10:33 p.m. Thursday. The quake has left 16 people dead and 65 injured, according to local authorities. Noting that the affected area is at a high altitude with low temperatures, Xi stressed the need to closely monitor seismic activity and weather conditions to prevent secondary disasters. Efforts should be made to properly accommodate the affected residents, repair damaged infrastructure as quickly as possible, and safeguard people's lives and property, Xi said. Premier Li Qiang, also a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee, called for solid disaster prevention and response efforts. The Ministry of Emergency Management and authorities in Xizang have mobilized resources for rescue and relief operations. Source: Xinhua

title: Reading Xi's vision for global governance through metaphors
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 24 (MNA) – The 2026 Global Governance Forum (Xiong'an) is set to open on Friday in the Xiong'an New Area, north China's Hebei Province.
The 2026 Global Governance Forum (Xiong'an) is set to open on Friday in the Xiong'an New Area, north China's Hebei Province, bringing into world focus a pressing question: How can countries work together to address shared challenges in an interconnected world amid growing protectionism and unilateralism?
In speeches and meetings on multiple occasions, Chinese President Xi Jinping has used vivid metaphors to articulate his vision for global governance. These metaphors offer insights into his approach to building a more just, equitable and inclusive global governance system.
"I was looking at the vast ocean when I boarded the ship, and it struck me that we are all indeed fellow passengers in the same boat," Xi said while addressing the 2018 APEC CEO Summit hosted at a unique setting -- onboard the giant cruise Pacific Explorer in Port Moresby, Papua New Guinea.
The metaphor embodies the essence of Xi's vision of building a community with a shared future for humanity, highlighting the interconnectedness of countries and the need for solidarity and cooperation in addressing common challenges.
Today, the interconnected world is grappling with four mounting deficits: a peace deficit that exacerbates geopolitical conflicts, a development deficit that widens the North-South divide, a security deficit that erodes mutual trust, and a governance deficit that undermines the effectiveness of multilateralism.
In 2019, at the China-France Global Governance Forum held in Paris, Xi proposed a four-pronged approach to addressing the four deficits. First and foremost, he called for fairness and reasonableness to address the governance deficit.
"It is advisable to uphold a vision of global governance featuring extensive consultation and joint contribution for shared benefits," Xi said, calling for actively advancing the democratization of global governance rules.
As the world has found itself in a new period of turbulence and transformation, global governance has come to a new crossroads. Against this backdrop, Xi put forward the Global Governance Initiative (GGI) at the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) summit in September 2025 in China's coastal city of Tianjin.
"I look forward to working with all countries for a more just and equitable global governance system and advancing toward a community with a shared future for humanity," Xi said, stressing sovereign equality and genuine multilateralism.
"A world without rules is like a crossroads without traffic lights, where chaos and disorder are all but guaranteed," Xi said at the 2026 BRICS Summit in New Delhi, India.
This metaphor highlights the importance of rules in maintaining the international order. While having rules in place matters, how they are made and who gets to make them matter even more. International rules must be written and upheld jointly by all countries based on the purposes and principles of the UN Charter, rather than dictated by those with the strongest muscles or the loudest voice, Xi once stressed.
He has also called for the purposes and principles of the UN Charter and other universally recognized basic norms of international relations to be observed comprehensively, fully and in their entirety.
"There should be no double standards, and the house rules of a few countries must not be imposed upon others," he said.
The GGI proposed by President Xi reflects the objective transformation of the world system and responds to the aspirations of most countries for a fairer and more representative system of global governance, said Rahmon Ulmasov, a professor at the Russian-Tajik (Slavonic) University.
Xi has repeatedly used the metaphor of a pie to describe the gains of international cooperation. "We should make the pie of win-win cooperation bigger, and ensure that more development gains will be shared more fairly by people across the world," he said at the 23rd meeting of the Council of Heads of State of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization in 2023.
The pie metaphor reflects the people-centered and action-oriented vision of the GGI: making the gains of cooperation bigger while ensuring that they are shared more widely and fairly. When proposing the GGI, Xi emphasized the importance of "ensuring that the people of every nation are the actors in and beneficiaries of global governance."The SCO, the platform where Xi proposed the GGI, provides an example. Within the grouping, China has announced the establishment of cooperation platforms in energy, green industries and the digital economy, as well as centers for scientific and technological innovation, higher education, and vocational and technical education.
The expanding scope of cooperation shows how the "pie" can be made bigger in practice: by opening up new areas of cooperation, creating more opportunities for development and ensuring that the benefits reach more people.
Beyond making the pie bigger, Xi has also called for sharing the pie fairly to ensure justice and equity. For him, the ultimate purpose of better global governance is to promote common development and improve people's well-being across the globe.
At the G20 summit held in Brazil in 2024, Xi called for building a just world of common development, saying "prosperity and stability would not be possible in a world where the rich become richer while the poor are made poorer, and countries should make global development more inclusive, beneficial to all, and more resilient."
To build such a world, Xi said, there should be more bridges of cooperation, and less "small yard, high fences," so that more and more developing countries will be better off and achieve modernization.

title: Mass blackouts reported across occupied Crimea
body:
Editor's Note: This is a developing story.
A sweeping blackout hit occupied Crimea overnight on Oct. 24 after an attack on a key electrical substation in southern Russia, according to Telegram monitoring channels.
"The entire peninsula is without electricity," the Telegram channel Exilenova+ reported on the evening of Oct. 23, citing satellite data, online monitors, and local accounts.
According to satellite imagery from NASA FIRMS, the Taman substation in Russia's Krasnodar Krai was damaged in an overnight attack. The substation supplies electricity to occupied Crimea.
Major cities, including Sevastopol and Yalta, were left without electricity following the hit on the key power station.
The online watchdog NetBlocks also reported widespread internet outages in Crimea .
Russia's proxy authorities in Crimea confirmed power outages, but then claimed they were resolved.
"As a result of an enemy attack on energy infrastructure outside of Sevastopol, our city is temporarily without power," Sevastopol's Russian-installed governor Mykhailo Razvozhaev said on Telegram.
Soon afterwards, local authorities said power had been restored in multiple cities. But according to the Crimean Wind Telegram channel, residents later said blackouts had again hit Simferopol, Yalta, and Alushta.
Another drone strike on energy infrastructure in southern Russia was also reported in Rostov Oblast overnight. Governor Yury Slyusar claimed drones damaged a transformer substation in the region's Myasnikovsky district, causing blackouts in nearly 130 homes.
The Kyiv Independent could not independently verify the extent of the blackouts or the reported attacks at the time of publication.
The Taman substation is a key energy node, bridging the Russian energy grid to the occupied peninsula via the Kerch strait.
Crimea, which was occupied by Russian forces in 2014, has been hit with widespread power outages before. This summer, Ukrainian forces reportedly hit 16 power stations across Crimea in 48 hours, in an effort to hinder Moscow in its war effort.
