title: China earmarks 80 mln yuan for Xizang quake relief
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 24 (MNA) – China has allocated 50 million yuan in emergency disaster relief funds and earmarked another 30 million yuan for recovery efforts following a 7.0-magnitude earthquake in southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region.
The earthquake struck Baqen County of the city of Nagqu at 10:33 p.m. on Thursday, leaving 16 people dead and 54 injured.
The Ministry of Finance and the Ministry of Emergency Management jointly allocated 50 million yuan to support rescue operations and assistance to affected residents, while the National Development and Reform Commission earmarked the additional 30 million yuan from the central budget to help restore damaged infrastructure and public service facilities. The country has also upgraded its national earthquake emergency response from Level IV to Level III, while activating a separate Level-IV national natural disaster relief response. China's national comprehensive fire and rescue force has dispatched a total of 350 rescuers and 83 vehicles for rescue operations. The emergency management ministry has guided Xizang's emergency management department in arranging for Wing Loong drone deployment to the quake-hit area for disaster reconnaissance. As of 6:30 a.m. on Friday, 120 rescuers and 27 vehicles had arrived in the quake-hit area, while the remaining 230 rescuers and 56 vehicles from the Xizang fire and rescue corps were en route as reinforcements, having all entered Nagqu's administrative area. Earlier, as of 4:30 a.m. on Friday, authorities had mobilized relief supplies at the central, regional, municipal and county levels, and delivered them in batches to the affected area. These supplies included 1,000 prefabricated housing units, 3,239 tents, 2,821 folding beds and 4,280 quilts, among other essentials. Source: Xinhua

title: Joyce Bawah Mogtari urges unity as NDC holds constituency elections
body: Senior Presidential Advisor and Senior Aide to President John Dramani Mahama, Joyce Bawah Mogtari, has urged members of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) to prioritise unity and solidarity as the party holds its constituency elections today, Saturday, October 24. In a Facebook post on Saturday, she extended her best wishes to aspirants, delegates and party members working to ensure a peaceful, transparent, credible and successful electoral process. She said the strength of the NDC had always rested on its members, particularly those who dedicate their time, energy and resources to the party’s growth, often without recognition. “To every aspirant, thank you for stepping forward to serve. To our cherished delegates, I trust that you will exercise your responsibility with wisdom, fairness, and the collective interest of our great party at heart,” she said. Mrs Bawah Mogtari urged successful candidates to lead with humility and reach out to those who lose, while encouraging unsuccessful aspirants to remain committed to the party. She stressed that the elections should not undermine the relationships built among members, insisting that the party’s collective responsibility to Ghanaians must remain paramount. “Our focus must remain on the bigger picture: supporting His Excellency President John Dramani Mahama and his government to ensure our shared commitment to improving the lives of the Ghanaian people,” she added. She said while the elections would pass and positions would change hands, the bonds of comradeship and the party’s responsibility to the people must endure. Mrs Bawah Mogtari concluded by wishing the NDC a peaceful and successful electoral process and called for continued solidarity among members.

title: Kim Jong Un orders creation of world’s strongest army — KCNA
body:
PYONGYANG, October 24. /TASS/. North Korean leader Kim Jong Un has named the creation of the world’s most powerful armed forces in the country as one of his top priorities, the Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) reported after the third meeting of company commanders of the Korean People’s Army on October 22-23.
"The Central Committee of the Party has set the task of creating the world’s strongest armed forces as one of the top priorities and realistic goals to be achieved in the new planned period," the agency quoted Kim Jong Un as saying.
He explained that this is precisely why the first army·wide event after the 9th Congress of the Workers’ Party of Korea was a meeting of company commanders. The North Korean leader said that companies are the main link in strengthening the Korean People’s Army, and improving their combat effectiveness will make it possible to qualitatively transform the country’s armed forces in the shortest possible time. He set the task of transforming all companies into elite combat units capable of independently carrying out various combat missions.
"To create the strongest army by training the strongest companies and to accelerate the military revolution of our model," Kim Jong Un formulated the main principle of the meeting. He also emphasized the need to improve combat training, strengthen military discipline, and enhance the professional qualities of commanders.
The event was attended by company commanders, Defense Minister Kim Song·gi, Chief of the General Staff Ri Yong·gil, and other representatives of the military leadership. After the meeting, an award ceremony was held to recognize the outstanding service members.

title: Nigerian woman jailed seven years for human trafficking in Tamale
body: A 24-year-old Nigerian woman has been sentenced to seven years’ imprisonment with hard labour for human trafficking after a trial at the Gender-Based Violence Court in Tamale. Mariam Yussif was convicted on October 22, 2026, following a police investigation into the alleged recruitment and movement of victims from Nigeria to Ghana for sexual exploitation. The Northern Regional Police Command said Yussif and her 22-year-old sister, Precious Clement, were arrested at Yendi on August 17, 2026, over their alleged involvement in the operation. Yussif was subsequently charged under Section 2(1) of the Human Trafficking Act, 2005 (Act 694), and appeared before the court on August 19. She pleaded not guilty and was remanded into custody while the case proceeded. After several adjournments, the court concluded the trial and found her guilty, leading to the custodial sentence. She has since been transferred to Tamale Central Prison to begin serving her term. Sister released, victims reunited with families The police said no case was established against Clement, who was released. The two victims connected to the case have also been repatriated to Nigeria and reunited with their respective families. The outcome brings the prosecution to a close against Yussif, while the release of her sister underscores the need for individual responsibility to be established through evidence in trafficking investigations. The Northern Regional Police Command said the conviction demonstrated the importance of intelligence-led operations, thorough investigations and effective prosecution in tackling human trafficking. It urged members of the public to report suspected trafficking cases to the appropriate authorities, reaffirming its commitment to protecting vulnerable people and pursuing those involved in the crime. Human trafficking involves the recruitment, movement or receipt of people through prohibited means for the purpose of exploitation. Sexual exploitation is one of the forms of abuse traffickers may seek to facilitate. The police have encouraged the public to remain alert to suspected cases and provide information that could help law enforcement agencies intervene and protect potential victims.

title: Kazakhstan Eyes Direct Flights to New York in 2027 as Air Astana’s Dreamliner Undergoes Testing
body: The Astana Times provides news and information from Kazakhstan and around the world. ASTANA – Kazakhstan could launch direct flights between Astana and New York in 2027, following the expected completion of a United States’ aviation safety assessment and the planned introduction of Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner aircraft, Vice Minister of Transport Talgat Lastayev said. Photo credit: Air Astana. Speaking on the sidelines of an International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) security week event , Lastayev said a team of auditors from the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) had visited Kazakhstan several weeks earlier and given a positive preliminary assessment of the country’s civil aviation system and its compliance with international standards. The final official report is expected in November. Kazakhstan aims to obtain authorization to operate flights to the U.S. by the end of this year, Lastayev said. Lastayev added that launching the route would also depend on aircraft readiness and the completion of required flight hours for crews and technical staff. “A Dreamliner capable of operating these flights is expected in December. Before it enters service, crews and technicians need to complete a certain number of flight hours. I think that, provided these conditions are met, we expect to launch a direct flight next year,” he said. Air Astana’s Dreamliner undergoes flight testing Air Astana’s first Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner, registered as EI-KZA, began factory flight testing in Charleston, South Carolina, on Oct. 1. Boeing is conducting the necessary certification procedures before delivering the aircraft, reported the Air Astana’s press service. The first three Boeing 787-9 Dreamliners are expected to enter service with Air Astana in 2027. The aircraft will be a major step in the airline’s fleet modernization, gradually replacing its Boeing 767-300ER aircraft, improving operational efficiency and creating opportunities to expand its international route network. Air Astana expands international network from Astana Air Astana Group is also expanding its international network from Kazakhstan’s capital, adding new routes and increasing flight frequencies on existing services. In 2026, the group launched eight new scheduled and charter destinations from Astana: Guangzhou, Bangkok, Larnaca, Dalaman, Batumi, Issyk-Kul, Salalah and Yining. Seven additional destinations were introduced in 2025: Sanya, Jeddah, Medina, Nha Trang, Da Nang, Alanya and Kutaisi. The group’s network from Astana now covers 32 destinations, including announced routes. The expansion targets major business and economic centers, such as Guangzhou and Bangkok, as well as popular tourist destinations. Air Astana Group is increasing weekly flights on existing international routes from Astana from 99 to 116, including services to Beijing, Seoul, Frankfurt, Istanbul and Dubai. Compared with 2025, capacity on the Astana-Beijing route has risen by 55%, while capacity on routes to Seoul and Istanbul has increased by 20%. The group is also expanding its operational presence in the capital. The number of aircraft based in Astana rose from 13 in 2024 to 16 in summer 2026 and is expected to reach 22 in 2027. The expansion is accompanied by growth in technical, training and administrative teams, as well as passenger services at Astana International Airport. The company said its increased presence also supports local businesses through a growing number of partners and higher procurement of goods and services. The post Kazakhstan Eyes Direct Flights to New York in 2027 as Air Astana’s Dreamliner Undergoes Testing appeared first on The Astana Times .

title: Mr Drew’s X Space outburst would not happen under my watch – NanaYaw Wiredu
body: Media entrepreneur and talent manager NanaYaw Wiredu says the recent social media incident involving Ghanaian musician Mr Drew would not have happened under his watch. Speaking to Evergreen Asantewaa on Woezor TV’s Breakfast Café , NanaYaw referred to Mr Drew’s heated exchange with a participant during an X Space discussion. The incident escalated after the participant addressed the singer as “chale”, prompting Mr Drew to insist that they were not age mates and to argue that differences in age and financial standing should command respect. The exchange ended with insults from both sides. “Recently you saw what happened to Mr Drew. It will never happen under my watch,” Nana Yaw said. He explained that artistes working with him are trained on how to speak on television, participate in radio interviews and respond when provoked. “Because you don’t want to put somebody off by saying the wrong thing,” he added. NanaYaw made the remarks during a discussion on building a successful music career. He stressed that artiste development involves more than producing hit songs and promoting music. It also requires preparing musicians to handle public attention and maintain a good relationship with their audience. Mr Drew’s X Space controversy The incident involving Mr Drew occurred during an X Space he hosted to interact with fans and promote his single Steeze . The discussion turned tense after a participant addressed him as “chale”, a popular Ghanaian expression often used informally among friends and peers. Mr Drew objected to the manner in which he was addressed, insisting that the participant was not his mate and arguing that differences in the age, social status and financial standing should be recognised. “I am not your mate. A lot of people think I am their mate, but I am not your mate. A lot of the boys think they are my age mates. When it comes to money and age, I am not your mate, and you need to put that in your head,” he said. The participant challenged the singer’s response, arguing that he was not an A-list artiste to make such a distinction. The exchange escalated, with both parties trading insults and Mr Drew threatening to block the participant. The confrontation attracted criticism on social media, with some users questioning the musician’s response, while others argued that artistes should be treated respectfully during online interactions. Mr Drew later clarified that his outburst was directed at trolls rather than his genuine fans. The importance of media training in artiste development NanaYaw Wiredu’s comments raises concerns about the importance of preparing musicians for public engagement as part of their professional development. Media training can help artistes communicate effectively during interviews, manage difficult questions and respond to provocation without escalating disagreements. In September 2023, Mr Wiredu, founder and creative director of Oneplay Africa, announced a free online Music Master Series aimed at helping emerging entertainment executives understand the business side of the music industry. His experience spans artiste management, publicity, publishing, events management and digital media. He has also managed artistes, including Nana Yaa, D-Flex and Mzbel, and worked on events such as Ghana Meets Naija and Mzbel at 10, according to published profiles. He is currently the PR Manager for Edem Goget’em.

title: Large-scale blackout hits Crimea after drone attack
body:

"Crimea is experiencing a blackout, with key substations knocked out of service. The entire peninsula is without electricity," the post said.
The monitoring channel Crimean Wind, citing eyewitnesses, reported that power suddenly went out, including in major cities. Widespread power outages were reported in Sevastopol, Simferopol, Yalta, Feodosia, Dzhankoi, Alushta, Yevpatoria and elsewhere.
Before the blackout, the channel reported, activity by Russian mobile fire groups engaging unidentified aerial targets had been heard near Baherove, close to Kerch. At least four explosions were also heard in Crimea's Pervomaiske district.
The so-called governor of occupied Sevastopol, Mikhail Razvozhayev, confirmed the blackout in the city. The pro-Russian official claimed that the outages had been caused by alleged damage to Crimean energy infrastructure outside Sevastopol.
"A special regime has been introduced at the facilities, and social infrastructure facilities have switched to backup power supply systems," Razvozhayev said.

title: Rubio reveals theory on Russia's war against Ukraine ahead of next US peace push
body:
U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said that Russia's full-scale war against Ukraine boils down to a dispute over Ukraine's eastern Donbas region, in an interview with India Today on Oct.22.
"(P)eople keep talking about it's a war in Ukraine. That war is about Donbas. It's about one region of the country," Rubio told reporters during a state visit to India.
"At its core, (the war) is about 11 percent of one part of that country that Russia wants and cannot take militarily and that Ukraine is unwilling to give up."
Rubio's comments, framing the war as a dispute over the region, come ahead of trilateral peace talks between the U.S., Ukraine and Russia in November. In recent weeks, the Trump administration has softened its stance on Russia, waiving sanctions and moving forward with purchasing Russian diesel .
In framing Russia's full-scale invasion as a narrow regional dispute, Rubio may be revealing where the Trump administration stands going into the next round of negotiations. It also exposes a profound misunderstanding of a years-long war of conquest that has reshaped Ukrainian society.
Russian drones and missiles have struck every single region of Ukraine, including western oblasts far from the front lines. Russia has also occupied territory beyond the Donbas region, including swaths of Zaporizhzhia and Kherson oblasts and the entire Crimean peninsula .
And while taking Donbas remains a goal for Moscow, Russian President Vladimir Putin has long signaled broader ambitions. At the St. Petersburg International Economic Forum in June 2025, he said Russians and Ukrainians are "one people" and that "in that sense the whole of Ukraine is ours."
The Donbas region, made up of Donetsk and Luhansk oblasts, is home to a key Ukrainian fortress belt in Donetsk Oblast: four industrial cities running north to south, including Sloviansk, Kramatorsk, Druzhkivka, and Kostiantynivka.
Capturing the entirety of the region has been a long-held Russian goal, but military deadlines to occupy it have repeatedly lapsed . Under the counteroffensive ' Operation Vivaldi ,' Ukrainian forces have made advances as they pushed into occupied areas of Donetsk Oblast, and Ukrainian forces have retaken more territory than Russia has captured this fall, Zelensky said on Oct. 18.
As part of the U.S.-led peace process, Russia has demanded that Ukrainian forces withdraw from Donbas entirely, rejecting a ceasefire without such concessions and effectively demanding Ukraine surrender territory that Moscow has been unable to seize militarily.
When asked by reporters about the conflict, Rubio described the war as "difficult" and conceded that Ukraine has "good reasons" not to surrender its territory, including sovereignty and long-term security.
President Volodymyr Zelensky told reporters earlier this week that he would support freezing the front lines to end the fighting, a position Kyiv has held in the past and Moscow continues to reject.
While Rubio described the core of the war as a dispute "about one region of the country," Russian attacks across Ukraine have escalated dramatically in the past year.
Just one day after Rubio's interview, Russian strikes on Ukraine's energy infrastructure on Oct. 23 killed eight civilians and wounded 67, Ukrainian officials said, with drone impacts recorded at 19 locations.
Kyiv , roughly 500 kilometers from Donetsk Oblast, has faced increasingly heavy overnight attacks.
The impact of Russian strikes has also spilled over into neighbouring countries. A Russian jet-powered Geran drone came down near residential homes in a village in central Moldova on Oct. 23, in what Moldovan President Maia Sandu called "Russia's latest dangerous act."
Last year, during a diplomatic push to end the fighting. U.S. President Donald Trump said the " swapping " of land between Ukraine and Russia may have to take place to end the war. Various media outlets reported at the time that Moscow had suggested Ukraine hand over the entirety of unoccupied Donetsk.

title: Air Astana starts flights to Salalah from two cities
body:
Salalah; Salalah Airport received its first direct charter flight from the Republic of Kazakhstan this evening—a development that strengthens air connectivity between the two nations and contributes to boosting tourism in the Dhofar Governorate. On Thursday, The Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) approved Air Astana to operate two weekly flights between Salalah and the cities of Astana and Almaty from October 23. Two weekly flights are scheduled to operate from the Kazakh capital, Astana, and the city of Almaty to Salalah Airport through the end of this year. This initiative is expected to attract more tourists from the Kazakh market and invigorate tourism activity within the governorate. The flight was welcomed by Dr. Salim bin Abdullah Al-Shanfari, Honorary Consul and Chairman of the Omani-Kazakh Business Council, alongside representatives from relevant authorities and tourism companies. Zakariya bin Yaqoub Al-Harrasi, Deputy CEO of Salalah Airport (Oman Airports), emphasized that the arrival of these flights expands the international flight network at Salalah Airport. He noted that this reflects the importance of collaboration among relevant stakeholders, airlines, and tour operators to enhance air connectivity and attract more international flights, thereby supporting year-round tourism growth. Talal bin Humaid Al-Khasibi, Director General of the Directorate General of Heritage and Tourism in Dhofar Governorate, explained that the launch of these flights helps diversify target tourism markets and increases the flow of visitors to Dhofar. It also serves to promote the governorate’s natural, heritage, and cultural assets, while supporting hospitality and tourism establishments and expanding partnerships with airlines and tour operators. These flights are part of efforts to enhance direct air connectivity with international markets, attract more visitors, and cement the status of Dhofar Governorate as a year-round tourist destination.

title: Xi chairs CPC leadership meeting
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 24 (MNA) – The Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee held a meeting on Friday to review a report on the seventh round of disciplinary inspection launched by the 20th CPC Central Committee.
Xi Jinping, general secretary of the CPC Central Committee, chaired the meeting.
The meeting hailed the work performance and results of the inspection.
According to the inspection results, central Party and government departments have made progress in their work, but some problems still exist and need to be taken seriously.
The meeting urged solid efforts to rectify the problems identified by the inspection.
It called on central Party and government departments to strengthen their sense of political responsibility in performing their duties, deepen reform, and ensure both development and security.
It also stressed the need to strengthen leadership teams, while adopting higher standards and taking more concrete measures to advance full and rigorous Party self-governance.
The meeting also discussed other matters.

title: Blue Bombers beat Lions, clinch playoff spot
body:
VANCOUVER – It’s been an up-and-down season for the Winnipeg Blue Bombers.
And it’s a season that will continue after the team once again weathered adversity to beat the B.C. Lions 34-10 on Friday.
The victory saw the Bombers (9-9) clinch a spot in the CFL playoffs for the 10th-straight season. The Calgary Stampeders (9-9) were officially eliminated from the post-season race.
“We’ve kind of had just an adverse year, a lot of kind of ups and downs. And I think that that’s a good thing,” said Winnipeg quarterback Dru Brown.
“I know that our fans of the team probably get frustrated about it, but ultimately, you have to ask yourself hard questions when you’re kind of up and down, and you really have to try and problem solve and find solutions. So we’re hoping that we can take all those lessons into the playoffs.”
Brown started Friday night’s contest on the sidelines and was called into action when Zach Collaros went down with an injury.
Collaros connected on nine of his 20 passes for 105 yards and an interception before being sidelined late in the third quarter after Lions defensive lineman Nathan Cherry hit him.
Bombers head coach Mike O’Shea did not have an update on the 38-year-old American QB after the game.
Brown stepped in and went 11-for-11 with 185 passing yards and two touchdowns.
“Dru, he’s just so calm, right?” O’Shea said of the performance. “He just understands that he’s going to walk in there, he’s going to operate the offence, and then if we make plays, then that’s great. If they make plays, then that’s part of it. But he is going to operate really well in a very calm manner.”
The Lions (10-8) came into Friday’s contest having already clinched a post-season berth and the right to host the West Division semifinal on Oct. 31.
Neither side will learn who they’ll face in the first game of the playoffs until Saturday, after the Edmonton Elks (13-4) visit the Saskatchewan Roughriders (9-8).
A Riders win would see Saskatchewan take on B.C. in the West semifinal, while Winnipeg would cross over to face the Toronto Argonauts in the East semifinal.
A Riders loss would set up a rematch between B.C. and Winnipeg in the West contest, while Saskatchewan would head to Toronto to play in the East.
O’Shea said he won’t be cheering for either side on Saturday.
“I cheer for good football,” he said. “I want everybody to play well. Whatever the score ends up, the score ends up. But you want everybody to play well because carrying a mistake around with you for an off-season is tough for any player.”
B.C. drew a crowd of 30,833 on Friday, despite playing without many of its usual starters, including No. 1 quarterback Nathan Rourke and marquee receivers Keon Hatcher Sr. and Justin McInnis.
“We knew some guys were going to get a lot of work, and deservingly so. And we were going to have some guys that are going to get healthy this week and be ready to go next week,” said Lions head coach Buck Pierce.
“I think overall, just right now, the original feeling is we feel pretty good, and I think we got a lot of information on some guys that you know really stepped up for us tonight.”
Kaidon Salter started under centre for the Lions and went 12-for-21 with 177 passing yards, including one TD and one interception. Chris Oladokun took over in the fourth quarter and tallied 48 passing yards with one interception.
The Lions started off strong with Salter sailing a 36-yard toss to Nate DeMontagnac in the end zone two minutes into the game. Sean Whyte made the one-point covert and B.C. took an early 7-0 lead.
Both sides struggled with uncharacteristically sloppy plays and turnovers through the first half.
Winnipeg finally got on the scoreboard with just over two minutes left in the second quarter when Sergio Castillo booted a 40-yard field goal, cutting B.C.’s lead to 7-3.
Sean Whyte responded by sending a 48-yard kick through the uprights with 16 seconds left on the clock, and Castillo missed a 54-yard attempt as time expired, leaving the Lions up 10-3 heading into the locker rooms.
No one in Winnipeg’s locker room liked the way the game was going offensively at halftime, O’Shea said.
“Sometimes the grind is really good … It’s good football,” he said. “We need to play better football. You just keep hoping that this is going to be the spark, the grind, that this is necessary, and flip this into something good.”
Collaros was sidelined late in the third on a hit from Cherry.
The Bombers’ QB lay on the ground for several minutes, getting looked at by trainers for what appeared to be a head or neck injury before walking to the medical tent on the sideline.
Cherry was called for roughing the passer.
Brown took over at quarterback and sailed a long pass to Dorian Singer, putting the Bombers at the B.C. 29-yard line. The duo connected again minutes later with Brown tossing Singer a 30-yard pass in the end zone for Winnipeg’s first major of the night. Castillo made the one-point convert to level the score at 10-10.
The Blue Bombers took an early fourth-quarter lead when star running back Brady Oliveira slipped through the Lions’ defence and ran all the way up the field for a 63-yard TD. Castillo’s convert gave the visitors a 17-10 advantage.
Oladokun, a former backup for Kansas City Chiefs star quarterback Patrick Mahomes, came in for B.C. in the final frame, making his CFL debut. Williams picked off the two-time Super Bowl winner’s attempt to DeMontagnac early in the quarter.
The Bombers boosted their cushion midway through the fourth when Brown connected with Demski at the back of the end zone for another major.
Castillo added to the tally with a 15-yard field goal before Oliveira closed out the game with a four-yard rushing TD, his second of the night.
The Canadian running back finished the night with 149 rushing yards on 15 carries.
Oladokun and the Lions came within inches of chalking up one last score when he connected with Emani Bailey deep in Bombers’ territory, only to see the running back brought down less than a yard before the goal line as time expired.
This report by The Canadian Press was first published Oct. 23, 2026.

title: Dana White on why Abu Dhabi is ‘a very special place’ for UFC as Usman Nurmagomedov waits in wings
body: Dana White is no stranger to Abu Dhabi. The UFC president has visited the emirate regularly for almost two decades. His enthusiasm shows no sign of waning. As the UFC returns to Etihad Arena for UFC 333 on Saturday, White says Abu Dhabi remains one of the most important destinations on the organisation’s global calendar. “Abu Dhabi is a very special place to us,” White tells The National . “We always try to deliver here.” The UFC’s relationship with Abu Dhabi dates back to 2009, while the extraordinary Fight Island series during the Covid-19 pandemic cemented the emirate’s place in the organisation’s history. White still looks back on that period with particular fondness. “Fight Island was really special for us,” he says. “We had a blast over here during probably the scariest time in human history. It was incredible. It was a great experience, and there’s always going to be a special place in our hearts here at the UFC for Abu Dhabi.” With a stacked card featuring two title fights, there is plenty for fans to get excited about. Etihad Arena is sold out, although White managed to find a few extra tickets for one particularly eager young Emirati fan at Thursday’s press conference. The youngster had offered to let White shave his head in exchange for tickets. White handed them over for free – meaning the fan got his UFC seats and kept his hair. White believes Abu Dhabi’s attraction extends beyond the fights themselves. “The thing about putting on events, fights, concerts, whatever it may be, it’s about destinations – the hotels, the restaurants, all the other things to do here, and then the fight.” The UFC’s business also grew dramatically during the pandemic, with Abu Dhabi playing a central role in keeping mixed martial arts alive while other sports were on life support. “Our business grew like 77 per cent during Covid,” White says. “Fans from all over the world were watching what was going on here in Abu Dhabi.” The UFC president believes that experience helped create a lasting connection between the world’s leading MMA organisation, its fighters and the UAE capital. “It was a special time,” he says. This is the second time since the Iran war kicked off that the UFC has returned to Abu Dhabi following UFC Fight Night in July . Between that and helping stage live events during the pandemic, Abu Dhabi’s relationship with the UFC is one defined by overcoming adversity. Expanding on the close ties, White said: “Relationships are based on how do you react when bad things happen? And Abu Dhabi’s been very good to us, and we reciprocate.” Looking back on UFC 321 That relationship has also survived some painful nights. At the last numbered event in Abu Dhabi 12 months ago, fans were left disappointed as the main event turned into a damp squib. The bout was ruled a no-contest after Tom Aspinall was unable to continue after receiving a knuckle-deep eye poke , ruled unintentional, by Ciryl Gane. The prevailing sense among many fight fans was that the UFC owed Abu Dhabi a memorable event to make up for it. White laughed off the suggestion. UFC 321 in pictures “I don’t know if UFC ‘owes us one’. I mean, this is a contact sport. Anything is possible. These things happen,” he says. “But, you know, Abu Dhabi is a very special place to us. We always try to deliver here.” Asked for an injury date on Aspinall, White said his staff were in contact with the Englishman and his team but gave no update on when he might be ready to return from his injuries. “When he's ready, he's going to let us know.” Gane has since been promoted from interim to full champion without having to fight, something unprecedented in the promotion’s history. Why the exception? “I mean, he's been here forever. He's fought everybody; we knew Tom wasn't coming back anytime soon.” Gane will defend the belt for the first time next month at Madison Square Garden against Josh Hokit. Nurmagomedov to the UFC? One fighter linked with a move to the UFC is Usman Nurmagomedov . He is officially out of contract with rival organisation the PFL following his win over Archie Colgan at PFL New York in July. He is locked into a 90-day exclusive negotiating period with the PFL, meaning he cannot officially sign or negotiate with other promotions like the UFC until this window expires. That window is closing soon. A switch to the UFC has long been mooted. There is already a familial connection: Usman’s brother, Umar, already fights there while their famous cousin, Khabib, is regarded as one of the UFC’s greatest champions of all time. When asked if any talks had been held with the Dagestani, White gave little away. “Well, contractually, I don't know where he's at right now, but obviously, when he's a free agent, and he's able to talk to us, we're interested.” RAF and boxing a threat to UFC? Another hot topic is crossover between disciplines and organisations. The UFC is happy to let stars such as Khamzat Chimaev and Arman Tsarukyan compete in RAF wrestling. Both are slated to compete at RAF’s inaugural Abu Dhabi event next month . While wrestling is an important part of MMA, so too is boxing. One fighter particularly keen to chance his arm in the latter is UFC middleweight champion Sean Strickland. The American went on an epic social media rant recently , threatening to quit the UFC as he voiced his frustration at the disparity between what the promotion’s top stars earn and the rest of the roster. Never one to miss an opportunity to step into the ring with a fighter capable of killing him, Jake Paul urged Strickland to reach out and set up a boxing match. White hasn’t commented on Strickland’s situation, which is not without precedent. Conor McGregor took part in a boxing match against Floyd Mayweather in 2017, while several former UFC stars who are no longer under contract have also swapped the octagon for the squared circle. So why is White happy to allow his fighters to cross over into one discipline but is seemingly less enthusiastic about boxing? Does he see it as a threat to the UFC’s product? “I’m trying to think off the top of my head. Tell me one good experience where a UFC fighter or an MMA fighter has crossed over into boxing and it’s ended unbelievably well?” He’s got me. I can’t. UFC 333 predictions As for UFC 333, White refuses to predict the outcomes of a card featuring two championship fights: Alexander Volkanovski defending his featherweight title against Movsar Evloev in the main event, and Petr Yan facing Merab Dvalishvili in their bantamweight trilogy bout. “I never give predictions,” White says. “I predict a great fight. That’s what I predict.” He expects plenty of intrigue in both title bouts, particularly given the contrasting styles. “I think that’s the fun of both of those fights: the co-main and the main,” he says. “ Merab is going to be shooting for the takedown, and if he doesn’t get him down, it’s going to be a long night. “And I think the same thing goes for Volkanovski. He said yesterday, ‘He [Evloev] thinks he’s going to be able to take me down, but he won’t, and he’s going to have to stand and strike with me’. So both the co-main and main event sort of have the same theme to them.” The focus is firmly on Abu Dhabi, a destination that White believes has become an integral part of the UFC story.

title: Six-year-old’s death at Fofie Yam Festival: Family demands justice
body: The Akwamu Royal Family of Nchiraa in the Bono Region has appealed to the President, John Dramani Mahama, and the Inspector-General of Police (IGP) to intervene in a fatal shooting incident that allegedly claimed the life of a six-year-old boy during the town’s Fofie Yam Festival. The deceased, Agyei Agyapong Gethro, was buried on Friday, October 23, 2026, following the incident on October 3, 2026. At a press conference, the acting head of the Akwamu Royal Family, Opanin Paul Kwabena Baffoe, called for a thorough and impartial investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the shooting and ensure that anyone found culpable was dealt with in accordance with the law. The family also appealed to the Bono Regional Minister, the Wenchi Municipal Chief Executive (MCE) and the Wenchi Divisional Police Command to intervene and provide answers to the bereaved family and the people of Nchiraa. It said it wanted the authorities to clarify what led to the shooting, identify those involved and explain the progress of police investigations. The family expressed concern about recurring misunderstandings and gunfire during celebrations of the Fofie Yam Festival, questioning why such incidents continued to occur during an occasion that should bring the community together. It called for calm while urging the security agencies to pursue the matter to its logical conclusion. The Assembly Member for the Dwomoo/Nteema Electoral Area, George Nketia, also appealed to the youth of Nchiraa to remain calm and allow the police to investigate the incident. He said those found to have been involved would be arrested, echoing the royal family’s call for accountability. Mr Nketia further cautioned the youth against carrying guns to public gatherings and other community events, warning against conduct that could lead to violence and loss of life.

title: Stubb seen as most likely European candidate for talks with Russia — newspaper
body:
BERLIN, October 24. /TASS/. Finnish President Alexander Stubb may become the key European mediator in negotiations with Russia on Ukraine after his talks earlier this week with US Special Envoy Steve Witkoff and Vladimir Zelensky in Oslo, according to Berliner Zeitung.
The story says that Stubb’s significant advantage over other European politicians is his good relations with US President Donald Trump.
Stubb’s participation in the negotiations would reduce the risk of a confrontation between Trump and Zelensky, as relations between Kiev and Washington have deteriorated sharply recently, the paper said.
Earlier, Politico said that EU countries are concerned about their indifferent stance in the negotiations on Ukraine and are trying to find someone who could represent the bloc’s interests.
Moscow has repeatedly stated its readiness to hold negotiations with European countries on the security framework on the continent, taking into account the interests of both sides. On Thursday, Russian President Vladimir Putin agreed with the US position that when discussing issues related to "ensuring future security for both Ukraine and Russia, it will naturally be necessary to talk about the framework of European security." Russia will monitor the situation in the coming days, Putin added.

title: Indian government sites are serving revoked eMudhra certificates
body:
On 17th October, eight eMudhra intermediate CAs chaining to emSign ECC Root CA - G3 were found to have trivially recoverable private keys . They were revoked the next day, and Mozilla and Chrome are now distrusting the G3 root. Separately, on 19th October eMudhra revoked 9,356 certificates on its unaffected RSA hierarchy (emSign Root CA - G1) with the reason “Superseded”. That batch matches every unexpired certificate missing a certificate-type policy OID required by emSign’s own CP/CPS ( Bug 2082782 ).
On 21st October, MeitY posted this thread :
A security incident concerning eMudhra’s Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) was reported in the public domain. […]
However, some social media accounts are indulging in fear mongering about the impact of this incident. […]
The impact of this incident on Indian websites and applications have been very limited and for a very short interval.
— @GoI_MeitY , 21st October 2026, 8:01pm IST
That last claim is wrong on both counts. The interval wasn’t short: the flawed keys were generated in April 2025, so anyone could have recovered them for 18 months before the report. The impact isn’t limited either: the compromised intermediates barely issued anything, but Mozilla and Chrome are now distrusting the entire G3 root, so eMudhra estimates 30,000 certificates from its unaffected G3 intermediates must be migrated. From what I could see, most of those seem to belong to US universities using eMudhra through InCommon rather than Indian sites.
Meanwhile, the 19th October revocations have left Indian government sites serving revoked certificates days later , including four bodies under MeitY itself: STPI , Bhashini , UIDAI , and the Controller of Certifying Authorities, whose India PKI site is serving a revoked eMudhra certificate. Notably, Controller of Certifying Authorities regulates eMudhra’s CA business in India.
The table below lists every government domain name on an unexpired certificate that eMudhra revoked in the 19th October batch: 2733 names. 854 of them are still serving the revoked certificate, 78 have switched to a certificate browsers don’t trust, 111 have moved to a valid new one, and 639 were not impacted because they were already serving a different valid certificate when it was revoked; the rest don’t respond. The full list of all 16161 names , government or not, is available as CSV. Most were revoked within minutes of each other on 19th October, and are listed in eMudhra’s CRLs such as DV/G2A-1 , OV/G2A-1 , EV/G2A-1 and G1 .
Whether these sites open depends on your browser. Firefox ships CRLite , which covers every revocation, and refuses to load them. Chrome’s CRLSet (version 10856, 24th October) has none of these certificates, nor any of the 6,235 entries on the DV/G2A-1 CRL, so Chrome, Edge and Android load them fine. So does Safari on iOS, which only checks OCSP for EV certificates. Two sites on the list have one: www.isea.gov.in and nfscnagpur.nic.in , and emSign’s OCSP responder reports the isea.gov.in certificate as revoked, so Safari on iOS refuses to load it. SSL Labs checks the CRL itself and marks all of these as Grade F / revoked.
Revocations happen (GoDaddy just revoked 4 lakh certificates), but they are usually accompanied by notifications to subscribers to get them to new valid certificates. I’m not sure if eMudhra is doing any of the sort, now that they don’t care about their TLS business.
My first count of 156 sites is now 1366 Indian government domain names on revoked certificates, after scanning every name on eMudhra’s revoked certificates instead of just the IGOD directory, and re-checking sites that block foreign visitors from India. 773 of them are still serving the revoked certificate.
Some notable sites still serving revoked certificates on 24th October:
Another ~2,470 revoked certificates couldn’t be mapped to domains yet, I am working on that.
The table will be updated with timestamps as cert rotations happen.
The tables now only include certificates revoked in the 19th October batch. Revocations on other days are routine (customers re-issuing, reporting key compromise, or shutting sites down) and are left out, but stay in the CSV. The batch lines up with Bug 2082782: of the revoked certificates I’ve checked so far, 519 of 520 from 19th October lack emSign’s certificate-type policy OID.
Many government sites block visitors from outside India. Sites that didn’t respond from Germany were re-checked from a server in India; 420 of the names above only respond from there.
G1 signed under emSign Root CA - G1 (RSA, still trusted by browsers) · G3 signed under emSign ECC Root CA - G3 (being distrusted by Mozilla and Chrome)

title: Israel's elections and not so great expectations for peace
body:
While they differ on domestic issues and in some ways on the West Bank, the two main parties in contention are very much still hardline on foreign policy
Israelis head to the polls on October 27 in a vote that will cast Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his right-wing and religious allies against a motley crew of opposition parties.
At the moment, neither side is expected to have a clear path to the 61-seat majority needed to form a government in the 120-seat Knesset. Netanyahu and his leading opponent are only projected to win some 20 seats each, but the biggest party doesn’t necessarily get the right to form the government. Instead, the Israeli president hands that job to whichever Knesset member has the best shot at winning the Knesset’s confidence. Tuesday’s vote should offer an early indication of which candidate will earn that right.
While both main parties in contention advocate continued wars against Hamas and Iran , they differ on key domestic issues as well as their approach to settler violence in the West Bank.
Electoral math Netanyahu's right-wing Likud is running on his military record. His ultra-Orthodox (Haredi) partners, Shas and United Torah Judaism, are campaigning to protect funding for their community's religious institutions and the military exemptions that have kept many yeshiva students out of the army. His other allies, far-right leaders Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich, want to double down on settlement expansion in the West Bank, initiate Jewish settlement in Gaza, and generally assert more Israeli control over Palestinian territory. This group’s main rival is former Israel Defense Forces Chief of Staff Gadi Eisenkot, whose centrist Yashar party is campaigning on judicial independence and broader national service. Alongside Yashar is Be-Yahad (“Together”) , a joint list of two former prime ministers, Naftali Bennett from the nationalist right and the centrist Yair Lapid. Politically they’re far apart, but they share a platform of security reform, lower living costs and drafting ultra-Orthodox men into the army. On the opposition’s left are Yair Golan’s Democrats , the result of a 2024 merger between the original Labor and Meretz parties. Golan is a retired general and former deputy chief of staff of the army, who wants a two-state solution, along with more money for public services. These parties all want Netanyahu out, and so far none of them has said who should get the job instead. They’ve promised an independent state inquiry into the Hamas attack of October 7, 2023 , which Netanyahu’s government has refused to set up. Final polling currently shows Netanyahu’s camp with 50 seats, Eisenkot’s camp with between 52–56 seats, leaving about 20 seats to parties with no clear tie to either side. Here, the math gets complicated. Arab parties, with the support of Palestinian citizens of Israel, are expected to earn 14-16 seats. This could cost Netanyahu his majority, but that wouldn’t automatically help his opponents, because Eisenkot’s bloc has said it won’t work with the Arab parties. Mansour Abbas’s Islamist Ra’am, which was part of the Bennett-Lapid government , is open to negotiations. The Joint List, a separate Arab-led alliance, says it could back a government from the outside without joining it, but they have a list of demands to any coalition, including action against crime in Arab communities, an end to home demolitions and a path toward Palestinian statehood. Key isssues Among the most important issues in the election is the Israeli judiciary. In 2023, Netanyahu's government attempted a judicial overhaul that would have curbed judicial oversight and increased politicians' influence over judges. A law changing how judges are appointed is set to take effect after this election. One of Eisenkot’s promises is that he will reverse it , along with measures that weaken the attorney general. Cost of living is another serious consideration for voters. Avigdor Lieberman of the small “Israel, Our Home” Party proposes housing and childcare assistance for working families with active reservists, while Be-Yahad wants to go after monopolies and import barriers. Both Be-Yahad and Yashar promise more competition in the market. The Democrats rely on public services as their main issue, but a future government's ability to pay will be constrained by enormous defense costs and the continuing dispute over subsidies for the ultra-Orthodox. Opposition to Netanyahu does not mean agreement on ending the occupation. Netanyahu and Bennett oppose Palestinian statehood. Eisenkot envisions autonomy or a "state-minus" under Israeli security dominance. The Democrats support a Palestinian state that would be demilitarized and subject to Israeli security control in sensitive areas, and they oppose annexation. The Arab parties also support a Palestinian state. The public has little interest in a Palestinian state: a Gallup release this month found that nearly two-thirds of Israelis oppose a two-state solution. Settler violence and the spread of settlements also divide the candidates. Netanyahu says international criticism of settler violence is overblown. Eisenkot, meanwhile, has vowed to reestablish control over civilian affairs in the West Bank, crack down on violent settlers and strengthen the Palestinian Authority, which has limited self-rule. He would tear down illegal outposts in areas under Palestinian civil administration but leave Israeli-approved settlements elsewhere. On E1, the settlement project east of Jerusalem that threatens Palestinian territorial contiguity, the Democrats and Yashar part ways. A Democrats representative opposed the project at an October forum, and Yashar's representative would not commit to stopping it. Wars in Gaza and beyond The U.S.-brokered framework tying Hamas's disarmament to Israeli withdrawal and reconstruction remains stalled. All the leading candidates agree that Hamas must be dealt with first, though not on how. Netanyahu would not allow reconstruction in Gaza until the full disarmament of Hamas and Bennett opposes any withdrawal before it. Eisenkot, however, promises to end Hamas rule , whether through Trump's framework or by military means. Lebanon presents a similar choice between continued Israeli deployments and negotiated security arrangements. Netanyahu has repeatedly said Israel will destroy Hezbollah if the Lebanese army does not. Eisenkot supports keeping troops in place until security arrangements are negotiated. The Democrats would rather rely on international enforcement than keep Israeli troops on the ground. Bennett would go further. He says he would respond to Hezbollah attacks by hitting Iran directly, which would turn the fight in Lebanon into a wider war. Iran is central to Netanyahu's reelection strategy . He describes the fall of the Iranian government as a strategic objective and says Israel must be able to act without U.S. approval. Eisenkot calls for a joint plan with Washington to prevent an Iranian nuclear breakout, remove nuclear capabilities, and conduct intrusive inspections. His proposal pairs the potential for military action with an inspection system to prevent rebuilding. The Democrats favor greater reliance on cooperation with the United States and regional partners to reach an agreement on the nuclear program. Whoever forms the next government will have to decide how closely to work with Washington and how far it’s willing to go militarily. Some, like Lapid, want to keep U.S. military aid, which Netanyahu has promised to phase out over the coming decade. Regardless of the winner, one thing is clear: Israel is not likely to pull back from its wars in Gaza and across the Middle East any time soon.

title: UAE Property: 'Should I sell my off-plan Dubai apartment amid uncertainty or wait?'
body: Question: I bought a two-bedroom apartment in February from Emaar at Expo City, in Terra Gardens. It’s a first-floor unit of around 1,100 sq ft, for which I paid Dh2.237 million ($609,000). So far, I’ve paid 20 per cent towards the property , plus the 4 per cent Dubai Land Department fee. I’ve been feeling a bit nervous recently given the current geopolitical situation and uncertainty around property prices. I’m currently considering whether I should continue making payments and get to around 40 per cent to 50 per cent before potentially selling, even if that means taking a loss, or whether I should simply hold the property until completion around 2030 and see how the market develops. Given the current situation, I’m second-guessing myself a little. What should I do? Ghery, Dubai Answer: I can understand why you're questioning your decision to invest at the moment. It's obvious that when you buy something and then the world becomes considerably more uncertain six months later, it's very easy to start looking back and wondering whether you should have waited. I wouldn't panic, though. You spent four to six months researching the purchase, you bought the property , but not with the intention of selling it six months later. So I would remind myself of why I bought it in the first place before allowing today's geopolitical situation to change what was originally a long-term decision. Your purchase works out at roughly Dh2,030 per sq ft. Looking at Terra Gardens today, the figures don't suggest you've suddenly bought something that's fallen dramatically out of the market. Current two-bedroom pricing numbers are at around the Dh2,100 – Dh2,200 per sq ft level, although individual units obviously vary considerably according to the building, floor, layout and of course the view. On the secondary market , some sellers are asking anything from Dh2.09 million to Dh2.5 million for similar-sized units, so I wouldn't confuse an anxious market with your property suddenly being worth substantially less. I wouldn't sell now. You're only 20 per cent into the payment plan. Selling now because you're nervous potentially means paying selling costs, accepting a discount to attract another buyer and giving away an investment before the main reason for buying Expo City has really had time to develop. You haven't bought a completed apartment in a mature community where we already know exactly what the area is going to become. You've bought into the future development of Expo City and that part of Dubai. If your investment was based on Expo City developing over the remainder of this decade, judging it in September 2026 is far too early. I'd only consider selling if something fundamental has changed and by this I mean either in your own finances or in the investment itself. Otherwise you're simply choosing a different date on which to make the same decision. What I would be asking myself is much more practical: Can I comfortably continue making the payments without this property putting me under financial pressure? If the answer is yes, I'd be inclined to continue with the investment. If reaching 40 per cent, 50 per cent or eventually completion is going to stretch your finances or keep you awake at night, that's different. No investment is worth putting yourself into financial difficulty for and in that situation I'd start planning an orderly exit rather than waiting until I was forced to sell. I'd also keep an eye on the actual evidence rather than the headlines. Watch what comparable two-bedroom units in Terra Gardens are actually transacting for, not just what sellers are advertising them at. Watch the progress of Expo City, infrastructure, new commercial activity and what Emaar continues to deliver around you. One other point to consider, you've already paid the 4 per cent DLD fee . If you sell and buy something else because you're nervous, you've crystallised that cost and potentially selling costs as well. The replacement investment therefore has to be sufficiently better to justify getting out of this one. If this were my investment and I could comfortably afford the remaining payments, I would be inclined to hold and give the original investment time to play out rather than sell because of the uncertainty we're experiencing today. That doesn't mean I'm telling you Terra Gardens will definitely be worth more in 2030, nobody can honestly promise you that. Dubai will have considerably more residential supply by then and Expo City still has to mature as a residential destination. But let's look at the facts, you bought from a major developer, at a price per square foot that doesn't look obviously out of line with today's data, in an area where there will be more activity in the years to come. Therefore, I wouldn't necessarily ask myself, “Am I concerned today?” I'd ask, “Has anything happened that fundamentally changes the reason I bought this property in February?” From what you've told me, I'm not sure that it has. So perhaps the biggest mistake you could make now would be turning a long-term investment decision into a short-term emotional one. Q: I have lived in the same two-bedroom apartment in Dubai for three years and my tenancy is coming up for renewal. For the past two renewals, my landlord increased the rent , which I accepted because rents everywhere seemed to be rising. This year he has offered to renew at exactly the same rent, Dh145,000, and initially I thought that was reasonable. The problem is that I've started looking online and there are now several similar apartments in my building and nearby for around Dh130,000 to Dh135,000. One even appears better upgraded than mine. My landlord says I should be happy that he isn't increasing my rent, but I feel I'm now paying above the market. Can I insist that he reduces the rent, or do I have to move out if he refuses? JB, Dubai A: This is a situation we're going to hear more and more about because the conversation between landlords and tenants is definitely changing. For several years now, tenants facing renewals were mainly concerned about how much their rent might increase by but in most parts of Dubai today, tenants are beginning to ask a different question. The important distinction is that a softer market doesn't automatically give you a legal right to a rent reduction. Your existing tenancy is a contract between you and your landlord. Just as a landlord cannot simply increase the rent by what they want, a tenant cannot unilaterally decide that the rent should fall because cheaper properties have appeared online. But that doesn't mean you shouldn't try to negotiate either. My advice would be to do some proper homework. Firstly, don't rely on just one unusually cheap portal listing. Find a few genuinely comparable apartments in your building or immediate community. Look for those with a similar size, condition, view, floor and furnishing status. There's a big difference between an asking price on a portal and the rent at which a property will actually transact, so recent rental evidence is even better if you can get hold of this information. Once obtained, this is when you should try to have a sensible conversation with the landlord. Don't underestimate yourself because you are actually bringing something valuable to the negotiation. You've been there for three years, presumably paid on time and looked after the property. If you leave, the landlord potentially faces a vacant period, possibly some agency commission, cleaning or maintenance costs and the very real chance that the next tenant pays less anyway. Let's say you pay Dh145,000, while a genuinely comparable apartment can now be rented for Dh135,000. Moving might save you Dh10,000 a year, but once you've paid the movers, deposits, connection charges, the agency commission and endured the inconvenience of relocating, the saving becomes much less attractive. Equally, your landlord needs to do the same calculation. Losing a good tenant and leaving the property empty for just one month costs roughly Dh12,000 at your current rent before any other expenses. Suddenly reducing your rent by Dh5,000 or Dh7,000 to keep you doesn't look unreasonable. That's where I'd try to find the middle ground. I wouldn't necessarily approach the landlord saying, that rents are falling so you must reduce mine but I believe it would be easier for you to get your point across if you showed him the evidence of what is available. Explaining that you'd genuinely prefer to renew , but the difference between your rent and today's market is becoming difficult to justify. And be prepared for him to say no. At that point, this becomes a financial decision rather than an argument about who's right or wrong. Work out the true cost of moving versus the true saving over the next 12 months. For quite a few Dubai tenants this year, I suspect renewal negotiations will be less about fighting against an increase and more about deciding whether renewing the contract will still be worth paying a premium for. The opinions expressed do not constitute legal advice and are provided for information only. Please send any questions to mario@evadxb.com

title: One killed, six injured in Russian airstrike on Kramatorsk
body:
According to Ukrinform, the Donetsk Regional Prosecutor's Office reported this on Telegram .
"On October 23, 2026, at 15:44, Russian troops dropped three FAB-250 bombs equipped with UMPK glide kits on Kramatorsk. A residential neighborhood was targeted," the statement said.
One person was killed in the attack. Six civilians sustained injuries of varying severity: two women aged 45 and 54, a 47-year-old man, and three children – girls aged 7 and 10 and their 1-year-and-10-month-old brother.
The victims were diagnosed with blast injuries, closed traumatic brain injuries, concussions, and shrapnel wounds. They are receiving qualified medical care.
Twenty-seven residential buildings were damaged at the site of the strikes.
The full extent of the damage is being established.
As Ukrinform reported, Russian forces killed two civilians and injured nine others in the Donetsk region on October 22.

title: NVIDIA Releases Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB: An Open Small Language Model for Local Voice Agents, Game Characters and Robots
body:
NVIDIA has just released Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB , an open small language model for fast conversational agents. It targets voice assistants, game NPCs and robot interfaces running locally on RTX, Jetson and Spark hardware. The model is post-trained from Google’s Gemma 4 E4B using reinforcement learning only. For developers, this is agent behavior in about 4GB of VRAM. That leaves room for speech and vision models. TL;DR Size: 8B total parameters , 4B effective, 64K context. Runs on: GeForce RTX, Jetson, RTX Spark and DGX Spark. The Q4_K_M build used 3.1 to 4.3 GB VRAM on RTX in NVIDIA tests. Performance: Top score on 15 of 21 benchmarks against Gemma 4 E4B, Qwen3.5-4B and Nemotron 3 Nano 4B (NVIDIA-measured). Best: IHEval 84.8, versus 67.0 for Gemma 4 E4B and 60.6 for Qwen3.5-4B. Worst: Tau2-Bench 55.1, about 20 points behind Qwen3.5-4B at 75.1. What is Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B? Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B is a small language model from NVIDIA that powers local conversational agents. It combines natural dialogue with multi-turn tool calling. NVIDIA lists 3 target workloads: device and voice assistants, interactive characters, and embedded or industrial agents. The research report shows a Reachy Mini robot running on a Jetson Orin Nano 8GB. In that demo, Cosmos 3 Edge handles vision while Bolt handles speech replies and tool calls. NVIDIA team also calls Bolt the third-generation small model for NVIDIA ACE game characters . Core features from the launch post : Multi-turn tool use, with guidance for asynchronous tool calls. A conversational_mode flag for short, speech-ready replies. Configurable reasoning, plus a runtime thinking budget to cap latency. 64K context for history, tool definitions and application state. How was Bolt E4B trained? NVIDIA skipped supervised fine-tuning entirely. As per the research report , SFT improved tool calling but hurt Gemma’s conversational quality and verbosity. Instead, the research team used RLVR and RLHF through NeMo-RL and NeMo-Gym . Every training sample ran in both reasoning and non-reasoning modes. Each batch kept a 2:1 ratio of non-reasoning to reasoning samples. Length penalties in the GenRM environment stopped answers from growing during training. The datasets and the full recipe are public. For deployment, NVIDIA quantized the BF16 checkpoint to Q4_K_M with importance-matrix calibration. Calibration used about 1M tokens of RL rollouts. The release also ships a DFlash drafter for speculative decoding. On an RTX 5070, Bolt with DFlash reached 272.6 tokens/s. Gemma 4 E4B with its MTP drafter reached 225.9 tokens/s, so Bolt is 1.21x faster. How does Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B perform on benchmarks? NVIDIA grouped 21 benchmarks into 5 capability areas. All scores here are BF16, measured by NVIDIA in its own NeMo-Gym harness. Bolt led 15 of 21 rows in reasoning mode. NVIDIA also reports roughly 40% higher average scores than Nemotron 3 Nano 4B. It claims up to 80% fewer output tokens in reasoning-enabled comparisons. Separately, Scale Labs ranked Bolt first among small models on MultiChallenge at 56.03%, per an X post .

title: Carney Warns Starlink Manipulation Puts Ukrainian Lives at Risk
body:
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney warned Friday, Oct. 23, that restrictions on Ukraine’s military satellite communications have had deadly consequences, raising serious concerns about reliance on American technology while Russia continues attacking Ukrainian civilians.
Speaking to reporters in Istanbul, Carney expressed alarm over reported manipulation of SpaceX’s Starshield system, the military-grade version of Starlink, which Ukraine relies on for drone operations and defense against Russian aerial attacks.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
“However the decision came about, it does seem clear that there was a slowdown of that system with real consequences, human consequences, direct casualties,” Carney said, according to Bloomberg .
The Canadian leader sharply criticized the decision to restrict a critical defense system while Ukraine fights Russia’s full-scale invasion.
“I search for the right adjective to describe whoever took this decision, or a group of people took this decision, against a country – and it’s against a country that is literally fighting for the lives of its citizens against naked aggression,” Carney said.
“So are we concerned? Yes, we are concerned.”
Carney linked the communications disruptions to the broader human cost of Russia’s continuing attacks on Ukrainian cities, citing a recent strike on Kyiv that targeted civilians.
“I just refer in the last 36 hours to the attack at the center of Kyiv,” he said.
“Kyiv, absolutely no dressing up on any sort of military or quasi-military target, just a direct attack on citizens and with immense human suffering. So this is real, this is concrete.”
His remarks came amid growing concern among Ukraine’s Western allies about the risks of relying on US technology, as sudden restrictions could undermine national security and disrupt critical military operations.

title: Demonstrators attempt to break into lower house of Czech parliament
body:
PRAGUE, October 24. /TASS/. A protest against changes to the funding system for the public·legal Czech Television and Radio is taking place in front of the Palace of the Chamber of Deputies (the lower house) of parliament with several dozen protesters trying to break into the building, police spokeswoman Eva Kropacova said.
"Several dozen people tried to force their way into the building of the Chamber of Deputies, and police officers from the special law enforcement unit had to stop them. No one was detained, and the situation was brought under control," the Novinky news portal quoted Kropacova as saying.
Late in the evening, several hundred activists held a rally on Malostranske Square in front of the palace of the lower house, where a vote on changing the system of financing public·legal media is to be held. Some of them, according to Czech media, are still there. It is expected that the vote will take place soon.
Earlier, the parties of the Czech government coalition put forward an initiative to abandon the historical practice of collecting concession fees from the owners of television and radio receivers and to revise the system of financing Czech Television and Radio.
The bill, which sparked protests in the republic, provides for a shift from direct funding through people’s contributions to the allocation of funds from the state budget. According to the protesters, this will mean a significant restriction of the activities of public·legal television and radio, and will also deprive them of independence from the government.

title: Bolt Food’s Kumasi business has more than doubled as growth continues into its second year
body: Nearly two years after expanding to Kumasi, Bolt Food saw strong growth in the city, with activity increasing by more than 100% year-on-year in its second year of operations. The continued growth points to sustained adoption of app-based delivery beyond Accra and the growing role of Kumasi as an important market for Bolt Food in Ghana. Since entering Kumasi, Bolt Food has continued to connect customers with local restaurants through its platform, giving local restaurants and other food merchants an additional channel to reach customers beyond physical footfall. Bolt Food’s General Manager, Ali Zaryab, said Kumasi’s performance demonstrates why expanding beyond the capital was an important part of Bolt Food’s growth strategy in Ghana. “When we expanded Bolt Food to Kumasi, we saw an opportunity to serve one of Ghana’s largest and most commercially active cities. Nearly two years later, the fact that the business is still growing at more than 100% year-on-year shows that the demand was not simply an initial launch effect. Customers are continuing to adopt delivery as part of how they access restaurants and increasingly other everyday products across the city,” he said. The growth also reflects a broader evolution in how customers are using delivery platforms. While restaurant meals remain an important part of the delivery experience, the sustained growth suggests that delivery is becoming a familiar option for customers seeking convenience. “What is particularly encouraging about Kumasi is not just the growth, but the breadth of demand we’re beginning to see,” Zaryab added. “Food delivery may have been the starting point, but customers are increasingly looking for convenience across different parts of their day. That creates an opportunity for restaurants to reach customers in new ways.” Bolt Food said it will continue working with local merchants and couriers as it strengthens its operations in Kumasi and responds to changing customer demand. The performance comes as Bolt Food continues to grow its delivery offering in Ghana, connecting customers with restaurants and retailers through its app.

title: The week in photos: October 17-23, 2026
body: MANILA, Philippines — France saw some of the worst unrest in years as huge protests occurred across the country over the cost of living and underfunded public services. Nationwide demonstrations had erupted into riots on October 17, with a town hall torched, shops pillaged, and buildings covered in graffiti as violent groups clashed with police in cities across the country. On October 18, French President Emmanuel Macron appealed for calm . “Looking at these images, we have all asked ourselves: What was going through their minds? How can French people do this to France?” “Nothing justifies it, nothing explains it, nothing excuses it. Tonight, we all feel anger and shame.” Macron said in a televised address to the nation. The unrest has been attributed to far-left groups, while the government faces criticism for underestimating public anger over living costs and declining services, leading to heightened tensions ahead of upcoming presidential elections. Meanwhile, Pope Leo returned to St. Peter’s Square on October 21, waving to pilgrims and blessing babies from his open-air popemobile as he held his first general audience at the Vatican since undergoing lung cancer surgery eight days ago.
