title: At least 500 people affected by typhoon Champi in Taiwan
body:
HONG KONG, October 24. /TASS/. The number of people affected by Typhoon Champi, which is approaching Taiwan, has reached 500, according to the island’s central emergency operations headquarters.
Previously, the agency reported one death and 94 injuries. Gales and downpours led to traffic accidents, the collapse of billboards and trees, which caused injuries. One person died on a beach in Pingtung County.
On Saturday, all official institutions, schools, and other educational facilities in Taipei, New Taipei, Keelung, Taoyuan, Hsinchu (city and county), and Taichung, as well as the counties of Yilan, Miaoli, Changhua, Nantou, Yunlin, and Lianjiang will be closed because of typhoon Champi.
Champi is approaching the north of the island; it brings with it wind with an average speed of 43 m/s, with gusts up to 53 m/s, as well as heavy downpours.

title: Russia launched 2,597 drones at Ukraine over past week, air defenses neutralized over 87%
body:
According to Ukrinform, the General Staff of the Ukrainian Armed Forces reported this on Facebook .
"Russia continues its massive air attacks against Ukraine, using attack drones to strike critical infrastructure and terrorize the civilian population. Over the past week, the enemy deployed 2,597 Shahed-131/136/238, Parodiya and Gerbera UAVs. Ukraine's Defense Forces neutralized 2,282 of them. The interception rate over these seven days was more than 87%," the statement said.
The General Staff stressed that this figure demonstrates the high effectiveness of Ukrainian air defenses, particularly given the scale and intensity of Russian attacks.
The General Staff noted that the enemy was constantly improving its drone tactics, using different flight routes and altitudes, combining attack drones with decoys, and attempting to overwhelm Ukrainian air defenses with multiple simultaneous aerial threats.
"Under these conditions, neutralizing nearly nine out of every ten enemy UAVs is the result of coordinated efforts by aviation, surface-to-air missile units, mobile fire groups, electronic warfare systems, and unmanned systems operators," the General Staff said.
Every aerial target neutralized reduces the risk of fatalities, damage to residential buildings, and damage to energy facilities and other critical infrastructure. At the same time, the General Staff added, even highly effective Ukrainian air defense cannot eliminate the threat entirely.
"We therefore continue to urge citizens not to ignore air raid alerts and not to share information about air defense operations," the General Staff said.
Ukraine's Defense Forces continue to strengthen the country's multilayered air defense system and improve methods for detecting and neutralizing enemy aerial targets.

title: Sole DXB music guide, from Lola Young to Nia Archives and Fatoumata Diawara
body: British singer Lola Young, electronic music duo Overmono and Malian musician Fatoumata Diawara are among the acts to be announced for Sole DXB, which will take place from December 11 to 13 at The Square in Nad Al Sheba. Moving from its previous home in the Dubai Design District, the festival will feature three days of concerts and DJ sets alongside fashion, art and street culture. Here are some of the notable artists performing at this year's event. Friday, December 11 Overmono (Main Stage) British brothers Tom and Ed Russell are to perform in Dubai, mixing UK garage, breakbeats and techno with soulful vocal samples. The duo gained wider recognition with their 2023 debut album Good Lies , featuring the single Is U . They return with their new album, Pure Devotion , released in August, featuring tracks including Lockup and Even Angels Ghost . Saturday, December 12 Lola Young (Main Stage) The British singer-songwriter arrives following the international success of Messy , from her acclaimed 2024 album This Wasn't Meant for You Anyway . Her smoky vocals move between soul, rock and R&B, with other notable tracks including One Thing and Spiders . Nia Archives (Main Stage) The British DJ, producer and singer mixes rapid jungle breakbeats and heavy bass with her own melodic vocals. Her 2024 debut album Silence Is Loud earned a Mercury Prize nomination, while its follow-up, Emotional Junglist , released in July, features Jorja Smith on Get Me Down and Sampha on Tender . Matthew Herbert (Stage 2) The British producer has spent more than three decades making music from disparate elements, including household objects, animal samples and sounds from food production. His work ranges from house and jazz to experimental compositions. His latest work, theukhasmorefoodbanksthanbranchesofmcdonalds.com , was released this month and uses recordings of food and household products to address poverty in Britain. Sunday, December 13 Hajaj (Main Stage) The Saudi singer-songwriter performs English-language alternative R&B and soul, with relaxed grooves and intimate vocals. Having lived in Jeddah, Switzerland, the US and Spain, he has earned a cult following across the region with his indie-pop sensibility, including in his 2021 EP Last Call for Coco , featuring Love to Last and Place to Call Home . Fatoumata Diawara (Stage 2) The Malian singer is a familiar performer in the UAE, known for energetic shows featuring West African blues and percussion. Her 2018 album Fenfo earned two Grammy nominations, while her latest solo album, Massa , released in June, explores family history and her Malian heritage. Peter Cat Recording Co (Stage 2) The New Delhi band moves between psychedelic rock, disco, jazz and cabaret, led by Suryakant Sawhney's deep, crooning vocals. Their catalogue includes Bismillah (2019) and their latest album, Beta (2024), featuring People Never Change and Suddenly . Gia Fu (Stage 2) The Hong Kong DJ specialises in salsa and Afro-Caribbean music, drawing on vinyl from the 1960s and 1970s. Her interest in Latin music began through breakdancing and led to Canton Mambo, a project examining musical connections between Chinese and Caribbean communities. She also worked with salsa musician Angel Melendez and Big Band Maquina on a 2021 recording project. Maii and Zeid (Stage 2) View this post on Instagram Egyptian singer Maii Waleed and Lebanese producer Zeid Hamdan pair Arabic vocals with guitar and electronica. Hamdan, who formed the pioneering Lebanese duo Soap Kills with Yasmine Hamdan in the 1990s, began working with Waleed after meeting her in Alexandria. Their early album Moga (2013) established their dream-pop sound, while recent recordings include Fashi (2025) and Manhoos (2026). Sole DXB runs from December 11 to 13 at The Square, Nad Al Sheba, Dubai, from 4pm to 2.30am; three-day tickets start from Dh495

title: Zelensky Lays Out Ukraine’s Conditions for Lasting Peace
body:
President Volodymyr Zelensky warned Friday, Oct. 23, that Ukraine still lacks clear answers on how the US and European allies would respond to another Russian invasion, calling for firm security guarantees and at least 10 years of international funding for Ukraine’s military before any lasting peace agreement.
Speaking via video link at Washington’s Hudson Institute, Zelensky emphasized that a ceasefire must come first, followed by strong security commitments, a powerful Ukrainian army and continued access to Western weapons, including advanced air defense systems.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
“We need not just peace. Peace which has to be fair and strong,” Zelensky said.
Zelensky proposed a European-led coalition of willing countries that could deploy personnel to Ukraine, backed by American security commitments.
But he questioned what that US “backstop” would mean if Russia launched another attack with missiles, drones or ground forces.
“Who will react? Not only our army. Who and how? And till now we don’t have answers,” he said.
Ukraine’s primary security guarantee, Zelensky argued, must be a strong national army supported by international financing for at least a decade.
“We need a big, big strong army, minimum ten years,” he said, explaining that Ukraine’s war-damaged economy would need time to recover and could not sustain such a force without outside assistance.
While Ukraine continues to pursue NATO membership, Zelensky said strong bilateral security guarantees from Washington could provide an alternative framework.
He warned that diplomatic assurances alone would not deter future Russian aggression.
“Russia will attack if they feel that they can, if they feel that you are weak,” he said.
Earlier this week, Zelensky said Ukraine was considering US security guarantees similar to NATO’s Article 5, insisting they must be approved by Congress to prevent a repeat of the failed 1994 Budapest Memorandum.
Addressing the Hudson Institute on Friday, Zelensky cautioned against easing sanctions against Russia, releasing frozen Russian assets or offering Moscow financial concessions without credible safeguards against renewed aggression.
Zelensky revealed that Ukrainian, American and Russian negotiating teams could meet in Abu Dhabi in early or mid-November, although the proposal remains dependent on Moscow’s response. The potential meeting follows recent diplomatic talks in Oslo and St. Petersburg.
“We are ready to meet any day, even tomorrow, but it all depends on the Russians,” Zelensky said.
He noted that Moscow had already derailed a planned October meeting by finding another reason not to participate.
Zelensky insisted that a ceasefire, rather than another round of negotiations without results, must be the starting point for peace.
“The right position for today is ceasefire. Point number one,” he said.
He also called for European participation and stronger US pressure on Moscow, arguing that technical-level negotiations must eventually advance to direct talks between national leaders.
Sevinj Osmanqizi is an experienced journalist who writes extensively for Kyiv Post on foreign policy, international security and geopolitics. Based in Washington, D.C., her work focuses on Ukraine, Russia’s war and the broader post-Soviet space.

title: Earthquake with magnitude of 7.2 hits off coast of Vanuatu
body:
SYDNEY, October 24. /TASS/. An earthquake with a magnitude of 7.2 was recorded off the western coast of Espiritu Santo, the largest island belonging to the Republic of Vanuatu in the Pacific Ocean, according to the US Geological Survey.
The epicenter of the disaster was located 200 km west of the city of Sola, where about 1,100 people live. The focus lied at a depth of 10 km.
The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration of the United States issued a tsunami warning.

title: Media Excellence Competition Awards 2026 on Monday
body:
The Ministry of Information will organize on Monday the Media Excellence Competition 2026 awards ceremony at the Ministry's theatre to honor the winners across the various fields of the competition. The competition aims to motivate national media cadres toward creativity and innovation, highlight their achievements, and consolidate positive competition among media institutions and individuals. This is alongside supporting digital media and electronic content creation, and documenting the winning works. The competition is divided into four main fields: press, radio, television, and electronic media. It targets media institutions, individual practitioners and those interested in the media, as well as media students in academic institutions. The press categories include the press article, press interview, investigative journalism, and photojournalism. The radio categories include talk shows, family programs, radio dramas, and cultural programs. Meanwhile, the television categories encompass talk and sports shows, variety programs, documentary programs and films, children's programs, and governorate reports. As for the electronic media field, it comprises electronic broadcasting channel programs, podcasts, digital media campaigns, institutional electronic newspapers, news accounts and social media content creation for individuals, in addition to electronic content for media students in higher education institutions. The prize is awarded to the first-place winner in each category of the competition, with a value of RO 1,500. The competition is held biennially to provide the opportunity to present distinguished works and expand the competitive options for participation, alongside providing the necessary time for preparation and readiness. The awards ceremony will be preceded by a number of accompanying events. These include a lecture titled "Future Media: Creativity and Innovation in the Era of Artificial Intelligence," presented by Abdulwahed Al Qahtani from the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia on 25 October. Additionally, a workshop on "Writing Television Drama Scripts" will be presented by writer and trainer Hassan Dahshan from the Arab Republic of Egypt on October 25 and 26. The Media Excellence Competition, which launched its first edition in 2004, is a national initiative aimed at supporting media creativity and consolidating the role of the media as an active partner in achieving the objectives of Oman Vision 2040.

title: Two earthquakes with magnitudes of 5.0 and 4.8 occurred near Taiwan
body:
HONG KONG, October 24. /TASS/. Two earthquakes took place on Saturday night off the eastern coast of Taiwan, the Central Meteorological Administration of the island said.
According to the agency, their epicenters were located in the sea about 31 km and 30 km east of the city of Hualien, at depths of 15.4 km and 16.6 km, respectively. The highest intensity of the tremors was recorded in the Hualien and Nantou counties.
There is yet no information about damage or casualties.

title: Bunkpurugu chieftaincy dispute: Chief Justice orders transfer of case to Tamale over security fears
body: The Chief Justice has granted a request by defendants in the Bunkpurugu chieftaincy dispute to transfer their case from the High Court in Nalerigu to Tamale over security concerns. One of the defendants, Elijah Saan, told JoyNews that they feared for their lives if they travelled to Nalerigu to attend court. He said the defendants had received intelligence suggesting they could be killed if they appeared in court in Nalerigu and had instructed their lawyer to apply for the transfer of the case to Tamale. The case was scheduled for hearing on Friday, October 23, 2026. The Registrar of the Nalerigu High Court confirmed to JoyNews on Friday that the Chief Justice had granted the request. The transfer comes amid heightened tensions in Bunkpurugu following the disputed enskinment of Melchizedek Musah Jamung as chief on September 14, 2026. The installation, which took place amid an ongoing chieftaincy dispute, reportedly triggered violence that left a woman dead and four others injured. Police have since been searching for the rival chief and other members of the Jamong royal family in connection with the disputed enskinment. The development has also prompted the Overlord of the Mamprugu Traditional Area, Naa Bohagu Abdulai Mahami Sheriga, to file an application at the High Court in Nalerigu seeking to have four people committed for contempt of court over the installation. In the application filed on October 14, 2026, the Nayiri accused the respondents of defying judicial processes by proceeding with the enskinment despite an ongoing legal dispute over the Bunkpurugu skin. The dispute between the Jamong and Jafouk royal families has contributed to persistent tensions in the area, with reports of farm destruction, arson and residents fleeing their homes amid fears of further violence.

title: Oman condemns church shooting in Jordan
body:
The Sultanate of Oman has strongly condemned the shooting at a church in Karak Governorate in the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan, which resulted in deaths and injuries. Oman reaffirms its firm rejection of all forms of violence, attacks on places of worship and acts that terrorise civilians. It also expresses its solidarity with Jordan, a statement from the Foreign Ministry said. Oman extended its condolences and sympathy to the families of the victims and to the Government and people of Jordan and wishes the injured a speedy recovery. At least seven people have been killed, and 34 others wounded, in an attack in Jordan’s Karak governorate that saw gunmen open fire during a funeral at a church. Director of Jordan’s Public Security Directorate Obaidullah Al-Maaytah told a press conference on Friday that seven people are confirmed dead after the assault on a Greek Orthodox Church in the village of Hamoud.

title: Arabian coalition shoots down Houthi ballistic missile over Riyadh
body:
DOHA, October 24. /TASS/. The Arabian coalition led by Saudi Arabia has destroyed a ballistic missile launched by the Houthis from the Yemeni rebel movement Ansar Allah in the direction of Riyadh, said the alliance’s official spokesman Turki al·Maliki.
"The air defense forces have intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile launched by Houthi terrorists in the direction of Riyadh," he wrote on X.
Saudi Arabia’s General Directorate of Civil Defense activated the National Early Warning Platform for Emergencies, notifying the Riyadh residents about a possible threat. Later it said on X that the alert had been lifted. "The danger to the city of Riyadh passed," the statement said.
AFP news agency reported two explosions in Riyadh amid the activation of air·threat warning systems.
An armed conflict in Yemen between government forces supported by the Arabian coalition and Houthi rebels has been ongoing since August 2014.
On October 19, military representative of the movement Yahya Saree said that Saudi Arabia had carried out a series of strikes, including on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, as well as on Saudi Aramco and military bases.

title: Martha Sazon, GCash’s newly Mynted billionaire
body: Martha Sazon stood on the trading floor of the Philippine Stock Exchange, huddled with her core leadership team, and took a selfie with no less than President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. It was a busy morning for Mynt’s top boss, who had overseen GCash’s spectacular rise into a fintech unicorn and was now ringing the bell on the biggest IPO in Philippine history . Now, her moment of reckoning. PUBLIC. Martha Sazon and Mynt’s leadership team pose for a photo with President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. at Mynt’s IPO ceremony on Tuesday, October 20. Photo from Sazon’s LinkedIn. With the toll of that bell, her considerable fortune has a public price tag. At Mynt’s P6.60 IPO price , her 220.1 million shares were worth a cool P1.45 billion. Sazon was also offering about 44 million of her shares for sale, potentially pocketing P290.55 million before taxes and fees, while keeping another 176.1 million shares worth P1.16 billion. Cheers to the newly Mynted billionaire. Of course, this moment didn’t magically make Mynt’s president and CEO rich. Those shares were valuable even before the initial public offering (IPO), when Mynt was still privately held . But an IPO is everybody’s favorite liquidity event, and Sazon — like GCash’s early private equity backers — turned some of that paper wealth into actual cash. Quite the reward for someone who wasn’t around when GCash started in 2004, back when it felt more like a fun party trick for Globe users to send money via SMS. Sazon’s journey to the top of fintech took more than a few turns. A University of the Philippines (UP) accountancy graduate, she started her career in banking, where the pay was good, but she had her eye on marketing. So much so that she willingly took a pay cut to move into sales, waking up early to learn the ropes from merchandisers and store personnel. “There is no shame in starting at the bottom,” she recalled in a 2023 graduation speech she delivered at the UP Virata School of Business. ALMA MATER. Sazon takes a selfie with the 2023 graduating class of the UP Virata School of Business. Photo from Sazon’s LinkedIn. From there came stints at Del Monte and GlaxoSmithKline, working across food, pharmaceuticals, and personal care, before she spent 12 years at Globe. She rose through the ranks managing its postpaid, small-business, and broadband operations. By the time then-Globe chief Ernest Cu tapped her to lead Mynt in 2020, she had a marketer’s understanding of Filipino consumers and a telco veteran’s discipline in delivering products to them fast. Fintech, however, is a different beast. Finance and technology weren’t exactly her specialties, and taking over a company in the middle of lockdowns — without even meeting much of the team in person — was hardly an inviting prospect. But the timing couldn’t have been better for GCash. With the pandemic raging, Filipinos suddenly needed ways to pay bills, move money, and shop without handling cash. Those who’ve complained about GCash’s demanding work culture might find Sazon’s talk of an “obsession” with solving customer problems and setting ever-higher targets painfully familiar. But the growth is hard to dispute. By June 2026, GCash had 41.5 million monthly active users. And the personal accolades have followed. Sazon made it into Forbes’ 2026 50 Over 50 Global list and Fortune’s Asia’s 100 Most Powerful Women , ranking 35th, up two spots from 2025 and the highest among Filipinas. Road ahead Now that Mynt has reached this milestone, where does Sazon take it next? “Becoming a public company is not the finish line,” she told the crowd at the PSE. title: Overseas Israelis mobilise for 'change' in election that could end Netanyahu era
body: Thousands of Israelis from overseas are flying into the country to vote for a “change” of government and end Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s time in office, voters have told The National . There has been a huge surge in overseas arrivals, with an estimated 67,000 Israelis living in the US and Europe having entered the country to vote in Tuesday’s election . This 25 per cent surge above the figures expected could well have a dramatic impact in a very tight election, with their numbers accounting for the equivalent of two seats in the 120-seat Knesset. “We may disagree on what needs to change but we all on the flight agreed that it needs to change and that 20 years of the current leadership has been ineffective and counterproductive,” said Ben, who had just flown in from Maryland, in the US. “You see so many people coming in from overseas, and you don't cross the world if you're happy with the current outcome. You're motivated because you are unhappy.” The American-Israeli, who did not want to give his last name, said he works in the travel sector and has been closely watching the numbers coming into Tel Aviv. “Passenger loads in the week leading up to the election are just astronomical – you would think it's tourist season and it's not. This is the off season.” The flight The National took from London to Tel Aviv on Thursday had a week earlier been just over half full, the seat bookings showed, but by take-off it was fully booked. While there were many orthodox Jews, the majority were secular Israelis, and it is understood this is causing deep concern in the Netanyahu camp. In part, that is because Israelis outside the country have been exposed to the widespread international unease at Israel’s actions in Gaza, where 74,000 people have been killed in the last three years. That followed the October 7 Hamas killings in which more than 1,200 Israelis died, many of them in the town of Sederot, where on Friday you could still hear gunfire. The distant ruins of Gaza, where there is supposed to be a ceasefire, are also visible. It is unclear what impact that major security lapse will have on Mr Netanyahu’s vote share but it is apparent that those flying in from abroad want a new approach. “These elections now are very critical, and it's really important that we change the government and make a change in Israel … especially after what happened in the last few years, since October 7,” said Shirley Segal, whose brother had just flown in from the US. She agreed that Mr Netanyahu had failed the country “big time” and that it was “very sad what happened in Gaza”. “But we need to find a way to live next to Gaza,” she added. Change is required, said her brother Danny Segal, because Israel needs “a different direction, a different understanding of what this country needs to look like in the next five, 10, 20 years”. He believes current policies threaten the idea of a Jewish homeland in Israel. “I don't know if we would be around for the next 10, 15, 20, or forever” on the current trajectory, he said. “We need it to be diverse and strong, and that's one of the reasons that I came to vote.” Israelis must learn to live with Palestinians because “we have to, there are no two ways about it”, he said. “We are surrounded by Arab countries, so we need to understand what they need. We need to coexist in this neighbourhood”. But Mr Segal, who will vote for the centre-right party of former prime minister Naftali Bennett, suggested that, given the October 7 attacks, “it will take a bit of time before we can see a Palestinian state”.

title: Joint Statement between Oman and the UK
body:
The United Kingdom and the Sultanate of Oman commit to strengthen and deepen our relationship, monitor progress against agreed priorities, and ensure that cooperation remains focused on mutual benefit, Oman’s Vision 2040, the UK’s growth agenda, and the shared goal of building a more secure, prosperous and resilient world. This was stated in the joint statement issued on the occasion of the state visit undertaken by His Majesty Sultan Haitham bin Tarik to the United Kingdom, the full text of which reads as follows: “During the State Visit of His Majesty Sultan Haitham bin Tarik, Sultan of Oman, to the United Kingdom as the guest of His Majesty The King on 20-22 October 2026, the United Kingdom and the Sultanate of Oman reaffirmed the enduring friendship between their two countries, reflected in the close relationship between His Majesty The King and His Majesty the Sultan, and agreed to build an ambitious, forward-looking partnership for the future. Priorities At 10 Downing Street on 21 October, the Prime Minister Andy Burnham and His Majesty Sultan Haitham bin Tarik welcomed the depth, warmth and longevity of the relationship between the United Kingdom and the Sultanate of Oman and agreed a set of priorities to shape cooperation in the years ahead. These priorities include modernising security, defence and national resilience cooperation; expanding trade and investment in green and advanced industries; working together on regional stability and global challenges; and strengthening ties between people and institutions. British Omani Society His Royal Highness the Prince of Wales and His Highness Sayyid Theyazin bin Haitham Al Said welcomed their roles in supporting the next generation of the relationship, including through joint patronage of the British Omani Society. Defense partnership The UK Defence Secretary and the Omani Deputy Prime Minister for Defence Affairs also reaffirmed their commitment to the enduring UK–Oman defence partnership and its continued modernisation. The UK Foreign Secretary and Foreign Minister of Oman continued their detailed discussions on bilateral affairs, covering matters of importance regionally and globally. UK-GCC Free Trade Agreement. The UK Minister of Trade also held discussions with the Omani Minister of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion to discuss all steps needed to ensure the highly anticipated signing of the UK-Gulf Cooperation Council Free Trade Agreement. The Omani Minister of Education also met with the CEO of the British Council to explore innovative approaches to integrating emerging technologies into education. UK-Oman partnership The UK-Oman partnership is rooted in historical friendship, sustained through resilience, and renewed through innovation. It is underpinned by the Comprehensive Agreement of Enduring Friendship and Bilateral Cooperation (2019) and the Joint Defence Agreement (2019), and delivered through the UK-Oman Ministerial Dialogue, Joint Defence Talks, and Strategic Advisory Group, among other bilateral fora. The United Kingdom and the Sultanate of Oman commit to strengthen and deepen our relationship, monitor progress against agreed priorities, and ensure that cooperation remains focused on mutual benefit, Oman’s Vision 2040, the UK’s growth agenda, and the shared goal of building a more secure, prosperous and resilient world. The United Kingdom and the Sultanate of Oman reaffirmed the central importance of their trusted defence partnership and their intent to deepen defence industrial cooperation, strengthen military-military cooperation, and increase focus on defence expertise, testing, innovation and future capability. The Saif Sareea exercise series remains a flagship expression of this relationship. Both countries welcomed preparations for Saif Sareea IV and agreed to explore the next phase of long-term exercise cooperation, including future capability development, testing and experimentation, and maritime security information exchange. Cybersecurity The United Kingdom and the Sultanate of Oman also agreed to deepen collaboration across security and national resilience and work more closely in several areas, including cyber security, to tackle shared international security challenges. The UK-Gulf Cooperation Council Free Trade Agreement will provide further opportunities to deepen trade and investment between the United Kingdom and Oman once signed and implemented. The UK-Oman Strategic Advisory Group will continue as the flagship dialogue for investment and growth, supporting knowledge exchange, structured innovation and delivery of shared economic objectives. The Sovereign Partnership for Cooperation and Promotion of Investment will provide a focal point for long-term economic cooperation, strengthen links between the UK’s Office for Investment and the Oman Investment Authority and advance cooperation on green growth, advanced technologies, critical minerals, space, innovation, scale-up finance, industrial clusters and regional connectivity. It will prioritise sectors within the UK’s Modern Industrial Strategy and Oman’s future-industries ecosystem, using Omani industrial zones and innovation clusters as platforms for UK expertise, while supporting Oman’s economic diversification and its role as a gateway for regional growth. Green industries Recognising green growth as a shared national priority, the United Kingdom and the Sultanate of Oman will advance cooperation on green industries and decarbonisation. UK Export Finance and the Oman Net Zero Centre also announced strengthened cooperation to support the sustainable, secure and responsible development of green and decarbonisation projects. The UK welcomed the proposed Oman Green Growth Roadshow delegation in 2027 to take these partnerships forward. Alongside this, UK Export Finance has increased its country limit for Oman by £1.6 billion, providing up to £7 billion of capacity to support UK exports to Oman. This will create greater capacity to support priority projects, deepen commercial ties and connect Omani opportunities with UK goods, services and expertise. Net Zero Industry Wales and the Oman Net Zero Centre will also launch a partnership to share knowledge and build links amongst industrial clusters, renewable energy sectors, academia and public bodies. Investment in AI, Data centres The United Kingdom and the Sultanate of Oman agreed to deepen cooperation in advanced technologies, including artificial intelligence, data centres, critical minerals and space, through targeted roundtables, delegations and technical exchanges. They welcomed an agreement between the UK Space Agency and the Oman National Space Programme to share best practice, explore future cooperation on space launch, and promote commercial partnerships. They also welcomed the UK-Oman Innovation Initiative, regional innovation links, Growth Hub and Growth Fund mechanisms to help UK and Omani businesses grow, scale and access each other’s markets. The United Kingdom and the Sultanate of Oman reaffirmed their shared commitment to peace, stability and dialogue in the Middle East and beyond, and agreed to strengthen cooperation on conflict prevention, peaceful resolution, humanitarian response and multilateral engagement. They reaffirmed their commitment to a two-state solution as the only viable basis for a just and lasting peace between Israel and Palestine. They also underscored the importance of adherence to international law, including the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, reaffirming in this context Oman’s sovereignty over Omani waters in the Strait of Hormuz and the importance of maintaining maritime security, freedom of navigation and the safe passage of international shipping in accordance with international law. To support this cooperation, they will develop joint work between His Majesty’s Diplomatic Service College and the Oman Diplomatic Academy. Net Zero The United Kingdom and the Sultanate of Oman reaffirmed their shared commitment to achieving Net Zero by 2050 and to demonstrating international leadership on climate, nature and environmental protection. Both countries recognised the importance of clean energy and resilient supply chains in supporting sustainable growth. The friendship between the United Kingdom and the Sultanate of Oman has been built over generations by the sailors, soldiers, scientists, students, diplomats and communities who have connected our two countries, creating a deep generational trust between our peoples. The United Kingdom and the Sultanate of Oman welcomed a package of announcements to build on this legacy and deepen links between their people and institutions for future generations, this includes closer cooperation on heritage, air connectivity and tourism, sport and the creative industries, and strengthen next generation and community links through the British Omani Society. Chevening Scholarship In education and skills, both sides welcomed the reopening of the Chevening Scholarship for the first time since 2021 as well as a British Council pilot on artificial intelligence assisted education in Omani schools, the new Oman Net Zero Centre-Cardiff University scholarships, and stronger links on skills and professional qualifications.”

title: Russia senator says Western sanctions may remain in place forever
body:
MOSCOW, October 24. /TASS/. Western countries may temporarily ease sanctions against Russia in their own interests, but they are unlikely to completely abandon them, Federation Council Vice Speaker Konstantin Kosachev said in an interview with TASS.
But Moscow should not worry, because it has proven its self-sufficiency.
"It can be assumed that we will live to see the moment when sanctions are lifted legally, but, in my view, their inclusion in US legislation and in the relevant directives of the European Union is, if not an eternal phenomenon, then at least an extremely long·term one, because lifting sanctions requires consensus — a convincing majority, in case of US Congress, or consensus, unanimity, in case of the European Union," the senator said.
According to Kosachev, temporary exceptions to the sanctions regime are possible thanks to the interests of the Western countries.
"My prediction is that the sanctions regime will be eased over time, because maintaining it at its current maximum level clearly runs counter to the interests of those who came up with and are using these sanctions," he explained.
However, the parliamentarian continued, the Westerners will certainly retain the ability to reinstate the sanctions at any time if "Russia behaves, in their view, in a way they do not like."
"I am convinced that this is not the issue we should be focusing on, because over these decades -- if we look at the period starting from 2008, when sanctions related to the Georgian issue first appeared -- we have proven that Russia cannot be isolated, that Russia cannot be broken even by the most severe sanctions, and that we are able to maintain our self·sufficiency and our ability to develop regardless of what is happening around us," the senator believes.
He added that the maintenance or lifting of anti-Russian sanctions in one form or another is "a headache for those who imposed these sanctions," not for Russia.
The White House is exempting Russian diesel fuel supplies to global markets from sanctions until April 7. On October 9, Russian President Vladimir Putin and US President Donald Trump discussed over the phone the supply of petroleum products. Later, the Russian president confirmed Moscow’s readiness to supply oil and oil products to the American and global markets. Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak previously told TASS that Russia is beginning to lift the ban on diesel fuel exports early and is ready to supply 100,000 tons of diesel in October, 500,000 tons in November, and 1 million tons in December, with the potential to increase this volume to 3 million tons per month.

title: Rubio received intel. warning of Iranian plots against US diplomats, official confirms to ‘Post’
body: A US official confirmed to The Jerusalem Post on Friday that US Secretary of State and National Security Adviser Marco Rubio received an intelligence memorandum warning that Iran has significantly increased its efforts to target American officials and citizens, with plots to carry out lethal attacks reaching advanced stages.The confirmation follows a report by Axios, which obtained the October 23 memorandum sent to Rubio by Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton, with a copy to CIA Director John Ratcliffe.According to the document, US intelligence agencies have received information through multiple channels indicating that Iran has substantially intensified its efforts to target American personnel.Scoop: U.S. intelligence finds Iran has "substantially increased" its efforts to target American diplomats & officials in the Middle East and beyond, with lethal plots reaching "advanced stages," per memo to Secretary of State Rubio. My story on @axios https://t.co/JpDxTvWdpT https://t.co/OHJRSIOnJd— Barak Ravid (@BarakRavid) October 24, 2026“The lethal plotting efforts by the Iranians against US citizens have reached advanced stages in both the Middle East and certain other countries,” Clayton wrote.The intelligence chief warned that information concerning Iranian plots to target American government personnel was relevant to a wider group of individuals than those currently authorized to receive it.Clayton said the underlying intelligence had already been shared with appropriately cleared senior members of Rubio's team and offered to provide the secretary with an additional briefing.He also pledged to make every effort to downgrade the classification of as much intelligence as possible, allowing Rubio to share the information more broadly with State Department personnel who could potentially be at risk.The memorandum, marked unclassified, did not identify specific targets, attack methods, or countries outside the Middle East where the alleged plots were being developed.US reduces diplomatic presence amid regional tensionsThe warning comes as the State Department moves to reduce its diplomatic presence across several Middle Eastern countries, amid concerns about Iranian retaliation and the possibility of renewed US military operations against Tehran.Earlier this week, Washington ordered nonessential government employees and family members to depart Saudi Arabia following an escalation in attacks by the Iranian-backed Houthis.According to Axios, additional reductions in US diplomatic personnel were ordered at embassies in the United Arab Emirates, Lebanon, Qatar, and Jordan.CNN also reported on Friday that the United States was accelerating the departure of diplomats and their families from several regional posts, with some personnel having only recently returned following evacuations earlier in the Iran war.The network further reported that Israel had pressed Washington to launch renewed strikes against Iran sooner, but those efforts had so far been unsuccessful.Washington weighing renewed military actionThe intelligence warning emerged as US President Donald Trump continued to leave open the possibility of additional military action against Iran.Speaking on Friday, Trump said the United States could launch another operation similar to Operation Epic Fury if Tehran failed to reach an agreement.“We may do another little Epic Fury. Or they'll agree,” Trump said.The latest warning underscores mounting US concerns about the security of American diplomatic personnel as Washington weighs further military action and continues diplomatic efforts to reach an agreement with Iran.

title: How Block Blast harvests its players for ad money
body:
Rules downloaded from their server decide your pieces, your score and your ads. One waits for an expensive ad, then asks for a hand you canât place.
I posted a video about this game that got over 15 million views, so I wanted to do the full technical write-up: the code, and how you can reproduce it yourself.
Some context on why it matters: between January and May 2026, Block Blast made an estimated $127 million from ads. Candy Crush Saga made $81.1 million over the same months (Sensor Tower estimates).
We started with the Android app, version 10.8.2. We decompiled the Java side with jadx and the native Cocos library with Ghidra, and found almost nothing interesting in the package you download from the store. Block Blast is built from small modules the code calls traits, and each trait has variants called arms. Running it on a clean Android 14 emulator with no account and watching its cache and logcat showed how it works: when the app launches, the server sends a config that says which arm of which trait you get, and the app downloads them as encrypted JavaScript. The config my install got names about 700 traits. My install selected 254 of them, and 101 were downloaded after install.
So two people playing side by side can be running different games, and the studio can change yours without an app update. Most of those 254 are ordinary: tutorials, animations, sounds. A handful are about when you lose. One of them is about ads.
Itâs called RewardHighValueAdHarvestTrait . By finding where the game unlocks these files in its own native library, we decoded it into 15,616 bytes of plain, minified JavaScript. Its constructor sets the parameters:
It waits for three things to line up: you finished your last three rewarded ads, the ad loaded right now is worth at least 3.5 times your last one, and youâre 1,000 points past your high score. All three get checked in one function. Here it is with the minified null checks rewritten as optional chaining; the logic is the same:
1. You finished your last three rewarded ads. Every time a rewarded ad starts, the rule pushes false onto a list and keeps the latest three (lines 174â183). If the ad SDK reports that the reward was earned, it flips that entry to true (191â199). The check needs all three to be exactly true :
That flag comes from AppLovin MAXâs onUserRewarded callback in the Java layer, so an ad you close early stays false .
2. The ad loaded right now is worth at least 3.5 times your last one. The rule reads the value of the best rewarded ad currently loaded with NativeAd.callNativeGetMaxEcpmNumber("2") (line 304). In the Java layer, that call goes through each ready rewarded ad slot, takes the revenue AppLovin MAX reports for it, multiplies it by 1,000, and returns the highest. The value of your last rewarded ad gets the same Ã1,000 (line 310), so the comparison is like for like:
3. Youâre past your old high score. At the start of each game the rule saves your high score (line 145). The bar is that high score plus scoreDeltaStep (lines 107â110). Each player gets one arm: mine, 332243014 , uses 1,000, and the appâs bundled config has others at 500 and 750. If you revive after the rule fires, the bar moves up another step, so it can fire again in the same game.
Then it asks for the lethal puzzle. Before dealing your next set, the game runs a list of âbottom offerâ rules in order. When this one qualifies, it replaces the list with a single generator:
deathAlgorithm returns hs.OFFER_TYPE.ZHI_SI_TI (line 102). The game sends that request to its puzzle engine and deals the three piece IDs it gets back (main script lines 45062â45121 and 15074â15123). If the engine fails to find a set, the rule resets and tries again on the next deal.
To watch it decide, we ran the downloaded file itself, unmodified, with test ad and score values. It requests the lethal puzzle exactly when all three conditions hold: 28 cases, including two ads instead of three, one ad closed early, a score 1 point short, and an ad worth just under 3.5Ã.
Then we ran it live, in a test copy of the iPhone app running in Appleâs simulator, and read the ruleâs inputs while we played. It had three good rewarded ads on record. The score was past the line. A rewarded ad from Google AdMob was loaded and ready. The rule priced it at 72.39, against 37.41 for the last one, which is 1.94 times. It needs 3.5. So on iPhone the rule is live, reading real ad prices, and waiting for an ad worth 3.5 times your last one.
The name maps through three tables in the main script:
Algorithm 24001 exists twice: in JavaScript, and in the gameâs native C++ library, where the function is called func_death_blcok (their spelling). They do the same search. Hereâs the JavaScript core:
It looks for two pieces that fit now and one that doesnât, and keeps the set only if no order and no set of positions places all three, counting every line youâd clear along the way. Two of the three fit when theyâre dealt, so the hand doesnât look impossible until you try it.
Hereâs what that looks like, with the gameâs own code running in your browser. Step through it:
Press âNew random boardâ for a fresh mid-game board, and the gameâs code picks a new hand for it. On the test board in the evidence bundle, the gameâs generator accepts a vertical domino, a horizontal domino and a 3Ã3 square as a lethal hand: we tried all 171 placements, and none of them finish it. On an empty board, those same three pieces fit 67,680 ways in each order.
The lethal puzzle is a generator, and any rule can ask for it. The ad rule is one caller. While we were testing it live on iPhone, a second caller fired on camera: PersonalMarginBreakTrait . Once youâre 10% past your high score, it rolls on every deal, and 20% of the time it asks for the same lethal puzzle:
Our record was 1,304, so its line was 1,434. At 3,356 points it rolled, and the game dealt a five-long bar, a five-tall bar and a zigzag. The gameâs own record of that deal names this rule as the caller, shows algorithm 9 both requested and used, and labels all three pieces è´æ­»é¢, lethal puzzle. There was no way to place them. Two separate exhaustive searches agree: zero. The rule, the live settings and the deal are in the live iPhone bundle .
The rules so far are hand-written. The game also downloads trained models and runs them on your phone, and one of them decides where in a level the lethal puzzle shows up.
Itâs a 500-tree XGBoost classifier for the gameâs level mode, which the code calls Chapter. Its file is named predict_travel_difficulty_dead , and its 52 inputs are mostly about how youâve been doing: your current level, how many times youâve tried it, how many games youâve finished this week, and how long youâve had the app. The game feeds it 12 options, four values of a setting called sw_process times three difficulty levels, and keeps whichever one the model scores highest:
Another rule turns that pick into a stretch of the level: the first 30%, 30 to 80%, or the last 20%. When you reach that stretch, it offers you an extra revive if you usually take them (more than 75% of the time). Then, from the fourth deal after that, it asks for the lethal puzzle:
Other rules read the same pick the opposite way and make a level easier when it lands on the fourth option.
A second model puts a price on you. The game downloads xgboost_regression_model111.json from its server and runs it on your phone.
Itâs an XGBoost regression model: 59 decision trees, up to 8 levels deep, 27 inputs. Most of it is about money: 18 of the inputs are about the ads the game has loaded for you, today and yesterday. The rest are where you are, your phone, when you installed, and how your first game went. The trees lean hardest on your first score, the price of your latest ad, your RAM, your phone model and your country.
The code calls its answer finalEcpm . eCPM is the ad industryâs name for what a thousand ads are worth, and itâs the same unit the game stores its ad prices in. So the model is estimating what youâre worth in ads.
GPT-6 Astra ported the gameâs input code and tree walk, and the port reproduces the gameâs own outputs to the last decimal. We ran it on a made-up new player in the US with a first score of 1,000, once on an iPhone 15 installed from the App Store and once on Android, then changed one input at a time:
Moving the same player from the US to Brazil cuts their value to about a third, and India cuts it further. Your first game matters too, but not in a straight line: on iPhone, a first score of 500 makes you worth more than 2,000 or 10,000.
The game uses prices like this to decide what kind of ads you get, and how many. The clearest case asks its server for two prices for you, one for full-screen ads and one for rewarded ads, and compares them:
In the versions the app ships, if your rewarded ads are worth at least twice your full-screen ads (1.5 or 2.5 times in other versions), you get an extra chance to revive, and a revive plays a rewarded ad. If full-screen ads pay more for you, you donât.
Other rules work the same way. FullScreenAdAddByEcpmTrait adds an extra full-screen ad when your price is high. IsOpenEcpmTooLowNoInterTrait skips full-screen ads when youâre worth almost nothing. A few more open an early or a third revive when your rewarded ads are worth enough.
Sorted by how many of the modelâs splits use each one.
Hereâs the part of the game that walks the trees. Itâs a plain loop: start at the root, go left or right on each input, add up the leaf weights.
Thereâs also a 1,000-tree LightGBM model with 93 inputs that predicts whether youâll be less active tomorrow. It leans hardest on how long youâve had the app, your high score, your RAM and your average score. If it scores you at 0.69 or above, a companion rule swaps in a pink revive button, and the revive skips the ad:
Some rules send your data out and act on the score that comes back, from server models with names like churn, LTV, revive-click and xDeepFM. Their weights stay on the server, so all we can show is what the phone sends. One of those requests, to /v1/ecpm_prediction , sends 40 fields, including your carrier, storage, the hour and stats on your recent ad prices.
The ad rule isnât the only one that changes your pieces or your score. We caught one working live on iPhone. MaturityDevelopmentV2Trait gives each session a âmaturityâ score made of three parts: habit (10.98), skill (14.66) and your ad history (19.27). Ours added up to 44.91, under its line of 65, so it swapped some of the hard puzzles it would have dealt for easy fills. Another, FailStreakStrategyTrait , stepped in after two games below our record and asked for easier pieces.
These came up while tracing the ad rule on Android, and each has the same kind of evidence in my research files.
Yes. We took apart Block Blast for iPhone too, version 7.4.9, and a second GPT-6 Astra run checked those findings from scratch. It downloads the same rule from its own update server, and the file matches the Android one except for one line. Everything else is identical: three ads, 3.5Ã, the score bar, and the same lethal-puzzle generator.
The iPhone app also lists a second version of the rule, RewardHighValueAdHarvestV2Trait , and in that one the ad-history check can be switched off:
The app ships 12 versions of it. Half turn that check off, and they need anywhere from 1 to 3 ads, so in some of them a single rewarded ad you closed early is enough. The price bar depends on how long youâve had the app: 3.2Ã the first ad loaded that session in your first week, 2.7Ã through day 30, and 3Ã your last ad after that.
This rule is saved on your phone after it downloads, so it still runs offline. But it only fires when a rewarded ad is loaded, and ads load over the internet, so once nothing is loaded it canât fire. Other rules keep going. On my Android install, the one that asks for hard pieces when youâre playing fast near your record runs entirely on your phone. The one that asks the server which players âdonât mind being forced to dieâ canât get an answer offline, so it stays off for that session.
It depends on the blocker. Browser ad blockers, on iPhone or Android, only work inside the browser, so they donât touch the game. A blocker that covers your whole phone, like Private DNS on Android or a DNS or VPN-based blocker on either, can stop rewarded ads from loading, and then this rule canât fire, for the same reason as playing offline. The rules that donât use ads keep running: the fast-play one, the experiment that times when the lethal puzzle can be requested, and, since youâre still online, the one that asks the server about you.
Thatâs exactly where these rules are aimed. We caught PersonalMarginBreakTrait doing it live: once youâre 10% past your record, every deal has a 20% chance of being the lethal puzzle. The ad rule waits for 1,000 points past your record (500 or 750 in other versions), and after a revive it moves the bar up and can fire again.
Not really. On Android, the original rule needs your last three rewarded ads to pay out, so closing one early does turn it off until youâve had three good ones in a row again. But on iPhone, the V2 versions can skip that check completely and fire after a single ad, even one you closed. And the other rules that ask for the lethal puzzle, like the timing experiment and the one that waits for a big clear, donât look at your ads at all. The one thing that stops this rule everywhere is not having a rewarded ad loaded, which is what happens offline or with a phone-wide ad blocker.
Adaptive difficulty changes the pieces based on how youâre playing. This rule doesnât look at how well youâre placing pieces. Its inputs are your recent ad results, the price of the ad sitting in memory, and your score relative to your record. And the generator it asks for isnât a harder set of pieces. Itâs a set chosen because no way of placing it works.
Apple reviews the app you download from the store, and this rule isnât in it. The app downloads it from the gameâs server after you install, and the server decides which players get which version. Apple does let apps download JavaScript updates like this, which is how tools like Expo Updates work, as long as the update doesnât change what the app is. Whether changing your pieces based on ad prices fits that is up to Apple.
The server does decide who gets the rule and which version. But the decision itself needs things only your phone knows in that moment: your board, the next set itâs about to deal, and the ad thatâs loaded right now. So that part runs on the phone, which is also why it could be taken apart.
There are three evidence bundles: Android (113 KB, SHA-256 bd55151e6a1527f628459c2fffa115d5b14a765a3fb5a3f729387fbac6f707c8 ) and iOS (2.7 MB, SHA-256 02bdb0e0e9b02d77844efbcf4b82f48e17f2b688fc48cbf84f83e75ae289df7d ), plus a third for the live iPhone catch (270 KB, SHA-256 5f36863daabd2b500c8062d005f41e6c5e7dcea5a238c89e558e19a928dcc57f ). They have the decoded rules, the encrypted originals, excerpts from the rest of each app with their original line numbers, the test scripts and the provenance records. You need Node.js and Python 3.
The key and the steps for getting past the appsâ protection arenât in the bundles. If youâre a journalist or researcher and want to verify the decoding step, email me .
I write up every breakdown in full, with the actual code. Put your email in and Iâll send you the next one.
Iâm Ayo, a data scientist and app developer. I post these breakdowns as videos on Instagram . If you find a mistake, email me and Iâll correct it here with a note.
Block Blast Android 10.8.2 (build 10820) and iOS 7.4.9 (build 7491). Ad revenue: Sensor Tower estimates via GameDev Reports and WN Hub . AppLovin on reported revenue precision: MAX advanced settings .
Original investigation by Ayo Omolewa (@ayoships), first published at https://ayoships.com/breakdowns/block-blast on October 15, 2026. Anyone quoting, summarizing or building on this work must credit Ayo Omolewa and link to the original.

title: Ghana needs 759 million cedis to implement 2025-29 health sector supply chain master plan
body: More than 759 million cedis — that is how much Ghana needs to fix critical gaps in the supply of medicines and essential medical supplies across the country’s health facilities over the next four years. But with some foreign aid to the health sector being withdrawn, the government is turning to domestic resources to fund the plan and keep Ghana’s universal health coverage target for 2030 within reach. At the launch of the 2025-2029 health sector supply chain master plan, stakeholder say effective funding, improved financial management and the recovery of outstanding debts owed under the National Health Insurance Scheme will be crucial to ensuring that health facilities, particularly those serving women and children, have the essential commodities they need to save lives. The master plan is a revised version of the 2021 – 2025 plan which was partially implemented due to the COVID-19 outbreaks with 35% of the overall targets achieved. The old plan revealed significant gaps in the planning, governance, workforce and operation sectors for the effective rollout of health The new plan is aimed at ensuring the completion of critical tasks while enhancing supply chain adaptability and responsiveness to emerging challenged. The master plan encompasses forty-seven (47) strategic interventions, each linked to the annual performance targets across the second (II) technical areas. The plan seeks to ensure availability, timely-access, affordability of high-quality health commodities across public and private sectors to successfully deliver universal health coverage ensuring Ghanaians have access to high-quality health care services. Targets by 2029 The masterplan seeks to build an integrated central and regional medical stores distribution on time and in full for all service delivery points while tracking cost components. It will also develop a well-coordinated financial system that supports the public health system. The implementation of the masterplan will include a mapping exercise to understand the flow of money and tracking of expenditures at each level. Speaking at the launch of the masterplan in Kumasi, Director for Procurement and Supply Chain at the Ministry of Health, Dr. Edward Bright Agyekum, noted that the government remains focused on generating revenue locally for the masterplan’s implementation. This comes amidst withdrawal of some foreign aid to the health sector, but Dr. Agyekum says strategies are in place to mobilize resources locally to achieve key priorities set out under the plan. “The supply chain master plan will be implemented with local funds. We are using whatever we have to generate. Whatever we are going to do to ensure it’s a local funding, we are mobilizing the scarce resources, the government is pushing for it. We are doing, we are mindful that come what may, the donors will withdraw. We are raising local funding to support implementation,” he said. Owning the SCMP implementation Technical Director with the Global Health Supply Chain, Daniel Oswald Owusu Afranie says the country make be deliberate in owning the masterplan for a universal health coverage by 2030. “The development partners have supported in putting this together. But its implementation is something government must take over and plan towards that. Resource mobilizing is very key,” he said. He noted that the government must devise ways to recoup all debts incurred under the health insurance scheme to complement revenue mobilization for the implementation. He acknowledged that these huge arrears affect the operations of the medical supply stores in procuring and distributing health commodities to health facilities. “How does the NHIS come in. Because in terms of health financing which the NHIA is already doing. We have to look at what role they will be playing in the implementation of the supply chain masterplan. There must be practical measures to ensure those debts are collected so that the regional medical stores will be able to function as business entities,” he added. Focus on Women and Children Women and children are among the most vulnerable groups in Ghana’s healthcare system, with access to essential medicines, vaccines and other medical supplies playing a critical role in their survival and well-being. Supply and Procurement Manager at UNICEF, Honorine Niyomana, stressed that the plan must deliberately and strategically focus on women and children. Ms. Niyomana says inadequate supplies could hinder mother and children from accessing equitable care. “Ghana has made important progress in improving health for women and children. But progress can be lost quickly when the commodities run out. A stock out of a single essential medicine can send a mother or caregiver home without care or force a family to travel far or pay off out of pocket,” she said.

title: Apple Security Research Device
body:
iPhone is the world's most secure consumer mobile device, which can make it challenging for even skilled security researchers to get started. We created the Apple Security Research Device Program to help new and experienced researchers accelerate their work with iOS.
This yearâs application period ended October 30, 2026. If you submitted an application, youâll hear from us soon.
The Security Research Device (SRD) is a specially fused iPhone that allows you to perform iOS security research without having to bypass its security features. You also benefit from access to software previews, security beta projects, the SRD research community, and special tooling to augment research and vulnerability discovery. Shell access is available, and you can run any tools, choose your own entitlements, and even customize the kernel. All iOS and iPhone components are eligible for SRD Program research, except Apple Pay and third-party apps. Using the SRD allows you to confidently report all your findings to Apple without the risk of losing access to the inner layers of iOS security. Plus, any vulnerabilities that you discover with the SRD are automatically considered for Apple Security Bounty â including bonus awards for preview and beta software programs.
The SRD is intended for use in a controlled setting for security research only. If your application is approved, we will provide you an SRD as a 12-month renewable loan. During this time, the device remains the property of Apple.
The SRD isn't meant for personal use or daily carry, and must remain on the premises of program participants at all times. Access to and use of the SRD must be limited to people authorized by Apple.
If you use the SRD to find, test, validate, verify, or confirm a vulnerability, you must promptly report it to us and, if the bug is in third-party code, to the appropriate third party.
Our ultimate goal is to protect users, so if you find a vulnerability without using the SRD for any aspect of your work, we'd still like to receive your report. We review all research submitted to us and consider all eligible reports for rewards through Apple Security Bounty .
Participation in the Security Research Device Program is subject to review of your application.
A limited number of Apple Security Research Devices are available each year. Applications are now closed.
* This program is available in: Argentina, Armenia, Australia, Austria, Azerbaijan, Belgium, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Brazil, Bulgaria, Canada, Croatia, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Georgia, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Iceland, India, Ireland, Italy, Japan, Latvia, Liechtenstein, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Moldova, Montenegro, Morocco, Netherlands, New Zealand, North Macedonia, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Senegal, Serbia, Singapore, Slovakia, Slovenia, South Africa, South Korea, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, United Kingdom (UK), United States.
This program is not available in any U.S. embargoed countries or regions, or to those on the U.S. Department of Treasury's Specially Designated Nationals List, on the U.S. Department of Commerce's Denied Persons List or Entity List, or on any other restricted party lists.

title: Zelensky 'maybe not such a big humanitarian as Putin,' he quips as Ukraine's relations with Trump unravel
body:
President Volodymyr Zelensky discussed his reaction to Washington's shifting allegiance in an interview with ABC News published Oct. 23.
While he maintained a calm and measured tone, avoiding getting into personal territory regarding his relationship with U.S. President Donald Trump , he did say the administration's recent actions were "not supportive" and acknowledged his frustrations.
"I'm a normal person. I'm just human. Maybe not such a big humanitarian as Putin, of course," Zelensky told ABC News.
Zelensky's remarks reference U.S. Special Envoy Steve Witkoff's recent praise of Russian President Vladimir Putin. Following Moscow's release of an American prisoner on Oct. 21, Witkoff hailed Putin as "a humanitarian."
Hours later, Russia bombarded Kyiv's city center with ballistic missiles and cluster munitions , killing two people and injuring dozens, including children.
Zelensky didn't dwell on Witkoff's admiration of Putin, instead focusing on Ukraine's urgent military needs: namely, restored Starlink service and prompt deliveries of air defense missiles . The president confirmed that Starlink is still not working at full speed on the Ukrainian battlefield, despite claims by Trump to the contrary.
Ukraine has also received only 24 air defense missiles from its strategic partners over the last 90 days, Zelensky said.
"We are not crying and not screaming, but this is very important," he said. "I'm just trying to say that each missile is important."
While the U.S. has denied responsibility for restrictions to Ukraine's Starlink speeds and delays in Patriot shipments, Ukraine has received no explanation — and no solution. Moreover, the incidents follow a series of pro-Kremlin policy moves from the Trump administration.
These include a deal to purchase Russian diesel , a new sanctions waiver , and pressure on Kyiv to halt attacks on Russian oil refineries .
Zelensky said on Oct. 23 that trilateral peace talks among Ukraine, Russia, and the U.S. will resume in November, with technical teams from each government meeting in Abu Dhabi.
The president told ABC News that Ukraine is still prepared to end the war by freezing the current battle lines.
"We are ready to stop this war as quick as possible," he said.

title: Ukraine lost about $6 billion from port downtime in last three months
body:
MOSCOW, October 24. /TASS/. The loss of Ukraine’s foreign exchange earnings from the downtime of the ports of Greater Odessa, which has been going on for more than three months, amounted to about $6 billion, according to TASS calculations.
Commercial merchant ships continue to boycott the ports of Odessa, Chernomorsk, and Yuzhnoye; only vessels associated with the Ukrainian army enter them. Maritime trade is conducted through the Danube ports — Ukraine’s Izmail and Romania’s Constan·a, which together can potentially account for no more than a third of the exports that previously passed through the ports of Greater Odessa.
As a result, in September, Ukraine was able to export only 44% of the agricultural products planned for exports that month. Exports of metallurgical products ceased completely by the end of September. Together, these items accounted for about 65% of Ukraine’s exports and about $26 billion in foreign exchange earnings per year.
By using the railway network and the Danube ports for exports, Ukraine managed to partially reduce losses, but only slightly -- from about $70 million per day in August to about $60 million in September-October.
The idle time of Greater Odessa has been ongoing since July 22.

title: White House lifts tariffs on some Canadian goods as midterm elections loom
body: The Trump administration is lifting some of its 50% tariffs on Canadian goods two weeks before the midterm elections, after a Republican candidate in a key Senate race said she had lobbied for the change. Starting on 30 October, tariffs will be eased on products including “plywood sheets, some paper products, certain machinery and refrigeration equipment,” the White House said on Friday. Republican Senator Susan Collins, who is in a tight race to keep her seat in Maine, first announced the exemptions, saying they would help her state’s agriculture industry. The US imposed a 50% levy on $20bn (£15bn) of Canadian goods after trade talks between the two countries collapsed in August. Maine Senator Susan Collins is seeking to keep her seat in November’s midterm elections Canada has imposed a series of countermeasures against US tariffs, which Prime Minister Mark Carney said were “necessary to protect our workers”. Last month, Carney matched the US tariffs “dollar for dollar” after the breakdown in talks. Trump had imposed them for what he called “unequal treatment” of US cars, dairy and alcohol. The White House said while tariffs would be lifted from some items, including some packing crates and boxes, they would be introduced on other items such as carpets and “waste products”. It said the action reflected President Trump’s “continued efforts to defend American workers and ensure fair trade”. “President Trump continues to address Canada’s discriminatory treatment of US commerce,” White House spokesman Matthew Middleton said. In a statement to the BBC, Canada’s internal trade minister Dominic LeBlanc said: “While we assess these latest steps, Canada stands ready to work constructively and in good faith towards a more mutually beneficial trading relationship that respects Canada’s interests.” The White House’s announcement comes less than a fortnight before the US midterm elections, which will determine whether Trump’s Republican Party or Democrats will control Congress, impacting the remaining two years of his term. Collins said she had repeatedly asked senior Trump officials for tariff relief and that she would “continue working directly with administration officials to seek additional relief and encourage a broader trade agreement with Canada, our neighbour, ally, and largest trading partner”. She wrote on X that the tariff exemptions were on products that were “crucial to Maine’s agricultural industries, including blueberry, potato, apple, and seaweed producers”. Collins’ Democratic challenger, Troy Jackson, responded: “Trump’s trade wars have made life harder and more expensive for Mainers. Susan Collins enabled this chaos, voted to confirm the people behind it, and now wants credit for bringing a cup of water to put out the fire.” Maine borders the Canadian provinces New Brunswick and Quebec. Its economy, as well as that of other border states, is deeply linked to Canada and they have felt the effects of the months-long trade war. Michigan lawmaker Mike Rogers, also a Republican, has called on Trump to end the standoff after spending months supporting the policy in recent advertisements airing in his trade-reliant state. Also on Friday, President Donald Trump said Canada was “working very hard” on a ⁠trade ​deal with the US. Carney, for his part, said that Canada was open to a mutually beneficial deal, but is willing to wait it out. “We could sign it this afternoon if the US were there. If it has to be months from now or longer than that, or another administration, before a proper deal comes into place, we will do that,” he said on Friday, according to Canadian broadcaster CBC. LeBlanc confirmed on Thursday that a delegation met with members of the Canada-United States Economic Relations Advisory Committee – the ninth meeting since April 2026. The committee members discussed the ongoing impact of US tariffs in Canada.

title: Russia, India to rise trade turnover to $100 bln by 2030 — ambassador to Moscow
body:
MOSCOW, October 24. /TASS/. Russia and India plan to increase their trade turnover to $100 billion by 2030, Indian ambassador to Russia Vinay Kumar said in an interview with TASS after the second Russian·Indian business forum Time.
He said that the two states continue to pursue the course of deepening relations, striving to push the trade volume to $100 billion and mutual investment to $50 billion by 2030.
Earlier, Manpreet Singh, President of the Indian Chamber of International Business, told TASS at the II Russian·Indian Time forum that trade turnover between Russia and India could reach $500 billion within the next three years if an agreement on free trade between India and the Eurasian Economic Union is signed.
The II Russian·Indian business forum Time was held in Kazan from October 15 to 16. The event was aimed at developing Russian·Indian trade and economic cooperation. During the forum, the participants discussed ways to implement joint initiatives, promising investment projects, and opportunities for technological and economic cooperation. TASS is the forum’s information partner.

title: Britt McHenry resigns from State Department after basketball game altercation
body:
The former ESPN reporter was appointed as a press adviser last month.
Former ESPN reporter Britt McHenry resigned Friday from her position as a State Department press adviser following an altercation at a basketball game this week, ABC News has learned.
McHenry was captured on camera appearing to throw a drink on someone during a Washington Wizards vs. Milwaukee Bucks NBA game on Wednesday.
Video obtained by TMZ appears to show McHenry being escorted from the stands at Capital One Arena following the incident.
McHenry was appointed to her role at the State Department last month. A Department official declined to comment on McHenry’s exit, saying it was an internal personnel matter.
ABC News was not immediately able to contact McHenry.
McHenry formerly worked as a reporter for ESPN. In 2015, she was suspended by the network for one week after a video showing her berating a clerk at a towing company went viral.
Her departure from the State Department was first reported by Page Six.
24/7 coverage of breaking news and live events

title: Hero dad who took down school shooter speaks out: 'I was supposed to be there'
body:
Kaylub Giamanco killed the gunman in the Bend elementary school shooting.
The father of two who took down a gunman in an Oregon school shooting last week is speaking out for the first time about how he ended the deadly rampage.
Kaylub Giamanco recounted to Oregon Public Broadcasting in an interview published Friday how he crawled through the shattered front doors of Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, swung open the door to a classroom and saw a teacher struggling with the gunman.
"I can tell you that I genuinely feel like I was supposed to be there," Giamanco, whose two daughters attend the school, told OPB.
Giamanco, a carpenter and lifelong Bend resident, said he was driving home on Oct. 15 when he saw a person in all black, armed with a gun, jump over the fence at the elementary school.
"That's when panic fled into my brain," he told OPB. "That's when I opened my center console and I just said, 'No, no, no, no, no,' and I grabbed my gun."
After shooting through the front doors of the school, the gunman entered a special needs classroom and opened fire, police said.
"I started hearing children pleading for their lives, and then I started hearing gunfire," Giamanco told OPB.
The dad said he crawled on his hands and knees toward the classroom.
"I swung the door out and open and I stepped in and I fired," Giamanco told OPB. "He was scrambling for his weapon, and I looked at him and I shot him two more times."
The shooter was killed, police said. Three students and a teacher were fatally shot by the gunman, according to police. Another student and teacher were also injured in the shooting.
Police lauded Giamanco as a hero, saying he "undoubtedly saved people" that day.
Giamanco grew emotional talking about the lives he could not save.
"I want to apologize for not saving their babies," he told OPB. "That's probably the biggest thing for me right now, because the gratitude for saving people's children is awesome. But there was ones that I didn't save."
The family of one of the victims killed in the shooting, 25-year-old Megan Lambert, have said they are grateful for Giamanco and called him a hero, saying in a statement, "You selflessly put yourself at risk for others."
Giamanco commended the teacher who police said tackled the shooter to the floor and tried to take the gun away from him, saying she allowed him the chance to act without getting hurt himself.
"I would love to give her a hug because that's a real true hero," he told OPB.
24/7 coverage of breaking news and live events

title: Carrick refuses to rule out dropping Fernandes in emotional address
body: Under-pressure Manchester United boss Michael Carrick delivered a passionate and emotional address lasting five minutes and 30 seconds as he battles to save his job. And he refused to rule out dropping skipper Bruno Fernandes for Sunday’s Premier League meeting with Bournemouth at Old Trafford. Instead of taking his seat and answering questions as normal in Friday’s scheduled pre-match media conference at Carrington, Carrick said he wanted to start himself. It was a strategy former boss Sir Alex Ferguson used, although the legendary Scot rarely spoke at such length. After a run of seven games without a win, culminating in Wednesday’s shocking 4-1 Champions League defeat by Como, and attacks on the club’s hierarchy by defender Lisandro Martinez and then Fernandes’ condemnation of his own tactics in Italy, Carrick wanted to reaffirm his view of what United stood for. “Recently we haven’t had a good time, I think that’s pretty obvious,” he said. “Wednesday was a bad night, and it hurt me to see us play like that. It was unacceptable. “My responsibility is to get a team on the pitch that represents this football club, and the supporters, and they can be proud of in the identity we show. We have gone away from that recently. It’s important we all recognise that. “The foundation and values of this football club have been etched for many years. I totally understand and get every single one of them. “There’s a resilience about this football club that runs very deep. I’ve seen it with my own eyes, I’ve felt it, I’m know some of the individuals closely who have been a big part of that history. “Entitlement cannot be at this football club. “It was based on being humble, having humility, and hard work.
