We can never lose that, and I won’t let us lose that.” Asked about Fernandes and whether he has considered dropping him, a defiant Carrick added: “The most important thing for me is the team, the squad and dynamics in the squad. “It’s about the football club. I’ll always do what is best for the football club.” No guarantees for Fernandes Image caption,Manchester United won 12 of their 17 games under Michael Carrick last season Club sources said on Thursday Fernandes would not have the captaincy taken away or be fined for his post-match observations following the Como defeat. In a further interview on Wednesday night with Sky Italia, the Portugal international referred to Manchester United’s storied history. “At this club, there’s too much focus on what’s been done in the past,” said Fernandes. “But we’re not those people anymore. The club and the players need to understand that. “Unfortunately for us – especially when it comes to the players – those who join expect to win trophies, win games, and reach the highest level, that’s been very difficult at this club in recent years.” Whether Carrick was aware of Fernandes’ comments about United’s history before he spoke was uncertain. When asked again if he would take the captaincy away from the 32-year-old midfielder, Carrick repeated: “I will always do what is best for the football club.” He then refused to say whether he had spoken to Fernandes about his conduct, adding: “I don’t think this is the time to go into too much detail.” Despite the challenge to his authority, Carrick said the United dressing room was not divided. “No, it’s not,” he added. “We just need to get back to doing what we do best.” Carrick also said the club were ‘doing everything’ to support Fernandes and his family, whose Cheshire home was burgled on Wednesday. “Thankfully they weren’t directly affected even though it is an awful situation.” ‘Hurt’ fuels motivation and inspiration Carrick named legendary United figures such as Ryan Giggs, Wayne Rooney and Ferguson as examples of the humility, sacrifice and hard work expected of United players. That was at odds with his post-match criticism on Wednesday, when he said if you don’t run forward or back properly, you will not win games. Asked how he would persuade his current squad to adhere to the values expected and he demanded, Carrick added: “It’s clear as day. “I’m not telling you anything new. I haven’t invented that. That’s the make-up of any good football team. You have to earn the right to be better than your opponent. That never changes. “What we look like as a group is my responsibility. That’s the privileged position I am in. I’ll hold that umbrella for me to get wet and everyone else to stay dry. “[Wednesday] hurts an awful lot, but that doesn’t stop me. That hurt is used as pure motivation and inspiration to want more, expect more and get us going in a different direction.”

title: ‘Interceptors Still Not Coming’ – Zelensky Says US Has Yet to Authorize Patriot Deliveries
body:
President Volodymyr Zelensky warned Friday, Oct. 23, that promised interceptor missiles needed to defend Ukraine against Russian ballistic attacks have still not arrived, leaving the country facing critical air defense shortages as Moscow continues its near-daily strikes.
Speaking during an online address to Washington’s Hudson Institute, Zelensky said Washington had yet to authorize deliveries of previously agreed Patriot interceptors, leaving Ukraine waiting for critical air defense missiles.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
“We are waiting for interceptors that we have already agreed on, but they are still not coming,” Zelensky said.
He expressed hope that the missiles were on their way but warned that the delay was a serious problem as Russian forces continued launching attacks on Ukraine almost every day.
Zelensky identified interceptor missiles for US-made Patriot air defense systems and energy supplies as Ukraine’s two most pressing winter requirements.
“We speak with different countries – Asia, the Middle East, and our European partners. Of course, we count on the American package,” Zelensky said during the Hudson Institute discussion.
Zelensky said Ukraine continues to defend its positions despite delayed military assistance and lingering Starlink and Starshield restrictions, even after reports that services had been restored.
“The speed limits on Starlink and Starshield are still there. The speed has not been restored,” he said.
He acknowledged that the restrictions had complicated military operations but stressed that Ukrainian forces continued to hold their positions.
“We are doing our best to keep our logistics working, and we continue defending ourselves,” Zelensky said.
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

title: Trump promises quick drop in oil prices
body:
WASHINGTON, October 24. /TASS/. US President Donald Trump expects the oil prices to sag soon.
"Oil prices will soon plummet, prices are coming down very substantially," he told a Republican rally in Florida ahead of the midterm Congressional elections.
Trump added that after the start of the US operation in Iran prices rose to record levels, but now the market is improving noticeably.

title: Ebola: FG Tightens Surveillance, Screening, Infected Woman Identified as Swiss Diplomat’s Wife
body: * Kenya Reports Second Death from the disease * WHO says source of infection remains unknown, calls for regional vigilance * Nigeria’s NCDC begins genomic sequencing *Edo sets up emergency response committee Onyebuchi Ezigbo in Abuja, Ayodeji Ake in Lagos and Felix Omoh-Asun in Benin City, with agency reports The federal government yesterday tightened Ebola control measures across Nigeria, directing ministries, departments and agencies (MDAs), public health institutions and other stakeholders to strictly enforce screening, surveillance and other approved entry protocols as Switzerland confirmed that the woman who tested positive for the virus in Nigeria was the wife of a Swiss diplomat. The directive by the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare followed concerns raised by the Office of the National Security Adviser (ONSA) over reported breaches of government-approved Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) entry protocols at Nigeria’s designated points of entry. The ministry’s directive was contained in circular PS/FMOH/08/VIII/48, dated October 22, 2026, and signed by the Permanent Secretary, Daju Kachollum S., on behalf of the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Prof. Muhammad Ali Pate. This comes as Kenya’s Health Ministry yesterday announced a second Ebola death, adding that the 65-year-old woman had developed symptoms during quarantine and was a close relative of a ‌Kenyan man who died of Ebola earlier this month. Also yesterday, Edo State Governor, Senator Monday Okpebholo, established a committee to coordinate the state’s emergency preparedness and response. Swiss Ministry Confirms Diplomat’s Wife Tested Positive Switzerland’s Foreign Ministry confirmed that the woman who tested positive for Ebola in Nigeria was the wife of a Swiss diplomat. The 42-year-old Ugandan-born woman, who lives in Abuja, tested positive on October 20, becoming Nigeria’s first confirmed Ebola patient in more than a decade. The couple had travelled to Uganda earlier in October. Her husband is currently in isolation but has not developed symptoms, according to the Swiss Foreign Ministry. The ministry told the BBC that all 25 staff members at its embassy in Nigeria were in good health and did not need to isolate. The decision, taken in consultation with Nigeria’s Ministry of Health and the World Health Organisation (WHO), covered eight Swiss staff members and 17 local employees. The embassy remains open and operational, with health and safety measures in place. The woman had reportedly spent about a week at a private clinic in Abuja experiencing symptoms before her diagnosis. She returned to Nigeria on October 3 after spending about two and a half weeks in Uganda. She developed symptoms four days after arriving in Abuja and sought treatment at two private health facilities before testing positive on October 20. WHO said the woman was receiving treatment in isolation and showing signs of improvement. Although there were reports that she had travelled to eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DR Congo) for business, the WHO, Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) and Nigeria’s health ministry said they had not received verified information confirming that she visited the country. The Swiss government had also told Reuters that she did not travel to DR Congo, contradicting accounts from Uganda. Health officials are investigating whether she may have crossed paths with a Kenyan man who died of Ebola after travelling through Uganda’s main airport on the same day. The Africa CDC said investigators were examining whether the two could have been exposed through shared equipment or other contact. The agency’s Head of Emergency Preparedness and Response, Dr. Wessam Mankoula, described this as one of the possible scenarios but stressed that no link had been established. The Kenyan man had travelled from DR Congo through Uganda before arriving in Nairobi on October 3. He subsequently died, becoming Kenya’s first recorded Ebola fatality. Kenya has since confirmed nine cases and traced 135 contacts, all of whom were placed in quarantine. Ebola has infected nearly 10,000 people and killed more than 4,600 in Congo. The disease can cause fever, vomiting, diarrhoea and, in severe ⁠cases, internal and external bleeding. Only people with symptoms can transmit the virus. The rare Ebola species behind the current outbreak has no approved treatment or vaccine. WHO said it was too early to determine where the woman in Nigeria contracted the virus. “The source of exposure is still not known. The travel history of the patient is still being pieced together,” said Dr Patrick Otim, a WHO emergency response official. He said investigators had struggled to obtain a complete account of her movements because opportunities to interview her were limited while she remained in hospital. The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) is conducting genomic sequencing to help establish whether her infection is linked to other cases. However, the woman has been confirmed to have the Bundibugyo species of Ebola, the same species responsible for the outbreak in DR Congo. “The investigation is reconstructing the full travel and exposure history. Genomic sequencing is given a high priority,” said Dr Pavel Ursu, WHO’s representative in Nigeria. Meanwhile, Nigerian authorities are tracing additional people who may have been exposed to the woman beyond the 44 contacts initially identified. Kenya’s Director-General of Health, Dr Patrick Amoth, said all nine confirmed infections in his country were linked to the first patient, with no evidence of wider community transmission. He urged the public to remain vigilant without panicking, while warning that the country was not yet out of danger. He added that the eight surviving patients remained in isolation and were responding well to treatment. The developments have renewed concerns about the movement of infected people across international borders, particularly between DR Congo and neighbouring Uganda, where thousands of people cross daily for trade, work and family visits. WHO’s Regional Director for Africa, Dr Mohamed Janabi, called for regional vigilance and urged countries to strengthen surveillance, investigate infections and protect frontline health workers. Ebola is a serious viral disease transmitted through direct contact with the blood or other bodily fluids of an infected person, or contaminated objects. It does not spread through the air like influenza. Symptoms can include fever, severe weakness, vomiting and diarrhoea, and the disease can be fatal. People are not considered infectious before developing symptoms. Health authorities say rapid contact tracing, isolation of suspected cases and early treatment are crucial to preventing further transmission. FG Orders Strict Compliance with Ebola Protocols In the circular, the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare directed relevant institutions to ensure strict adherence to approved EVD screening, health declaration, surveillance and other applicable entry requirements at all designated points of entry into Nigeria. According to a statement signed by the Assistant Director, Information and Public Relations, Ado Bako, the directive followed concerns communicated to the Coordinating Minister by ONSA over reported non-compliance with government-approved protocols. The ministry emphasised the need for consistent, effective and non-discriminatory enforcement of the measures to mitigate potential cross-border transmission and protect public health and national security. It also called for stronger coordination, communication and information-sharing among stakeholders to support effective surveillance, early detection and prompt responses to potential threats. “All concerned institutions have been urged to promptly document and report any actual or attempted breach of approved protocols through established channels, provide necessary support to officials responsible for enforcement, and establish effective monitoring and accountability mechanisms to sustain compliance,” the statement said. The ministry stressed that personnel responsible for enforcing the protocols should be allowed to perform their duties professionally and without undue interference. It also directed the immediate and widespread dissemination of public advisories to relevant departments, units, field offices and personnel to ensure that they understood their responsibilities. “All concerned MDAs are expected to accord the directive the highest priority, address identified lapses promptly and sustain compliance with approved EVD entry protocols in the collective interest of public health and national safety,” the statement added. The directive comes amid efforts to contain the confirmed Ebola case in the Federal Capital Territory, with the government intensifying surveillance at airports, seaports and land borders. Kenya Reports Second Death from Ebola Kenya has recorded a second Ebola death, the health ministry said yesterday, adding that the 65-year-old woman had developed symptoms during quarantine and was a close relative of a ‌Kenyan man who died of Ebola earlier this month. The outbreak, which started in the Democratic Republic of Congo, has now been reported in four countries across eastern, central andwestern Africa, giving it the widest geographic spread of any Ebola outbreak on the continent to date. The Ebola victim who died yesterday, was a direct contact of the index patient, Reuters quoted the Kenyan ministry to have revealed. “This loss brings the number of deaths to two among the nine confirmed cases. The remaining seven patients continue to receive care in the ‌two ⁠isolation facilities,” the ministry said, adding there was no evidence of community spread in the country. Late on Monday, the US State Department advised Americans to reconsider travel to Kenya and raised its travel advisory level for the countrybecause of health risks. Edo Sets Up Ebola Emergency Response Committee Edo State Governor, Senator Monday Okpebholo, has established a committee on Ebola emergency preparedness and response. The committee is chaired by the Deputy Governor, Dennis Idahosa, according to a statement issued yesterday by the Chief Press Secretary to the Governor, Dr Patrick Ebojele. The committee is expected to coordinate the state’s preparedness and response to any Ebola threat. Its members are drawn from the state ministries responsible for health, environment, livestock, local government, finance, and information and communication; the Edo State House of Assembly Committee on Health; the governor’s Special Adviser on Health; the State Emergency Management Agency; the Department of Port Health; and the National Orientation Agency. Other members include personnel from the Department of State Services, Nigeria Immigration Service, Nigeria Police Force and Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps. The committee also includes representatives of the University of Benin Teaching Hospital, Irrua Specialist Teaching Hospital, Edo State University Teaching Hospital, Federal Neuropsychiatric Hospital in Uselu, Edo Specialist Hospital, Central Hospital in Benin City and Stella Obasanjo Hospital. Professional bodies represented include the Nigeria Medical Association, National Association of Nigeria Nurses and Midwives, and the Edo State chapter of the Association of Private Medical Practitioners of Nigeria. Other members include a traditional ruler, a leader of the Christian Association of Nigeria in Edo State, the state’s Chief Imam and a market women’s leader. Development partners and agencies represented on the committee include the WHO, UNICEF, Nigeria Red Cross Society, DataFi, National Primary Health Care Development Agency and Edo State Primary Health Care Development Agency. The committee will operate through the Public Health Emergency Operations Centre, which has designated areas of responsibility covering coordination, epidemiology, surveillance, infection prevention and control, risk communication, logistics, laboratory services, case management, and safe and dignified burial. A centre manager will oversee operations. The statement added that a stakeholders’ meeting would be scheduled for the committee.

title: State Police: 25 Assemblies Approve Amendment, Bill Crosses Constitutional Hurdle
body: • Lagos, Ondo, Ebonyi, Kogi, Niger, Borno, Bauchi, Jigawa, Katsina, Kano, Sokoto yet to approve Deji Elumoye in Abuja The constitutional amendment seeking to establish State Police in Nigeria has crossed a major legislative hurdle, with 25 of the 36 State Houses of Assembly approving the 2026 Constitution (Sixth Alteration) Bill, surpassing the two-thirds threshold required for the amendment to proceed to the next stage. However, 11 States —Lagos, Ondo, Ebonyi, Kogi, Niger, Borno, Bauchi, Jigawa, Katsina, Kano and Sokoto — have yet to approve the amendment. With the required constitutional threshold secured, the amendment can now be returned to the National Assembly for transmission to President Bola Tinubu for assent. Chief of Staff to the President and Chairman of the Presidential Working Group on the National Policing Bill, Hon. Femi Gbajabiamila, disclosed the development in a statement, commending the State Houses of Assembly for their decisive action on the reform. He also expressed appreciation to the National Assembly for passing the amendment in both chambers. The development came as the National Policing Bill and 29 consequential amendment bills were undergoing legislative drafting review and validation at the Federal Ministry of Justice. Gbajabiamila explained that the approval by 25 state assemblies had provided the constitutional backing required for the proposed dual policing framework. He stated: “The approval gives constitutional backing to the policing framework that the Working Group’s draft National Policing Bill, 2026 is designed to implement. “The Working Group’s efforts remain on track. The draft Bills are currently undergoing legislative drafting review and validation at the Federal Ministry of Justice and are expected to be returned on or before Friday, 30th October 2026. Thereafter, the Group will give them final consideration before presenting them to Mr President. “The Working Group urges all stakeholders to support a smooth transition to a dual policing system that makes Nigerians safer.” The Presidency had on Tuesday disclosed that the draft National Policing Bill, 2026, was ready. Gbajabiamila explained that the Working Group had completed the drafting stage of its assignment and formally submitted the proposed National Policing Bill, together with 29 consequential amendment bills, to the Federal Ministry of Justice for legislative drafting review and validation. According to him, the submission was made to the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice on Monday, October 19, 2026, in accordance with the Working Group’s work plan. He said the ministry’s review would ensure that the proposed legislation conformed to established legislative drafting standards and conventions and did not conflict with existing laws. The Ministry of Justice, he added, was expected to return the validated draft bills to the Working Group on or before October 30, 2026. Thereafter, the Working Group would give the bills final consideration before presenting them to the President, thereby concluding its mandate. Gbajabiamila stated: “The proposed National Policing Bill seeks to establish the constitutional and legislative framework for a dual policing structure, comprising a Federal Police Service and State Police Services. “The Working Group remains committed to a rigorous and transparent process that will deliver a comprehensive legislative proposal for consideration by the President and subsequent transmission to the National Assembly. “The work on preparing the National Policing Bill is proceeding alongside the ongoing consideration of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026 by the States Houses of Assembly, which must be completed before the Bill is transmitted to the National Assembly.” The Presidency had last Thursday indicated that the National Policing Bill would be transmitted to the National Assembly within two weeks. Speaking with journalists after a steering committee meeting at the State House, Abuja, Gbajabiamila said the proposed legislation was nearing completion. “The National Policing Bill is more or less ready for transmission to the National Assembly. We will probably have one more meeting after this to cross the t’s and dot the i’s and make sure every area is covered. So, we are 90 percent ready. “The governors have one or two observations, and we should be ready in about a week or so,” he said. Gbajabiamila described the proposed legislation as “the most consequential Bill of the administration so far,” explaining that it had undergone extensive deliberations since the Working Group’s steering committee commenced its meetings on August 3, 2026. Responding to concerns that some states might delay approval of the Sixth Constitution Alteration Bill on state police, particularly when only about six states had reportedly approved the amendment, Gbajabiamila expressed confidence that the required support would be secured. He maintained that there was a “national consensus” among Nigerians on the need for the constitutional amendment. “I see no reason why anyone will want to have a rethink on it,” he said. Those present at Thursday’s steering committee meeting, held at the conference hall of the Chief of Staff’s Office at the State House, Abuja, included the Chairman of the Nigeria Governors’ Forum and Governor of Kwara State, AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq; Ogun State Governor, Dapo Abiodun; Kaduna State Governor, Uba Sani; Inspector-General of Police, Tunji Disu; and the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, represented by the Solicitor-General and Permanent Secretary of the Federal Ministry of Justice, Mrs Beatrice Jedy-Agba. Others included the Chairman of the Policy Advisory Committee, Justice Abdullahi Liman (retd.); Head of the Nigeria Police Reform Secretariat, Professor Olu Ogunsakin; Special Adviser to the President on National Assembly Matters (House of Representatives), Dr Lanre Smart; and Senior Special Assistant to the President on Planning and Research and Secretary of the Committee, Nnadubem Moghalu. Also in attendance were a representative of the President of the Nigerian Bar Association and AIG Abraham Nabhon Thomas, who represented the National Security Adviser, among others. President Tinubu had, on July 7, 2026, inaugurated the Presidential Working Group on the National Policing Bill to prepare the legal framework for the implementation of state police across the country. The inauguration followed the National Assembly’s passage of the Constitution Alteration (State Police) Bill, 2026, which provides for a dual policing structure comprising a Federal Police Service and 36 State Police Services. Tinubu had explained that although the constitutional amendment would establish the framework for state police, the National Policing Bill would provide the legal structure necessary for its implementation. “The Constitution Amendment Bill establishes the framework for dual policing, but it does not operationalise it. That work is left to the National Policing Bill,” the President stated.

title: Oramah: Africa Must Break Economic Bondage, Build Its Own Industrial Power
body: · Says political independence incomplete without economic freedom · Urges investment in manufacturing, skills, technology Nume Ekeghe The immediate past President of the African Export-Import Bank (Afreximbank), Dr. Benedict Oramah, has urged African countries to intensify efforts to achieve economic independence through industrialisation, deeper intra-African trade, strategic deployment of capital and investment in human development. Oramah, who spoke in an interview on the sidelines of the recently concluded International Monetary Fund (IMF)/World Bank Annual Meetings in Bangkok, Thailand, said the continent’s political independence would remain incomplete unless African countries developed the capacity to produce goods, create decent jobs and determine their economic future. He called on governments, financial institutions, businesses and other stakeholders to see themselves as fighters for Africa’s economic freedom, warning that the continent must overcome the fragmentation and dependence that continue to constrain its development. “Everybody in the banking business, including our governments and corporates, has to regard themselves as economic freedom fighters. We are combatants for economic freedom. Those in banking and financial services are engaged in financial guerrilla warfare,” he said. According to him, political independence was only the beginning of Africa’s struggle, with the ultimate objective being economic self-determination. “Political independence gives you the platform to achieve the ultimate independence, which is economic independence,” Oramah said, adding that the struggle must now be fought through ideas, industrial production, technology and human capital rather than weapons. “The fight we are in now is not going to be fought in trenches, but on factory floors, in technology incubation centres and so on. It is not going to be fought with brute force. It will be fought with ideas. Capital is key, not bullets. That capital includes human capital,” he added. Oramah, who recently completed his tenure at Afreximbank after two terms, said he had established Marob Strategies, a strategy and advisory firm, to continue contributing to Africa’s development by helping institutions formulate and implement strategies. He explained that Africa’s challenge was not merely a shortage of ideas but the inability to execute them effectively and mobilise the resources required to achieve continental ambitions. On regional integration, he lamented that Africa’s trade with external partners remained disproportionately high compared with trade among its own countries, despite the continent’s significant infrastructure assets and productive capacity. He said existing infrastructure could support between $1 trillion and $1.4 trillion in African trade, yet intra-African trade accounted for only about $170 billion to $200 billion. Oramah further urged African countries to develop their own artificial intelligence capabilities rather than remain mere users of technologies developed elsewhere.

title: Babalakin Hails Tinubu Over Resolution of 19-year MMA2 Dispute, Pledges Jobs for Nigerians
body: Dike Onwuamaeze The Chairman of Bi-Courtney Aviation Services Limited (BASL), Dr. Wale Babalakin, SAN, has commended President Bola Tinubu for facilitating the resolution of the longstanding dispute surrounding the Murtala Muhammed Airport Terminal Two (MMA2), describing the settlement as a victory for Nigeria. Babalakin also pledged that Bi-Courtney would fulfil its obligations under the agreement and pursue projects expected to create quality employment opportunities for Nigerians. He spoke at the signing ceremony of the settlement agreement involving the Federal Government, the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN), Bi-Courtney Limited and Stabilini Visinoni Limited, which resolved an impasse that had lasted more than 18 years. The BASL chairman attributed the breakthrough to Tinubu’s intervention through the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Olorogun Festus Keyamo, SAN. “This is not a win for us alone; it is a win for Nigerians,” Babalakin said, expressing appreciation to the President, the minister and Nigerians who had followed the dispute over the years. He said the resolution sent a positive signal to investors that longstanding disputes between the government and private enterprises could be settled through dialogue and constructive engagement. According to him, prolonged uncertainty over commercial agreements could discourage long-term investment, making the settlement an important step towards strengthening confidence in Nigeria’s investment environment. The agreement is also expected to pave the way for the advancement of key development projects at MMA2, particularly the proposed hotel and conference centre, as well as the commencement of regional flight operations. Babalakin said completing the hotel and conference centre would enhance the airport environment by providing accommodation and conference facilities for business travellers, corporate organisations and other airport users. He added that the project could generate employment across construction, engineering, hospitality, facility management and related services. The commencement of regional flight operations, alongside the planned expansion of the airport apron, would also create opportunities for skilled employment and commercial growth. The settlement further addresses outstanding issues arising from the parties’ longstanding commercial relationship, including matters relating to the General Aviation Terminal (GAT), which remained under FAAN’s control and operation. The agreement incorporates reciprocal concessions and revised obligations, providing a framework for the parties to move forward. Babalakin acknowledged the responsibility to translate the settlement into tangible results, assuring stakeholders that Bi-Courtney would fulfil its obligations and work constructively with the relevant parties. “We will not disappoint the President, the Ministry of Aviation and Aerospace Development, FAAN or Nigerians,” he said. He reiterated his appreciation to Tinubu for facilitating the resolution, describing the agreement as an opportunity to renew cooperation, deliver infrastructure projects and realise the full potential of MMA2.

title: Atiku Accuses Tinubu of Using 90-day Cost of Living Relief to Woo Voters
body: Chuks Okocha in Abuja Former Vice President and presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Alhaji Atiku Abubakar, has accused President Bola Tinubu of using the 90-day cost-of-living relief plan announced by the National Economic Council (NEC) to woo voters ahead of the presidential election. Atiku, through his Director of Strategic Communication at the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Phrank Shaibu, said the timing of the initiative raised questions about the government’s commitment to easing the hardship Nigerians had endured over the past three and a half years. Addressing a press conference on behalf of Atiku, Shaibu said: “The presidential election is 86 days away. Yet President Bola Tinubu’s National Economic Council has announced a cost-of-living plan that will run for 90 days. “The arithmetic is plain: the plan ends after Nigerians have voted. After three and a half years of hardship, this government is asking families to carry another promise into the polling booth and wait for relief until the votes are counted. “This is election bait. Tinubu is offering hungry Nigerians the promise of affordable food, but the promised relief comes with a deadline that outlasts the election. The message is simple: vote first; relief later. Nigerians should refuse the bait and judge this government by the three and a half years they have already lived through,” Atiku added. The plan, according to Atiku, identifies five priorities: food affordability, tax harmonisation, completion of important projects, removal of investment bottlenecks and household support. He argued that these were problems Nigerians had expected the administration to address since taking office. “Families have cut meals. Workers spend more of their wages getting to work. Manufacturers struggle to produce, and businesses have closed. Tinubu cannot erase three and a half years of hardship with a 90-day announcement,” he said. Atiku argued that the consequences of petrol subsidy removal on transport, food and production costs had been predictable, insisting that measures to protect vulnerable households should have accompanied the decision. “Instead, the government imposed the costs immediately and left Nigerians to wait for the benefits. Now, after years of hardship, it has suddenly discovered that people need affordable food. “A government cannot put a 90-day deadline on hunger, the cost-of-living crisis and insecurity and call it an economic policy,” he said. Atiku also questioned the effectiveness of the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited’s (NNPC) petrol discount promotion, which began on October 1 and was subsequently presented by the government as part of its relief efforts. He said he had visited NNPC Retail stations and was told that no discount was available, adding that he bought petrol at N1,405 per litre. “With barely a week left before the offer expires, my experience as a customer was simple: a promise of relief, and a higher price at the pump. If NNPC says motorists can access a discount through an app, it must explain why customers arriving at its stations were told there was none. “How many customers received the discount? At which stations? How many litres were sold at the reduced price? Publish the figures,” he said. Atiku questioned the reach of the promotion, noting that NNPC had about 900 retail stations in a country where motorists bought petrol from thousands of outlets. “What reach can a N66-per-litre promotion have when it is confined to that network? And what lasting relief does N66 offer families whose transport and food bills remain high?” he asked. He added: “Tinubu announces relief at a podium. Nigerians arrive at the pump and pay more. Now his government expects the country to trust another announcement, this time with a 90-day deadline.” The former vice-president said the timing of the initiative was significant because the cost-of-living crisis had become central to his campaign, which he said was focused on making Nigeria affordable again. He accused the Tinubu administration of attempting to appropriate that message with a relief plan whose timeline extended beyond the election. “Nigerians should not trade three and a half years of lived hardship for three months of promises,” he said. Atiku challenged the government to provide details of the five priorities outlined in the plan. On food affordability, he asked which costs would fall for farmers, transporters and traders, when consumers would begin to see lower market prices, and how the government would sustain affordability beyond the 90-day period. On tax harmonisation, he demanded details of the charges to be removed or consolidated and urged the government to publish the full tax schedule, including whether the promised relief would be followed by higher charges after the election. He also questioned which projects would be completed within 90 days, how much remained to be paid for them and when Nigerians would be able to use them. “A project is complete when it serves people, not when it is marked complete on a government dashboard,” he said. On investment bottlenecks, Atiku asked which barriers the government intended to remove within the period, arguing that manufacturers needed reliable power, manageable transport costs and access to affordable finance to expand operations and create jobs. He also demanded details of the proposed household support, including eligibility criteria, the amount each household would receive, when payments would begin, the budget and the payment mechanism. Atiku raised concerns about a registration form reportedly being circulated under the name “Arise for Tinubu 2027”. He said the form requested voter identification, bank details and telephone numbers, and questioned who was collecting the information, how it would be used and whether the exercise was linked to the government’s household support programme. “No Nigerian should have to hand over voter or bank details to a political group to receive public relief,” he said. He urged the government to clarify whether the registration exercise was connected to any publicly funded programme and, if not, explain how it would prevent household support from being used to recruit voters or collect their personal data. Atiku maintained that Nigerians who had borne the burden of the government’s reforms were entitled to evidence that the promised benefits would reach them and continue beyond election day. “People do not reject reform because they fail to understand it. They reject being told to sacrifice today for relief that never arrives—or arrives with an expiry date,” he said. He pledged to make Nigeria more affordable through disciplined public spending, targeted household relief, lower costs of producing and transporting essential goods, and policies that would enable Nigerian manufacturers to expand and employ more people. “Economic policy should be judged by what families can afford, not by how many deadlines a government announces,” he said. Atiku challenged Tinubu to answer two questions: whether Nigerians were better off than they were in May 2023, and whether they would still be able to afford food on the 91st day of the proposed relief plan. “Until he can answer both, Nigerians have every reason to see this 90-day exercise for what it is: a political timetable dressed up as economic relief. “President Tinubu made life expensive. Atiku Abubakar will make life affordable again,” he said. Atiku also questioned Tinubu’s record on security in Kaduna State ahead of the President’s expected visit to launch his re-election campaign today. He said the President should reflect on the state’s experience with deadly attacks, civilian casualties and natural disasters before seeking another mandate. “Tinubu is also expected in Kaduna to launch his re-election campaign. Before the music starts and the crowd is assembled, he should remember what the state has endured under his presidency,” he said. Atiku cited the December 3, 2023, military drone strike on civilians attending a Maulud celebration in Tudun Biri, in which at least 85 people were killed. He said Tinubu sent the Vice-President to visit survivors but did not personally visit grieving families. He also referred to reports by residents of Giwa in September 2024 that another military airstrike had killed at least 24 civilians. In Kajuru, he said, families had buried loved ones and searched for relatives abducted by bandits. He also cited a kidnapping-related attack in Kachia in September 2025 that affected 152 people, with eight deaths and nine injuries recorded. Atiku further highlighted the impact of storms and floods in the state. He said windstorms and rain in July 2025 affected 6,172 people and damaged hundreds of shelters across five local government areas, while flooding in Zaria in September affected 476 people and left dozens injured. “When families were burying their dead, searching for their children and clearing wreckage from their homes, Kaduna needed the attention of its President,” he said. Atiku questioned the Presidency’s account of Tinubu’s September 2025 visit to Kaduna, which he said listed a wedding and a courtesy call. “Tinubu can find his way to Kaduna for a wedding. He can find his way there for votes. Why was he absent when grieving families needed their President?” he asked. He urged Tinubu not to use affected families as a backdrop for a campaign event, calling on the President to explain what had been done for the victims of Tudun Biri, the outcome of investigations into civilian deaths and the measures being taken to protect communities still threatened by abductions. “Before asking Kaduna for another mandate, he should explain what has been done for the victims of Tudun Biri, what became of investigations into civilian deaths and how his government will protect communities still threatened by abduction,” Atiku said.

title: Harrow Abu Dhabi to open next year as plans for capital's first boarding school take shape
body: As one of the world's most prestigious schools opens a branch in Abu Dhabi, its principal is banking on attracting families from the UAE and Gulf region that would normally send their children overseas to study. Harrow Abu Dhabi is expected to begin operating in August 2027, after the opening was delayed earlier this year. Families can expect to pay fees between Dh80,000 and Dh106,000 per pupil, and even more if they opt for boarding. Adrian Frost, its founding headmaster, compared bringing the 450-year heritage British school’s education to the UAE to buying a Rolls-Royce overseas: some features would change to suit the country, while the thinking behind it should remain the same. “You could buy a Rolls-Royce in the UK, and you can buy a Rolls-Royce here, and you'll notice that there are certain differences,” he told The National. “It's a different regulator. It's a different location. It's quite plausibly a different demographic that will be interested in the school, but yeah, the ethos and culture is very, very much the same.” For parents, that will be reflected in an extended school day with activities, shared mealtimes, supervised homework, along with an emphasis on reading and handwriting, and reduced reliance on screens. Families looking for boarding options will have to wait beyond its first year, Mr Frost said. Food will be regulated on campus, with pupils not allowed to bring lunch boxes from home. There are several dining halls that serve an array of meals and snacks throughout the day, focusing on the nutritional value of meals while ensuring pupils learn proper etiquette and table manners. “It is a very different education offering,” he said, “one that is not really replicated in quite the same way in any school in Abu Dhabi.” The Saadiyat Island campus will initially admit children from Foundation Stage 1 to Year 6. Boarding will be considered as the school expands into its next phase. The opening date or fees for accommodation have not yet been confirmed. “It’s a few years away though, and we will obviously need to set up the first phase, which is FS1 to Year 6,” said Mr Frost. That timeline puts Abu Dhabi's first boarding school at least two years away. Half the building would not be needed for at least a year after the school opens, Mr Frost said. The school was initially planned to accommodate 1,800 pupils on a site of about 70,000 square metres, which is 30 per cent larger than the Dubai campus, which opened earlier this year. Alternative to boarding abroad Mr Frost hopes families in the UAE and the wider Gulf region who might otherwise send their children overseas will consider Abu Dhabi. Having attended boarding school himself, he recalled studying alongside children whose families lived in countries including Jordan and Bahrain. He intends to bring his experience and knowledge of boarding schools to Abu Dhabi’s first one. “There are parents who want boarding. I hope that they will look to us as an alternative option,” he said. He sees Saadiyat’s cultural institutions, including the Louvre Abu Dhabi and Guggenheim museums, as well as proximity to New York University Abu Dhabi, as part of the appeal, particularly for a school that intends to place importance on music and performing arts. “That location is not just an address, it’s a teaching resource,” he said. Mr Frost previously worked as vice-principal of Brighton College Abu Dhabi and has experience in British day and boarding schools, and in establishing a boarding school in Portugal. He said work was still under way with regulators, school operator Taaleem and Harrow to establish the policies and arrangements for boarding. The school intends to align with standards set by the Boarding Schools’ Association, Mr Frost added. Although being a boarding advocate himself, he warned against treating the option as the right choice for every family. “All the children are different, every single one of them,” he said. “There are some children that thrive in that type of environment, and there are some that can find it a struggle.” What parents will pay for Mr Frost said annual school fees are expected to range from Dh80,000 for FS1 to Dh106,000 for Year 6. He added that although some schools charge extra for after-school activities, Harrow intends to include sport, performing arts and other activities within the premium fee range, but the arrangements with external providers in Abu Dhabi have not been finalised. The extended day would begin with activities, followed by breakfast, continue through lessons, and finish with tea and supervised homework, known as prep. Teachers are called “beaks”, following Harrow tradition. “That is all part of the provision that comes within that price,” he said. At the Dubai school, where Mr Frost was completing his induction, about 96 clubs and activities were running for 400 pupils. Boarding will carry an additional charge in Abu Dhabi but that price has not yet been finalised. “There will obviously be a higher cost associated with it,” he said. “But it’s important to us that we don’t price ourselves out of the market.” British families form a large proportion of the Dubai school’s intake, which Mr Frost said is “unsurprising”. Why the opening was delayed The Abu Dhabi campus was initially expected to open this year. Mr Frost said the postponement to 2027 was due to operational constraints on Saadiyat Island, including infrastructure requirements and approvals from authorities. “It was nothing from the school's side, they were ready to go,” he clarified. He said those obstacles had been overcome and construction had reached the third and final floor, allowing work to move towards the windows and interior fittings. The Abu Dhabi campus would broadly reflect the Dubai school, although the shapes and sizes of the sites are different, he said. During the visit, he highlighted Dubai’s early-years spaces, an auditorium, music rooms and sports amenities as examples of the provision planned for the capital.

title: T-Rex Glamping Dubai review: A Jurassic Park-inspired staycation
body: Jurassic Park is a work of fiction, but T-Rex Glamping at Dubai Parks and Resorts is probably the nearest you'll get to experiencing it in real life. As a child, I was obsessed with t he movie, so I was just as excited about a dinosaur-themed getaway as the little ones. The campsite offers two-storey cabins surrounded by moving dinosaur models, with some of Dubai's biggest theme parks just a short distance away. The welcome Located directly off the Sheikh Zayed Road, T-Rex Glamping is easily accessible by car. The experience starts as soon as you drive into the park. Dinosaur illustrations line the walls, giving you a little preview of the prehistoric world you're entering. A huge Tyrannosaurus rex welcomes you as you arrive. These aren't just giant dinosaur statues; they move their heads, wag their tails, blink their eyes and even roar. The movements seem so realistic that even as an adult, you can't help but stop and watch. At reception, I noticed a little girl who was completely fascinated by one of the dinosaurs. I watched her for a little while before realising I was probably just as amused. The room The best part of T-Rex Glamping is that you spend the night surrounded by these dinosaurs. The two-storey cabins combine the feel of camping with the comforts of a hotel room. Inside, you'll find double beds and a modern bathroom. The space is compact but well designed, with everything you need for a relaxing night. I found the beds particularly cosy, and having air conditioning on both floors was another plus. The layout works particularly well for families. Children can sleep upstairs while parents stay downstairs, or the other way around. One of my favourite features was the upstairs balcony, where you can sit with a coffee and look out over the grounds. There's also a private garden area with a barbecue and outdoor dining space, giving you plenty of room to unwind. And despite having your own little corner to yourself, you're never far from the action. One moment, you hear a dinosaur roaring in the distance. The next, it's people screaming on a nearby roller coaster. The food and facilities Roaring Dinosaur, the on-site restaurant, offers a selection of casual dining options. I stopped here for lunch and ordered a burger and fries. As well as guests having barbecue facilities outside the tents, breakfast is included in the booking. One of my favourite parts of the campsite was the outdoor cinema, where you can settle into a beanbag with some popcorn and watch a movie under the stars. There's also a large outdoor pool and plenty of play areas for children. Theme parks on your doorstep What makes T-Rex Glamping even more interesting is that you're not just booking a night in a cabin. You're staying at Dubai Parks and Resorts, which means there's plenty to explore at Motiongate Dubai, Real Madrid World, Legoland Dubai and the Legoland Water Park. I'd recommend arriving late morning, dropping off your bags and heading straight to the parks. As an adrenalin junkie, I was naturally drawn to the roller coasters and rides, but there's something for everyone. Motiongate Dubai has plenty of movie-inspired rides, including the indoor DreamWorks area, which is perfect when it gets too hot outside. An unexpected highlight was the Submarine Adventure ride at Legoland Dubai, where I spotted a tiger shark for the first time in my life. Real Madrid World's Hala Madrid roller coaster is definitely worth trying if you love a thrill. Approximately 34.5 metres tall, it was the first wooden roller coaster to open in the Middle East. At Riverland Dubai you'll find cafes, restaurants and other immersive experiences. After a day of exploring the theme parks, I'd suggest heading back to T-Rex Glamping in time to enjoy the evening. The following morning doesn't need to be rushed either. Enjoy breakfast, spend some time by the pool and relax before checking out. You can always return to Dubai Parks and Resorts afterwards to explore any attractions you missed the previous day. T-Rex Glamping is at Dubai Parks and Resorts on Sheikh Zayed Road. Check-in is from 3pm and checkout is at noon. Nightly rates start at Dh720 for two adults. This review was conducted at the invitation of the resort and reflects standards during this time

title: Poland intends to deploy French and US nuclear weapons on its territory — Defense Ministry
body:
WARSAW, October 24. /TASS/. Poland is seeking to participate in the US nuclear deterrence program and is conducting similar negotiations with France, said Defense Minister Wladysіaw Kosiniak-Kamysz said.
In an interview with the WNP.pl portal, he noted that the initiative to jointly use nuclear weapons by some NATO countries could be implemented as part of cooperation with the United States to establish an American base on the republic’s territory. Kosiniak-Kamysz did not specify the timeframe for making decisions due to the need for preliminary consultations with the European allies.
He noted that Poland is also actively developing nuclear cooperation with France. "Participation in the American nuclear cooperation program does not preclude the establishment of relations with France," he said. He added that Paris is offering its European partners a larger share in the nuclear deterrence system.
On June 3, Kosiniak-Kamysz suggested to Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth that the United States establish a permanent base in Poland. In early September, an American delegation visited Poland to inspect potential locations. On September 17, US President Donald Trump announced "significant progress" in the negotiations on this matter.

title: Zelensky differs from his predecessors for worse — Russian senator
body:
MOSCOW, October 24. /TASS/. Vladimir Zelensky differs from his predecessors for the worse; he has failed to keep all his pre·election promises and has not achieved any results for the country, Russian Federation Council Vice Speaker Konstantin Kosachev said in an interview with TASS.
According to Kosachev, it is the failed pre-election promises prevent Zelensky from holding presidential elections. When he ran for office, his main election promises were to bring peace back to Ukraine, normalize relations with Russia, and resolve the people’s pressing problems related to wages, pensions, access to electricity and fuel, the senator said.
"It was thanks to these promises that Zelensky won; in fact, people expected him to pursue a different policy compared to his predecessors. And now, after seven or eight years of what is known as Zelensky’s presidency, we can say that he is indeed different from his predecessors. But not for the better -- he has definitely failed to keep his own campaign promises, and, most importantly, he has failed to achieve any positive results for Ukraine and its population through his policy, which differed from his campaign promises," the parliamentarian believes.
Zelensky’s presidential powers expired on May 20, 2024, but Kiev has not held elections during this entire period, claiming that it is impossible until martial law ends.

title: Woman, 65, becomes second patient to die of Ebola in Kenya
body: Kenya has recorded its second death from Ebola as it handles its first ever outbreak of the disease. A woman, aged 65, who was a close family member of the first victim, a man who had travelled from the Democratic Republic of Congo, died after being placed in quarantine, the health ministry said. Seven other Ebola patients were receiving treatment at two isolation facilities, it added. All the cases were within “one cluster, with no evidence of community spread”, the ministry said. More than 4,000 people have died in Africa since Ebola was confirmed in DR Congo in May, making it the second most deadly outbreak of the disease. Kenya’s latest victim was a “direct contact and close family member of the first case (deceased) and was under quarantine when she developed symptoms” on 13 October, the health ministry said. The first death, on 5 October, was that of a man who fell ill in September and was treated in several hospitals in DR Congo before arriving in the Kenyan capital, Nairobi, where he died a few days later. Those still being treated are three other relatives of the first victim, three health workers and a hospital cleaner. The US has warned its citizens against travelling to Kenya, while neighbouring countries such as Uganda, Ethiopia and Somalia are also on alert. Ebola is a rare but deadly disease caused by a virus. As the disease progresses, vomiting and diarrhoea develop and it can lead to organ failure. Some, but not all, patients develop internal and external bleeding. The disease spreads from one person to another by contact with infected bodily fluids such as blood or vomit. The Bundibugyo species of Ebola is relatively rare, with no approved vaccine or treatment – though trials are under way. With more than 9,500 cases in DR Congo, Kenya faces a steady risk of new cases arriving across borders, according to the International Rescue Committee, which has been working alongside both governments to contain the spread. Kenya has introduced enhanced screening for travellers arriving from DR Congo and nine other countries it considers to be at high risk: Uganda, Tanzania, Rwanda, Burundi, Angola, Zambia, Ethiopia, South Sudan and the Central African Republic. Travellers arriving from those countries are required to complete a digital surveillance form before boarding their flights, and to present a QR code to port health officials on arrival. Kenya also ordered enhanced public health screening of aircraft arriving from those countries, as authorities seek to prevent further imported cases. Within the country, the government has been sharing public messages to create awareness about Ebola, including encouraging people to promptly report any suspected cases and seek care at a hospital. It has also focused on hygiene and safety measures, such as washing hands and avoiding close contact with sick people.In another development, Nigeria’s health minister has said the country’s single confirmed case of Ebola appears to be genetically related to a strain identified earlier in Kenya. Professor Ali Pate said there was no evidence so far that the Kenyan patient had travelled to Nigeria, but that further testing was under way. He emphasised that Nigeria had so far recorded only one confirmed case of the virus. “We are conducting additional tests. Some of the results are negative, while others are pending,” Pate said. Health officials have been investigating whether Nigeria’s first case crossed paths with Kenya’s first patient. Both are believed to have travelled through Uganda’s Entebbe International Airport earlier this month.

title: Ethiopian Ambassador Visits Pakistan’s GIDS to Explore Defence Cooperation
body: Ethiopia’s ambassador to Pakistan, Dr Oumer H. Oba, has visited the headquarters of Global Industrial and Defence Solutions (GIDS) in mid-October to explore opportunities for bilateral cooperation. We were informed this week. GIDS Chief Executive Officer Asad Kamal received the ambassador, briefed him on the organisation’s role, capabilities and operations, and took him on a tour of the facility. Talks centred on matters of mutual interest and potential areas for collaboration. Both sides described the engagement as part of an effort to strengthen bilateral ties and advance South-South cooperation. No specific agreements or projects were announced, so the visit is best read as an exploratory step, not a deal. H.E. Ambassador Dr. Oumer H. Oba has visited the headquarters of Global Industrial and Defence Solutions (GIDS) in Pakistan to explore opportunities for bilateral cooperation with Ethiopia. Who GIDS Is GIDS is Pakistan’s state-owned defence export conglomerate, established in 2007 in Rawalpindi. Its portfolio includes the Shahpar family of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), the Fatah guided rocket systems and, more recently, components for third-party loitering munitions. In a profile published in April, Kamal said more than 18 armed forces operate systems represented by GIDS, which works in nearly 30 countries and exports to more than 20 markets. Military Africa carried that account , which came from the company. A Busy Fortnight in Islamabad The GIDS visit follows other high-level contacts in Pakistan’s capital. On 8 October, Pakistan’s Defence Minister, Khawaja Muhammad Asif, met the ambassadors of Ethiopia, Rwanda and Tajikistan on the same day, and Pakistani press reported that defence and aviation cooperation was on the agenda. Dr Oumer was among those received. The material reviewed gives no detail on what Ethiopia asked for or was offered. The contact builds on an earlier track. Horn Review asked in September 2025 whether Ethiopia was looking to Pakistan for air power, following a visit to Islamabad by the Ethiopian Air Force commander that August. No purchase has been publicly confirmed. Discussions focused on matters of mutual interest and potential areas for collaboration between Ethiopia and Pakistan. The engagement reflects both countries’ interest in strengthening bilateral ties and advancing South-South cooperation. Why Ethiopia Is Shopping Widely Ethiopia has assembled one of East Africa’s most varied air arms from many suppliers. Military Africa reported in February that it operates Russian Yak-130 trainers and Orion-E UAVs. In 2024 it unveiled a Sukhoi Su-30 fighter and a Turkish Akinci combat drone , and it has flown Iranian Mohajer-6 drones since at least 2021. Military Africa’s Ethiopia coverage charts that growth. The visit also comes while Ethiopia is in a fast-moving confrontation along its northern border. Press reports describe Ethiopian forces fighting Eritrean troops and Tigrayan militia, and Africanews reported Ethiopian drone strikes near Adigrat on 8 October . Accounts of the fighting are contested and Military Africa has not verified them. Neither side has linked the GIDS visit to those events, and any connection would be inference. It is reasonable to note, though, that the clearest demand in Ethiopia’s current situation is for air power, drones and munitions, the categories in which GIDS trades. GIDS is a Pakistani defense organization involved in the development and promotion of defense products and solutions. The visit provides an opportunity to explore potential cooperation in the defense sector, although specific agreements or projects were not announced. GIDS’s African Push GIDS has courted Africa steadily since 2024. It demonstrated the Shahpar II drone for delegates from 11 countries , including Nigeria and Kenya, and two months later signed a partnership with Nigeria’s Proforce . A delegation then visited Nigeria’s Defence Industries Corporation in September 2025 . In December 2025, Egypt’s Arab Organisation for Industrialisation signed a memorandum of understanding with GIDS covering co-production of loitering munitions. In February, Military Africa reported a 1.5 billion US dollar Pakistani arms agreement with Sudan , the scope of which remained unconfirmed. At the Africa Aerospace and Defence exhibition in September, GIDS reported hosting senior delegations from a long list of African countries, according to its own account in Military Africa’s AAD 2026 coverage . That list now sits on both sides of regional fault lines. Egypt is in a long-running dispute with Ethiopia over the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam on the Nile, yet it is a GIDS partner, as Ethiopia may become. This does not necessarily signal a conflict of interest. Defence exporters sell to many buyers, and GIDS’s own pitch is that it works with whoever wants its products. It does show how Pakistan’s defence industry is positioning itself across the Horn of Africa and the Nile basin.

title: Ukraine repatriates seven more civilians in exchange with Russia
body:
Dmytro Lubinets, the Verkhovna Rada’s Human Rights Commissioner, announced this on Facebook , according to Ukrinform.
“Thanks to my humanitarian channel of communication with Russian Human Rights Commissioner Yana Lantratova, we were able to reach agreements on the mutual return of civilians. Seven Ukrainians returned to territory controlled by Ukraine, and seven traveled to the Russian Federation as part of family reunification efforts supported by the ICRC,” Lubinets noted.
According to him, among those who are finally home are a 90-year-old woman with limited mobility and a 50-year-old Ukrainian woman who has suffered a heart attack and a stroke and has other medical conditions. Given the health conditions of both women, the necessary transportation arrangements were made when organizing their return.
In addition, as the ombudsman noted, they were able to arrange the return of a young woman and her child. When the full-scale invasion began, the woman was temporarily staying in Mariupol. Due to the hostilities and the subsequent occupation of the city, she was unable to return to her family. A major obstacle to their return to territory controlled by Ukraine was the child’s documentation. “They are now back home. Although they need psychological support, they are happy to be on their native soil,” said the Human Rights Commissioner.
As reported by Ukrinform, Ukrainian human rights activists released from Russian captivity and relatives of those held by Russia have called on European politicians to raise the issue of the release of civilian captives during every round of negotiations , as well as to coordinate the work of existing international mechanisms.

title: Massive Blackout Hits Russian-Occupied Crimea After Drone Attacks
body:
A massive blackout swept across Russian-occupied Crimea overnight into Saturday, Oct. 24, following reported drone attacks on energy infrastructure, leaving major cities without electricity as key power substations were reportedly knocked out.
The Ukrainian OSINT channel Exilenova+ reported that critical substations had been disabled, causing widespread power outages across the peninsula, according to Ukrinform .
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
The monitoring channel Crimean Wind , citing eyewitnesses, reported simultaneous outages in Sevastopol, Simferopol, Yalta, Feodosia, Dzhankoi, Alushta and Yevpatoria.
Residents also reported Russian mobile air defense units firing at unidentified aerial targets near Baherove, close to Kerch, while at least four explosions were heard in Crimea’s Pervomaiske district.
Sevastopol’s Kremlin-appointed governor, Mikhail Razvozhayev, confirmed widespread electricity disruptions , attributing them to reported damage to energy infrastructure elsewhere on the peninsula.
He said critical facilities had been placed under special operating procedures, while social infrastructure had switched to backup power supplies.
Russia has occupied Crimea since 2014, using it as a major military and logistical hub for its war against Ukraine.
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

title: India to send required number of labor migrants to Russia, ambassador says
body:
MOSCOW, October 24. /TASS/. India will send the necessary amount of skilled workers to Russia, ambassador Vinay Kumar said in an interview with TASS after the II Russian·Indian business forum Time.
He said that India’s goal is to ensure the supply of high·quality, skilled labor in the required amount in accordance with the Russian requirements. He said that on average India accounts for 25 to 30% of the foreign workers quota.
He said that India remains the most populous country in the world with a population of almost 1.5 billion people. According to Kumar’s forecasts, in the coming decades, India will become a global center of skilled personnel.
The average age of workers stands at 29 years, and they account for about 69% of the workforce. India trains specialists not only for the domestic market but also for work abroad. India has proposed to Russia to open educational institutions in India or to cooperate with existing Indian institutions to train the personnel needed for its industries the ambassador concluded.
The II Russian·Indian business forum Time was held in Kazan from October 15 to 16. The event was aimed at developing Russian·Indian trade and economic cooperation. During the forum, the participants discussed ways to implement joint initiatives, promising investment projects, and opportunities for technological and economic cooperation.
TASS is the forum’s information partner.

title: Huang Backs Kazakhstan’s AI Plans as NVIDIA Expands Partnerships
body: NVIDIA is expanding its partnerships in Kazakhstan as the country draws on its energy resources, engineering talent, and industrial base to develop AI computing facilities and deploy advanced technology in mining, manufacturing, robotics, and other industries. Kazakhtelecom has already installed NVIDIA processors, while much larger projects involving Firebird and Freedom Holding are under development. On October 23, NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang made his first visit to Kazakhstan, at the invitation of Deputy Prime Minister Zhaslan Madiyev. Huang met President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev and discussed computing investment, robotics, and technology development with government and business leaders. “I commend you for declaring your nation an AI nation,” Huang told Tokayev during their meeting at the Akorda presidential palace. Tokayev described AI and digitalization as national priorities, noting that 2026 had been declared the Year of Digitalization and Artificial Intelligence. He said Huang’s visit would strengthen cooperation with NVIDIA and welcomed its partnership with Higgsfield, a San Francisco-based AI video and image-generation company co-founded by Kazakh entrepreneur Yerzat Dulat. Huang highlighted partnerships with Kazakhtelecom and Firebird AI KZ and proposed developing Kazakhstan as a global hub for physical AI. Tokayev awarded Huang the Order of Dostyk, First Class, a senior state honor also conferred on former Singaporean Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong and Italian President Sergio Mattarella . Robotics and Industrial AI At Astana’s alem.ai center, Huang joined Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Artificial Intelligence and Digital Development Zhaslan Madiyev for a fireside discussion on the country’s AI strategy. Madiyev said Kazakhstan’s energy resources, industrial base, and engineers could support the development of physical AI, which enables robots and autonomous machines to operate in the real world. He said Kazakhstan wanted to test and deploy these systems in industrial settings and build companies capable of competing internationally. In an earlier TCA interview, Madiyev said operational data from Kazakhstan’s mines and factories could be used to develop industrial AI systems. “Instead of just exporting energy, in the future, you could transform energy into intelligence and export intelligence,” Huang said. Madiyev also emphasized AI that understands the Kazakh language and cultural context. Freedom Holding presented plans for digital replicas of Almaty and Astana that could be used to train and test autonomous robots in simulated city environments using NVIDIA technology. Separately, inDrive, Pony.ai, and NVIDIA signed a memorandum of understanding to explore autonomous ride-hailing in Kazakhstan. Astana is the proposed first market, subject to feasibility assessments and an agreement with the Kazakh government. AI Computing Infrastructure Freedom Holding CEO Timur Turlov met Huang at alem.ai to discuss the company’s infrastructure plans. Turlov said Freedom was placing an order for its first NVIDIA B300 computing cluster, with a public GPU cloud for businesses and developers planned for 2027. The Turlov-backed Akashi data center campus in Astana is under construction, with a planned capacity of up to 100 megawatts and first-phase commercial operations scheduled for 2027. On October 19, the Eurasian Development Bank announced that it had signed an agreement with AKASHI Data Center PLC to provide $31.2 million in project financing. In November 2025, Freedom announced plans for a $2 billion sovereign AI hub with Kazakhstan’s AI ministry. Under the proposal, described as nonbinding in the company’s August 2026 filing , Freedom would serve as the principal financing and implementation partner. Kazakhtelecom CEO Bagdat Musin presented Data Center Valley in Ekibastuz to Huang, outlining the project’s infrastructure and power supply. According to NVIDIA , Kazakhtelecom has deployed 400 H200 and 480 B300 graphics processing units in Astana and Almaty. Firebird signed an investment agreement with Kazakhstan at a ceremony at Akorda attended by co-founder and CEO Razmig Hovaghimian. NVIDIA said Firebird had secured a U.S. export license for 45,000 Grace Blackwell GPUs. Its first phase is under construction with Kazakhtelecom at Data Center Valley, targeting a commercial launch in the third quarter of 2027. Under the previously reported arrangement , Kazakhtelecom would provide power, cooling, and telecommunications infrastructure, while Firebird’s Kazakh unit would finance the computing hardware and related systems. Higgsfield and AI Education Higgsfield announced on October 23 that NVIDIA and investment firm TCV had joined an extension of its Series B funding round. The announcement did not disclose the size of their investments. The financing follows an August round that raised $400 million at a $5.4 billion valuation . During the visit, Huang met Dulat. The company’s other co-founders are CEO Alex Mashrabov and Mahi de Silva. Higgsfield maintains ties to Kazakhstan through Astana Hub. ARC Aero presented its work in autonomous aviation, while QazTWIN and Astana Dynamics showcased industrial digital twins and robotic inspection. He also saw projects from DeepInfra in cloud computing, MiraiTech in wearable technology, and Blockchair in blockchain analytics. Huang met TUMO Astana and Tomorrow School students, as well as winners of the HackAlem AI competition. Science and Higher Education Minister Sayasat Nurbek participated in the Tomorrow School meeting, where Huang was briefed on Qazaq AI Research University and its AI training initiatives. In a recent TCA interview , Nurbek emphasized teaching students to use AI while preserving independent judgment and critical thinking. Astana Hub CEO Magzhan Madiyev presented Startup City , a digital platform bringing together startup support, education, laboratories, venture financing, and international partnerships. The visit concluded Kazakhstan’s AI Month program.

title: Twelve years of distributed SQLite
body:
In September 2014 I published a short post announcing rqlite . The idea was simple: take SQLite , put a Raft log in front of it, and replicate every write to a cluster so that the loss of a node did not mean the loss of the data. The source went on GitHub that same weekend. As far as I can tell, that was the first open-source system to combine Raft and SQLite. Nobody else was doing it, and for several years nobody else tried.
Today “distributed SQLite” is a category with a dozen projects in it, a few of them venture-funded, two of them acquired. Since the people now writing about the category tend to start the story around 2021, I thought I should write down the version that starts in 2014. I was there for all of it.
The need was concrete. A clustered system I worked on at jut.io needed a small amount of relational storage, and the question of which node should hold it had no good answer. I realized that replicating SQLite with a consensus protocol was the answer. We went another way at work, but I kept building rqlite because the problem was general and the solution was small. The first version used goraft , the same library InfluxDB and etcd used at the time (I subsequently joined InfluxDB as a core developer around the same time). In early 2016 I replaced it with Hashicorp’s Raft implementation which rqlite still uses.
The design decision that mattered most was made then and never changed. rqlite is a CP system . Writes must go through the leader, a majority must acknowledge, and a partitioned minority refuses writes. Everything else, the HTTP API , the read-consistency levels , the snapshotting , followed from that.
Two things deserve mention for honesty’s sake. Expensify had been replicating SQLite inside its own infrastructure for years with a Paxos -style protocol; they released it as Bedrock in 2016 . And ActorDB, an Erlang system that gave each “actor” its own SQLite database replicated by Raft, appeared around the same time as rqlite . Neither was widely adopted outside its origin, but both show the idea was in the air. What rqlite did was make it a standalone, general-purpose, open-source thing anyone could run.
Canonical built dqlite to get LXD and later MicroK8s an embedded replicated store without running etcd. Mark Shuttleworth actually called me once, and we talked, hoping that rqlite could be made to work, but it never quite fit. dqlite began in Go and was rewritten in C with its own Raft library. It is the project most similar to rqlite in intent, and the main difference is of one of packaging: dqlite is a library you embed, rqlite is a server you run. Canonical’s need was a database inside their products: mine was a database beside anyone’s product.
Ben Johnson (whom I worked with at InfluxDB) released Litestream in early 2021 . Litestream does not use consensus at all. It watches the SQLite WAL and streams it to S3 , giving you disaster recovery for a single-node SQLite database at almost no cost. Ben’s argument was that most applications do not need a cluster; they use one machine and need a way to recover if it dies. He was right about a great many applications, and the “SQLite is enough” movement of the next few years, with blog posts and conference talks, owes a lot to that argument.
Litestream and rqlite answer different questions. Litestream: what if the machine dies? rqlite: what if the machine dies and I cannot wait to restore? The first question is more common, the second is the one people have when they come to rqlite.
Fly.io hired Ben in 2022 and shipped LiteFS , which replicates SQLite at filesystem level with leases from Consul . It was the first attempt to make replicated SQLite a platform feature rather than a thing you deploy. And in a final twist, Litestream inspired rqlite’s v8.0 approach to handling the SQLite WAL.
Two projects in 2022 took approaches that neither rqlite nor Litestream had. cr-sqlite added CRDTs to SQLite as an extension, so that multiple writers could diverge and merge without a leader. That is the AP corner of the design space, and it suits local-first applications where rqlite’s CP guarantees would be a hindrance.
libSQL forked SQLite itself. ChiselStrike, later Turso , wanted to change things inside the engine that the SQLite project, which does not accept outside contributions, would not change. On top of the fork they built a hosted service with replicas at the edge. Turso raised venture money on that, and in 2026 Supabase acquired them .
Around the same time, SQLite Cloud appeared, offering hosted SQLite replicated with Raft. It is the project closest to rqlite’s original design, wrapped in a cloud service.
Cloudflare announced D1 in 2022, SQLite as a serverless database inside their edge network, and later put SQLite storage inside Durable Objects . This is replicated SQLite as a managed product from a company that does not need to tell you how it works. Turso’s service is the same shape. The category had gone from “a thing you run” to “a thing you buy.”
The core was right. SQLite as a storage engine, with replication added on the outside, has been reinvented by at least eight teams with different needs and different protocols. Nobody has found a reason to stop doing it.
The design space has three corners, and they appeared in order. Consensus first (rqlite, dqlite): one leader, strong consistency, a cluster.
