In the education sector, the Vice President also inaugurated Yerwa Practice Mega Primary School, built by the Zulum administration, and another mega primary school delivered under the Kashim Shettima Free Education Programme. The programme, regarded as one of the Vice President’s key education initiatives, provides free education for orphans and vulnerable children. The projects underscore the Borno government’s strategy of linking post-conflict recovery with investments in essential public services, particularly healthcare and education. For a state grappling with the long-term effects of insurgency, expanding access to specialist medical services and strengthening the institutions responsible for training health workers remain critical to improving living conditions and rebuilding public infrastructure. The new teaching hospital is expected to provide a major boost to those efforts by bringing advanced diagnostic services, specialist treatment and medical training together in one institution.

title: CBN Grants JPMorgan Approval-in-Principle to Establish Merchant Bank in Nigeria
body: ·Cardoso says objective is to build stable, internationally connected financial system ·Apex bank seeks public feedback to close gaps in financial reforms, improve policy delivery James Emejo in Abuja and Nume Ekeghe in Lagos The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) has granted approval-in-principle to global financial services group, JPMorgan to establish a merchant bank in the country. The approval serves to deepen international participation in the country’s financial markets. The apex bank disclosed the approval in a statement issued yesterday by CBN Director, Corporate Communications and Investor Relations Department, Mr. Michael Akuka. Commenting on the development, CBN Governor, Mr. Olayemi Cardoso, was quoted to have said the central bank remained committed to building a financial system capable of attracting investment and supporting economic growth. Cardoso explained, “Our objective is to build a financial system that is stable, competitive and internationally connected, one that commands confidence and can effectively support investment and economic growth.” He said the central bank was encouraged by growing interest from international financial institutions but stressed the importance of sustaining reforms and maintaining credible financial markets. The proposed institution, to operate as JPMorgan Merchant Bank Nigeria Limited, must, however, fulfil outstanding regulatory requirements and obtain a final banking licence before commencing operations. The approval also aligns with the central bank’s broader efforts to strengthen financial stability, deepen domestic financial markets and restore international confidence in the Nigerian economy. Under the approval, the apex bank disclosed that it had cleared Adedapo Adedayo Olagunju for appointment as managing director of the proposed merchant bank. It also approved Latter Kevin George, Nzelu Chinedum Izunwanne and Syed Gabriel Murtaza as non-executive directors. Alade Sarah Omotunde, Ajayi Olukonyinsola and Adetu Seni were approved as independent non-executive directors. Akuka clarified that the approval-in-principle represented an initial regulatory clearance and does not authorise the proposed bank to begin business. JPMorgan Merchant Bank Nigeria Limited is expected to complete the necessary incorporation process with the Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC) and satisfy other applicable operational and regulatory conditions before the CBN considers issuing its final licence. The apex bank reaffirmed its commitment to maintaining a sound and competitive financial system capable of supporting sustainable economic growth and strengthening Nigeria’s links with global financial markets. The development comes after the conclusion of the recent banking sector recapitalisation programme, which the CBN said had strengthened the capacity, resilience and competitiveness of the industry. Meanwhile, the CBN has said feedback from businesses, financial institutions, state governments and community groups could reveal gaps between the design of its monetary and financial sector reforms and their impact on households and enterprises. The bank also called for closer collaboration with stakeholders to improve implementation and expand access to financial services nationwide. CBN Director, Stakeholder Engagement and Institutional Relations Department, Mrs. Hakama Sidi Ali, stated this in Ibadan, Oyo State, at the CBN Listens Programme, a platform for public engagement on monetary and financial sector policies. Speaking on the theme, ‘Towards a Robust, Resilient and Inclusive Financial System for Sustainable Economic Growth’, Sidi Ali said sustained dialogue was essential not only to build public confidence and correct misconceptions about the Bank’s policies, but also to identify practical challenges facing businesses and households. She said the reforms under Cardoso were designed to restore macroeconomic stability, strengthen financial markets, improve transparency and position the financial system to support investment, wealth creation and poverty reduction. Among the measures she highlighted were the unification of foreign exchange rates and the introduction of the Bloomberg BMatch trading system, which she said were intended to improve transparency, efficiency and confidence in FX transactions. She also described the completion of the banking sector recapitalisation programme as a major milestone, saying stronger capital positions would improve banks’ ability to absorb shocks and finance productive sectors. However, she stressed that the reforms went beyond financial stability to ensuring that economic opportunities and financial services reached underserved communities. The CBN director also highlighted the Bank’s introduction of the Non-Resident Bank Verification Number (NRBVN), designed to improve banking access for Nigerians living abroad, and the unveiling of the Nigeria Payments System Vision 2028. She said the Bank had introduced measures to strengthen liquidity management and improve monetary policy transmission, including the application of a 75 per cent Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) to non-Treasury Single Account public sector deposits. The policy forms part of the CBN’s efforts to manage liquidity in the banking system and contain inflationary pressures. She also cited the Nigerian Overnight Financing Rate (NOFR), developed in collaboration with the Financial Markets Dealers Association. According to her, the benchmark provides a transparent, market-based reference rate for short-term funding transactions and brings Nigeria’s money market infrastructure closer to international best practices. The measures, she said, reflected the Bank’s efforts to improve monetary policy effectiveness, strengthen market operations and restore confidence in the financial system. On financial inclusion, the CBN director said sustainable growth would remain out of reach without broader access to financial services, particularly for people and businesses in underserved and unserved communities.

title: 98 Bag First Class as Achievers University Graduates 836
body: .Says private varsity students deserve NELFUND, TETFund benefits Fidelis David in Akure No fewer than 98 students of Achievers University, Owo, Ondo State, will graduate with First Class honours as the institution prepares to graduate 836 students at its 16th convocation ceremony scheduled for October 31. The graduating class comprises 786 undergraduate and 50 postgraduate students. Of the undergraduates, 423 earned Second Class Upper Division degrees, 229 obtained Second Class Lower Division, while 36 graduated with Third Class degrees. The Vice Chancellor, Prof. Omolola Irinoye, disclosed the figures yesterday during a press briefing at the university’s Senate Chamber in Owo, where she outlined preparations for the convocation and defended the institution’s academic standards. Nursing Science recorded the highest number of undergraduate graduates, with 191, followed by Computer Science (HIM) with 64, while Law and Medical Laboratory Science produced 61 graduates each. Accounting recorded 56 graduates, while Human Anatomy had 41. The 50 postgraduate graduates comprise 25 Master of Science (M.Sc.) students, 22 students in doctoral or combined MPhil/Ph.D. programmes, and three Postgraduate Diploma (PGD) students. Accounting recorded the highest postgraduate enrolment, with 16, followed by Business Administration with 15 and Nursing Science with 10. Responding to accusations that private universities award too many first class compared with public institutions, Irinoye said Achievers University had no reason to apologise for its students’ performance, insisting that the institution invested substantially in quality assurance and an enabling learning environment. “We have 98 students with First Class. For private universities that believe in quality education and invest in giving quality education, to whom so much is given, so much is also expected,” she said. The Vice Chancellor explained that the university maintained detailed records of students’ continuous assessments and other academic requirements, stressing that students who failed to meet the stipulated attendance threshold or complete their continuous assessment requirements were not permitted to sit examinations. “In our university, if a student does not meet up with 70 per cent attendance of classes, we don’t do exams. If you do not fulfil all the continuous assessment requirements, you do not do exams. If you fail, you must do whatever you are expected to do to pass,” she said. Irinoye said the university had established a well-funded quality assurance unit to monitor teaching and learning, with personnel assigned to observe classroom activities and assess lecturers’ compliance with academic standards. Heads of departments and level advisers were also expected to monitor students’ progress, while lecturers were required to submit course syllabuses for review before the commencement of each academic session. She attributed the institution’s growing patronage to its investment in teaching facilities, electricity, staff development and technology, as well as confidence built among parents and guardians through the performance of their children. She added that the university had developed an artificial intelligence policy for implementation in the current academic session and was training staff and students to adapt to emerging technologies. The Vice Chancellor called on the federal government to extend student financing and research support opportunities to qualified students and institutions in the private university system, arguing that access to public support should not be determined solely by institutional ownership. “Our students are not benefiting from NELFUND. We don’t benefit from TETFund,” she said, advocating equitable access to educational support. She also said the university had sustained scholarship schemes and flexible payment arrangements since its establishment in 2007 to support students from less-privileged backgrounds. On medical training, she disclosed that the institution was developing its own teaching hospital but would continue collaborating with the Federal Medical Centre and other clinical facilities to provide students with practical experience and access to specialists. She stressed that the convocation activities will begin on Saturday, October 24, with the maiden White Coat Ceremony for 91 medical students. Other events include the induction of graduate engineers on October 26, Public Health graduates on October 27, Medical Laboratory Science graduates on October 28 and graduate nurses on October 29. “The convocation lecture, scheduled for October 30, will be delivered by the Director General of the Securities and Exchange Commission, Dr. Emomotimi Agama, while the award of degrees, presentation of prizes and conferment of honorary doctoral awards on three eminent Nigerians will take place on October 31. The ceremonies will conclude with a thanksgiving service on November 1.”

title: Counterfeit Products: Ex-NBA Secretary Seeks Life Sentence, N20m Fine
body: Wale Igbintade A former Secretary of the Nigerian Bar Association (NBA), Adebisi Iyaniwura, has petitioned the Senate to consider life imprisonment for aggravated counterfeiting offences, a minimum fine of N20 million and a mandatory 10-year jail term as part of proposed measures to curb the circulation of fake and adulterated products in Nigeria. In a petition dated October 21, 2026, and received at the Federal Secretariat in Abuja, Iyaniwura urged the Senate Committees on Industry, Trade and Investment and Health to initiate amendments to existing laws governing the production, importation, distribution and sale of counterfeit and unwholesome products. He also addressed the petition to the Attorney General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, seeking coordinated legislative and executive action against what he described as a serious threat to public health, consumer safety and national security. The legal practitioner expressed concern over the continued circulation of counterfeit goods in Nigerian markets, warning that unscrupulous manufacturers, importers, distributors and traders were exposing consumers to products capable of causing serious illness, injury and death. Describing the practice as a “satanic act”, Iyaniwura accused some business operators of placing profits above human lives. “Nigerians are daily being killed by the satanic acts of unscrupulous business people in their desperation to make profits at the cost of Nigerians’ blood,” he said. He argued that counterfeiting should not be treated merely as commercial fraud, given its potential consequences for public health, consumer safety and legitimate businesses. Among the products identified in the petition are food items, pharmaceuticals and automobile spare parts. According to him, consumers who unknowingly purchase counterfeit products risk suffering financial losses, serious health complications and, in some circumstances, death. He warned that fake food products and medicines could expose consumers to harmful substances or products that fail to meet established safety and quality standards. He also raised concerns about substandard automobile components, which could compromise vehicle safety and contribute to fatal road accidents. To address the problem, Iyaniwura called for amendments to existing legislation to introduce stiffer penalties capable of deterring individuals and businesses involved in the manufacture, importation, storage, distribution and sale of counterfeit products. Under his proposal, offenders would face a minimum fine of N20 million and a mandatory 10-year prison sentence, while life imprisonment would be considered for aggravated offences warranting the most severe punishment under the proposed framework. He maintained that tougher sanctions would send a clear message that the deliberate manufacture and distribution of potentially dangerous products for financial gain should attract serious criminal consequences. Beyond imprisonment and fines, the former NBA secretary called for the forfeiture of premises, properties and other assets linked to counterfeiting operations. He proposed that such assets be forfeited in accordance with applicable proceeds-of-crime legislation, arguing that the measure would help authorities deprive offenders of the financial benefits of the illegal trade and disrupt the networks sustaining it. Another major proposal is the introduction of provisions requiring counterfeit-related cases to be concluded within 90 days. He argued that prolonged prosecutions could undermine enforcement efforts and allow alleged offenders to continue operating while cases remain pending. He therefore urged lawmakers to consider measures to expedite the determination of cases involving the production, importation, storage and distribution of counterfeit goods. The proposed 90-day timeline would, however, require careful consideration of court procedures, evidential requirements and the capacity of the justice system to ensure timely adjudication without compromising fair hearing and due process. In addition to tougher penalties and expedited trials, Iyaniwura proposed mandatory QR-code traceability for consumable products nationwide, beginning with pharmaceuticals. Under the proposed system, QR codes would enable consumers and regulatory authorities to verify product information and trace goods through the supply chain. He argued that the technology could help identify suspicious products, establish their origins, track distribution channels and support investigations into suspected counterfeiting. The petitioner maintained that combating counterfeiting required a comprehensive approach combining tougher criminal sanctions, asset forfeiture, faster prosecution and improved product-tracking systems. He also highlighted the implications for legitimate businesses, which face unfair competition when counterfeit products are sold alongside genuine goods. The petition was received at the Federal Secretariat in Abuja on October 21, 2026. No formal response from the relevant Senate committees or the Attorney General of the Federation was included in the information provided.

title: Nestle Nigeria Inaugurates Climate-smart Boreholes, Water Treatment Plants in Agbara
body: Charles Ajunwa Nestle Nigeria Plc has marked a major milestone in its Water Regeneration Project with the inauguration of eight climate-smart boreholes and water treatment plants in communities within the Agbara catchment in Ogun State. A statement by the Corporate Affairs Manager, Nestle Nigeria, Toju Egbebi, said these facilities form part of a wider programme spanning the Agbara catchment in Ogun State and the Abaji catchment in the Federal Capital Territory. “The water regeneration project is structured around four connected pillars: Water Access, delivered through 24 climate-smart boreholes-eight in Agbara and 16 in Abaji; water quality, supported by treatment plants, routine monitoring, the national water quality advocacy campaign and practical water safety guidance; water conservation, advanced through rainwater harvesting systems; and water governance, strengthened through community water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) committees and governance training. These measures provide local oversight, clarify responsibilities for safe operation, preventive maintenance, fault reporting and water quality checks, and strengthen community ownership to protect the long-term value of the infrastructure. “For Nestle Waters and Premium Beverages, the water regeneration project links measurable community impact with watershed resilience, responsible water management and business continuity. “It provides an integrated model in which infrastructure expands access, treatment safeguards quality, rainwater harvesting supports conservation, advocacy strengthens stewardship and local governance sustains performance,” the statement noted. Speaking at the inauguration, Olutayo Olatunji, Business Executive Officer, Nestle Waters and Premium Beverages, Nestle Nigeria Plc, said, “The Agbara commissioning is an important milestone within our wider Water Regeneration Project and reflects Nestlé’s commitment to helping regenerate local water cycles. By combining treated water infrastructure with local governance and performance monitoring, we are creating a model that improves access, strengthens watershed resilience and delivers enduring value. As we finalise the remaining scope, our focus remains on rigorous delivery and measurable outcomes that benefit communities and support business continuity.” Also Speaking on the project, the Minister of Water Resources and Sanitation, Prof. Joseph Terlumun Utsev, said, “Commissioning a facility is only the beginning; ensuring that it continues to provide safe, reliable and sustainable service is the true measure of success. It is encouraging that this initiative places strong emphasis on governance and water stewardship through the development of a governance training manual for water regeneration and stewardship.” In his address, the Minister of Environment, Balarabe Abbas Lawal, added: “This project demonstrates what strategic public-private collaboration can achieve. By working with regulators, local authorities and host communities, Nestlé has supported an ecosystem for sustainable and equitable access to safe drinking water. The initiative advances Sustainable Development Goal 6 and aligns with Nigeria’s environmental priorities.” Welcoming the project on behalf of the host community, His Royal Majesty, Oba Lukman Jayeola Agunbiade, Olute III, the Alagbara of Agbara Kingdom, said, “Today is a day of gratitude for the people of Agbara. Safe water touches every part of our lives: the health of our children, the dignity of our homes and the hopes of our families. Today, it has come closer to all of us. But Agbara has received more than boreholes; we have received a responsibility. As custodians of this land, I charge our chiefs, Baales, WASH committees and every resident to treat these facilities as our own, guard them against misuse and report faults promptly. What has been started here today, Agbara will sustain for our children and for generations yet unborn.” Victoria Uwadoka, Corporate Communications, Public Affairs and Sustainability Lead, Nestle Nigeria Plc, said, “Through the National Water Quality Advocacy Campaign and the National Water Quality Handbook developed with the Federal Ministry of Water Resources and Sanitation and OPS-WASH, we are helping to take water safety knowledge beyond project sites into homes, schools, communities and institutions. Access alone is not enough. Water must be safe, it must be protected, and communities must have the knowledge to manage it responsibly.” The inauguration of the projects in Agbara reflects the strength of collaboration among public authorities, regulators, traditional institutions, community leaders, WASH Committees, OPS-WASH and other technical partners. As the Abaji sites are completed and handed over, Nestle Nigeria will maintain its focus on disciplined delivery, transparent validation and strong local ownership to create lasting value for communities, strengthen watershed resilience and support the long-term sustainability of the business.

title: FG Adds 544MW Grid Capacity, Unveils 300MVA Transformer in Kano
body: . Upgrades 4 substations to boost industrial, commercial power supply .Targets March 2027 for completion of 132/33kV substation in Katsina Emmanuel Addeh in Abuja and Ahmad Sorondinki in Kano The federal government has added 544MW of electricity transmission capacity in Kano following the inauguration of four substations, with the reconnection of Lee Group to the national grid after more than 30 years of off-grid operations highlighting the economic significance of the projects. It also fixed March 2027 for the completion of a new 132/33kV transmission substation in Mashi Local Government Area of Katsina State, as part of efforts to strengthen electricity supply and boost economic activities across the state. The substations, located at Walalambe, Kumbotso, Dakata and Dan-Agundi, were inaugurated by the Federal Ministry of Power through the Transmission Company of Nigeria (TCN), in partnership with the Kano State Government. Special Adviser on Media and Publicity to the Minister of Power, Adeola Labzy, in a statement in Abuja, said the investments reflected the administration’s commitment to strengthening electricity infrastructure and translating it into economic opportunities across the country. At Walalambe, a new substation with two 40MVA transformers now provides 80MW of capacity, while Kumbotso has received additional infrastructure at the 330kV level, including 300MVA and 100MVA transformers. Dakata and Dan-Agundi have each gained an additional 100MVA transformer at the 132kV level. The projects are expected to ease congestion at overloaded substations and improve bulk electricity supply to industrial clusters, commercial centres and residential communities that have faced constraints in accessing power. For businesses, the government said the expansion is expected to create room for increased production and reduce the limitations imposed by inadequate electricity infrastructure. Lee Group’s return to grid supply after three decades of operating independently, the government said, is one of the most notable outcomes of the intervention. At Walalambe, six outgoing feeders will serve the Tokarawa Industrial Area, Eastern Bypass, Maiduguri Road, Hadejia Road and neighbouring communities, extending the benefits of the new infrastructure to businesses and households across the state. The Dan-Agundi upgrade is also significant for Kano’s ancient town, the Emir’s Palace and adjoining communities, following the restoration of substantial capacity at the substation after fire damage. The federal government said the projects aligned with President Bola Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda, which places improved power infrastructure at the centre of efforts to stimulate economic activity and national development. Meanwhile, in Kumbotso, the government inaugurated a new 1x300MVA, 330/132/33kV and 1x100MVA, 132/33kV power transformer, boosting electricity supply capacity in the state by 25 per cent. The Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe, who performed the inauguration in Kano, said the project was part of the administration’s commitment to strengthening the nation’s electricity infrastructure. Speaking at the ceremony, Tegbe said the Kumbotso reinforcement will support businesses, industries and households in Kano metropolis and environs. “Its true value lies in the factories that are able to sustain production, the small businesses that are able to serve more customers, and a community better equipped to pursue its aspirations,” the minister said. He disclosed that before the upgrade, Kumbotso Transmission Substation had an installed transformation capacity of 600MVA at the 330/132kV level, comprising four 150MVA transformers, while at the 132/33kV level, capacity stood at 220MVA. “The project we are commissioning today replaces one existing 150MVA transformer with a 300MVA, 330/132/33kV transformer, and the existing 40MVA transformer with a 100MVA, 132/33kV transformer. “Upstream transformation capacity has therefore increased from 600MVA to 750MVA, a 25 per cent increase. Downstream capacity has risen from 220MVA to 280MVA, an increase of approximately 27.3 per cent,” Tegbe explained. In his remarks, the Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer of the TCN, Sule Abdulaziz, has described the newly inaugurated 2x40MVA, 132/33kV Walalambe Transmission and other substations as a critical addition to Kano’s power infrastructure. He said the project, awarded in 2005 to ease load on the Dakata and Dan Agundi substations, will strengthen bulk supply to Kano metropolis. Abdulaziz said the substation provides a combined capacity of 80MVA, approximately 64MW, to serve Tokarawa Industrial Area, Eastern Bypass, Maiduguri Road, Hadejia Road and adjoining communities through KEDCO’s network. In another development, the Minister of Power, Tegbe, said that the federal government has fixed March 2027 for the completion of a new 132/33kV transmission substation in Mashi Local Government Area of Katsina State. Tegbe, who disclosed this during the groundbreaking ceremony for the project in Garo, Mashi LGA, noted that compensation for affected properties had been fully paid before the commencement of construction. The project, being executed through the Transmission Company of Nigeria (TCN), comprises 2x60MVA transformers, providing a combined transmission capacity of 120MVA, equivalent to 96 megawatts. The minister also unveiled 2×60MVA, 132/33kV power transformers in the Kankia Local Government Area of the state, as part of efforts to strengthen electricity infrastructure in the state. He also inspected the 2x100MVA, 132/33kV GIS transmission substation project at Katsina 330/132/33kV substation alongside Governor Dikko Umaru Radda and other top federal and state governments officials. Speaking at the groundbreaking ceremony in Garo, Tegbe said the Mashi substation would enhance the transmission network’s capacity to deliver available electricity to Katsina and its environs upon completion. “The federal government, through the Transmission Company of Nigeria, is providing this new 2×60MVA, 132/33kV transmission substation. “On completion, it will provide 120MVA of transmission capacity, equivalent to 96 megawatts. This will strengthen the network’s ability to deliver available electricity within Katsina and its environs and support productive activity and household welfare,” he said. Tegbe urged TCN, the contractor and supervising engineers to ensure strict adherence to the March 2027 completion deadline, while maintaining high standards of workmanship and safety throughout the construction process. He stressed that every phase of the project, including equipment manufacturing, civil works, installation and testing, must comply with the required technical standards to prevent defects and ensure the facility’s long-term reliability. The minister described the substation as part of the federal government’s commitment to providing critical infrastructure to support enterprise, employment generation and economic prosperity. He commended President Bola Tinubu for supporting investments in the power sector, adding that dependable infrastructure was essential to achieving the country’s economic development objectives. Tegbe called on residents of Mashi to cooperate with the construction team, protect the facility and report suspicious activities around the project site to safeguard the infrastructure and facilitate its timely completion. He urged all institutions involved to ensure that the groundbreaking ceremony translated into measurable progress, while keeping the host community informed throughout the construction and commissioning process. In his remarks, Governor Radda commended President Tinubu for approving three transmission substation projects in the state to strengthen electricity transmission and supply to the growing population. Radda described the projects as significant investments in the state’s economic development and expressed appreciation to the president for extending critical infrastructure to the state. He said the federal government’s intervention demonstrated its commitment to improving electricity infrastructure and supporting economic growth.

title: Oil Theft: Navy Uncovers Another Set of Reservoirs Containing 25,000 Litres of Stolen Crude Oil
body: .Pushes for indigenous manufacturing of military hardware, greater investment in research, innovation Linus Aleke in Abuja The Nigerian Navy has uncovered three dugout reservoirs containing approximately 25,000 litres of a substance suspected to be crude oil in Obodo Omadino, Delta State. It also called for greater investment in indigenous manufacturing of military equipment, arguing that a navy that depends entirely on other countries for its technology cannot fully control its operational readiness. The Service also disclosed that at least 19 suspected drug peddlers were arrested during a series of joint operations with the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) in Warri. Substances suspected to be illicit drugs were also recovered during the operations. According to a statement by the Director of Naval Information, Navy Captain Abiodun Folorunsho, the discovery of the suspected crude oil was made by Nigerian Navy Ship (NNS) Delta on 21 October 2026 under Operation Delta Sentinel. He said the reservoirs and their contents were handled in accordance with established procedures, stressing that the discovery had disrupted a suspected storage facility that could have facilitated the accumulation and onward movement of stolen crude oil. He added that two joint operations conducted between 19 and 22 October 2026 by NNS Delta and the NDLEA led to the arrest of 19 suspects at locations suspected of being used for the illicit storage, sale and distribution of drugs within the Warri area. “Recovered exhibits included 10 cards of tramadol, 20 litres of Monkey Tail, 35 kilogrammes of cannabis, 18 kilogrammes of Colorado and other related items,” he said. Captain Folorunsho said the suspects and recovered exhibits had been handed over to the NDLEA Warri Area Command for further investigation and necessary legal action. He noted that crude oil theft and illicit drug distribution posed distinct but serious threats to economic security and public safety. He added that the Nigerian Navy would intensify intelligence-led operations and strengthen cooperation with relevant agencies to disrupt illicit petroleum activities, tackle drug distribution networks and support the prosecution of offenders. The Navy also urged members of the public to provide timely and credible information to security agencies to help identify criminal activities, protect national assets and safeguard communities across the Niger Delta. Apart from calling for greater investment in indigenous manufacturing of military equipment, the Service also noted that the rising cost of imported platforms and spare parts, coupled with lengthy supply lead times, made the development of indigenous capabilities imperative. It therefore called for increased investment in research and innovation to support a robust domestic defence manufacturing industry. The Chief of Naval Transformation and Innovation (CNTI), Rear Admiral Chijioke Onyemaobi, made this call at the ongoing Nigerian Navy Research and Development Seminar 2026, being held at Naval Headquarters in Abuja. He said, “Our maritime environment is changing rapidly. Unmanned systems, artificial intelligence, advanced sensors and additive manufacturing are reshaping how navies fight, sustain and maintain their fleets. Research and development are the bridge between emerging technologies and our operational needs, and the pathway from dependence to self-reliance. “I urge all participants to share their knowledge openly and constructively so that our deliberations yield practical recommendations for capabilities that are relevant, sustainable and responsive to our operational requirements.” Declaring the seminar themed ‘Deepening the Application of Emerging Technologies for Operational Effectiveness’ open, the Chief of the Naval Staff (CNS), Vice Admiral Idi Abbas, said progress in indigenous shipbuilding and maintenance through naval dockyards and shipyards demonstrated the Navy’s growing capacity to develop and sustain operational capabilities locally. He added that emerging technologies were relevant beyond the maritime domain, particularly in supporting the Navy’s contributions to counter-terrorism and counter-insurgency operations. Vice Admiral Abbas, who was also the Special Guest of Honour and keynote speaker, said the seminar provided an opportunity to examine how emerging technologies could address operational challenges, optimise available resources and strengthen the Navy’s contribution to national security amid the growing influence of technology on contemporary naval operations. He noted that the maritime security landscape was changing rapidly, with threats becoming increasingly sophisticated. “Criminal networks continue to exploit technology to evade detection and threaten critical national assets. An effective response must therefore be driven by corresponding improvements in timely intelligence, accurate surveillance and the ability to deploy appropriate forces where they are most needed. The objective is not simply to acquire more technology, but to achieve greater operational effect with the resources available to us,” he said. He added that experience had demonstrated the value of technology-enabled maritime surveillance in improving maritime domain awareness and directing patrols towards identified threats. According to him, this intelligence-led approach had enabled more efficient deployment of limited naval assets, reduced fuel and maintenance costs, and improved operational responses. He noted that surveillance of offshore installations and other critical national infrastructure had strengthened the Navy’s efforts to combat crude oil theft and related economic crimes, helping to create a more secure environment for oil production. He further stressed that emerging technologies offered opportunities to extend these capabilities to creeks and adjoining coastal areas for pipeline monitoring and protection, thereby safeguarding vital national assets and supporting sustained oil production.

title: IDF, Shin Bet launch multi-day West Bank counterterrorism operations after deadly Hamas attack
body: IDF troops, the Shin Bet (Israel Security Agency), Border Police officers, and the Judea Regional Brigade launched a counterterrorism operation in the Hebron area following Friday morning's deadly Hamas terrorist attack, the IDF and Shin Bet announced in a joint statement on Friday night.Security forces are conducting systematic searches for terrorist infrastructure and weapons in the area and questioning dozens of suspects, according to the joint statement.The operation is focused on the area out of which the terrorists operated and is expected to last several days.⭕️ In response to the shooting attack in which 2 IDF soldiers fell and several others were wounded, the IDF along with other security forces launched a targeted & limited counterterrorism operation in the Hebron area, from which the terrorists had emerged. Troops have begun conducting precise searches throughout the area to locate and dismantle terrorist infrastructure and weapons, while questioning suspects. Residents living in the area where forces are operating will be able to leave through 3 designated exit points, following questioning and security screening. Individuals who raise suspicion during the screening process will be referred to security forces for further questioning.— Israel Defense Forces (@IDF) October 23, 2026Residents living within the operational area will be permitted to leave through three designated exit points after undergoing questioning and security checks. Anyone who raises suspicion during the screening process will be taken for further questioning by security forces.Parallel operations were underway in the Jenin and Nablus areas to locate weapons and carry out arrests, alongside the ongoing counterterrorism operation in Hebron, Walla reported Saturday morning. Security forces were also operating in Kafr Aqab in east Jerusalem and the West Bank town of Tamun, according to the report.The operation follows a series of counterterrorism measures carried out since Friday morning, including mapping the terrorists' homes, sealing off the Hebron and Halhul areas, establishing roadblocks, and conducting operations in nearby villages. Security forces are also removing illegal infrastructure that could pose a security threat near the site of the attack.Security forces are currently operating at dozens of locations throughout Judea and Samaria as part of ongoing efforts to prevent terrorist attacks, protect Israeli civilians, and eliminate security threats, the statement added.Terrorists attacked IDF soldiers at Judea JunctionThe attack took place at Judea Junction, where two terrorists traveling in a car opened fire on four soldiers stationed at the junction. IDF sources estimated that the attackers had originally intended to continue past the junction and carry out a larger attack on the heavily traveled Route 35, but opened fire after realizing they would be unable to proceed.Staff Sergeant Ron Yonatan Roytman, 23, from Ashkelon, and Sergeant Yuval Shai Svilem, 20, from Hod Hasharon, were killed in the attack, while three others were lightly wounded.Both terrorists were killed during the confrontation, and the IDF said no additional terrorists were involved.Netanyahu orders closure of Hebron following attackFollowing the attack, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered security forces to seal off Hebron and prepare for a broader lockdown across the West Bank."I have instructed the IDF and security forces to immediately impose a closure on the city of Hebron and prepare for a full lockdown of all of Judea and Samaria, beginning today," Netanyahu said, adding that the IDF would carry out extensive waves of arrests."We will pursue Hamas terrorists and those who send them, wherever they are and at any time," Netanyahu said. "You have nowhere to hide."Yonah Jeremy Bob, Tzvi Jasper, Amichai Stein, and Ariella Roitman contributed to this report.

title: Severe flooding hits Four Corners region, more expected through the weekend
body:
Aaron Schenk rafted down the flooded Animas River in southwestern Colorado on Friday. He passed by an inundated event space. Aaron Schenk/Aaron Schenk hide caption
On Thursday morning in Hurricane, Utah, Juana Puga stood in ankle-deep brownish water asking herself: "Why again?"
Just a couple hours earlier, at around 8:30am, Puga went out to run some errands. It wasn't raining outside, she says. But when she returned to her house, rainwater had flooded her whole yard.
"It was just coming in so fast that it was just hard to even understand," Puga says. "Within five minutes most of my house was underwater."
Rare, heavy rainfall started to hit New Mexico, Colorado, Utah and Arizona on Wednesday. Since then, brown-colored floodwaters have led to road closures, mandatory evacuations and emergency declarations across the four states. The southern Utah city of Hurricane issued an emergency declaration on Thursday after flooding damaged more than 100 homes and RVs.
The view inside Juana Puga's flooded house in Hurricane, Utah, when she opened the door on Thursday. Juana Puga/Juana Puga hide caption
Puga, her husband, and five young boys just moved back into their house on Oct. 1. A flood in August forced them to renovate and rebuild. Less than a month after her sons fixed up their new rooms, Puga says she's living through a "nightmare" again.
"We were literally in our house for only 22 days," she says. The family is staying with Puga's in-laws in one room, but are hoping to move to a rental next week.
"It's just devastating," Puga says. "So much work we put into our house and I just thought, 'why again?' "
In response to a post on X that showed brownish-red floodwaters in Hurricane, Gov. Spencer Cox, wrote on Thursday: "Our hearts are with the families whose homes and livelihoods have been impacted."
Floodwater filled one of the rooms for Juana Puga's kids in Hurricane, Utah. Juana Puga/Juana Puga hide caption
Over the weekend, the flood watch extended to central and southern New Mexico and far west Texas.
As of Saturday, areas of southern Utah, southwest Colorado, and the northern parts of Arizona and New Mexico had been hit the hardest. The intense rain led to rapidly rising floodwaters, Thursday and Friday.
In San Juan County, N.M., looking out a window on Friday afternoon, Devin Neeley saw light, puffy clouds and a blue sky. The county's public information officer for emergency management called the stark contrast to the brown rainwaters "surreal."
"[The sky] belies really the danger that is coming down the river in historic levels," Neeley says. "We have not seen flooding like this in generations."
Neeley says emergency responders rescued people on their roofs after floodwater inundated their homes. The county was put under an emergency declaration and residents in susceptible areas were told to evacuate Thursday afternoon.
"These are communities that have beautiful riverfront places to live," Neeley says. "And unfortunately, that's a problem today."
In Farmington, N.M. , located in the center of the hard-hit regions, Police Chief Steve Hebbe said at a press conference on Friday that "this is singular and this is real."
"So far, we have not had any deaths that is very fortunate, but this is not something that should be played with," Hebbe said.
Colorado Gov. Jared Polis declared disaster emergencies in 12 counties. Polis also authorized the use of National Guard members to assist with rescue efforts in southwest Colorado.
Floodwaters surround trailers at the Fun Valley Family Resort campground and RV part in South Fork, Colo., early Friday, Oct. 23, 2026. South Fork Fire Rescue/AP hide caption
On Friday morning, La Plata County sheriff closed parts of the Animas River in Durango, Colo. to recreation, KSUT reported .
Aaron Schenk took out a 14-foot cataraft to glide down 26 miles of the Animas River that weren't closed.
"There were real big waves, fast currents, lots of water flooding," Schenk says. "The river in spots was half a mile wide when normally it's a couple hundred feet at most."
Schenk, who owns a sewage disposal company called Mountain Septic , expects to see an uptick in repairs across La Plata County.
"This is definitely not normal," he says, adding that the region has "received more moisture in the last, 6 or 8 weeks than we have in the entire 12 months prior."
The flooding comes after extreme weather hit the Southwest throughout the week. Arizona saw baseball-sized hail and a possible tornado that injured at least one person Wednesday evening.
The region's mountainous and desert terrain is conducive to flooding. In August, intense flash flooding in the Grand Canyon led to multiple deaths.
Severe thunderstorm warnings started earlier in the week, says Kris Sanders, a meteorologist at the National Weather Service in Grand Junction, Colo. The remnants of Hurricane Trudy, which was active from Oct. 15 to Oct. 18, in the Pacific Ocean formed into a slow-moving low-pressure system that worked its way southwest.
Sanders says a lot of the storms weakened as they came through the region, but the heavy rain did not. Portions of southwest Colorado and southeast Utah saw two to four inches, whereas areas with higher elevations, like the San Juan Mountains, got up to six inches. This caused small creeks and streams and rivers to flood.
"Those rainfall amounts are records in themselves," Sanders says.
While the amount of rainfall is rare, he says, these storms typically happen in the region at this time of year. An event last year caused major flooding in the same spots, "like a carbon copy" of this year, Sanders says.
The threat is not over, he says, and thunderstorm watches are active in many of the same areas through Sunday.
Daniel Swain, a climate scientist with the University of California Agriculture and Natural Resources, says the severe thunderstorms are fueled by the large amount of moisture in the air. He says that moisture comes from the record-warm waters off parts of the West Coast, which are driven by an ongoing strong El Niño event and a recent marine heat wave (which he attributes largely to human-caused climate change).
The flooding isn't a surprise, he says, pointing to a prediction he and others made in the spring – that if El Niño materialized according to forecasts, southwestern U.S. could see extreme precipitation events through October.
Now, "that is exactly what we've seen," he says, "because this isn't even the first event this fall."
Puga, whose home flooded in Hurricane, Utah, says she and her neighbors have been cleaning up their properties and are trying to "see the light." She doesn't want to move and leave the community she loves, she says.
"We already did this. We can do it again," Puga says. "But it's just hard."

title: Drug parcels: Teen girl suspected of poisoning Ukrainian servicemen detained in Zhytomyr region
body:
According to Ukrinform, the National Police of Ukraine reported this on Facebook .
"Acting on instructions from her Russian handler, she packaged drugs and sent them by mail, providing fictitious sender details. She was promised at least UAH 5,000 for this," National Police Chief Maksym Tsutskiridze said.
According to him, the organizers contacted servicemen via Telegram and offered them free drugs.
"After the parcels were delivered, the recipients were instructed to take the drugs on camera. They did not know that the capsules contained a lethal dose of methadone," he added.
He said two servicemen in the Zhytomyr region had died from poisoning.
"While investigating these murders, police identified other recipients of the parcels. This made it possible to prevent four more killings in the Kirovohrad, Zaporizhzhia, Chernivtsi and Ivano-Frankivsk regions," Tsutskiridze said.
The girl has been notified of suspicion of aiding and abetting the premeditated murder of two people by prior conspiracy, as well as mailing narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances for the purpose of sale.
Police are also checking whether she was involved in other crimes.
Tsutskiridze added that two of the deceased servicemen had left their military units without authorization, while the servicemen who were saved continued to serve.
Tsutskiridze urged Ukrainian defenders and their relatives to remember that a person offering help, sending gifts or persistently seeking a face-to-face meeting could be acting on behalf of the enemy.
"Be careful when making new acquaintances. Do not accept medicines or other substances, or food or drinks of dubious origin, from people you barely know," he said.
He advised service members and their relatives to save their correspondence and report it to the police by calling 102 if anyone pressures or threatens them or tries to persuade them to consume something.

title: Kostroma paratroopers deliver humanitarian aid to Alyoshki
body:
GENICHESK, October 24. /TASS/. The Kostroma paratroopers have delivered humanitarian aid to the front·line Alyoshki in the Kherson Region located in the area where enemy UAVs operate, a soldier who delivered the cargo to the front line told TASS.
"Our trip was without problems. Everyone understands it, humanity remains. That’s why we’re bringing food and warm clothes to Alyoshki; our backpacks are filled with aid for civilians. The closer you get to the front, the more dangerous it is to move around; there are a lot of drones flying around," the paratrooper said.
He said that despite the threat to their lives, the paratroopers delivered food, medicines, and essential supplies to the local residents. Also, the military personnel ensured the safety of civilians during the delivery.

title: Turkey, Egypt, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia call on Houthis to stop attacks on Saudi Arabia
body:
ANKARA, October 24. /TASS/. Turkey, Egypt, Pakistan, and Saudi Arabia have condemned the Houthi attacks on the kingdom, including strikes against the civilians, infrastructure, and commercial vessels in the Red Sea and the Bab·el·Mandeb Strait, a joint statement by the foreign ministers after a meeting in Istanbul said.
"The ministers have condemned in the strongest terms the unacceptable escalation by the Houthis, which has exacerbated humanitarian suffering. They also condemned the ongoing Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, particularly on the civilian population and infrastructure, and the attacks on commercial shipping in the Red Sea and the Bab·el·Mandeb Strait," the statement issued by the Turkish foreign ministry said.
The foreign ministers expressed "full solidarity with the government of Yemen and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia" and "called on the Houthis to immediately cease all military actions, threats, and attacks and return to the political process" to resolve the conflict.
The foreign ministers "emphasized that the Israeli occupation is the main source of instability in the region and beyond. The ministers called for an immediate end to the ongoing Israeli violence, as well as to attempts to change the legal and historical status of Jerusalem and to put an end to further destruction and the humanitarian tragedy in Palestine. They condemned [Israel’s] previous and current settlement activities in the West Bank and in Jerusalem, as well as settler violence against Palestinians," the statement says. The foreign ministers also "stressed the urgent need to ensure an uninterrupted flow of humanitarian aid to Gaza and to rebuild the region."

title: "The Kindness Mob" has come to the rescue of hundreds of online bullying victims
body: Kahri Salyars of King George, Virginia, was just starting her weight loss journey when her proud husband encouraged her to post a video about it to TikTok."I liked how I looked," Salyars, 28, told CBS News of her feeling after losing 40 pounds. "I liked how happy I genuinely looked."However, the response to the video that was posted in March was toxic. "Then like overnight, hundreds of hate comments," Salyars said. "â¦ 'You're really ugly, you're fat, your husband deserves better.' It just kept going."For a full month after, people piled on with hundreds of insults.  That is, until the tide turned and a wave of encouragement drowned out the trolls."It was weird because, where are all these really nice people coming from?" Salyars asked. It was such a drastic shift, it really defied explanation. To Kahri Salyars it almost felt like an organized effort, like an army of kindness warriors had just come rushing to her defense. That turned out to be exactly what it was.Tyler Brickley of Kansas City, Missouri, runs "The Kindness Mob," a group about half a million strong that secretly battles internet spite. "We make every effort for them to never find out," Brickley said. First, the Kindness Mob picks a target, someone who is being bullied. Then, they shower that person with compliments.Brickley said the goal is to try and make the internet seem kind. "It feels outrageous, but that's exactly what we're trying to do," Brickley said. "And it's the most beautiful thing I've ever been a part of."Since starting the group in 2023, Brickley and his Kindness Mob have digitally rescued about 400 strangers, like Salyars, who just can't stop reading the comments.Salyars eventually figured out Brickley was behind the shift, but it didn't matter. She says her confidence is back. "I would say so," Salyars said. "Positivity overtook the hate."

title: Melania Trump Announces Oleshky Truce as Ukraine and Russia Agree to Civilian Evacuations
body:
In a rare, surprise announcement Friday, Oct. 23, US First Lady Melania Trump said she had brokered a localized ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine in the devastated city of Oleshky, where civilians remain trapped under Moscow’s occupation amid severe shortages of food, medicine and clean water.
The temporary ceasefire, scheduled to begin Oct. 29 according to an official White House statement , is intended to allow humanitarian aid deliveries and evacuations through a designated safe corridor.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
Both countries agreed to temporarily suspend military operations in Oleshky, the statement said, with the first lady and her representative working with Ukrainian and Russian leaders to negotiate the agreement’s timing, technical procedures and implementation.
“The situation in Oleshky is dire. Oleshky is a frontline war city on the brink of disaster,” Melania Trump said.
She warned that the city’s remaining residents, primarily elderly people, urgently need medical attention, medicine, food and clean water. Many have limited electricity, live amid mined roads and face regular military attacks.
“It was abundantly clear that without my intervention, the possibility to bring humanitarian aid into the city and to evacuate the elderly would be impossible,” she added.
Ukrainian officials confirmed preparations to establish safe evacuation routes and deliver humanitarian aid to Russian-occupied Oleshky.
Davyd Arakhamia, head of President Volodymyr Zelensky’s Servant of the People parliamentary faction, said an operation to assist Oleshky and surrounding communities would begin soon.
Ukraine’s Human Rights Commissioner Dmytro Lubinets, who led Kyiv’s negotiating team, confirmed the agreement, outlining three priorities: a ceasefire, humanitarian aid deliveries and safe civilian evacuations.
The Kremlin also confirmed the ceasefire, with spokesman Dmitry Peskov saying Russian military officials were coordinating its implementation, according to AFP.
According to the White House, Melania Trump served as an “Exclusive Intermediary,” helping negotiate the ceasefire’s objectives, procedures and conditions.
Civilian representatives from Ukraine and Russia are expected to visit Oleshky residents in their homes to assess their humanitarian needs.
“Residents who wish to evacuate will receive coordinated support and transportation to their preferred destination. I anticipate some will want to go to Russia, and some to Ukraine,” she said.
The agreement also involves preparations for demining, a critical requirement for transporting aid and evacuating civilians along roads contaminated by explosives.
Melania Trump said she had arranged for an independent American media organization to accompany the humanitarian teams and document their work to help ensure residents’ choices were respected.
Melania Trump said the initiative began after she learned about conditions in Oleshky during a private discussion at her Fostering the Future Together event in New York City, held during the 81st United Nations General Assembly.
She said her team used communication channels established with Russia and Ukraine during six previous operations that reunited 34 children separated from their families during the war.
Ukraine has documented 20,651 cases of children deported or forcibly transferred by Russia since the full-scale invasion. As of mid-October, 2,689 had been returned, leaving thousands still separated from their families.
Both governments subsequently assigned teams to coordinate the Oleshky humanitarian mission, including demining and arrangements for safe passage.
US President Donald Trump praised his wife’s involvement, describing the ceasefire as her initiative.
“What she wants to do is save children,” Trump told reporters.
Asked whether she could participate in upcoming trilateral negotiations involving Ukraine, Russia and the US, Trump replied: “No, but it’s not the worst idea I’ve ever heard.”
Oleshky is located in southern Ukraine, across the Dnipro River from Kherson. Before Russia’s full-scale invasion, the city had approximately 24,000 residents. Today, an estimated 1,700 to 2,000 people remain, primarily elderly residents unable to evacuate, along with approximately 50 children, according to the White House statement.
Sevinj Osmanqizi is an experienced journalist who writes extensively for Kyiv Post on foreign policy, international security and geopolitics. Based in Washington, D.C., her work focuses on Ukraine, Russia’s war and the broader post-Soviet space.

title: Clerk-to-Parliament Djietror resurrects debate and justifies why new Chamber for MPs is important
body: The Clerk-to-Parliament, Ebenezer Ahumah Djietror, has reiterated the need for a review of Parliament’s infrastructure needs to enhance legislative business. He said the Legislature needed a new Chamber, adequate workspaces and meeting facilities to accommodate Members of Parliament (MPs) and staff of the Parliamentary Service. He explained that the existing facilities were inadequate to accommodate MPs and support the effective discharge of their constitutional responsibilities, with the shortage of meeting spaces forcing some caucuses to seek alternative venues. “We do not have a Chamber with complementary facilities that will enable us to discharge our duties properly. We should be able to have enough workspace, meeting areas, division rooms, ministers’ lobbies, caucus lobbies so that when there are issues, a caucus will not necessarily have to file out and travel all the way to Job 600,” he said. Addressing a workshop for members of the Parliamentary Press Corps (PPC) a in Accra, Mr Djietror said the existing caucus meeting rooms could accommodate only about 30 to 35 people, making it difficult for larger groups of MPs to meet effectively. “Look at the Majority Caucus and where in Job 600 will you have space for them to meet and yet you are to meet as a caucus, as it is part of the rules of engagement” he said. The two-day event, sponsored by Parliament, was meant to build the capacity of PPC members in the execution of the mandate as parliamentary reporters. Mr Djietror said the infrastructure constraints were particularly concerning as Parliament prepared for budget consideration, when committees would invite ministries, departments and agencies (MDAs) to provide information on their programmes and expenditure. He explained that committee meetings could involve several officials from each agency, in addition to committee members, putting further pressure on the limited space available. Accurate reportage The Majority Leader, James Agalga, said Parliament’s image should be enhanced through improved performance, accountability and responsible journalism rather than the suppression of criticism. He called on parliamentary journalists to ensure that their reports were accurate, balanced and contextual. Mr Agalga said the media played an indispensable role in helping the public understand Parliament’s work and its contribution to democratic governance. Commendation The Chief Information Officer of Parliament, Dr Kate Addo, commended the media for its contribution to bringing Parliament closer to the people since the inception of the Fourth Republic. She said reports and documentaries produced by journalists had helped the public to understand the work of the Legislature. The Director of the Media Relations Department, David S. Damoah, urged members of the PPC to uphold accuracy, fairness, balance and responsibility in their coverage of parliamentary proceedings to strengthen public trust in the legislature. The Dean of the Parliamentary Press Corps, Simon Agianab, urged parliamentary journalists to uphold professionalism, accuracy and constitutional awareness in their coverage of Parliament.

title: Senators plan to block Trump’s nominees over Ukraine satellite network restrictions — NYT
body:
NEW YORK, October 24. /TASS/. Senators from the Republican and Democratic parties have warned the White House that they will block the confirmation of US President Donald Trump’s government nominees unless the administration guarantees the restoration of Ukraine’s access to satellite communications, The New York Times (NYT) reported citing sources.
It is noted that disagreements between the senators and the administration may escalate after the November 3 midterm elections, when Republicans will likely try to secure the confirmation of dozens of Trump’s nominees to various positions before the new Congress begins its work.
Earlier, American Congresswoman Anna Paulina Luna (a Republican from Florida) called on Democratic lawmakers to stop advocating for the continuation of the Ukrainian conflict and to support Trump’s efforts to resolve it.
The American leader said on Thursday that Ukraine’s access to Starshield military·grade satellite communications was restored. He was commenting on media reports saying he had asked SpaceX CEO Elon Musk to lift restrictions on the use of Starshield in Ukraine. However, former adviser to the Ukrainian Defense Minister Sergey Sternenko later said that the restrictions are partially still in place.

title: Deadly shooting near Paris is a ‘racist terrorist attack’, Macron says
body: French President Emmanuel Macron has labelled a gun attack in a Parisian suburb which killed one person and injured five others “a racist terrorist attack”. Macron said the attack was a “turning point in the life of our Republic and our nation” – the first time there has ever been a random racial killing like this. The attack unfolded over some 15 minutes with the attacker opening fire from his car – first in Trappes to the south-west of Paris, and then in nearby La Verrière – appearing to target people of migrant origin. He was subsequently arrested. Three of those injured, including a 12-year-old girl, remain in a serious condition. Visiting the scene of the attack in Trappes, Macron said people had been targeted for their skin colour or religion and urged the public not to give an inch in the face of what he called “ideologies taking root”. The exact motive remains unclear, but the National Anti-Terrorist Prosecutor’s Office (PNAT) said the incident appeared to be “murder in connection with a terrorist enterprise”. The suspect has been named in French media as Kevin T who, according to PNAT, had four previous convictions which had been “automatically expunged”. The 39-year-old was known to police but not to France’s intelligence services, local media report. He was not on a list of individuals considered to be a serious threat to French security, the national anti-terrorism prosecutor’s office told BFMTV. A member of the suspect’s “immediate family circle” was also taken into custody on Friday, it added. The Mayor of Trappes, Ali Rabeh, said that “an individual fired shots from his vehicle at several people he encountered” on Friday morning. The gunman drove through several neighbourhoods in a grey Renault Clio, according to witnesses. Rabeh said he had “fired randomly” with the seeming intent of causing “as many casualties as possible… he wanted to cause carnage”, he said. The mayor said people had been targeted at a petrol station, a medical centre and a playground in Trappes before the attacker had driven on to nearby La Verrière. A police union official said the suspect had been detained in La Verrière on the main N10 road that runs through the town.The mother of the injured 12-year-old told French broadcaster RTL her daughter suffered eight gunshot wounds and needed surgery. “How could anyone do this to a child?” she asked. The mother said her daughter had been wearing a headscarf and questioned whether this was why she was attacked. “She’s a child who was born in France, in Trappes. She has the right to live in France, to make her life in France,” she added. The attacker reportedly travelled down a main road, shooting intermittently out of his car window. A local police chief told BFMTV that the suspect had used “an older-style semi-automatic weapon” with bursts of fire. Le Parisien reports that the gun dated back to World War Two. PNAT said its investigation also includes “possession of a Category A weapon” – which includes military-grade weapons or weapons capable of firing in bursts. The anti-terrorist office also said its investigation is looking into “conspiracy with a terrorist group for the purpose of preparing crimes against persons”.

title: Kyutai CADRE: Video Autoencoders That Cut World Model Lag Below 230 ms
body: Kyutai has released CADRE , open causal diffusion representation autoencoders for interactive world models. The Kyutai CADRE video autoencoder targets one problem: action lag. Many world models borrow autoencoders from text-to-video generators. Those autoencoders pack many frames into one latent, so every action waits. Per the research paper , CADRE world models run at 20 fps on 1 H100 and react within 230 ms. TL;DR Size: 7 autoencoders, each about 476M trained parameters plus a frozen 86M DINOv3 ViT-B/16 . The world model is 1.2B parameters. Video runs at 288×512, 20 fps. Runs on: 1 H100 (bf16, batch 1). Quantized variants: Not disclosed. Performance: CADRE forms most of the latency-quality frontier. It is as fast and better in 42 of 48 comparisons with MIRA, Wan 2.2, Cosmos and LTX-2. Best: Driving FVD of 162.6 (CADRE-2×16×16, 1 step) against 599.7 for Wan 2.2. Worst: Robot manipulation action following (ARR) of 0.45 for CADRE-2×32×32, against 0.85 for Wan 2.2. What is CADRE? CADRE is a family of video autoencoders from Kyutai built for action-conditioned world models. A world model generates in the autoencoder’s latent space. So the autoencoder’s compression sets both cost per frame and action delay. Compression is written τ×s×s. τ is frames per latent, and s is the spatial factor. The research gives the latency as τ/f plus generation and decode time. At τ = 8 and 20 fps, the chunk alone adds 400 ms. Humans notice their own movement lagging beyond about 230 ms. How does CADRE work? The encoder reuses the MIRA recipe. A frozen DINOv3 extracts per-patch features from each frame. One trained 3D convolution then compresses them into a 64-channel latent. Only this bottleneck changes between the 7 members. The decoder is a causal diffusion transformer with 24 blocks. It streams chunk by chunk. Progressive self-distillation teaches it to decode in 1 or 2 steps. This happens in a single training stage, without an adversarial loss. The autoencoders train on 23 public video sources, about 76k hours. The mix spans web, robot, driving and game video. How was CADRE evaluated? Kyutai trained the same 1.2B causal diffusion transformer on each autoencoder. It used 4 environments: robot manipulation (ABC), human manipulation (EgoDex), driving (PhysicalAI AV) and indoor navigation (RealEstate10K). Each model sees 2 s of real video, then generates 4.8 s. Scores cover image quality (FID), motion quality (FVD) and action following (ARR). ARR uses a frozen inverse dynamics probe. An ARR of 1 matches real video. (function(){var f=document.getElementById('mtp-cadre-frame');window.addEventListener('message',function(e){if(e.data&&e.data.mtpEmbed==='cadre'&&e.data.height){f.style.height=e.data.height+'px';}});})(); What do the benchmarks show? On one H100, CADRE-2×32×32 reacts in 185 ms and sustains 23.4 fps with 1 decoding step. The Wan 2.2 autoencoder needs 317 ms, LTX-2 492 ms and Cosmos 605 ms. DC-AE is faster at 118 ms but frame-by-frame. The gap is widest with a moving camera. In driving, Wan 2.2 FVD reaches 599.7 and LTX-2 913.3. In indoor navigation, LTX-2 ARR falls to 0.04. Against the retrained MIRA decoder, the 1-step diffusion decoder lowers FVD by 1.4 to 2.5×. What are the 4 findings? Decode by diffusion: at strong compression, perceptual regression blurs, while diffusion samples 1 sharp video. Compress time in the autoencoder: patching inside the world model loses detail. At 8 frames, ARR drops from 0.72 to 0.56. Camera motion decides compression: still cameras tolerate temporal compression. Moving cameras favor fewer frames and coarser spatial tokens. Coarse tokens hurt motion first: in robot manipulation, 32× spatial compression multiplies FVD by 2.4 over 16×. FID barely moves. CADRE uses 1 decoding step. All figures are self-reported by Kyutai. Where does CADRE fall short? CADRE does not win everywhere. In robot manipulation, Cosmos posts an FVD of 39.5 against 47.6 for the best 1-step CADRE. At the fast end, DC-AE beats CADRE-1×48×48 in manipulation. Wan 2.2 also reconstructs held-out video far better, at 35.02 dB PSNR. Kyutai team argues reconstruction does not predict rollouts. Wan 2.2 ranks last on indoor rollout FVD. Long latents leave visible seams between chunks. At τ = 8, boundary excess reaches 1.6 to 1.8 across environments. CADRE-4×24×24 is an outlier in navigation, with FVD 403 in driving. Each world model covers one environment at 288×512. Whether findings transfer to generalist models remains open. How can developers use CADRE? The code is MIT licensed. Weights on Hugging Face are CC BY-NC 4.0, so commercial use is excluded. The release covers 7 autoencoders, 4 longer-trained multi-resolution versions and 4 world models on CADRE-2×16×16. A live demo lets you drive them by keyboard. Key Takeaways 7 open autoencoders, one bottleneck apart, isolate compression as the only variable. World models on CADRE run at 20 fps on 1 H100, under 230 ms lag. Driving FVD drops to 162.6, against 599.7 for Wan 2.2. Still cameras favor temporal compression; moving cameras favor spatial compression. Weights are non-commercial (CC BY-NC 4.0); code is MIT. Check out the paper , the Kyutai blog , the GitHub repo and the model collection . All credit goes to the researcher of this project.
